programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and ADCC
functional_description: This signature defines non-classical CD16 monocytes with enhanced iron storage capacity and Fc receptor-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. The programme integrates iron homeostasis (FTH1, ferritin heavy chain) with ADCC machinery (FCGR3A/CD16, FCER1G) and actin-cytoskeleton remodelling for vascular patrolling and immune surveillance.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Master marker of CD16 monocytes; high-affinity FcγRIII for ADCC and immune complex clearance
FTH1: Iron storage protein elevated in CD16 monocytes; supports oxidative metabolism and antimicrobial responses
FCER1G: γ-chain subunit of high-affinity IgE receptor and Fc receptor complexes; essential for ADCC signalling
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein required for Fc receptor signal transduction in ADCC
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator; promotes macrophage activation and vascular smooth muscle interactions
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein; facilitates cell migration and cytoskeletal dynamics during vascular patrolling
COTL1: Actin-binding protein; regulates leukotriene synthesis and cytoskeletal architecture for crawling
LST1: Lipopolysaccharide-inducible membrane protein; enhanced by IFN-γ; involved in pathogen sensing
S100A4, S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins; support cell migration and monocyte activation
CTSS: Cathepsin S; antigen processing and presentation
PSAP: Saposin precursor; lysosomal lipid hydrolysis and autophagy
SERPINA1: Protease inhibitor; tissue protection and inflammatory control
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: CD16+ CD14lo FTH1+ FCGR3A+ with functional ADCC assay (NK-like cytotoxicity). Quantify ferritin and iron content in sorted CD16 vs CD14 monocytes. Assess CX3CR1 expression and vascular crawling capacity in intravital microscopy.

functional_description: This signature defines non-classical CD16 monocytes with elevated iron storage capacity (FTH1), actin-remodeling machinery (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1), and Fc-receptor signaling infrastructure (FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP) for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. The programme integrates metabolic reprogramming with enhanced migratory and cytotoxic effector functions characteristic of patrolling monocytes.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Canonical CD16 marker; enables ADCC and immune complex recognition
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain indicating iron-dependent metabolic remodeling in patrolling monocytes
FCER1G: Gamma chain of Fc receptors; ITAM-bearing signaling adaptor essential for ADCC
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor; couples Fc receptors to downstream cytotoxic signaling
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein; enables rapid cytoskeletal remodeling for crawling and degranulation
COTL1: Actin-binding protein; supports cell migration and 5-lipoxygenase signaling
AIF1: IFN-induced actin-binding protein; promotes macrophage activation and vascular interaction
LST1: LPS/IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein; lymphocyte inhibition linked to immune surveillance
S100A11, S100A4: Calcium-binding proteins; facilitate cell motility and monocyte activation
CTSS: Lysosomal protease; supports antigen presentation and granule-mediated cytotoxicity
PSAP: Saposin precursor; lysosomal protein required for granule maturation
MT-CO2: Elevated mitochondrial respiration; matches high metabolic demand of patrolling monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD16+FCGR3A+CX3CR1highCD14low with functional ADCC assay and FTH1 expression by qPCR; validate iron metabolism via Prussian blue or ferritin protein quantification in CD16 vs CD14 monocytes; confirm actin dynamics through live-cell migration tracking under chemokine gradients (CX3CL1).

functional_description: This signature reflects the cytoskeletal and lysosomal machinery driving non-classical monocyte morphodynamics and patrolling capacity. The co-expression of actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1), Fc receptor signaling components (FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP), and iron/metabolic regulators (FTH1, SAT1) indicates active cellular remodeling required for endothelial crawling and ADCC surveillance.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Canonical CD16 monocyte marker; essential for ADCC and antigen-immune complex sensing
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration protein directly enabling dynamic cytoskeletal reorganization for vascular crawling
COTL1: F-actin binding and 5-lipoxygenase interaction; regulates migration and immune response
AIF1: Cytokine-induced actin-calcium binding protein; promotes macrophage activation and smooth muscle interaction
FCER1G: ITAM-signaling subunit shared with FCGR3A; amplifies pattern recognition and Fc engagement
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor; couples Fc and pattern recognition receptors to calcium mobilization
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron homeostasis for oxidative metabolism in patrolling cells
LST1: Lymphocyte proliferation inhibitor; LPS/IFN-γ induced; suppresses bystander activation during surveillance
S100A11, S100A4: Calcium-binding proteins supporting actin dynamics and leukocyte trafficking
PSAP: Saposin precursor; lysosomal hydrolase delivery supporting antimicrobial and endocytic capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry gating on CD16+ FCGR3A+ CX3CR1+ monocytes with phospho-TYROBP/LAT signaling assays; live-cell imaging of TMSB4X-GFP dynamics during endothelial transmigration; validate actin polymerization rates in COTL1-silenced CD16 monocytes.

programme_name: CD16 Mono iron metabolism and ADCC
functional_description: This signature defines CD16 non-classical monocytes with elevated iron storage capacity, Fc-receptor mediated cytotoxicity, and antiviral interferon signalling. The programme integrates innate immune effector functions (FCGR3A-driven ADCC, TYROBP/FCER1G ITAM signalling) with metabolic reprogramming (FTH1 iron homeostasis) and interferon-induced antiviral state (IFITM3), characteristic of patrolling monocytes engaged in vascular surveillance and antibody-dependent cellular responses.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Definitive CD16 monocyte marker; high expression enables IgG-mediated cytotoxicity and immune complex clearance
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain indicates elevated iron storage capacity, supporting metabolically active CD16 monocytes with high migratory and oxidative capacity
IFITM3: Interferon-induced antiviral protein reflecting type I IFN-primed state; key antiviral effector in patrolling monocytes
TYROBP/FCER1G: ITAM-bearing signalling adaptors essential for Fc-receptor clustering and ADCC signal transduction
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibitory receptor enhanced by IFN-γ and LPS; supports immune regulatory and activated monocyte phenotype
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator induced by IFN; facilitates actin dynamics required for crawling and vascular surveillance
COTL1/TMSB4X: Actin-binding proteins controlling cytoskeletal remodelling; support patrolling motility and transmigration
S100A4/S100A6/S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins involved in cell migration and inflammatory amplification in monocytes
CD68: High expression consistent with CD16 monocyte activation and lysosomal maturation supporting phagocytosis and ADCC
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: CD14−/CD16+/FCGR3A+ with FTH1 protein, IFITM3, and TYROBP; transcriptomic validation of master TF targets NR4A1/NR4A2; functional ADCC assay with opsonised target cells; measure CX3CR1 and ITGAL surface expression to confirm patrolling phenotype.

functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte programme centered on lysosomal protease expression (CTSS, PSAP), Fc receptor signaling (FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP ITAM adaptor), and iron homeostasis (FTH1). The constellation of actin-regulatory proteins (TMSB4X, AIF1, COTL1) coupled with calcium-responsive S100A11 and LST1-mediated lymphocyte suppression reflects activated cytoskeletal dynamics and immune surveillance characteristic of patrolling non-classical monocytes.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Canonical CD16 marker; enables ADCC through FcγRIII signaling
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor crucial for Fc receptor signalling in CD16+ cells
FCER1G: Gamma-chain component of high-affinity Fc receptors; amplifies activation signals
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease for antigen presentation and immune activation
FTH1: Iron storage protein; elevated in activated myeloid cells during immune response
LST1: LPS/IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein; suppresses lymphocyte proliferation in myeloid context
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein enabling rapid cytoskeletal remodelling for cell crawling
AIF1: IFN-inducible actin-binding protein; macrophage activation marker
COTL1: F-actin binding protein; regulates myeloid cell motility and morphodynamics
S100A11: Calcium-responsive cytoplasmic protein; supports inflammatory activation
MS4A7: MS4A family member; myeloid lineage marker enriched in CD16 monocytes
CD68: Pan-myeloid marker; confirms monocyte identity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry gating on FCGR3A+CD14-/low CX3CR1+ cells; ATAC-seq to confirm NR4A and NFAT motif enrichment in ITAM signalling genes; functional assay of ADCC capacity via anti-CD16 crosslinking with FcγRIII-bearing target cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects the metabolic and structural adaptations of non-classical CD16 monocytes for rapid vascular patrolling and immune surveillance. The program integrates iron homeostasis (FTH1), actin-mediated cellular motility (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1), and Fc-receptor signaling (FCGR3A, FCER1G) essential for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and endothelial crawling.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Definitive CD16 monocyte surface marker; mediates ADCC and immune complex handling characteristic of patrolling subset
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein critical for cell migration and morphological plasticity required for vascular surveillance
FTH1: Iron storage essential for metabolic flexibility during patrolling; links to inflammatory adaptation
FCER1G: Fc-receptor gamma chain enabling FCGR3A-mediated signaling and immune activation
COTL1: Actin-binding protein facilitating dynamic cytoskeletal remodeling for crawling behavior
AIF1: IFN-inducible protein promoting macrophage activation and vascular interactions
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibitor with enhanced expression in CD16 monocytes under inflammatory/bacterial stimuli
S100A4, S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins supporting cellular motility and migration programs
MS4A7: CD16 monocyte-enriched membrane protein suggesting specialized surface properties
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation (CD16+CD14low, FCGR3A+, CX3CR1high) combined with functional assays: transendothelial migration assays, ADCC function with immune complexes, and intravital imaging to confirm vascular crawling behavior. Single-cell RNA-seq correlation with surface phenotype (CD16/FCGR3A co-expression) would strengthen assignment.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Cytoskeletal and Fc-Receptor Activation
functional_description: This signature represents activated CD16 non-classical monocytes (93% composition) with enhanced cytoskeletal remodeling, innate immune receptor signaling, and lysosomal proteolytic capacity. The gene set reflects cells primed for rapid migration, ADCC via FCGR3A engagement, and pathogen surveillance through actin dynamics and calcium signaling.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Definitive CD16 monocyte marker; Fc-gamma receptor III mediating ADCC and immune complex recognition
FCER1G: Component of Fc receptor signaling complexes; amplifies activation signals downstream of FCGR3A
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein; critical for coupling Fc receptors to intracellular signaling cascades
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein; regulates cytoskeletal dynamics essential for crawling and transendothelial migration
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator; induced by IFN-gamma and cytokines; promotes macrophage activation
COTL1: F-actin binding protein; coordinates cytoskeletal remodeling during cell migration and surveillance
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibitory membrane protein; induced by LPS and IFN-gamma in activated monocytes
CTSS: Lysosomal cathepsin; participates in antigen processing and proteolysis
S100A4: Calcium-binding protein; promotes cell migration and is elevated in activated myeloid cells
FTH1: Iron storage protein; elevated in metabolically active immune cells with high oxidative stress
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD16+/FCGR3A+/CX3CR1high/CD14low phenotype; functional ADCC assay with opsonized targets; assess phospho-signaling downstream of FCGR3A/TYROBP axis; validate cytoskeletal gene expression correlates with F-actin dynamics and transendothelial migration capacity.

functional_description: This signature captures non-classical monocytes with enhanced antimicrobial and ADCC capabilities, characterized by high FCGR3A (CD16) expression enabling antibody-dependent responses, combined with elevated lysosomal proteases and innate immune activation pathways. The gene set reflects CD16 Mono specialization in patrolling surveillance with actin-cytoskeleton remodeling for cellular trafficking and antimicrobial effector functions.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Canonical CD16 monocyte marker enabling ADCC and immune complex clearance
FCER1G: ITAM-signaling adaptor in Fc-receptor complexes, critical for CD16-mediated activation
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM-containing adaptor amplifying Fc-receptor signaling in non-classical monocytes
AIF1: Interferon-induced actin-binding protein promoting macrophage activation and cytoskeletal dynamics
COTL1: Actin-regulating protein enabling cell migration and crawling behavior essential for patrolling
LST1: Lipopolysaccharide and IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein marking antimicrobial activation state
CXCL16: Interferon-γ-responsive chemokine with antimicrobial function, indicative of activated surveillance state
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease for pathogen degradation and antigen presentation
PSAP: Saposin processing for lysosomal antimicrobial functions
FTH1: Iron storage regulator supporting metabolic demands of activated innate immunity
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein facilitating monocyte migration and morphodynamics
MS4A7: MS4A family member associated with non-classical monocyte identity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CD16+ monocytes co-expressing FCGR3A, TYROBP, and AIF1; confirm low CD14 and CCR2 expression; functional assays measuring ADCC activity and antimicrobial capacity; assess ITAM signaling pathway activation via phospho-SYK and phospho-LAT.

functional_description: This signature reflects the activated cytoskeletal and phagocytic machinery of CD16 monocytes, characterized by enhanced actin dynamics, Fc receptor signaling, and myeloid cell mobilization. The programme integrates components of cellular migration, ITAM-dependent immune receptor signaling, and iron homeostasis required for patrolling monocyte function.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Canonical CD16 monocyte marker; mediates ADCC and IgG-immune complex engagement via FcγRIII
FCER1G: Encodes γ-chain subunit of FCGR3A complex; essential for ITAM-dependent signaling in CD16 monocytes
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor protein; couples Fc receptors to downstream activation cascades in myeloid cells
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein; regulates cytoskeletal dynamics critical for monocyte crawling and endothelial surveillance
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator; induced by IFN-γ and macrophage activation; supports myeloid cell migration
COTL1: F-actin binding protein and 5-LO interaction partner; modulates inflammatory lipid mediator production in monocytes
LST1: Membrane protein enhanced by LPS and IFN-γ; associated with activated myeloid phenotype
S100A4/S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins regulating cytoskeletal organization and cell migration in myeloid lineage
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage capacity supporting oxidative burst and sustained activation
PSAP: Saposin precursor; lysophagocyte function and lipid antigen presentation
MS4A7: Tetraspanin family marker of monocyte maturation and activation state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-expression of FCGR3A, FCER1G, and TYROBP with CX3CR1-high/CD14-low gate; functional assays of Fc-mediated cytotoxicity and transendothelial migration capacity in CD16+ cells isolated by FCGR3A+ sorting; single-cell RNA-seq validation confirming >90% CD16 Mono enrichment and exclusion of inflammatory CD14 Mono markers (CCR2, IL1B, TNF)

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte ADCC and Iron Metabolism
functional_description: This signature defines mature CD16 non-classical monocytes enriched for Fc-gamma receptor-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and iron homeostasis. The programme combines surface receptors for immune complex recognition (FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP) with actin-cytoskeletal dynamics (AIF1, COTL1, TMSB4X) and iron storage capacity (FTH1), supporting the patrolling monocyte's role in vascular surveillance and humoral immune responses.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 surface marker; ADCC effector function via IgG recognition
FCER1G: ITAM-bearing adaptor in Fc receptor signalling complex
TYROBP: ITAM-containing transmembrane adaptor for Fc and integrin signalling
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein; macrophage activation and cytoskeletal control
COTL1: Actin-binding protein promoting cytoskeletal dynamics for crawling/extravasation
FTH1: Iron storage; supports oxidative metabolism in patrolling monocytes
LST1: Membrane protein upregulated by IFN-γ and bacterial sensing
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease; antigen processing and presentation
CD68: Pan-myeloid marker; elevated in non-classical monocytes
MS4A7: Membrane-spanning tetraspanin; monocyte differentiation marker
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD16+ CD14low FCGR3A+ AIF1+ with ADCC functional assay (NK cell-like activity against opsonized targets); transcriptomic validation of FCGR3A, TYROBP, and FTH1 expression in sorted CD16+ vs CD14+ monocytes; assess vascular adhesion markers (JAM-C, LFA-1) to confirm patrolling phenotype.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and Immune Surveillance
functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte programme centered on iron homeostasis (FTH1), lysosomal/phagosomal maturation (CD68, PSAP, TYROBP), and myeloid transcriptional control (SPI1). The coordinated expression of cytoskeletal regulators (COTL1, RHOC), protease inhibitors (TIMP1, SERPINA1), and interferon-responsive chemokines (CXCL16) supports vascular patrolling, phagocytic capacity, and tissue surveillance functions characteristic of non-classical monocytes.
key_evidence: FTH1: ferritin heavy chain—central to iron storage and oxidative stress management in long-lived patrolling monocytes
CD68: canonical monocyte/macrophage lysosomal marker, reflects phagocytic and endosomal trafficking capacity
SPI1: PU.1 myeloid master regulator; sustains monocyte identity and differentiation programmes
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM-adaptor protein; couples innate immune receptors (FCGR3A, TLRs) to signalling
CXCL16: IFNγ-inducible chemokine supporting T-cell and NK-cell recruitment at vascular and inflammatory sites
COTL1: actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics during crawling and extravasation
PSAP: saposin precursor; lysosomal and endosomal function, pathogen degradation
TIMP1: tissue protease inhibitor; preserves vascular integrity during patrolling
LST1: LPS/IFNγ-inducible lymphocyte inhibitor; restrains bystander T-cell activation
SAT1: polyamine catabolism; metabolic adaptation in activated myeloid cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of FTH1, CD68, FCGR3A (CD16), and CX3CR1 in CD14-negative monocytes; validate SPI1 and TYROBP as co-regulators via ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq in sorted CD16 Mono; measure iron content and reactive oxygen species (ROS) to link FTH1 expression to oxidative stress buffering in patrolling function.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Cytoskeletal and ADCC Activation
functional_description: This signature reflects CD16 monocyte activation characterized by cytoskeletal remodeling, calcium-responsive signaling, and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity machinery. The program encompasses actin dynamics regulation, iron homeostasis, and Fc-receptor mediated immune responses essential for patrolling monocyte vascular surveillance and immune complex handling.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 surface marker defining non-classical monocytes; ADCC effector function via Fc-receptor signaling
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein essential for monocyte cytoskeletal dynamics and migration during patrolling
S100A4/S100A6/S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins driving cytoskeletal remodeling and cell motility in activated monocytes
FCER1G: ITAM-containing signaling adaptor shared with Fc-receptors; amplifies ADCC and immune surveillance responses
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator induced by interferon; promotes monocyte activation and vascular responses
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for Fc-receptor signaling cascades; core ADCC effector molecule
LST1: Membrane protein upregulated by LPS/IFN-γ; involved in immune activation of CD16 monocytes
COTL1: Actin-binding protein and 5-lipoxygenase interactor; modulates inflammatory lipid mediator synthesis
SPI1: PU.1 transcription factor; master regulator of myeloid differentiation and CD16 monocyte identity
FTH1: Iron storage protein; supports metabolic demands of patrolling and activated immune responses

RNA-seq on sorted CD16 vs CD14 monocytes to verify absence of classical inflammatory markers (CCR2, IL-1β, TNF-α) and confirm high S100A/TMSB4X expression. Functional assessment of actin polymerization capacity and calcium mobilization upon Fc-receptor cross-linking.

functional_description: This signature defines a core myeloid activation and cytoskeletal remodeling program characteristic of CD16+ non-classical monocytes, with enrichment for actin-binding proteins, Fc receptor signaling (ADCC), and lysosomal proteolysis. The programme supports rapid morphodynamic responses, immune complex handling, and antimicrobial surveillance functions typical of patrolling monocytes.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 surface marker and defining receptor for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity in non-classical monocytes
FCER1G: Gamma chain of high-affinity Fc receptors (FcγRI/III) enabling ADCC and immune complex clearance
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM-containing adaptor protein required for Fc receptor signaling downstream of FCGR3A
AIF1: IBA1, calcium-binding actin-regulator induced by cytokines; promotes macrophage activation and cell migration
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein regulating polymerization for rapid morphological changes during vascular crawling
COTL1: Actin-binding protein with 5-lipoxygenase interaction; coordinates cytoskeletal dynamics and lipid mediator production
CTSS: Cathepsin S for lysosomal antigen processing and MHC class II presentation
LST1: LPS/IFNγ-induced membrane protein inhibiting lymphocyte proliferation; marks activated myeloid state
S100A4/S100A11: Calcium-binding cytoskeletal modulators associated with myeloid cell motility and surveillance
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain indicating iron homeostasis and oxidative stress management in activated monocytes
CD68: Pan-myeloid marker confirming monocyte/macrophage lineage
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of FCGR3A+CX3CR1+CD14low/- phenotype combined with functional ADCC assay; RNA-seq of sorted CD16 monocytes vs CD14 monocytes to confirm signature enrichment; assess LST1, AIF1, TYROBP co-expression as activation triad for non-classical monocyte identification.

functional_description: This signature defines mature CD16 non-classical monocytes with activated antimicrobial and antiviral effector functions. The programme combines cytoskeletal remodeling for vascular patrolling with innate immune activation, featuring the FCGR3A-TYROBP signaling axis for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and interferon-stimulated antiviral defence.

IFITM3: Type I interferon-induced antiviral protein; strong marker of activated CD16 state
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor critical for FCGR3A signal transduction in patrolling monocytes
FCER1G: Gamma-chain co-receptor amplifying Fc receptor-mediated activation
COTL1: Actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics for vascular crawling/extravasation
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration driving monocyte migration and patrolling capacity
AIF1: IFN-gamma and cytokine-inducible, promotes macrophage activation in inflammatory surveillance
LST1: LPS/IFN-gamma-responsive membrane protein; enhanced in activated non-classical monocytes
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease for antigen processing in ADCC-activated cells
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron metabolism and ROS buffering in activated monocytes
S100A4/S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins supporting migration and inflammatory responsiveness

functional_description: This signature represents a lysosomal-macrophage activation programme highly enriched in CD16 monocytes (92.5%), characterized by elevated expression of actin-binding proteins, iron metabolism, and Fc receptor signalling machinery. The programme reflects enhanced endosomal-lysosomal processing capacity, cytoskeletal dynamics for patrolling surveillance, and ADCC competence typical of non-classical monocytes.

TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein essential for Fc receptor and TLR signalling in myeloid cells
FCER1G: Gamma-chain component of Fc receptors; amplifies ADCC and immune surveillance signalling
CD68: Pan-monocyte/macrophage marker; elevated in activated myeloid subsets with enhanced phagocytic capacity
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator induced by IFN-γ; promotes monocyte activation and endothelial surveillance
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration protein; essential for cytoskeletal remodelling during patrolling and extravasation
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; reflects iron handling and oxidative stress response in activated monocytes

functional_description: This signature reflects the actin-dependent cytoskeletal dynamics and lysosomal machinery underlying CD16 monocyte patrolling behavior and vascular surveillance. The enrichment of actin regulators (TMSB4X, AIF1, COTL1) coupled with Fc-receptor signaling (FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP) and lysosomal proteases (CTSS, PSAP) indicates active cell migration, immune surveillance, and ADCC-preparation characteristic of non-classical monocytes.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Definitive CD16 marker; high expression required for ADCC and immune complex handling
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein essential for monocyte crawling and vascular patrolling dynamics
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein; cytokine-induced expression in activated macrophages and monocytes
FCER1G: ITAM-bearing subunit; couples Fc-receptor signaling to cytoskeletal responses and degranulation
TYROBP: ITAM adapter; essential for amplifying FCGR3A signaling in non-classical monocytes
COTL1: F-actin binding protein; regulates migration and leukotriene signaling during vascular surveillance
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibitor expressed under IFN-γ and LPS; marks activated patrolling monocytes
CTSS and PSAP: Lysosomal proteases; support antigen presentation and endocytic trafficking in ADCC
FTH1: Iron storage; marks metabolically active monocytes with elevated oxidative stress handling
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of FCGR3A+ (CD16+) monocytes co-expressing TMSB4X, COTL1, and TYROBP; compare with CD14+ classical monocytes. Functional assays: assess actin polymerization dynamics, vascular adhesion under shear, and ADCC capacity in FCGR3A-high population. Verify absence of classical markers (CD14, CCR2, pro-inflammatory IL6/TNF) to exclude intermediate monocytes.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Lysosomal and Cytoskeletal Activation
functional_description: This signature reflects activation of lysosomal proteolysis, cytoskeletal remodeling, and intracellular iron/oxidative stress handling in CD16 non-classical monocytes. The program supports crawling behavior and vascular patrolling through actin dynamics (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1), coupled with enhanced antigen processing capacity (CTSS, CD74, PSAP) and innate immune signaling (TYROBP, FCER1G). This matches CD16 monocyte specialization for endothelial surveillance and ADCC-competent functions.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-containing DAP12 signaling adaptor; critical for Fc receptor and integrin cross-talk in CD16 monocytes
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain; enables ADCC and antibody-dependent activation via FCGR3A signaling
TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1: Actin-binding proteins driving cytoskeletal plasticity required for crawling and transendothelial migration
CTSS, PSAP, CD74: Lysosomal proteolysis and MHC-II antigen presentation pathway components
LST1: LPS/IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein; marks inflammatory-licensed CD16 monocytes
FTH1, SAT1: Iron and polyamine metabolism; support oxidative stress tolerance during vascular patrolling
CD16 monocyte enrichment: 80.5% of top activators; signature absent from progenitors and CD14 monocytes
suggested_validation: Co-stain CD16+ cells for TYROBP, FCER1G, CTSS protein expression; correlate with CX3CR1high/CD14low/FCGR3Ahigh surface phenotype; confirm ADCC capacity via FCGR3A-mediated NK-like killing assays; validate cytoskeletal dynamics via live-cell F-actin imaging during endothelial crawling.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Patrolling and Antiviral Surveillance
functional_description: This signature defines non-classical CD16+ monocytes with enhanced antiviral immunity, cytoskeletal dynamics for vascular patrolling, and Fc-receptor-mediated antibody-dependent cellular responses. The programme integrates interferon-induced antiviral proteins, actin-regulatory machinery for crawling behaviour, and ironically coordinated iron metabolism and immune activation.

IFITM3: Type I interferon-induced antiviral protein; marks trained innate immunity state
LST1: Membrane protein upregulated by IFN-γ and bacterial products; supports patrolling phenotype
AIF1: Calcium-binding, IFN-inducible protein; promotes monocyte activation and vascular interactions
COTL1: Actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics essential for endothelial crawling
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein; controls polymerization for monocyte migration and transmigration

functional_description: This signature defines CD16 monocytes (77% of activating population) with elevated lysosomal and phagolysosomal machinery, reflecting high antimicrobial and antigen-processing capacity. The gene set emphasizes actin cytoskeletal dynamics (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1) coupled with cathepsin-mediated proteolysis (CTSS) and iron homeostasis (FTH1), supporting active intracellular pathogen handling and oxidative stress management characteristic of patrolling monocytes.
key_evidence: FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain mediates Fc-receptor clustering for ADCC and phagocytosis in CD16+ monocytes
CTSS: Lysosomal cathepsin S essential for antigen presentation and pathogen degradation in monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-containing signaling adaptor amplifying Fc and pattern recognition receptor responses
FTH1: Iron storage protein supporting ROS detoxification in metabolically active patrolling monocytes
TMSB4X & COTL1: Actin-binding proteins facilitating cellular crawling and amoeboid migration on endothelium
AIF1: Allograft inflammatory factor-1 induced by IFN-γ, promotes macrophage activation and vascular surveillance
LST1: Lipopolysaccharide-stimulated gene upregulated by pathogen-associated molecular patterns in mononuclear phagocytes
CD74: MHC-II chaperone supporting antigen presentation, highly expressed in CD16 monocytes
CD68: Pan-monocyte/macrophage marker confirming mononuclear phagocyte identity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: FTH1+, CTSS+, FCER1G+ with CD16++CD14-/low CX3CR1high; functional validation by Fc-receptor-mediated phagocytosis assays and transendothelial migration on TNF-α-activated endothelial monolayers

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened actin dynamics, calcium signaling, and lysosomal proteolysis in CD16 monocytes, supporting enhanced crawling, vascular surveillance, and cellular remodeling. The strong representation of S100 calcium-binding proteins and actin regulators (S100A4, AIF1, COTL1, RHOC) indicates active cytoskeletal reorganization required for patrolling behavior. Integration of antiviral (IFITM3), Fc-receptor signaling (FCER1G, TYROBP), and protease activity (CTSS, SERPINA1) suggests simultaneous priming for ADCC and antimicrobial responses.
key_evidence: S100A4: Master regulator of actin dynamics and metastatic/migratory phenotype in myeloid cells; essential for crawling
AIF1: IFN-γ and cytokine-induced, promotes macrophage activation and vascular smooth muscle interaction; calcium-actin binding
FCER1G: ITAM-containing γ-chain for high-affinity Fc receptor signaling; critical for ADCC via FCGR3A (CD16)

functional_description: This signature reflects activated myeloid cells with enhanced lysosomal proteolysis, iron metabolism, and ITAM-coupled signaling. Confirm reduced/absent expression of CD14-Mono markers (CCR2, CD14, inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, TNF-α).

The genes encode the core machinery for phagocytic degradation, ITAM-coupled Fc receptor signaling (ADCC), and cellular surveillance—hallmarks of non-classical patrolling monocyte function.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and Cytoskeletal Dynamics
functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 mono-enriched (91%) programme centred on iron homeostasis (FTH1), actin cytoskeleton remodelling (COTL1, TMSB4X, RHOC), and Fc-receptor signalling for ADCC (FCGR3A, FCER1G). The co-expression of LST1, AIF1, and CXCL16 indicates activation of inflammatory sensing and chemokine-mediated vascular surveillance typical of patrolling non-classical monocytes.

COTL1: Actin-binding protein; enables crawling and endothelial patrolling behaviour

CXCL16: Chemokine; IFN-γ-responsive; vascular surveillance and positioning
AIF1: Calcium-binding; IFN-induced; macrophage activation and vascular smooth muscle engagement
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration; cell migration and probing behaviour
FCER1G: Fc-receptor signalling platform; amplifies ADCC responses
CD68: Lysosomal marker; monocyte maturation and tissue-resident capacity
S100A11: Calcium signalling; consistent with activation state

programme_name: CD16 Mono Iron Metabolism Lysosomal Homeostasis
functional_description: This signature reflects CD16 monocyte specialization in iron storage, lysosomal-mediated antigen processing, and proteolytic regulation. The enrichment of ferritin (FTH1), saposin precursor (PSAP), and lysosomal markers (CD68) alongside protease inhibitors (TIMP1, SERPINA1) indicates active management of oxidative stress and controlled tissue remodeling characteristic of patrolling monocyte surveillance physiology.

PSAP: Lysosomal saposin precursor; supports antigen processing and endosomal maturation in CD16+ cells

TYROBP: ITAM-signaling adaptor; couples FCGR3A (CD16) engagement to downstream immune responses

COTL1: Actin-binding protein; regulates cytoskeletal dynamics essential for crawling behaviour
SERPINA1: Serine protease inhibitor; protects host tissues during monocyte extravasation
LST1: LPS/IFN-γ-induced lymphocyte inhibitor; marker of activated innate immune state
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein; induced by IFN and promotes monocyte activation

RT-qPCR on sorted CD16 vs CD14 monocytes. Functional assay: assess crawling capability and oxidative stress resistance in FTH1-modulated CD16 cells.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and Antiviral Priming
functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte (non-classical, patrolling) programme characterized by iron homeostasis, cytoskeletal dynamics, and early antiviral innate immunity. The dominant genes reflect metabolic preparation for rapid response, oxidative stress buffering, and interferon-stimulated antiviral defences typical of patrolling monocytes surveying the endothelium.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Defines CD16+ monocytes; essential for ADCC and immune complex handling
FTH1: Iron storage capacity; critical for managing ROS in activated myeloid cells during immune surveillance
IFITM3: Type I interferon-induced antiviral protein; hallmark of patrolling monocyte antiviral priming state
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin-regulatory protein; enables cytoskeletal remodelling for endothelial crawling and extravasation
COTL1: F-actin binding and 5-LOX interaction; supports lipid mediator signalling and monocyte motility
LST1: Lymphoproliferation inhibitor; LPS/IFN-γ-inducible; marks bacterial/pathogen-responsive CD16 monocytes
S100A4/S100A6/S100A11: Calcium sensors regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and migration; consistent with vascular patrolling phenotype
FCER1G: FcRγ chain component of FCGR3A signalosome; critical for CD16-mediated ADCC
CTSS: Cathepsin S; lysosomal proteolytic capacity for antigen processing in activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: Sort CD16+CD14low cells and validate FTH1, IFITM3, LST1 expression by qPCR. Functional assays: Assess ADCC (FCGR3A/FCER1G signalling), endothelial crawling (F-actin dynamics via COTL1/AIF1), and type I IFN-stimulated state (IFITM3 knockdown antiviral assay). Iron metabolism: Measure ferritin stores and ROS buffering capacity.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Antimicrobial Defense and Iron Metabolism
functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte state characterized by integrated antiviral immunity (IFITM3), Fc-receptor-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP), and heightened cytoskeletal dynamics supporting patrolling surveillance. Iron homeostasis via ferritin (FTH1) and polyamine catabolism (SAT1) support metabolic demands of activated immune cells, while actin-binding proteins (AIF1, COTL1, TMSB4X, RHOC) enable dynamic cellular migration and morphological adaptation.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Definitive CD16 monocyte marker; encodes IgG-Fc receptor mediating ADCC and immune complex clearance
IFITM3: Type I interferon-induced antiviral protein; marks active antiviral state in non-classical monocytes
FCER1G: ITAM-containing signaling component of Fc receptors; essential for ADCC signaling in CD16+ cells
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor protein coupling Fc receptors to downstream activation; critical for ADCC
AIF1: Actin-binding protein induced by cytokines; supports macrophage activation and cytoskeletal remodeling
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; maintains iron homeostasis under heightened metabolic demand
LST1: Lymphocyte proliferation inhibitor; induced by LPS/IFN-γ; marks activated antimicrobial state
COTL1: Actin regulator interacting with 5-lipoxygenase; supports dynamic motility required for patrolling
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein; enables cytoskeletal plasticity for migration
S100A4, S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins supporting cellular signaling and migration in activated monocytes

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD16 monocyte state characterized by actin cytoskeleton remodeling and enhanced phagocytic/signaling capacity, driven by Fc-receptor and adaptor protein engagement. The programme combines cellular motility infrastructure (TMSB4X, COTL1, S100A4) with immunoreceptor signaling machinery (FCGR3A, TYROBP, FCER1G) and metabolic/stress response elements, supporting patrolling monocyte surveillance and antibody-dependent cellular activation.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 surface antigen; defines non-classical monocyte identity and ADCC capability
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor for Fc and immune receptors; couples FCGR3A signaling
FCER1G: γ-chain subunit of FcγRIII and FcεRI; essential for ADCC signaling amplitude
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration and polymerization control; enables cytoskeletal dynamics for crawling/extravasation
COTL1: F-actin binding and 5-lipoxygenase interaction; supports arachidonic acid signaling in activated monocytes
S100A4: Calcium-responsive actin regulator; associated with migration and inflammatory monocyte activation
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibition and LPS/IFN-γ induction; marker of activated innate immune state
AIF1: Calcium-binding, interferon-induced; promotes macrophage activation and immune responses
FTH1: Iron storage; supports oxidative metabolism and ROS-dependent antimicrobial function
PSAP: Saposin processing; links to lipid antigen presentation and lysosomal function

Confirm signature absence of CCR2 and low CD14 to exclude intermediate/classical monocytes.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Antiviral and Cytoskeletal Activation
functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte (90.5% composition) programme characterized by type I interferon-induced antiviral defences, cytoskeletal remodelling for vascular patrolling, and innate immune activation. The co-expression of IFITM3 with actin-regulatory proteins (COTL1, S100A4, AIF1, RHOC) and Fc receptor signalling (FCER1G) indicates primed non-classical monocytes poised for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and endothelial surveillance.
key_evidence: IFITM3: canonical interferon-induced antiviral transmembrane protein, hallmark of type I IFN-primed CD16 monocytes
FCGR3A-proxy FCER1G: FcγRIII signalling axis essential for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity in CD16 monocytes
COTL1, RHOC, S100A4, AIF1: coordinated actin cytoskeleton remodelling enabling crawling and vascular patrolling behaviour
LST1: bacterial lipopolysaccharide-responsive membrane protein, enhanced in activated non-classical monocytes
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain indicating iron homeostasis and oxidative stress tolerance in patrolling monocytes
CST3, SERPINA1, TIMP1: protease inhibitor and tissue remodelling control for safe vascular navigation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: CD14 (low/neg) + CD16 (high) + IFITM3 (intracellular) + FCER1G (high); confirm CX3CR1 and LFA-1 expression; functional ADCC assay with opsonized targets; RNAscope ISH for IFITM3 + COTL1 co-localisation in bone marrow sinusoids

functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor commitment with concurrent activation of antimicrobial effector functions and oxidative metabolism. The dominance of Early ProMono (57.5%) combined with elevated LYZ, RNASE2, and RETN indicates initiation of bactericidal capacity while maintaining mitochondrial bioenergetics to support functional monocyte differentiation.

RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease; marks transition from progenitor to functionally mature myeloid cell
MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND5: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes; reflect elevated energy demands of early ProMono commitment
RNASE2 + RETN: Dual antimicrobial granule proteins indicative of early monocyte-specific granule assembly
Early ProMono enrichment (57.5%): Confirms signature captures commitment phase rather than terminal differentiation
MPO presence: Modest residual neutrophil-associated gene reflecting GMP-Mono intermediate population (29%)

ATAC-seq to assess chromatin accessibility at antimicrobial loci in Early vs Late ProMono.

functional_description: This signature reflects the core myeloid differentiation and activation state of CD16+ non-classical monocytes, characterized by robust actin cytoskeletal remodeling, Fc receptor-mediated signaling capacity, and interferon-responsive antiviral priming. The programme captures the transcriptional and proteomic infrastructure required for patrolling surveillance, adhesion dynamics, and rapid immune responsiveness rather than pathogenic inflammation.

TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics required for crawling and vascular patrolling

FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain reflecting elevated iron metabolism in metabolically active patrolling monocytes

LST1: Lymphocyte-inhibiting membrane protein upregulated by IFN-γ and bacterial stimuli in activated monocytes

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and Antiviral Surveillance
functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte state characterized by elevated iron homeostasis (FTH1), actin-cytoskeletal remodeling supporting patrolling motility (COTL1, RHOC, AIF1), and type I interferon-induced antiviral defenses (IFITM3). The program integrates FCGR3A-mediated antibody recognition with iron-dependent metabolic fitness and vascular surveillance capacity.

IFITM3: Type I IFN-induced antiviral protein; supports intracellular pathogen restriction
FTH1: Iron storage protein; regulates ROS metabolism and metabolic fitness in activated monocytes

AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator; promotes monocyte activation and vascular interaction

SAT1: Polyamine catabolism; supports metabolic reprogramming during immune activation

functional_description: This signature captures the monocytic maturation phase of GMP-Mono progenitors (74% composition) transitioning toward early ProMono, marked by robust myeloid peroxidase expression and granule protein priming characteristic of committed monocytic lineage. The gene ensemble reflects active myeloid differentiation with nucleotide metabolism support and cytoskeletal dynamics during terminal maturation.

functional_description: This signature reflects the actin-cytoskeletal remodeling and cellular migration machinery of CD16+ non-classical monocytes, with emphasis on dynamic cell shape changes required for vascular patrolling and endothelial crawling. The programme integrates Fc-receptor signalling (FCGR3A, FCER1G) for ADCC capability with calcium-dependent cytoskeletal regulation and proteolytic homeostasis.

COTL1: F-actin binding protein; regulates cytoskeletal remodeling during transendothelial migration
S100A4, S100A11: EF-hand calcium sensors; coordinate calcium-dependent motility and shape changes
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibitory membrane protein; LPS/IFN-γ inducible; consistent with activated CD16 state
RHOC: Rho GTPase; drives actin polymerization and cellular contractility for crawling
CALM2: Calmodulin; calcium-dependent signalling hub for cytoskeletal and migration machinery
SERPINA1, PSAP: Protease inhibitors and lysosomal proteins; support tissue remodeling and survival in inflammatory microenvironments

functional_description: This signature reflects early-to-intermediate monocyte progenitor commitment with elevated oxidative phosphorylation capacity and chromatin remodelling activity. The programme combines mitochondrial bioenergetics (MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1) with antimicrobial proteases (LYZ, RNASE2) and chromatin accessibility factors (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN1/2), characteristic of ProMono cells transitioning towards functional monocyte biology while maintaining active chromatin dynamics.

LYZ: Canonical monocyte antimicrobial protease, marks loss of GMP-Neut identity (MPO/ELANE-low phenotype)
RNASE2: Non-secretory ribonuclease with antimicrobial function, reinforces committed monocyte lineage signature
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN1, HMGN2: High mobility group chromatin proteins maintaining transcriptionally active/open chromatin state required for ProMono-specific TF networks (KLF4, IRF8)
PTMA, STMN1: Cell cycle checkpoint and mitotic regulator—consistent with Early ProMono still cycling (pre-CD14 Mono exit)

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated oxidative phosphorylation capacity and protein synthesis machinery in early GMP and GMP-Mono populations committed toward monocytic lineage. The enrichment of mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND5, UQCRH) coupled with ribosomal proteins indicates metabolic ramping and translational readiness characteristic of early monocytic progenitors transitioning from quiescence toward differentiation.

UQCRH: complex III electron transport; coordinates with cytochrome oxidase activity for ATP generation
RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A: ribosomal structural proteins; indicates heightened protein synthesis capacity during GMP-to-monocyte transition
PTMA: DNA-binding factor; apoptosis suppression; supports survival during early commitment phase
HMGN1: open chromatin architecture; enables transcriptional reprogramming during lineage priming
GSTP1, PPIA: oxidative stress protection and protein chaperone function; metabolically active cells require antioxidant buffering

suggested_validation: Co-stain activating cells (CD34+KIT+) with MitoTracker Red and measure ATP/ADP ratio; validate monocytic priming by FACS for CSF1R+IRF8+ GMP-Mono cells; quantify mtDNA copy number and OCR by Seahorse in sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono populations

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and robust mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH), indicating heightened protein synthesis and metabolic activity. The enrichment in Early GMP (62.5%) suggests this programme captures the anabolic demand of early progenitors preparing for rapid division and differentiation, with secondary contribution from cycling GMPs (GMP-Cycle: 29.0%).

EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting efficient mRNA-to-protein conversion
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain components reflecting elevated oxidative metabolism
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme indicating active energy metabolism
HNRNPA1, PTMA: RNA processing and nuclear transport support for high transcriptional/translational flux
Early GMP enrichment (62.5%): consistent with metabolically active early progenitors before lineage restriction
suggested_validation: Measure mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker), oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse), and protein synthesis rate (puromycin incorporation or O-propargyl-puromycin) in sorted Early GMP vs. mature monocytes. Correlate ribosomal protein expression with proliferation markers (Ki-67, cell cycle phase) to confirm metabolic priming precedes differentiation commitment.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein (RPS, RPL families) and translation elongation factor expression (EEF1B2) coupled with oxidative phosphorylation (MT-CO2, UQCRH) and glycolytic capacity (GAPDH, LDHB). The program represents active protein synthetic capacity and metabolic demand consistent with early GMP progenitors undergoing terminal differentiation and maturation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components indicating high translational machinery abundance
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting rapid protein synthesis during lineage commitment
RPLP0: ribosomal stalk protein essential for translocation during translation
MT-CO2, UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain components reflecting heightened oxidative metabolism
GAPDH, LDHB: glycolytic enzymes indicating bioenergetic demand during GMP maturation
HNRNPA1, SNRPE: RNA-binding proteins involved in pre-mRNA processing and splicing during transcriptional remodeling
Early GMP dominance (68.5%): signature enriched in least committed GMP stage with highest biosynthetic demand
suggested_validation: Assess ribosomal biogenesis markers (NPM1, NCL), nascent protein synthesis by puromycin incorporation, and correlate with cell cycle phase within Early GMP vs GMP-Cycle to clarify whether signature represents G1/S biosynthetic priming or metabolic baseline in non-cycling early progenitors. Compare myeloid lineage TF expression (CEBPA, CEBPE, IRF8) to determine if translation capacity correlates with mono vs neutro commitment.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Lysosomal and Innate Activation
functional_description: This signature reflects the lysosomal and proteolytic machinery characteristic of CD16 non-classical monocytes, with enrichment in cysteine proteases (CTSS, CST3) and iron metabolism (FTH1) supporting their high metabolic and antimicrobial capacity. The co-expression of TYROBP, FCER1G, and AIF1 indicates engagement of ITAM-signalling pathways essential for Fc-receptor-mediated ADCC and phagocytic activation, consistent with CD16 Mono's role in antibody-dependent cellular responses and vascular surveillance.

CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine cathepsin for antigen processing and pathogen degradation
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor mediating FCGR3A (CD16) signalling for ADCC
FCER1G: Gamma chain component of high-affinity Fc receptors driving CD16 Mono activation
LST1: LPS/IFN-γ-inducible lymphocyte inhibitor associated with activated monocyte phenotype
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator induced by IFN, supporting patrolling cell motility
COTL1: Actin cytoskeleton reorganisation enabling crawling and vascular patrolling behaviour
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration supporting dynamic migration and extravasation
CST3: Cystatin cysteine protease inhibitor regulating proteolytic activity in lysosomal compartments
SAT1: Polyamine metabolism acceleration supporting rapid CD16 Mono proliferation and activation

programme_name: Proliferative ProMono maturation with monocytic commitment
functional_description: This signature reflects early-to-intermediate ProMono progenitors undergoing active proliferation and chromatin remodeling while acquiring monocytic effector functions. The enrichment of histone-binding proteins (HMGN1/2, NUCKS1), actin regulators (TMSB4X), and DNA-binding cofactors (PTMA, ANP32B) indicates ongoing transcriptional remodeling coupled with cell cycle activity. Concurrent upregulation of LYZ and RNASE2 marks emergence of monocytic antimicrobial programs.

HMGN2, HMGN1, NUCKS1: nucleosomal DNA-binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin during differentiation
TMSB4X: actin sequesterer regulating migration and differentiation, essential for promonocyte cytoskeletal maturation
PTMA: DNA-binding cofactor and anti-apoptotic factor supporting proliferative progenitor survival
RNASE2: monocyte-enriched antimicrobial ribonuclease, marks departure from GMP program
LGALS1: galectin-1 mediates cell-cell interactions and autocrine growth regulation in differentiating progenitors
HSP90B1, PPIA: molecular chaperones supporting protein folding during transcriptional remodeling
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: mitochondrial oxidative metabolism reflecting elevated energy demand in proliferative progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of Early/Late ProMono (CD34+CD13+MS4A3hi) with LGALS1, HMGN2, and LYZ to confirm proliferative state (Ki-67) and monocytic commitment. ATAC-seq on sorted Early ProMono to validate open chromatin at monocytic TF loci (IRF8, KLF4) and confirm downregulation of neutrophil-associated peaks.

functional_description: This signature reflects Early ProMono (77.5%) progenitors activating innate immune effector programmes dominated by S100A8/A9 calprotectin heterodimer and LYZ lysozyme, coupled with elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. The programme represents metabolic and antimicrobial priming before full monocyte terminal differentiation, with MNDA and RNASE2 marking myeloid lineage commitment and cytotoxic capacity.
key_evidence: S100A8: S100A8/A9 calprotectin is a hallmark of activated monocytic progenitors; calcium-binding and inflammatory signalling (top rank)
S100A9: Co-expression with S100A8 as functional calprotectin complex; validates myeloid activation state
LYZ: Canonical monocyte antimicrobial enzyme; present in Early ProMono as lysozyme expression begins
MNDA: Myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen; lineage-restricted to granulocyte-monocyte compartment, marks commitment
MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND5: Respiratory chain oxidoreductases; elevated OXPHOS supports metabolic demand of differentiating progenitors
RNASE2: Non-secretory ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity; monocytic innate immune effector
PTMA, HMGB2: Chromatin-associated proteins supporting nuclear remodelling during progenitor differentiation
CSTA: Cystatin protease inhibitor; regulates cysteine proteases during monocytic differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: S100A8+ LYZ+ CSF1R+ MS4A3+ CD14dim population in Early ProMono gate; confirm MNDA nuclear expression. RNA FISH for S100A8/A9 localisation in cytoplasm of CD34- CSF1R+ gated cells. Compare OXPHOS signature (Seahorse) between Early vs Late ProMono to confirm metabolic ramp-up.

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and cytoplasmic remodelling
functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression and cytoskeletal reorganisation in Early ProMono cells, marked by elevated expression of core monocyte lysosomal protease LYZ and proliferation-associated factors. The enrichment of nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGB1/2, HMGN2), tubulin components (TUBB, TUBA1B), and anti-apoptotic factors (PTMA) indicates cells undergoing chromatin remodelling and mitotic divisions prior to terminal monocyte maturation.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte lysosomal antimicrobial enzyme; marks monocytic lineage commitment
HMGB1/HMGB2: nucleosome dynamics and transcriptional remodelling during differentiation
PTMA: anti-apoptotic cofactor maintaining viability during cell cycle transit
TUBB/TUBA1B: microtubule polymerisation required for mitotic progression
S100A8/A9: calcium-binding cytoplasmic proteins enriched in myeloid progenitors undergoing expansion
PCLAF/STMN1: cell cycle checkpoint and microtubule destabilisation factors
HMGN2: active chromatin maintenance during transcriptional remodelling
95.5% Early ProMono composition: validates early-stage progenitor signature
suggested_validation: Co-stain Early ProMono (CD34+CD117+CD13+CD115+MS4A3hi) for LYZ protein and proliferation markers (Ki-67, phospho-H3); compare S100A8/A9 expression against Late ProMono (CD14+CD11b+) to confirm early-stage restriction; validate HMGB1/2 nuclear localisation by immunofluorescence

functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor differentiation characterized by acquisition of antimicrobial effector functions and chromatin remodeling for mono-specific transcription. The programme is dominated by antimicrobial proteins (LYZ, RNASE2, AZU1) and shows chromatin accessibility markers (HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2), consistent with Early ProMono transitioning toward functional monocyte identity.

RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease, monocyte-enriched bactericidal activity
AZU1: Azurocidin, early granule protein in mono progenitors
HMGN1/HMGN2/HMGB1/HMGB2: Nucleosome-associated proteins indicating open chromatin and active mono-lineage transcription programmes
LGALS1: Galectin-1, monocyte adhesion and immune modulation marker
RETN: Resistin homologue, monocyte antimicrobial factor
ELANE/MPO: Presence suggests GMP-Mono (28.5%) contamination; absent in pure Late ProMono
Early ProMono dominance (60%) confirms progenitor commitment stage pre-CD14 surface expression
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: sort Early ProMono (CD34+CD38+CD45RA+MS4A3+CD14-) and validate LYZ/LGALS1/RNASE2 protein expression; confirm ELANE/MPO downregulation vs GMP; RNA-seq on sorted Early vs Late ProMono to assess KLF4/IRF8 TF activity and CSF1R/CCR2 pre-egress markers.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened ribosomal protein synthesis and mitochondrial oxidative capacity in early GMP-stage progenitors preparing for rapid protein production. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4) coupled with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and mitochondrial respiration genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) indicates metabolic priming for the biosynthetic demands of differentiation rather than lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4: Canonical ribosomal protein subunits (40S/60S), indicating elevated translational machinery
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: Oxidative phosphorylation complex components; support high ATP demand during myeloid progenitor proliferation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; facilitates aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, reflecting active protein synthesis
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting functions; often elevated in metabolically active progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor; protects cycling progenitors from stress-induced cell death
Cellular composition (88.5% Early GMP + GMP-Cycle): Signature is driven by cell cycle-active, non-committed progenitors, not differentiation signals
No master TF lineage markers (IRF8, CEBPE, SPI1): Absence of commitment signatures; signature is metabolic not transcriptional
suggested_validation: Perform metabolic flux assays (Seahorse, mitochondrial respiration) and polysome profiling on sorted Early GMP vs. GMP-Mono to confirm elevated translation and OXPHOS activity. Validate ribosomal protein abundance by Western blot or flow cytometry (anti-ribosomal protein antibodies). Compare to canonical GMP commitment markers (IRF8, CEBPE, CD64, CSF1R expression) to confirm metabolic priming precedes lineage decision.

functional_description: This signature reflects early myeloid progenitors (predominantly GMP-Mono, Early GMP, GMP-Cycle) undergoing metabolic activation and ribosomal biogenesis in preparation for differentiation. The dominance of mitochondrial OXPHOS components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, UQCRH) indicates elevated ATP production supporting biosynthetic demands, while ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23) and translation factors (PPIA) enable protein synthesis required for lineage commitment. MPO presence confirms early myeloid differentiation context.
key_evidence: MT-CO2/MT-CO3/MT-ND1/MT-ND5/UQCRH: Respiratory chain complexes I & IV assembly; energetic demand during GMP expansion and early commitment
RPS24/RPL37A/RPS23: Ribosomal subunits; biosynthetic capacity for rapid protein synthesis during myeloid priming
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase; protein folding during translational burst accompanying differentiation
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic function; survival signal during metabolically demanding progenitor expansion
MPO: Early myeloid marker; validates GMP-stage context with nascent granulocytic/monocytic priming
HMGB1/HMGN1/H2AFV: Chromatin remodeling; transcriptional activation accompanying differentiation initiation
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics; supports cell cycle progression in GMP-Cycle populations (21% of activating cells)
suggested_validation: Correlate with flow cytometry sorting: CD34+ KIT+ MPO+ MPO- (GMP substages), quantify mtDNA content by qPCR, measure oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse) in sorted GMP-Mono vs Early GMP, confirm MPO protein by immunofluorescence on bone marrow cytospins, validate CEBPA/IRF8 co-expression patterns to confirm monocytic bias within this energized GMP compartment.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated translational capacity in GMP-Mono stage progenitors, driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS/RPL subunits) and translation factors. The dominant composition of GMP-Mono cells (77%) coupled with MPO expression indicates priming of monocytic differentiation while maintaining high protein synthesis rates characteristic of actively differentiating progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins—coordinate upregulation indicates global translational amplification
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery—supports sustained protein synthesis during GMP-Mono commitment
MPO: Myeloperoxidase expression confirms monocytic differentiation priming while maintaining GMP-stage identity
UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport component indicating elevated energy production supporting biosynthetic demand
NPM1, PTMA: Nucleolar/cytoplasmic chaperones facilitating ribosome assembly and cell proliferation coordination
GAPDH, PPIA: Glycolytic enzyme and prolyl isomerase supporting rapid protein folding and metabolic demands of differentiating progenitors
suggested_validation: Assess ribosomal biogenesis markers (NCL, FBL) and polysome profiling in sorted GMP-Mono vs Early GMP; validate MPO co-expression with ribosomal signature by flow cytometry and confirm monocytic trajectory by CSF1R/CD64 upregulation kinetics.

programme_name: Early GMP translational capacity and biosynthesis
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP progenitors, supporting high protein synthesis demand during active myeloid progenitor expansion. The predominant Early GMP composition (89%) with minimal GMP-Mono contribution indicates this programme is activated before monocytic lineage commitment, when cells maintain robust translational capacity for proliferation and differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: clustered 40S and 60S ribosomal proteins indicating active ribosome biogenesis in proliferating progenitors
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting protein synthesis at scale during GMP expansion phase
NPM1: nucleolar protein regulating centrosome duplication and cell cycle progression, consistent with cycling Early GMP
GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH: glycolytic and mitochondrial metabolic enzymes supporting ATP/NADH demands of active protein synthesis
HNRNPA1, PTMA: RNA-binding and nuclear proteins facilitating mRNA processing in actively dividing progenitors
89% Early GMP enrichment: signature marks pre-commitment GMP state before IRF8/CEBPE-driven lineage bifurcation
suggested_validation: Validate translational activity using polysome profiling or 4EGFPp reporters in FACS-sorted Early GMP vs. GMP-Mono subsets. Cross-reference with MYC/MTOR pathway activity signatures. Confirm absence of monocytic differentiation markers (CSF1R, CD64, IRF8) in activating cells to exclude ProMono contamination.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Cytoskeletal and Iron Metabolism
functional_description: This signature reflects CD16 monocyte intrinsic metabolic and structural adaptations, dominated by actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1) supporting cytoskeletal dynamics required for patrolling surveillance, combined with iron homeostasis (FTH1, HBA1/2, HBB) and lysosomal proteolysis (CTSS, PSAP) enabling rapid antigen processing. The enrichment of hemoglobin genes and ferritin suggests metabolic reprogramming linked to oxidative stress handling and vascular patrolling activity in non-classical monocytes.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: actin-sequestering protein essential for monocyte migration and cellular plasticity during patrolling
AIF1: calcium-binding, actin-regulating protein induced by IFN-γ; supports macrophage activation and vascular patrolling
COTL1: F-actin binding protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics required for endothelial crawling
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain managing intracellular iron; critical for redox stress tolerance in vascular surveillance
HBA1/HBA2/HBB: hemoglobin expression in monocytes linked to metabolic reprogramming and oxygen sensing
FCER1G: Fc receptor γ-chain supporting ADCC via FCGR3A (CD16) signaling in non-classical monocytes
CTSS: cathepsin S enabling antigen processing for peptide presentation
LST1: lymphoproliferation inhibitor; IFN-γ/LPS-induced, consistent with CD16 monocyte activation state
S100A4/S100A11: calcium-binding motility factors supporting dynamic cellular migration
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD16/CD14/FCGR3A with TMSB4X, FTH1, and AIF1; single-cell qPCR validation of hemoglobin genes in FACS-sorted CD16+ vs CD14+ monocytes; assess correlations with migration assays and ferritin quantification to confirm metabolic reprogramming signature.

functional_description: This signature marks the energetic transition of GMP-Mono progenitors through coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complexes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5) coupled with protein quality control (HSP90B1, HSPB1, PPIA). The dominant activation in GMP-Mono (57%) and GMP-Cycle (15.5%) with MPO co-expression indicates metabolic reprogramming concurrent with monocytic commitment and proliferation, supporting the increased energy demands of differentiating myeloid progenitors.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Core OXPHOS complexes (I, IV) consistently rank top, indicating metabolic shift from glycolytic progenitors to OXPHOS-dependent monocytic lineage
MPO: Myeloperoxidase expression confirms GMP-Mono stage identity; typically downregulated in mature monocytes, supporting intermediate differentiation state
HSP90B1, HSPB1, PPIA: Molecular chaperones indicate proteostatic stress from heightened protein synthesis and mitochondrial unfolding during lineage commitment
STMN1, PTMA: Cytoplasmic/nuclear regulators of differentiation signalling and apoptosis protection consistent with active monocytic priming
RNASE2: Antimicrobial effector priming for monocytic function; modest elevation fits GMP-Mono stage before full granule assembly
Cell composition: 57% GMP-Mono + 15.5% Early ProMono establishes lineage trajectory; 15.5% GMP-Cycle reflects proliferative context of myeloid expansion
suggested_validation: qPCR/flow for MT-encoded OXPHOS proteins + MitoTracker staining to confirm mitochondrial mass/membrane potential in sorted GMP-Mono vs Early GMP; co-stain MPO/CD64/CSF1R to verify intermediate monocytic differentiation state and distinguish from cycling progenitors

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and chromatin remodelling
functional_description: This signature reflects the active proliferative state of Early ProMono progenitors with concurrent transcriptional remodelling. The co-expression of cell-cycle machinery (UBE2C, PTTG1, CKS1B), chromatin accessibility factors (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2, H2AFZ), and early monocytic differentiation markers (LYZ, RNASE2) indicates commitment to mono fate while maintaining proliferative capacity prior to terminal maturation.
key_evidence: HMGB2: Chromatin-associated protein marking transcriptionally active state characteristic of Early ProMono
HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA-binding protein associated with open chromatin during active differentiation
UBE2C: Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme essential for cell-cycle progression in proliferating progenitors
PTTG1: Cell-cycle regulator (securin) marking G2/M phase transition in dividing ProMono
CKS1B: CDK regulatory protein required for active cell-cycle progression
LYZ: Monocytic commitment marker, lysozyme expressing upon mono fate lock
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease reflecting early monocytic functional specification
TMSB4X: Actin-regulatory protein supporting cytoskeletal dynamics during proliferation and differentiation
S100A8: Calcium-binding protein marking inflammatory monocytic programme initiation
LGALS1: Galectin autocrine regulator of cell-cell interactions during progenitor coordination
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm Early ProMono surface phenotype (MS4A3+, CD34+/-, CSF1R+, CD14-) with Ki-67/phospho-histone H3 co-staining to validate active cycling; RNA-FISH for LYZ, HMGB2 co-expression; ChIP-seq to confirm HMGB2/HMGN2 occupancy at monocytic commitment loci (KLF4, IRF8 targets)

functional_description: This signature reflects a shared myeloid differentiation state characterized by iron metabolism (FTH1), lysosomal/phagosomal maturation (CD68, CTSS), and MHC class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1). The strong representation of both CD14 and CD16 monocytes (55.5% vs 44.5%) indicates this programme captures a convergent maturation phenotype rather than subset-specific activation, with enrichment for ITAM signaling (TYROBP) and calcium-dependent actin dynamics (AIF1, COTL1) supporting enhanced phagocytic capacity.
key_evidence: FTH1: iron storage and oxidative stress buffering in activated myeloid cells
CD68: pan-monocyte/macrophage marker reflecting differentiation maturity
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor enabling TLR/FcR cross-talk and inflammatory responses
CTSS: lysosomal protease essential for antigen processing and MHC II presentation
HLA-DRA/DPA1/DPB1: coordinated MHC class II expression supporting antigen presentation
AIF1: calcium-binding actin regulator downstream of pattern recognition and integrin signaling
COTL1: actin-binding protein supporting cytoskeletal remodeling during phagocytosis
SAT1: polyamine catabolism supporting metabolic shift in monocyte activation
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis fueling energy-demanding antimicrobial functions
LST1: LPS-responsive membrane protein with lymphocyte-suppressive capacity
suggested_validation: Compare CD14 vs CD16 subset enrichment within top 200 activating cells; validate with flow cytometry co-staining of CD68/HLA-DR; assess FTH1 and CTSS protein expression by imaging flow; confirm TYROBP-dependent signaling via phospho-SYK/ERK in stimulated monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP progenitors (84% of activating cells), indicating high protein synthesis demand during active myeloid progenitor expansion. The enrichment of 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) coupled with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, LDHB) suggests Early GMP cells maintain robust anabolic capacity to support rapid proliferation and differentiation priming.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins defining translational machinery upregulation in actively proliferating Early GMP
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting efficient protein synthesis during progenitor expansion
NPM1: Nucleolar protein involved in centrosome duplication and cell proliferation, consistent with Early GMP cell-cycle dynamics
GAPDH, LDHB: Glycolytic and metabolic enzymes reflecting heightened bioenergetic demand in Early GMP progenitors
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein supporting mRNA processing in proliferative myeloid progenitors

suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression across Early GMP vs GMP-Mono vs ProMono via flow cytometry (e.g., puromycin incorporation assay for active translation) or RT-qPCR of RPS2/RPL7A/RPLP0. Validate Early GMP cell-cycle status with Ki67/PCNA co-staining to confirm proliferative context of translational upregulation. Confirm absence of lineage commitment markers (CSF1R, CD64, CD14) in signature-enriched cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP cells, indicating active protein synthesis capacity during early myeloid progenitor expansion. The enrichment of ribosomal structural components (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0) combined with translation factors (EEF1B2) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1) suggests a highly translating progenitor population preparing for rapid differentiation and cytoplasmic expansion required in myeloid commitment.

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor essential for efficient protein synthesis during progenitor expansion

GAPDH, MT-CO3: Glycolytic and mitochondrial respiratory chain components supporting high metabolic demand

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened translational capacity in Early GMP progenitors, driven by coordinated upregulation of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1). NPM1: nucleolar protein involved in centrosome duplication and cell proliferation; marks actively cycling progenitors
HNRNPA1, PTMA, H3F3A: RNA-binding and nuclear proteins supporting rapid proliferation
HSP90AB1: heat shock protein; supports protein folding demand during intensive biosynthesis
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme; indicates high metabolic activity consistent with proliferating progenitor state

suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein abundance via polysome profiling or ribosome immunoprecipitation in Early GMP vs. differentiated monocyte subsets; correlate with puromycin incorporation assays to confirm elevated translation rates; validate that signature distinguishes Early GMP from post-commitment GMP-Mono and mature monocytes where translational activity normalizes post-proliferation.

programme_name: Early ProMono metabolic and chromatin remodelling
functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor (ProMono) commitment characterised by activation of housekeeping metabolic machinery (mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, glycolysis) and chromatin remodelling factors supporting transcriptional plasticity. The dominance of nucleosomal architecture regulators (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2) alongside LYZ expression indicates active transcriptional remodelling during ProMono maturation, with concurrent antimicrobial granule priming.

HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2: Chromatin-associated proteins regulating transcriptionally active domains critical for ProMono fate establishment
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Mitochondrial OXPHOS upregulation supporting metabolic transition from GMP towards monocytic energy demands
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease expression consistent with early ProMono granule programming
PTMA, ANP32B: Chromatin regulators involved in apoptosis inhibition, supporting ProMono survival during commitment
H2AFZ, GAPDH: Metabolic and histone variant factors supporting glycolytic shift in early differentiation

functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte-enriched (83.5%) program centered on antimicrobial effector functions, actin-driven surveillance motility, and Fc receptor-mediated immunity. The transcriptome emphasizes cytoskeletal remodeling (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1), interferon-induced antiviral defense (IFITM3), proteolytic capacity (CTSS, PSAP), and CD16-dependent antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (FCGR3A, FCER1G/TYROBP ITAM signaling).

IFITM3: Type I IFN-induced antiviral transmembrane protein, hallmark of antimicrobial CD16 monocytes
FCER1G: Gamma chain of high-affinity IgE receptor and FcγRIII amplifier, ITAM-bearing for immune activation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor, essential for FCGR3A and pattern recognition receptor signaling in myeloid cells
AIF1: Interferon-induced actin-binding protein, promotes macrophage activation and vascular patrolling
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration and cytoskeletal dynamics, enables crawling and endothelial surveillance
LST1: Membrane protein induced by IFN-γ and bacterial PAMPs, associates with CD16 monocyte activation
S100A4, S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins regulating migration and inflammatory responses in patrolling cells
PSAP, CTSS: Lysosomal proteases for antigen processing and antimicrobial peptide generation
FTH1: Iron homeostasis, supports oxidative antimicrobial metabolism in activated monocytes

programme_name: Early GMP metabolic priming and translation
functional_description: This signature captures early myeloid progenitors (predominantly GMP-stage cells) undergoing active mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis in preparation for lineage commitment. The strong enrichment of mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5) combined with ribosomal proteins and translation factors reflects heightened metabolic demand during the transition from cycling progenitors to committed monocytic precursors. MPO expression indicates myeloid lineage priming consistent with GMP-Mono and GMP-Cycle composition.
