RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23: Ribosomal structural proteins indicating elevated protein synthesis capacity required for differentiation
PPIA: Prolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding during biosynthetic expansion
MPO: Myeloperoxidase marking early myeloid lineage commitment, present in both monocytic and neutrophilic pathways at GMP stage
PTMA: Nuclear/cytosolic protein supporting survival signalling during active differentiation
STMN1, HMGB1: Cytoskeletal dynamics and DNA-binding regulation consistent with cycling GMP-Cycle cells (25.5% composition)
UQCRH: Complex III component reinforcing mitochondrial bioenergetic activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry gating on CD34+/CD38+/CD123+/FLT3+ GMP population with co-staining for MPO and mitochondrial mass (TMRM/JC-1); correlate metabolic signature with CFU-GM colony assays; validate respiratory capacity via Seahorse analysis in sorted GMP-Mono vs GMP-Cycle subsets.

functional_description: This signature reflects robust protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP progenitors, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPS23, RPL4) and translation factors (EEF1B2). The co-expression of NPM1 (nucleolar organizing factor), HNRNPA1 (RNA processing), and metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, LDHB) indicates active biomass accumulation required for rapid proliferation and progenitor maintenance.

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—direct evidence of active protein synthesis machinery
NPM1: Nucleolar protein involved in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation; hallmark of progenitor metabolic state
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing; supports high transcriptional/translational demand
GAPDH/LDHB: Glycolytic and anaerobic metabolism enzymes; consistent with proliferating progenitor energy metabolism
HSP90AB1: Heat shock protein for protein folding/quality control under high synthesis demand
PTMA: Nucleolar protein with anti-apoptotic function; supports progenitor survival during active proliferation
88% Early GMP composition: Signature reflects predominantly quiescent/early-cycling GMP biology, not mature monocyte differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate via: (1) Sort Early GMP vs ProMono vs mature CD14 monocytes; quantify ribosomal protein mRNA by qPCR and protein by flow (surface CD71 transferrin receptor as proxy for translational demand); (2) Polysome profiling to confirm elevated translation rate in Early GMP; (3) Confirm NPM1 and nucleolar localization is retained in Early GMP but diminished in ProMono/mature mono; (4) Cross-reference against published GMP proliferation signatures (e.g., Laurenti/Göttgens cell cycle modules).

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened metabolic activity and protein synthesis capacity in committed monocyte progenitors, particularly Late ProMono cells. The programme combines oxidative phosphorylation (NDUFB9, UQCRH), ribosomal machinery (RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, EEF1B2), and the monocyte-defining antimicrobial lysosomal enzyme LYZ, characteristic of the transition toward functional monocyte identity. Elevated TYMS indicates active DNA synthesis supporting ProMono cell cycle progression.

NDUFB9, UQCRH: mitochondrial Complex I/III subunits driving elevated oxidative metabolism in metabolically active progenitors
RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, EEF1B2: ribosomal proteins and translation factors reflecting protein synthesis capacity required for monocyte effector function
TYMS: deoxyribonucleotide synthesis enzyme indicating S-phase activity compatible with ProMono cycling status
HMGN1, HMGB2: nucleosomal chromatin-associated proteins suggesting open chromatin at monocyte commitment loci
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme supporting bioenergetic demands of differentiating progenitors

programme_name: Monocyte lysosomal and innate immune activation
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened lysosomal/phagolysosomal biogenesis and proteolytic capacity combined with innate antiviral priming, characteristic of activated non-classical monocytes engaged in pathogen surveillance and tissue monitoring. The enrichment of iron-handling, actin-regulatory, and immunoreceptor signalling proteins indicates metabolic readiness for rapid antimicrobial responses.

TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein essential for Fc receptor (FCGR3A) and TLR signalling in CD16 monocytes
IFITM3: Type I IFN-induced antiviral transmembrane protein; canonical marker of IFN-primed innate immunity
FCER1G: Gamma chain of IgE and Fc receptors; required for ADCC and immune complex sensing
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease; enhanced in antigen-presenting and pathogen-degrading monocytes
AIF1: Interferon-inducible actin-binding protein; driver of macrophage activation and vascular surveillance
PSAP: Saposin precursor; essential for lysosomal lipid breakdown and antigen presentation
LST1: LPS and IFN-γ inducible membrane protein; restricts lymphocyte proliferation and aids microbial sensing
COTL1: Actin regulator binding 5-lipoxygenase; enables chemotactic crawling during vascular patrolling
CD68: Lysosomal-associated glycoprotein; marker of phagocytic and endocytic capacity

functional_description: This signature marks GMP-stage cells transitioning towards monocytic commitment, characterized by elevated protein synthesis capacity and oxidative stress resilience. The dominance of ribosomal proteins, chaperones, and antioxidant enzymes reflects heightened translational demand and metabolic maturation typical of mono-primed GMP-Mono cells rather than cycling progenitors.

functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor commitment characterized by upregulation of antimicrobial and degradative enzyme programs (LYZ, RNASE2, CSTA) alongside chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2) supporting transcriptional activation of monocyte-fate genes. The predominance of Early ProMono cells (78%) indicates engagement of nascent monocytic differentiation prior to full surface marker maturation and cell cycle exit.

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and biosynthetic activity
functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression and biosynthetic demands in Early ProMono progenitors, characterized by elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and chromatin accessibility. The dominance of proliferation-associated factors (STMN1, PCLAF, HMGB2) alongside mitochondrial genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND5) indicates metabolically active, cycling Early ProMono cells. LYZ expression marks monocytic commitment, though the signature lacks late ProMono maturation markers (CD14, CCR2) and monocyte-specific antimicrobial genes (CTSL, CTSS, FCGR1A), confirming early-stage progenitor biology.

STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator essential for active mitosis
PCLAF: Cell cycle control protein; marks dividing progenitors
HMGB2: Chromatin accessibility factor in transcriptionally active nuclei

HNRNPA2B1: RNA processing in actively transcribing cells
RNASE2: Antimicrobial RNase, early monocytic differentiation marker

programme_name: Early ProMono cytoplasmic maturation and antimicrobial priming
functional_description: This signature reflects cytoplasmic protein accumulation and innate immune effector priming in Early ProMono cells, characterized by abundant S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex, S100A4/A6), antimicrobial hydrolases (LYZ, RNASE2), and cytoskeletal regulators. The programme supports monocyte commitment through actin dynamics (TMSB4X, CAPG) and chromatin accessibility (HMGN2, HMGB1/2) required for ProMono differentiation, without yet expressing surface markers characteristic of Late ProMono or CD14 Mono.

LYZ: Canonical monocyte antimicrobial hydrolase, marks commitment away from neutrophil fate
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering for cellular remodeling during Early-to-Late ProMono transition

RNASE2: Ribonuclease antimicrobial activity characteristic of monocyte lineage

functional_description: This signature reflects type I interferon-induced antiviral and antimicrobial effector functions in classical monocytes, characterized by interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) and autophagy-mediated immune responses. The program is activated in both CD14 and CD16 monocytes but enriched in CD14 populations, suggesting a shared innate immune response to viral or microbial PAMPs that triggers interferon signaling cascades.

TP53INP1: Autophagy regulator and oxidative stress sensor promoting autophagic cell death responses

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened ribosomal biogenesis and translation capacity in early GMP and GMP-Mono stages. The coordinated upregulation of 40S and 60S ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL4) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) indicates cells actively synthesizing proteins required for myeloid differentiation and commitment.

NPM1: Centrosome duplication and protein chaperoning—consistent with Early GMP cell cycle activity (64.5% of activators)

functional_description: This signature represents a committed monocyte progenitor programme characterized by elevated antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, RNASE2) and stress-response chaperones (HSP90B1), alongside chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN2) supporting active transcription during lineage commitment. The high representation of Late ProMono (48%) and Early ProMono (41%) with minimal CD14 Mono contamination indicates this reflects the transitional progenitor state between GMP and mature monocyte, distinct from terminal differentiation programmes.

programme_name: Monocyte lysosomal and innate immune activation
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened lysosomal/phagosomal maturation and innate immune receptor signalling in both CD14 and CD16 monocytes. The programme is dominated by lysosomal hydrolases (CTSS, PSAP), actin dynamics regulators (TMSB4X, AIF1), and ITAM-bearing adaptor proteins (TYROBP, FCER1G) that coordinate phagocytic capacity and danger-associated molecular pattern recognition.

RNA-seq on sorted CD14+ and CD16+ monocytes to quantify expression ratios and confirm programme is active in both subsets despite 54/46 split.

functional_description: This signature captures constitutive ribosomal biogenesis and translation machinery in Early GMP progenitors, reflecting their active protein synthesis capacity during progenitor expansion. NPM1: Nucleolar protein involved in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation control
GAPDH/LDHB: Glycolytic metabolism supporting energetic demands of active progenitors

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened ribosomal biogenesis and protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP progenitors, driven by elevated expression of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A), translation factors (EEF1B2), and associated machinery (HNRNPA1, NPM1). This metabolic programme supports the rapid proliferation and biosynthetic demands characteristic of committed myeloid progenitors preparing for lineage differentiation.

programme_name: CD16 Mono Iron Homeostasis Stress Response
functional_description: This signature reflects a metabolically active CD16 monocyte state centered on iron storage and oxidative stress management, coupled with actin cytoskeletal remodeling and antigen presentation capacity. The dominance of FTH1 and SAT1 suggests heightened intracellular iron sequestration and polyamine catabolism, consistent with metabolic reprogramming in patrolling monocytes responding to inflammatory or oxidative challenges.

Confirm vascular surveillance competence via CXCL16, COTL1, and ITGAX/ITGAM expression. Validate TYROBP/CLEC7A axis for ADCC via CD16-crosslinking experiments measuring degranulation.

programme_name: Early Monocytic Differentiation and Chromatin Priming
functional_description: This signature marks the transition from GMP to early ProMono stages, characterized by chromatin remodeling, oxidative stress management, and preparation for monocytic differentiation. The enrichment of nucleosome-associated proteins and metabolic machinery suggests active transcriptional reorganization prior to full commitment to the monocytic lineage.

functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor commitment with activation of antimicrobial and lysosomal programmes characteristic of ProMono differentiation. functional_description: This signature captures the basal translational capacity and protein synthesis machinery of Early GMP progenitors, dominated by 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL7A, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP and GMP-Mono populations, characterized by robust ribosomal protein expression (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). GSTP1, UQCRH: oxidative stress management and mitochondrial function supporting metabolic demands of differentiating progenitors

programme_name: Myeloid antigen presentation and ITAM signalling

SERPINA1: Elastase inhibitor; protease regulation in inflammatory myeloid microenvironments
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for TYROBP+FCGR3A+ vs TYROBP+CD14+ to resolve CD16-specific ITAM signalling. Immunofluorescence microscopy to assess HLA-DR surface expression and pMAPK/pERK activation downstream of FCGR3A crosslinking in sorted CD16 Mono vs CD14 Mono. Single-cell CITE-seq to map surface protein abundance of CD16, CD14, HLA-DR and LST1 expression concordance within this activated myeloid compartment.

functional_description: Pan-monocyte programme centred on HLA class II antigen presentation and processing, with co-activation of iron homeostasis and translational capacity. This signature reflects constitutive MHC-II expression across CD14 and CD16 monocyte subsets, coordinated with cellular stress buffering and protein synthesis machinery required to support high-level antigen presentation.
key_evidence: CD74: Invariant chain essential for HLA-II assembly, trafficking and peptide loading—canonical marker of antigen-presenting monocytes
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQB1: Complete HLA class II presentation module spanning DR, DP and DQ loci—defines pan-monocyte antigen presentation capacity
HLA-DMA: Non-classical HLA-II molecule functioning as peptide editor in endosomal compartments—essential for optimal peptide selection
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron storage and detoxification—critical buffering of iron used in cytochrome c oxidase during OXPHOS-dependent antigen presentation
AIF1: Calcium and actin-binding protein induced by interferon—supports monocyte activation state compatible with high antigen presentation
YBX1: Cold shock protein with RNA-binding function—co-regulated stress response protein supporting cellular proteostasis under antigen presentation demand
SLC25A5: ADP/ATP mitochondrial transporter—supplies ATP for protein synthesis and MHC-II assembly
RPS2, RPL4: Ribosomal proteins—indicate elevated translational demand for sustained HLA-II and CD74 synthesis
BID: Pro-apoptotic BCL-2 family member—stress-sensing component in antigen-presenting cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: HLA-DR+CD74+ on CD14+ and CD16+ monocytes; functional assay of antigen presentation capacity in sorted populations; correlate FTH1 and ferritin levels with HLA-II surface expression intensity and antigen processing efficiency

programme_name: Early ProMono metabolic and antimicrobial activation
functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor commitment characterized by upregulation of lysozyme-mediated antimicrobial defense (LYZ, RNASE2) coupled with elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1) to support metabolic demands. Concurrent expression of chromatin remodeling factors (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2) and cell-cycle machinery (TUBB, TUBA1B, STMN1) indicates active transcriptional remodeling and proliferative capacity characteristic of Early ProMono stage prior to terminal maturation.
key_evidence: LYZ: Canonical monocyte lineage marker; lysozyme antimicrobial function essential for mono fate specification
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1: Mitochondrial respiratory chain components reflecting high metabolic activity during ProMono proliferation
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease supporting innate immune priming in committed progenitors
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2: Chromatin remodeling and transcriptional activation during lineage commitment
TUBB, TUBA1B, STMN1: Cytoskeletal and cell-cycle regulators consistent with proliferative Early ProMono state
S100A8: Early myeloid differentiation marker enriched in immature monocyte progenitors
96.5% Early ProMono composition: Dominant cell-type validates early commitment stage
suggested_validation: Flow sort Early ProMono (CD34+CD13+MS4A3+CD14−) and perform RT-qPCR on LYZ, RNASE2, and mitochondrial genes; validate absence of KLF4, IRF8 transcriptional activity and CD14/CD11b surface expression to confirm pre-terminal progenitor status; assess mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM) to confirm elevated OXPHOS.

functional_description: This signature captures the translational machinery and protein synthesis infrastructure characteristic of Early GMP progenitors. The dominant ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPS2, RPS17) reflect high biosynthetic demand in early uncommitted GMPs preparing for rapid proliferation and lineage priming, supported by translation factors (EEF1B2) and glycolytic metabolism (GAPDH, LDHB). The inclusion of NPM1 (nucleolar/centrosomal functions) and PTMA (proliferation licensing) further supports active progenitor expansion rather than committed monocytic differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPLP0: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit core components—baseline high in proliferating progenitors
RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4: 60S large subunit structural proteins—sustain translation of early myeloid transcription factors
EEF1B2: elongation factor GEF function—critical for translational throughput in synthetic-phase cells
GAPDH, LDHB: glycolytic/lactate metabolism—support energetic demands of Early GMP biosynthesis
NPM1: nucleolar chaperone and centrosome duplication—marks proliferation licensing phase
PTMA: anti-apoptotic mediator and DNA-binding TF cofactor—preserve progenitor viability during commitment priming
HNRNPA1: RNA processing and stability—enable rapid myeloid TF mRNA turnover during early lineage decisions
95% Early GMP composition: signature is specifically enriched in the earliest GMP subset, not late/committed stages
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression across sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono vs ProMono by qPCR; confirm inverse relationship with monocytic maturation markers (CD14, CD16); perform polysome profiling to validate active translation in Early GMP vs non-cycling GMP subsets; cross-validate with BM bulk RNA-seq from CD34+CD45RA+ vs CD34+CD45RA- progenitors.

functional_description: This signature marks the transition from GMP-Mono through early ProMono stages, characterized by upregulation of antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, RNASE2), cell migration machinery (TMSB4X), and chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN1/2) that enable transcriptional activation of myeloid differentiation programs. The dominance of ribosomal proteins and metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, GPX1) reflects active protein synthesis and oxidative stress management during monocytic commitment.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte antimicrobial enzyme; marks commitment beyond GMP stage
RNASE2: monocyte-enriched ribonuclease with bactericidal activity; lineage-specific marker
TMSB4X: actin-binding protein essential for monocyte migration and cytoskeletal remodeling
HMGN2/HMGN1: nucleosome-associated proteins maintaining open chromatin during myeloid TF engagement
PTMA: anti-apoptotic factor supporting survival during progenitor-to-monocyte transition
RPS24/RPL37A/RPS23: translational machinery supporting high protein synthesis in differentiating monocytes
GPX1: oxidative stress management critical during monocytic differentiation
LGALS1: galectin-mediated autocrine signaling regulating monocyte proliferation and differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain LYZ+RNASE2+ cells with CSF1R/CD64 to confirm early ProMono identity; distinguish from GMP-Mono (MPO+) and mature monocytes (CD14++CD16+). qPCR validation of IRF8 and CSF1R co-expression to confirm monocytic lineage bias relative to neutrophil-biased (CEBPE+) progenitors.

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in GMP-stage progenitors undergoing early myeloid commitment. The predominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0) combined with MPO expression and oxidative phosphorylation genes (UQCRH, MT-CO2, MT-CO3) indicates metabolic priming for granule biogenesis during GMP-to-monocyte differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0: coordinate ribosomal protein overexpression indicating active translation for myeloid protein synthesis
MPO: myeloid peroxidase essential for both neutrophil and monocyte development, present in GMP-Mono (41.5%) cells
UQCRH, MT-CO2, MT-CO3: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation supporting energetic demands of differentiating progenitors
HMGN1, PTMA: nucleosome-associated proteins facilitating transcriptional reprogramming during lineage commitment
HSPB1: heat shock protein supporting protein folding during active synthesis and stress conditions
PRSS57: serine protease precursor targeting azurophil granule storage (monocyte-biased marker)
GMP-Mono (41.5%) + Early GMP (31.5%) + GMP-Cycle (26.0%): signature concentrated in cycling and committed GMP populations with minimal ProMono
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry correlating RPS/RPL transcript levels with MPO+ and CD34+ populations; single-cell protein synthesis assay (O-propargyl-puromycin) in Early GMP vs GMP-Mono; validate PRSS57 as monocyte-bias marker distinguishing from CEBPE-driven neutrophil commitment

programme_name: Early ProMono cytoplasmic maturation and antimicrobial
functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor differentiation marked by upregulation of antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, RNASE2), cytoskeletal remodelling proteins (TMSB4X, ACTG1, CAPG), and chromatin accessibility factors (HMGN1, HMGN2). The prominence of Early ProMono (60%) and Late ProMono (22.5%) with suppression of GMP-Neut markers indicates commitment to monocyte fate with acquisition of innate immune functional capacity.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte antimicrobial enzyme, replaces MPO/ELANE of neutrophil lineage
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease supporting monocyte bactericidal function
LGALS1: galectin-1 mediates cell-cell interactions during ProMono egress and tissue recruitment
TMSB4X, ACTG1, CAPG: actin-regulatory proteins enabling ProMono migration and morphological maturation
HMGN1, HMGN2: chromatin remodellers supporting transcriptional activation of myeloid programs
CSTA: cysteine protease inhibitor protecting monocyte from autolysis during maturation
HSP90B1: molecular chaperone stabilising nascent monocyte proteins during differentiation
ANXA2: calcium-dependent phospholipid binding supporting cytoskeletal organisation and signalling
Cell composition: 82.5% Early+Late ProMono vs 17.5% GMP+CD14, indicating stage-specific activation
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry: LGALS1 surface expression (nascent ProMono marker), co-staining with MS4A3, CSF1R, and KLF4 intracellular; confirm loss of MPO/ELANE relative to GMP; assess LYZ, RNASE2 functional capacity via bacterial killing assays in sorted Early vs Late ProMono populations.

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodelling and antimicrobial
functional_description: This signature reflects active transcriptional remodelling and antimicrobial effector priming in Early ProMono cells. The enrichment of chromatin-associated proteins (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2, H2AFZ, H2AFV) coupled with monocyte-specific antimicrobial factors (LYZ, RNASE2, RETN) indicates transcriptional activation of pro-monocytic programmes alongside loss of proliferative constraints. The dominance of Early ProMono (61%) and GMP-Mono (23%) with minimal Late ProMono/CD14 Mono representation suggests this marks the transition from bipotent GMP toward committed mono fate.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte lysozyme, essential antimicrobial and differentiation marker
HMGN2: nucleosomal remodelling protein marking transcriptionally active early commitment chromatin
TMSB4X: actin dynamics regulator supporting pro-migratory monocyte differentiation
HMGB1/HMGB2: chromatin architectural proteins driving inflammatory monocyte programmes
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease specific to monocyte antimicrobial arsenal
LGALS1: galectin-1 mediating cell-cell interactions during mono progenitor egress
RETN: resistin family member associated with myeloid activation
PTTG1: securin suggesting active cell cycle but with reduced proliferative output vs GMP
suggested_validation: Sort Early vs Late ProMono by MS4A3/CSF1R surface markers; validate HMGN2/HMGB1 enrichment by flow+RNA; confirm loss of MPO/ELANE vs GMP-Neut; assess IRF8/KLF4 TF activity by ChIP or ATAC at LYZ/RETN enhancers

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis capacity in actively cycling GMP-stage progenitors. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPL37A, RPS24, RPS17, RPLP0) and mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) indicates metabolic upregulation supporting rapid biosynthesis during cell cycle progression. Chromatin remodelling factors (HMGN1, HMGN2) and translation initiation cofactors (PPIA, ANP32B) further support active transcription and proliferation in GMP-Cycle and GMP-Mono subsets.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPL37A, RPS24, RPS17, RPLP0: Coordinate ribosomal protein expression indicating heightened translation demand in proliferating progenitors
MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: Mitochondrial OXPHOS machinery enabling ATP generation for rapid cell division and biosynthesis
HMGN1, HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in cycling cells
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding during high translation rates
PTMA, ANP32B: Nuclear factors supporting survival and transcriptional regulation in proliferative stress
suggested_validation: Validate via mitochondrial mass/membrane potential assays (TMRM, BODIPY C11) and protein synthesis rates (puromycin incorporation) in sorted GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono vs early ProMono populations. Confirm cell cycle distribution using Ki-67/DNA content flow cytometry to correlate ribosomal/OXPHOS expression with S/G2M phase.

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodelling and translation
functional_description: This signature captures chromatin accessibility and nucleosome dynamics during early monocytic commitment, marked by enrichment of histone variants (H2AFZ, H2AFV), non-histone chromatin proteins (HMGB1, HMGB2, NUCKS1), and cytoskeletal/translational machinery (TUBB, TUBA1B, STMN1). The dominance of Early ProMono cells (48%) with supporting GMP-Mono and GMP-Cycle populations suggests active chromatin remodelling coupled to cell cycle progression during monocytic lineage specification.
key_evidence: H2AFZ: Histone H2A variant enriched in transcriptionally active chromatin; marks open configurations during lineage commitment
HMGB1/HMGB2: Non-histone chromatin proteins regulating DNA accessibility and transcriptional licensing during early monocytic priming
NUCKS1: Phosphorylation hub integrating cell cycle signals with chromatin structure in proliferating progenitors
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics and mitotic checkpoint control; consistent with GMP-Cycle (20.5%) component
TUBB/TUBA1B: Cytoskeletal proteins supporting cytokinesis and cell cycle progression in Early ProMono compartment
HMGN2: Maintains open chromatin architecture in transcriptionally poised early monocytic cells
LSM5/SNRPG: Spliceosomal components indicating active pre-mRNA processing during differentiation
MT-CO2/UQCRQ: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation supporting energy demands of proliferating Early ProMono cells
suggested_validation: Compare H2AFZ, HMGB1, NUCKS1 protein localization and chromatin co-IP in flow-sorted Early ProMono vs Late ProMono to confirm open chromatin state. Correlate STMN1/NUCKS1 phosphorylation status with Ki67 expression across GMP-Cycle enriched fraction. Use ATAC-seq on Early ProMono subset to validate accessible regulatory regions.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP progenitors, indicating high biosynthetic capacity characteristic of proliferating progenitor cells. The dominance of 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) supports active protein synthesis required for rapid myeloid differentiation. Co-expression of NPM1 (nucleolar protein, centrosome/proliferation-related) and HMGN1 (active chromatin) further indicates a proliferative, transcriptionally permissive progenitor state.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunits essential for sustained protein synthesis in proliferating GMPs
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting rapid synthesis capacity during early myeloid lineage specification
NPM1: nucleolar shuttle protein associated with active cell proliferation and centrosome duplication in progenitors
HMGN1: nucleosomal DNA binding protein marking transcriptionally active chromatin state typical of Early GMP
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing in proliferative cells
GAPDH, LDHB: glycolytic/metabolic enzymes sustaining energy demands of biosynthetically active progenitors
PTMA: nucleocytoplasmic protein with anti-apoptotic function maintaining progenitor viability
87.5% Early GMP composition: signature peaks in earliest GMP stage before lineage-specific differentiation
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein/translation machinery signature between Early GMP, GMP-Mono, and GMP-Cycle via flow cytometry (CD34+/CD33+/CD13+ gating) with protein synthesis assays (puromycin incorporation, O-propargyl-puromycin labeling). Validate NPM1 and HMGN1 as proliferation markers in Early GMP by immunofluorescence. Confirm decline of this programme upon transition to GMP-Mono and ProMono stages where biosynthetic demands decrease. Assess whether FLT3 signalling or Notch pathway activation sustains this translational programme in Early GMP.

functional_description: This signature reflects active translation machinery and metabolic homeostasis in mono-lineage committed progenitors, particularly GMP-Mono and Early ProMono stages. The dominant ribosomal and translation elongation factors indicate high protein synthesis capacity concurrent with monocytic differentiation, while housekeeping metabolic enzymes support rapid cell proliferation and antimicrobial protein production.
key_evidence: LYZ: Lysozyme is the canonical monocytic antimicrobial effector; high expression marks functional monocytic commitment and distinguishes GMP-Mono/ProMono from undifferentiated GMP

RPS24, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS2, RPLP0, RPS23: Ribosomal proteins comprise >50% of signature, indicating translational upregulation during monocytic maturation to support LYZ and other secreted/granular proteins
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor reinforces active protein synthesis capacity in differentiating monocytic cells
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme supporting metabolic demands of proliferating early ProMono cells
GSTP1: Detoxification enzyme indicating metabolic activation and oxidative stress handling in differentiating monocytes
HMGN1, YBX1: Chromatin and RNA binding proteins facilitating transcriptional remodeling toward monocytic gene expression programmes
PPIA, PTMA: Protein chaperones and anti-apoptotic factors stabilizing the monocytic differentiation programme
suggested_validation: Validate by co-staining LYZ with CSF1R/CD64 and flow-sorting GMP-Mono and Early ProMono; verify ribosomal protein co-expression by qPCR; confirm GSTP1 and HMGN1 upregulation marks IRF8-driven monocytic commitment versus CEBPE-driven neutrophilic branch

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis machinery activation in early monocytic progenitors transitioning from GMP toward ProMono stages. The enrichment of mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1) alongside ribosomal proteins and molecular chaperones indicates heightened metabolic demand and proteostatic capacity during lineage commitment, consistent with the energetic requirements of early monocyte differentiation.
key_evidence: MT-CO2: Core Complex IV component; high expression supports enhanced OXPHOS capacity in metabolically active early ProMono
MT-CO3: Complex IV assembly; validates mitochondrial bioenergetic upregulation signature
MT-ND1: Complex I electron transport; reinforces coordinated OXPHOS complex maturation
MPO: Myeloid peroxidase; early priming marker present in GMP-Cycle and Early ProMono (75% of activating cells)
RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23: Ribosomal proteins; indicate elevated translation demand during differentiation
HSP90B1, HSPB1: Heat shock chaperones; support protein folding stress during commitment
HMGN2, HMGN1: Chromatin remodeling factors; facilitate transcriptional remodeling of monocyte lineage genes
SFPQ, SNRPF: Splicing factors; enable alternative transcript processing during lineage specification
suggested_validation: Perform metabolic flux analysis (seahorse) comparing GMP-Cycle vs Early ProMono to quantify OXPHOS/glycolysis ratios; validate MPO and IRF8 co-expression by flow cytometry to confirm monocytic lineage bias; measure mitochondrial mass (TMRM) and reactive oxygen species (CM-H2DCFDA) in sorted populations.

programme_name: Early ProMono metabolic and antimicrobial priming
functional_description: This signature reflects the metabolic activation and antimicrobial effector priming characteristic of Early ProMono cells transitioning toward monocyte commitment. The dominant enrichment of housekeeping metabolic genes (GAPDH, PPIA, mitochondrial electron transport MT-CO2/MT-CO3) coupled with antimicrobial proteases (LYZ, RNASE2) and chromatin remodelling factors (HMGN1/HMGN2, HMGB1) indicates heightened biosynthetic capacity and preparedness for immune effector functions. This represents the pre-egress metabolic priming phase preceding full CD14 surface marker expression and monocyte egress.
key_evidence: LYZ: Core monocyte antimicrobial lysosomal protease, hallmark of commitment; lost in GMP-Neut
MT-CO3, MT-CO2: Elevated mitochondrial respiration consistent with metabolically active Early ProMono
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease reinforcing monocyte effector phenotype
HMGN2, HMGN1, HMGB1: Chromatin accessibility factors supporting active transcriptional reprogramming during commitment
GAPDH, PPIA: Glycolytic and protein-folding capacity enabling rapid biosynthesis in early progenitors
TMSB4X: Actin dynamics supporting migration and cell differentiation processes
62% Early ProMono composition: Signature robustly enriched in the earliest committed progenitor stage
suggested_validation: Compare IRF8, KLF4, and PU.1 expression levels in Early ProMono vs GMP and CD14 Mono via qPCR; confirm loss of MPO/ELANE vs GMP-Neut; validate CSF1R and MS4A3 surface expression by flow cytometry to distinguish Early ProMono metabolic signature from downstream CD14 surface maturation.

functional_description: This signature reflects a shared transcriptional programme in both CD14 and CD16 monocytes centred on MHC class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPB1, CD74) and lysosomal proteolytic capacity (CTSS, PSAP) for professional antigen-presenting cells. The co-expression of iron storage (FTH1), calcium-binding proteins (AIF1, S100A11), cytoskeletal remodelling factors (TMSB4X, COTL1), and ITAM-bearing adaptors (TYROBP, FCER1G) indicates integrated signalling competence in response-ready monocytes.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPB1: complete MHC class II heterodimer composition required for antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells
CD74: essential chaperone for MHC class II loading and trafficking; also CD40-binding partner for costimulation
CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease critical for proteolytic processing of antigens into presentation-competent peptides
PSAP: generates saposins for lysosomal hydrolase activation and lipid antigen processing
FTH1: iron homeostasis in metabolically active antigen-presenting cells; iron depletion restricts bacterial growth
TYROBP + FCER1G: ITAM adaptor molecules providing signalling integration downstream of Fc and TLR pathways
AIF1 + S100A11: calcium-dependent cytokine-inducible effector proteins promoting macrophage activation
TMSB4X + COTL1: actin polymerization regulators supporting migration and intracellular trafficking in activated monocytes
50.5% CD14 / 49.5% CD16 composition: signature is not discriminatory between classical and non-classical monocytes; suggests shared antigen presentation potential across subsets
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining HLA-DR, HLA-DP, CD74 and CTSS (intracellular) on CD14+ vs CD16+ monocytes; functional assay: antigen uptake and processing capacity with fluorescent bacterial peptides; compare to resting monocytes and mature dendritic cells to confirm intermediate APC phenotype.

programme_name: CD16 Mono Iron Homeostasis Stress Response
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD16 monocyte state characterized by iron metabolism and oxidative stress management, coupled with cytoskeletal remodeling and protease inhibition. The program is consistent with metabolic adaptation in patrolling monocytes exposed to endothelial surveillance and oxidative microenvironments, rather than canonical patrolling or antiviral transcriptional programs.
key_evidence: FTH1: Heavy chain ferritin dominates signature—iron storage protein essential for managing oxidative stress in activated monocytes during vascular patrolling
HMOX1: Heme oxygenase-1 upregulation indicates oxidative stress response and iron recycling in CD16 Mono
COTL1: Actin-binding protein and 5-lipoxygenase interaction partner; supports cytoskeletal dynamics required for crawling and cellular surveillance
TIMP1: Metalloproteinase inhibitor; restrains ECM degradation during non-destructive endothelial interaction
SAT1: Polyamine catabolic enzyme; metabolic marker of cell cycle arrest and stress adaptation typical of patrolling state
CXCL16: Chemokine with IFN-γ responsiveness; positions CD16 Mono for inflammatory recruitment and scavenging
LST1: Lymphocyte proliferation inhibitor enhanced by LPS/IFN-γ; marks inflammatory/interferon-primed state in CD16 compartment
RHOC: Rho GTPase; mediates cytoskeletal dynamics required for trans-endothelial migration and patrolling behavior
YBX1: RNA-binding protein with broad stress-response roles; consistent with metabolic sensing in activated monocytes
HLA-DPA1: MHC class II antigen presentation capability; indicates capacity for immune priming in CD16 Mono subset
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of FTH1, HMOX1 protein expression in sorted CD16 Mono (FCGR3A+CD14lo) vs CD14 Mono; correlate with intracellular iron/ROS measurements and assess functional link to crawling capacity via live-cell imaging on endothelium. Confirm absence of NR4A1/NR4A2/ISG15 upregulation to exclude canonical patrolling or antiviral programs.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated translational capacity and oxidative phosphorylation in Early GMP cells, marking metabolic commitment to active protein synthesis and energy production during myeloid progenitor expansion. The dominance of ribosomal proteins and mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicates heightened metabolic demand characteristic of proliferating GMP populations, particularly Early GMP (67%) and cycling GMP (24%).
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPL7A, RPS2, RPL4: coordinated ribosomal protein upregulation supports high translation rates during GMP expansion
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes indicate enhanced ATP generation for biosynthetic demands
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor reflects active protein synthesis machinery engagement
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme suggesting metabolic switching to support rapid cell division in cycling GMP populations
PTMA: anti-apoptotic function supports progenitor survival during proliferation
High Early GMP/GMP-Cycle composition: signature enriched in proliferative stages where translational and metabolic burden peaks
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring TMRM (mitochondrial membrane potential) and protein synthesis rates (puromycin incorporation) in sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono populations. Confirm ribosomal loading status by polysome profiling. Compare with metabolic stress markers (glucose uptake, lactate production) to assess metabolic state transitions during GMP differentiation.

functional_description: This signature captures heightened protein synthesis capacity and metabolic activity in Early GMP cells, characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and glycolytic/oxidative phosphorylation enzymes. This reflects intense biosynthetic demand during early myeloid progenitor expansion before lineage commitment, consistent with the 93% Early GMP composition of activating cells.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A: coordinated ribosomal subunit proteins indicating elevated translation machinery
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor essential for rapid protein synthesis during progenitor proliferation
NPM1: nucleolar/centrosome protein supporting ribosome biogenesis and cell cycle progression in progenitors
GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH: glycolytic and mitochondrial metabolic enzymes supporting high energy demand of proliferating GMPs
HSP90AB1: heat shock chaperone facilitating protein folding during intensive biosynthesis
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA processing in metabolically active cells
suggested_validation: Validate by correlating ribosomal protein expression with cell cycle markers (MKI67, TOP2A) and early GMP master TFs (CEBPA, SPI1) in sorted Early GMP vs. differentiated monocyte populations; confirm reduced signature in mature CD14+ monocytes where translation demand decreases post-commitment.

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodeling and antimicrobial preparation
functional_description: This signature reflects an active chromatin remodeling and transcriptional licensing programme characteristic of Early ProMono progenitors transitioning toward monocyte commitment. The coordinated upregulation of nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2) and chromatin remodelers indicates preparation for large-scale transcriptional reprogramming, while simultaneous expression of monocyte-specific antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, RNASE2) marks the early establishment of myeloid identity. The presence of MPO and cell-cycle regulatory factors (BIRC5, PTMA) suggests this programme captures Early ProMono cells still retaining modest proliferative capacity but progressively silencing neutrophil differentiation pathways.
key_evidence: LYZ: Canonical monocyte-specific antimicrobial lysosomal enzyme, marks mono commitment
HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2: Nucleosome-binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin and epigenetic remodeling during lineage commitment
RNASE2: Monocyte-enriched antimicrobial ribonuclease supporting early mono functional programme
MPO: Residual neutrophil marker present in Early ProMono but downregulated relative to GMP, indicating incomplete commitment
BIRC5, PTMA: Anti-apoptotic and cell-cycle factors consistent with progenitor proliferation status of Early ProMono
LGALS1: Galectin implicated in cell-cell interactions and growth regulation during differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry: sort Early ProMono (MS4A3+, CSF1R+, CD14-/low) and confirm co-expression of LYZ+/MPO+/low (intermediate state). Perform single-molecule FISH for HMGN2/HMGB1 to assess chromatin accessibility at monocyte fate-determining loci (IRF8, KLF4 targets). Compare chromatin landscape (ATAC-seq) of this Early ProMono cohort to GMP-Mono and Late ProMono to demonstrate progressive chromatin opening at mono-specific regulatory regions.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis machinery and translational capacity in early GMP-stage progenitors (70% Early GMP), characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S: RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24; 60S: RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0) and translation factors (EEF1B2). The enrichment of nucleolar/ribosomal assembly factors (NPM1, HMGN1) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1) suggests active ribosomal biogenesis supporting the biosynthetic demands of proliferative early myeloid progenitors rather than lineage commitment signals.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPS2: core 40S ribosomal subunit proteins, coordinate expression indicates active ribosome assembly
RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0: large 60S subunit proteins, essential for translational competence
EEF1B2: elongation factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, rate-limiting for protein synthesis
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein driving ribosomal biogenesis and centrosome duplication in cycling progenitors
HMGN1: chromatin architecture regulator associated with transcriptionally active ribosomal protein genes
HNRNPA1: pre-mRNA splicing modulator of translation machinery components
GAPDH, UQCRH: glycolysis and OXPHOS support energetic demands of protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) ribosome profiling or polysome fractionation in sorted Early GMP vs. mature monocytes; (2) quantitative proteomics of ribosomal protein content; (3) 35S-methionine pulse-chase to measure translation rates; (4) confirm suppression in GMP-Mono and mature CD14+ monocytes where translation demand decreases during differentiation.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A) and translation elongation machinery (EEF1B2) in GMP-Mono cells, indicating high translational demand during monocytic progenitor differentiation. Supporting cofactors (PTMA, PPIA) and metabolic capacity (UQCRH, LDHB, GSTP1, TXN, HMGN1) suggest active protein synthesis coupled with oxidative metabolism and redox homeostasis, consistent with biosynthetic requirements of early committed monocyte progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A: Core ribosomal subunits; 60S/40S composition reflects translational machinery upregulation during lineage commitment
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity; necessary for tRNA delivery during active protein synthesis in differentiating progenitors
PTMA: DNA-binding cofactor and apoptosis antagonist; supports nuclear-cytoplasmic partitioning during G1/S progression in GMP-Mono
UQCRH, LDHB: Oxidative phosphorylation and glycolytic metabolism; supports energy demand of translating cells
GSTP1, TXN: Antioxidant detoxification; manages ROS generated by elevated metabolic activity
HMGN1: Chromatin-associated protein; facilitates transcriptional access for differentiation genes during monocytic commitment
Cell composition: 49.5% GMP-Mono + 39.5% Early GMP (89% early-committed progenitors); 9% GMP-Cycle suggests active proliferation during differentiation
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein and EEF1B2 expression across sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono vs ProMono by RT-qPCR; correlate with polysome profiling to quantify translation rate; examine PTMA and HMGN1 ChIP-seq in GMP-Mono for co-occupancy at monocytic lineage genes (SPI1, CEBPA targets); validate metabolic shift via Seahorse assay (ECAR/OCR ratio GMP-Mono vs Early GMP).

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery activity in Early GMP and GMP-Cycle cells. The dominant ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS2, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4) and translation factors (EEF1B2) indicate heightened protein synthetic capacity supporting rapid cell proliferation and differentiation during early myeloid commitment.

RPS23, RPS2, RPS17: Multiple 40S subunit proteins indicating robust ribosomal assembly

functional_description: This signature captures enhanced protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP and GMP-Cycle progenitors, predominantly through upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation elongation machinery. The co-presence of MPO indicates early azurophil granule priming concurrent with rapid protein production typical of proliferating GMPs preparing for myeloid differentiation.

EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis during GMP expansion and differentiation
MPO: azurophil granule protease component, consistent with Early GMP and GMP-Cycle developmental stage where granule biogenesis initiates
PRSS57: serine protease stored in azurophil granules, reinforcing early neutrophil/monocyte-lineage priming

programme_name: Monocyte lysosomal and innate immune activation
functional_description: This signature captures a core lysosomal-endosomal maturation and phagocytic effector programme active in both CD14 and CD16 monocytes, characterized by high expression of lysosomal proteases, iron metabolism, and ITAM-coupled pattern recognition machinery. The 50:50 CD14:CD16 composition and absence of canonical pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL1B, IL6) suggest this represents a constitutive myeloid activation state rather than acute LPS/TLR4 response, likely reflecting steady-state antimicrobial surveillance and tissue trafficking capacity.
key_evidence: CD68: canonical lysosomal membrane glycoprotein, marker of monocyte/macrophage maturation and phagocytic capacity
CTSS: cathepsin S required for antigen presentation and intracellular pathogen degradation in myeloid cells
TYROBP (DAP12): ITAM adaptor coupling multiple pattern recognition receptors (TLRs, C-type lectins, Fc receptors) to intracellular signalling
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain, component of FcγRI/FcγRIII signalling essential for antibody-opsonized pathogen phagocytosis
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain reflecting high iron turnover in metabolically active monocytes
AIF1 (Iba1): actin-binding protein induced by IFN-γ and lipopolysaccharide, marker of activated myeloid cells
PSAP: saposin precursor involved in lysosomal lipid hydrolysis and antigen presentation
LST1: LPS-inducible membrane protein inhibiting lymphocyte proliferation in inflammatory contexts
TMSB4X: actin sequesterer supporting high cellular motility required for recruitment and extravasation

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP cells, driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and RNA-binding proteins. The enrichment indicates metabolic and translational intensification characteristic of GMP cells preparing for rapid myeloid differentiation and lineage commitment.

RPLP0, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: 60S ribosomal subunit structural proteins supporting translation capacity
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, rate-limiting for translation elongation
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme and moonlighting protein supporting both energy metabolism and RNA binding during differentiation priming
HNRNPA1, YBX1: RNA-binding proteins regulating mRNA stability and translation of lineage-commitment transcripts
UQCRH: mitochondrial Complex III component supporting oxidative phosphorylation energy demands of active protein synthesis
HMGN1: chromatin remodelling protein associated with transcriptional activation during myeloid differentiation

Confirm co-expression with IRF8 or CEBPA in monocytic Early GMP subsets to link translation programme to mono-lineage priming.

functional_description: This signature reflects early committed monocyte progenitor differentiation marked by acquisition of antimicrobial effector functions and oxidative metabolism. The enrichment of S100A8/A9 (calprotectin), LYZ, and RNASE2 indicates priming of innate immune capacity, while elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-CO2/3) support energetic demands of differentiating myeloid cells.

S100A9: Calprotectin partner; co-induced with S100A8 in committed monocyte progenitors; signals ProMono engagement

RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease; signature of activated myeloid cells gaining effector functions
MT-CO2/MT-CO3: Mitochondrial OXPHOS genes; reflect metabolic shift supporting ProMono proliferation and differentiation

RETN: Resistin family; antimicrobial and inflammatory mediator; elevated in activated monocyte progenitors

functional_description: This signature reflects late-stage ProMono and early CD14 monocyte differentiation characterized by upregulation of antimicrobial proteins (S100A8/A9 calprotectin, LYZ lysozyme, RNASE2), calcium-binding and cytoskeletal regulators, and inflammatory mediators. The programme captures the transition from committed progenitors to functionally mature monocytes capable of pathogen recognition and inflammatory response.

LYZ: Lysozyme, key monocyte bactericidal enzyme; confirms lysosomal programme activation characteristic of ProMono maturation
FCN1: Ficolin-1, pattern recognition receptor expressed in mature monocytes; drives innate immune sensing
S100A4/A6: S100 family calcium-binding proteins; regulate cytoskeletal dynamics and cell migration in differentiating monocytes

RETN: Resistin; inflammatory adipokine with monocyte-specific expression during maturation

Metabolic genes (PKM, GAPDH, ACTG1): Support energy demands and cytoskeletal remodeling of differentiating monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of S100A8/A9 with CD14, CSF1R, and MS4A3 across sorted ProMono and CD14 Mono populations; validate that S100A8/A9 co-expression marks Late ProMono→CD14 Mono transition; compare S100A8/A9 levels in GMP-sorted cells to confirm monocyte-lineage specificity and absence in neutrophil branch.

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic reprogramming toward oxidative phosphorylation and antimicrobial effector upregulation characteristic of early monocyte commitment. The dominance of mitochondrial electron transport genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5) coupled with canonical mono differentiation markers (LYZ, RNASE2) and cytoskeletal reorganization factors indicates active metabolic transition from progenitor to committed ProMono state, with preserved proliferative capacity.

functional_description: This signature represents a translational machinery programme dominated by ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation factors, with secondary contributions from nucleolar proteins (NPM1) and RNA-binding proteins. The enrichment in Early GMP (78%) with minimal GMP-Mono (5%) indicates this reflects high basal protein synthesis capacity in early-stage, proliferating progenitors rather than monocyte-specific commitment signals.

RPS23, RPS17, RPS2: Additional 40S components consistently highly expressed across ribosomal signature
RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4: 60S subunit components; comprehensive ribosomal architecture coverage
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; supports active mRNA translation in proliferating progenitors
NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone and proliferation marker; elevated in cell cycle-active Early GMP and GMP-Cycle (16.5%)
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic; supports progenitor survival during active protein synthesis
GAPDH, HNRNPA1: Glycolytic enzyme and RNA-binding protein; moonlighting roles in actively dividing cells

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis capacity in early GMP-stage progenitors transitioning toward monocytic lineage commitment. STMN1: microtubule dynamics integrator supporting mitotic progression in GMP-Cycle and GMP-Mono populations (22–34.5% composition)

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPS17, RPL37A) and translation elongation factor (EEF1B2) expression in Early GMP cells, consistent with the high protein synthesis demands of actively proliferating myeloid progenitors. NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone and centrosome regulator—elevated in cycling/proliferative progenitors undergoing cell division

programme_name: Early ProMono antimicrobial maturation and proliferation
functional_description: This signature reflects Early ProMono cells undergoing active monocytic differentiation with robust antimicrobial protein expression and DNA replication machinery activation. The programme integrates myeloid-specific immune effector functions (S100A8/A9 calprotectin, LYZ lysozyme, RNASE2) with proliferative capacity (PCNA, DUT, PCLAF), characteristic of committed progenitors transitioning toward functional monocytes while maintaining cell cycle activity.

functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor differentiation with emphasis on antimicrobial effector molecules and transcriptional remodelling. The dominance of Early ProMono (54.5%) and GMP-Mono (35.0%) combined with elevated LYZ, RNASE2, and myeloid proteases indicates active preparation for innate immune function prior to full CD14 surface marker acquisition.

RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease; elevated in early ProMono vs mature CD14 Mono

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation factor activity characteristic of actively proliferating GMP progenitors. functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis machinery and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity in Early GMP cells, indicating metabolic priming for rapid proliferation and differentiation. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPL37A, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL4) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and mitochondrial respiratory chain components (MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) suggests metabolically active progenitors preparing for lineage commitment.

MT-ND1/MT-CO2/MT-CO3/UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components reflecting enhanced ATP production for anabolic processes

Verify elevated OXPHOS dependency via Seahorse mitochondrial stress test. Compare with proliferation markers (MKI67, Ki-67) to confirm association with cycling GMP-Cycle subset.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated mitochondrial electron transport chain activity and oxidative phosphorylation in committed monocyte progenitors, supporting the bioenergetic demands of myeloid differentiation. The enrichment of respiratory complex components (MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1) coupled with glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, PKM, TPI1) and protein folding chaperones (PPIA) indicates metabolic remodeling characteristic of ProMono cells transitioning away from rapid GMP proliferation toward monocytic maturation.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD16 monocyte specialization in intracellular iron storage, cytoskeletal regulation, and extracellular matrix remodelling through coordinated expression of ferritin heavy chain, actin-binding proteins, and protease inhibitors. The programme supports the metabolic demands and tissue-surveillance capacity of patrolling monocytes during vascular crawling and endothelial interaction.

functional_description: This signature reflects the establishment of monocyte-intrinsic antimicrobial and proteolytic programmes during ProMono commitment, characterized by upregulation of lysozyme, S100 alarmin proteins, and ribonuclease effectors. The co-expression of myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA) with active chromatin remodelling factors (HMGB2, HMGN2) indicates simultaneous engagement of monocyte fate-specific transcriptional programmes alongside acquisition of bactericidal capacity.

The dominant activation in Early GMP (71%) with secondary GMP-Cycle representation (25.5%) reflects basal translational capacity required for active protein synthesis during early myeloid progenitor maintenance, rather than lineage-specific differentiation commitment.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein synthesis and translation elongation factor activity, coupled with glycolytic and oxidative metabolism, characteristic of metabolically active Early GMP progenitors preparing for rapid proliferation and differentiation. functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor commitment characterized by elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity and monocyte-associated antimicrobial effector proteins. The dominance of Early ProMono (55.5%) activating cells combined with upregulation of lysozyme, S100A8/A9 (calprotectin), and ribonuclease 2 indicates initiation of the bactericidal programme typical of committed ProMono cells transitioning away from multipotent progenitor metabolism.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression, indicative of high protein synthesis capacity in early GMP progenitors. The dominance of Early GMP (69.5%) and GMP-Mono (19.0%) cells suggests active anabolic metabolism supporting rapid proliferation and differentiation during the GMP stage, prior to lineage-specific commitment.

functional_description: This signature defines classical CD14+ monocytes with robust antimicrobial and innate immune effector functions, characterized by elevated S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex, enhanced bactericidal capacity via lysozyme, and metabolic activation. The programme reflects primary antimicrobial granule components, iron handling, and pattern recognition receptor signalling in response to bacterial pathogens.

NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; supports metabolic activation and sustained inflammatory responses in activated monocytes
CSTA: Cystatin A; protease inhibitor maintaining intracellular proteostasis during antimicrobial activation

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression enriched in Early GMP cells, indicating active protein synthesis required for progenitor maintenance and proliferative capacity. The dominance of 40S and 60S subunit components (RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and metabolic cofactors (GAPDH, LDHB) suggests a cell state optimized for biosynthetic demands rather than lineage-specific differentiation.

RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—basal protein synthesis machinery
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor—committed to active mRNA translation
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating centrosome duplication and cell proliferation—indicator of progenitor proliferative state
GAPDH, LDHB: glycolytic and anaerobic metabolism—metabolic support for high biosynthetic demand
HNRNPA1, HSP90AB1: RNA/protein handling—quality control for rapidly synthesized proteins

Use polysome profiling to demonstrate elevated active translation in Early GMP vs. differentiated stages. Compare MPO, CSF1R, and CEBPE expression to confirm these cells lack monocytic lineage markers—signature reflects progenitor metabolic state, not mono-commitment.

programme_name: Early GMP protein synthesis translation machinery
functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive ribosomal biogenesis and active protein translation machinery, predominantly expressed in Early GMP progenitors. The enrichment of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS, RPL families), translation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar organizing factors (NPM1) indicates heightened anabolic capacity required for rapid cell cycle progression and proliferation in early myeloid progenitors prior to lineage commitment.

RPS2, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit components, essential for active translation

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation factor expression in Early GMP cells, indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity during early myeloid progenitor expansion. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS24, RPS2, RPS23, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and nucleolar chaperones (NPM1, HSP90AB1) suggests active biosynthetic programming consistent with proliferative early GMP metabolism.

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting active protein synthesis
NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone and centrosome duplication regulator active in proliferating progenitors
HSP90AB1: Heat shock chaperone supporting protein folding during high biosynthetic demand
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing in metabolically active cells

programme_name: Monocyte antimicrobial maturation and metabolic readiness
functional_description: This signature reflects antimicrobial effector protein synthesis and oxidative stress management in committed monocyte progenitors transitioning toward functional maturity. The dominance of LYZ, S100A8/A9, and RNASE2 indicates robust innate immune programme activation, while concurrent expression of metabolic cofactors (GPX1, GSTP1, mitochondrial enzymes) and ribosomal proteins supports heightened protein synthesis capacity required for monocyte differentiation and antimicrobial secretory function.

S100A8/S100A9: calprotectin complex, hallmark of monocyte antimicrobial armoury and myeloid maturation
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease, augments innate immunity in differentiated myeloid cells
GPX1 + GSTP1: detoxification and antioxidant machinery protecting against oxidative stress during metabolic escalation

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis capacity and translational activity, characteristic of Early GMP progenitors with elevated anabolic demand. The enrichment of ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and RNA-binding proteins indicates active biomass accumulation and cellular growth during myeloid progenitor expansion. This metabolic state supports rapid proliferation and differentiation commitment within the GMP compartment.

H3F3A: Histone variant regulating chromatin dynamics in actively proliferating cells

Compare ribosomal RNA content and protein synthesis rates between Early GMP vs differentiated CD14+ monocytes. RNA-seq confirmation of coordinated upregulation of RPL/RPS genes in sorted Early GMP relative to ProMono and mature monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects early-to-intermediate ProMono progenitors undergoing metabolic reorganization and cytoskeletal remodeling to support monocyte commitment. The enrichment of mitochondrial OXPHOS genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH), ribosomal proteins (RPS26, RPS24), and actin dynamics machinery (TMSB4X) indicates heightened energy demand and protein synthesis capacity during lineage commitment, coupled with the emergence of monocyte identity markers (LYZ).

TMSB4X: Actin-binding protein supporting cytoskeletal remodeling required for myeloid differentiation and migration
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH: Mitochondrial respiratory chain components indicating increased OXPHOS metabolism for anabolic demands of commitment
RPS26, RPS24, PPIA: Ribosomal and translation factors supporting high protein synthesis during differentiation

functional_description: This signature captures the activated inflammatory monocyte state characterized by robust antimicrobial pattern recognition, oxidative stress handling, and metabolic reprogramming. The programme is dominated by damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) sensors, calcium-binding alarmin proteins, and iron/redox homeostasis machinery, reflecting the heightened state of CD14+ classical monocytes primed for pathogen encounter and tissue inflammation.

FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor; mannose-binding lectin pathway; recognizes bacterial ligands and apoptotic cells
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor (Dectin-1); fungal PAMP recognition; partners with TYROBP for signaling
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage and ROS buffering; elevated in activated myeloid cells under oxidative stress
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase; antioxidant defense; counteracts ROS generated during NADPH oxidase activation
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; energetic support for inflammatory macromolecule synthesis and sustained signaling

functional_description: This signature reflects a monocyte state characterized by active MHC class II antigen presentation machinery and cytoskeletal remodeling, coupled with intracellular iron storage and protease inhibition. The enrichment in HLA genes (CD74, HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1) alongside actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1) and iron metabolism (FTH1) suggests activated monocytes engaged in antigen presentation rather than acute inflammatory responses.

TMSB4X: Actin sequestration and cytoskeletal dynamics required for antigen presentation and cellular migration
FTH1: Iron storage protein reflecting cellular metabolic stability and oxidative stress buffering in activated monocytes

PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lysosomal function and antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DR/CD74 expression on CD14+ monocytes; correlate with activation markers (CD40, CD80) and functional assays of antigen presentation capacity (T cell stimulation assays). Distinguish from CD16 monocytes which typically show lower HLA-DR. Compare RNAseq profiles to LPS-activated vs resting monocyte states to confirm antigen presentation vs acute inflammatory context.

functional_description: This signature captures a shared interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) programme active in both CD14 and CD16 monocytes, characterized by antiviral effector proteins (IFITM3, ISG15, IFI6, IFI44L), lysosomal hydrolases (CTSS, PSAP), and iron/redox homeostasis machinery. The balanced activation across monocyte subsets (50.5% CD14, 49.5% CD16) indicates a cell-intrinsic IFN-responsive state rather than subset-specific inflammatory programming.

TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor coupling Fc and TLR receptors to downstream signaling

FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain component of activating immune receptors
AIF1: calcium-binding protein induced by IFN and cytokines supporting macrophage activation

PSAP: lysosomal saposin precursor supporting lipid antigen presentation
suggested_validation: Validate IFN-β/IFN-γ stimulation dependency via qPCR time-course; confirm IFITM3 and ISG15 induction across both monocyte subsets with flow cytometry; assess whether signature marks activated/recently recruited monocytes versus resting bone marrow pool; consider cross-referencing with bulk RNA-seq datasets of LPS or viral PAMP-stimulated monocytes.

programme_name: Monocyte Cytoskeletal Remodeling and Lysosomal Function
functional_description: This signature reflects active cytoskeletal dynamics and lysosomal proteolytic capacity in classical monocytes, driven by actin-binding proteins and cysteine proteases. The high representation of hemoglobin genes and iron metabolism markers suggests either recent phagocytosis of RBCs or contamination from erythroid precursors, while the strong TYROBP and FCER1G signal indicates preserved ITAM-mediated signaling capacity for immune activation.

CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease for antigen processing and intracellular pathogen degradation
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor balancing CTSS activity in proteolytic environment

FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron storage after RBC phagocytosis or iron handling
PSAP: Saposin precursor for lysosomal lipid degradation and pathogen killing

Confirm TYROBP and FCER1G co-expression with CD14, CD64, and inflammatory mediators (TNF, IL1B) via flow cytometry or immunofluorescence to confirm classical monocyte identity. programme_name: CD14 Mono antimicrobial maturation and iron homeostasis
functional_description: This signature reflects a mature CD14 monocyte programme centered on antimicrobial effector functions, lysosomal proteolysis, and iron metabolism. The dominant features are bactericidal lysozyme (LYZ), ITAM-signaling via TYROBP for phagocytic activation, and ferritin-mediated iron storage (FTH1) to restrict pathogenic iron availability and manage ROS-induced oxidative stress.

TYROBP: ITAM-signaling adaptor coupling phagocytic receptors (FCGR1A) to downstream activation
FTH1: Iron sequestration limiting bacterial siderophore scavenging and oxidative stress buffering
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease mediating antigen processing and bacterial protein degradation
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase protecting against H2O2 generated during respiratory burst
HLA-DRA/DMA/DQB1: MHC class II antigen presentation machinery, consistent with activated monocyte phenotype

functional_description: This signature defines mature CD14+ classical monocytes characterized by constitutive expression of S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A6) and myeloid lineage markers. The programme reflects terminal myeloid differentiation with enhanced inflammatory alert status and PAMP-sensing capacity, rather than acute TLR-driven inflammation.

S100A8: S100 calprotectin heterodimer partner; marks mature myeloid compartment
S100A12: Extended S100 family member; reinforces myeloid maturation signature
CD14: Co-receptor for TLR4/LPS; defines classical monocyte identity; PAMP recognition
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor; couples pattern-recognition receptors to intracellular signalling in myeloid cells

RNA-FISH to confirm co-localization of S100A8/A9/A12 in CD14+ classical monocyte subset. Functional assay: LPS-stimulated S100A9 secretion and cytokine response (TNF/IL6) to confirm inflammatory competence of this differentiation state.

functional_description: This signature captures actively cycling GMP cells (GMP-Cycle 43.5%, Early GMP 42%) undergoing intense protein synthesis and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to support rapid proliferation. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17) and respiratory chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, NDUFS5, UQCRH) indicates heightened biosynthetic demand coupled with energy production for cell division. Concurrent MPO and PRSS57 expression reflects early myeloid lineage priming during the GMP stage.

MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, NDUFS5, UQCRH: complex I and IV components showing elevated mitochondrial OXPHOS for ATP production in proliferative cells

PRSS57: serine protease for azurophil granule biogenesis, early myeloid differentiation marker

HSPB1: stress response chaperone for proteostasis during high-rate protein synthesis

functional_description: This signature reflects a monocyte programme dominated by MHC class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQA1, CD74) coupled with iron storage and oxidative stress management (FTH1). The balanced CD14/CD16 composition (47.5%/41.0%) and presence of SPI1 indicate differentiation toward antigen-presenting monocytes with heightened immunological surveillance capacity.

FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage and ROS buffering in activated monocytes

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened translational machinery activity and oxidative stress management in GMP-Mono and early ProMono cells during monocytic commitment. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPLP0), translation factors (PPIA), and cytoprotective enzymes (GSTP1, GPX1) indicates active protein synthesis coupled with antioxidant priming characteristic of early monocyte differentiation.

GSTP1, GPX1: Antioxidant detoxification enzymes reflecting metabolic remodelling and ROS management during early myeloid differentiation
PTMA, HMGN1: Nuclear/chromatin regulators supporting transcriptionally active chromatin remodelling during lineage priming
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein supporting cytoskeletal remodelling and migration capacity in committed progenitors
GAPDH, PPIA: Metabolic and protein folding support for translational surge
suggested_validation: Validate by quantifying ribosome biogenesis markers (RPL genes, RRP1B) and measuring translation rates via puromycin incorporation or polysome profiling in sorted GMP-Mono vs. Late ProMono vs. CD14+ monocytes. Confirm MPO protein levels distinguish this from mature monocyte populations. Co-stain GSTP1/GPX1 activity with CD34/CD64 to map metabolic transition during monocytic commitment.

functional_description: This signature represents active protein synthesis machinery in early GMP-stage progenitors, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS, RPL families) and translation factors (EEF1B2). The enrichment reflects high metabolic and biosynthetic demand during early myeloid progenitor expansion, consistent with the 73% Early GMP composition and 16.5% cycling GMP cells.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Structural ribosomal protein components enabling global protein synthesis
RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit protein, fundamental translation machinery
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, rate-limiting for protein synthesis
NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone and proliferation co-factor, marks actively cycling progenitors
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing and translation regulation
HSP90AB1: Heat shock protein supporting protein folding under high biosynthetic stress
MT-CO2: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation component, energetic support for translation
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase supporting glycolytic energy generation
suggested_validation: Confirm translational activity via polysome profiling or puromycin incorporation assays in Early GMP vs mature monocyte populations. Validate NPM1 and HSP90AB1 as co-markers of biosynthetic stress. Compare ribosomal protein expression between GMP-Cycle and non-cycling Early GMP to discriminate proliferation-linked versus baseline synthesis programs.

functional_description: This signature reflects active mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and protein synthesis in GMP-stage progenitors transitioning toward monocyte lineage commitment. The predominance of respiratory chain complexes I and IV subunits (MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) indicates elevated metabolic demand characteristic of proliferating and differentiating myeloid progenitors, coupled with ribosomal proteins and chaperones supporting protein synthesis during lineage priming.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, UQCRH: Complex I and IV respiratory chain components indicating heightened OXPHOS in metabolically active GMP-Mono and GMP-Cycle populations (67.5% of activating cells)
MPO: Myeloperoxidase present but not dominant, consistent with GMP priming before peak protease expression in mature monocytes
