RPL37A, RPS24: Ribosomal proteins supporting robust protein synthesis during progenitor proliferation and differentiation
HSP90B1, PPIA: Molecular chaperones facilitating protein folding during lineage commitment transitions
STMN1, PTMA, HMGB1, HMGN1, H2AFZ: Cell cycle regulators and chromatin modulators supporting proliferation in GMP-Cycle (23.0%) and Early GMP (23.0%)
Early ProMono enrichment (15.5%) with modest CD14 Mono (3.0%) indicates signature captures GMP→ProMono transition, not mature monocyte state
suggested_validation: Validate via metabolic flux analysis (seahorse OXPHOS assay) on sorted GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono populations; confirm MPO/CD14 expression levels to verify progenitor stage and exclude mature monocyte contamination; single-cell metabolic profiling (scNMT-seq or similar) to link mtDNA-encoded OXPHOS genes with monocyte lineage commitment markers (CSF1R, IRF8).

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis machinery and oxidative phosphorylation capacity in early GMP-stage progenitors (98.5% composition). The enrichment of ribosomal proteins, translation factors, and mitochondrial electron transport components indicates heightened metabolic activity and biosynthetic demand consistent with proliferating myeloid progenitors preparing for differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins, enabling robust protein synthesis in proliferating GMPs
RPLP0: ribosomal P protein essential for ribosome function and translation efficiency
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor and guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery
UQCRH, MT-CO2: mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicating high oxidative phosphorylation capacity
TXN: redox homeostasis protein supporting metabolic stress management in proliferative progenitors
GSTP1: detoxification enzyme managing reactive oxygen species from elevated mitochondrial activity
PTMA: anti-apoptotic function protecting metabolically active progenitors during expansion
HMGN1: chromatin accessibility factor enabling transcription of metabolic genes
LDHB: lactate dehydrogenase supporting glycolytic-to-oxidative metabolic flexibility
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring MitoTracker/TMRM intensity and EdU incorporation in Early GMP vs GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono subsets. Confirm RPS protein expression correlates with CD34+KIT+ progenitor phenotype and validate diminished signature in ProMono (CSF1R+CD64+ committed cells) where translation demand declines prior to terminal differentiation.

functional_description: This signature represents the core antimicrobial effector module of classical CD14+ monocytes, centered on S100 calprotectin heterodimers (S100A8/A9), bactericidal lysozyme, and lysosomal proteases. The program reflects pre-loaded cytoplasmic granules for rapid bacterial killing and inflammatory DAMP/PAMP signaling through TYROBP-coupled Fc receptors.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin heterodimerization (S100A8/A9) - major antimicrobial and inflammatory alarmin in CD14 monocyte granules
S100A8: Calprotectin partner; neutrophil/monocyte co-expression marker of inflammatory activation
LYZ: Lysozyme; canonical bactericidal enzyme in monocyte granules for peptidoglycan degradation
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor for bacterial ligands; promotes opsonization
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor; ITAM-mediated signaling via FCGR1A (CD64) and TLRs in classical monocytes
CD14: Surface LPS/LBP co-receptor; defines classical monocyte phenotype; PAMP sensing
CTSS: Cathepsin S; lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and bacterial degradation
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain; ITAM-containing component of FCGR1A signaling axis
VCAN: Versican; ECM modulation associated with monocyte migration and tissue infiltration
S100A4, S100A6, S100A11, S100A12: S100 family cluster; calcium-binding alarmins and migration factors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming S100A8/A9 co-expression in CD14++CD64+ gate; immunofluorescence co-localization of S100A9 and CTSS in cytoplasmic granules; RNA-scope validation on bone marrow monocyte subsets; functional assay of bactericidal activity (S. aureus/E. coli killing) correlating with S100A9 expression level.

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis machinery in Early GMP progenitors (81% composition), characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). The enrichment of glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, ENO1, LDHB) alongside ribosomal components indicates metabolic coupling to support sustained biosynthesis during active progenitor proliferation, consistent with the GMP-Cycle subset (15.5%).
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0: core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components, essential for mRNA translation
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, rate-limiting for translation elongation
GAPDH, ENO1, LDHB: glycolytic enzymes indicating elevated metabolic flux to support ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis
NPM1: nucleolar protein and translation regulator involved in ribosome assembly and cell proliferation
YBX1: cold shock domain protein with roles in translation initiation and mRNA stability
PTMA: nucleolar/cytoplasmic shuttle protein supporting ribosome biogenesis
Early GMP dominance (81%): progenitors require elevated translation for lineage priming and proliferative expansion
suggested_validation: Measure global translation rates via puromycin incorporation or OP-puro labeling in Early GMP vs. mature monocytes. Perform ribosomal profiling (Ribo-seq) to confirm active translation of GMP identity factors (CEBPA, SPI1, MYB). Assess ribosome abundance by flow cytometry (anti-RPS6 phosphorylation) and validate EEF1B2 dependency via genetic knockdown.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened oxidative phosphorylation capacity and active cell cycle progression in Early ProMono cells. The dominance of mitochondrial electron transport chain genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5) coupled with proliferation markers (STMN1, PCLAF, NUCKS1, HMGB2) indicates energetic demand during committed monocyte progenitor expansion prior to terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: MT-CO2: Complex IV assembly component; enriched in metabolically active Early ProMono
MT-ND1: Complex I NADH oxidoreductase; mitochondrial respiratory chain engagement
MT-CO3: Electron transfer and Complex IV assembly; respiratory capacity indicator
MT-ND5: Complex I assembly; sustained NADH utilization for ATP generation
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator; active in G2/M phase proliferation
PCLAF: PCNA-associated factor; centrosome cycling and DNA synthesis
HMGB2: Chromatin-associated protein; cell cycle-regulated transcription factor
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease; monocyte granule component emerging in commitment
MPO: Present but lower tier; progenitors retain some neutrophil capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry measuring MitoTracker intensity and Ki-67 co-expression in CSF1R+MS4A3+KLF4+ Early ProMono; correlate mtDNA copy number with ProMono progression; assess OCR/ECAR ratios to confirm bioenergetic switch vs. CD14 Mono quiescence.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened lysosomal protease activity and iron metabolism in classical monocytes, supporting intracellular pathogen degradation and antigen processing. The dominance of cysteine proteases (CTSS, CSTA) and ferritin (FTH1) indicates active phagolysosomal function coupled with iron sequestration to limit pathogen growth, characteristic of CD14+ monocyte antimicrobial effector responses.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine proteinase essential for antigen presentation and intracellular pathogen degradation
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain critical for iron sequestration as antimicrobial strategy against iron-dependent pathogens
CSTA: cysteine protease inhibitor supporting proteolytic balance in lysosomal compartments
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor linking C-type lectin recognition (CLEC7A, CLEC4A) to downstream signalling
CLEC7A: Dectin-1 fungal/β-glucan pattern recognition receptor on classical monocytes
NCF2: NADPH oxidase component supporting ROS-mediated microbicidal activity
TMSB4X: actin remodelling supporting phagolysosomal maturation and cytoskeletal dynamics
LGALS2: galectin-2 lectin involved in pattern recognition and immune regulation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: sort CD14+ monocytes and measure CTSS/cathepsin S activity by flow (DQ-gelatin assay), iron content (calcein fluorescence), and ROS production (DHE/DCFDA). Validate CLEC7A surface expression and functional response to fungal β-glucans (zymosan stimulation). Assess lysosomal morphology and maturation by confocal microscopy (LAMP1/CTSS co-localisation).

functional_description: This signature represents elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery activity in early GMP and GMP-Mono populations, indicating heightened anabolic demand during early monocytic commitment. The dominance of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0) combined with translation factors (PPIA, EEF1B2) and nucleosome remodelling activity (HMGN1) reflects active chromatin accessibility and protein synthesis required for lineage priming rather than terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0: Coordinated ribosomal biogenesis signature characteristic of anabolic progenitor state
PPIA, EEF1B2: Translation elongation machinery supporting active protein synthesis during commitment
HMGN1: Open chromatin association consistent with transcriptionally active early GMP stage
GSTP1: Oxidative stress detoxification reflecting metabolic demands of actively differentiating progenitors
PTMA: DNA-binding co-factor with anti-apoptotic function supporting progenitor survival during transition
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation supporting energy demands of early monocytic priming
Cell composition (50.5% GMP-Mono, 36.5% Early GMP): Signature enriched in early committed stage before MPO downregulation
suggested_validation: Validate through dual RNA-FISH for ribosomal proteins (RPL37A/RPS24) with IRF8/CSF1R to confirm co-expression in GMP-Mono; quantify polysome association in sorted GMP-Mono vs ProMono; measure protein synthesis rates via puromycin incorporation; assess whether signature precedes CSF1R upregulation and MPO downregulation in pseudotime trajectory.

programme_name: Early GMP ribosomal and translational capacity
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery activity in Early GMP progenitors, indicating high biosynthetic demand during early myeloid progenitor expansion. The dominance of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS24, RPS23, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) coupled with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and glycolytic/metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, LDHB) suggests active protein synthesis and energy metabolism required for GMP proliferation and differentiation priming.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPS26: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins - core translational machinery
RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins - ribosomal structural components
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor - active protein synthesis capacity
NPM1: nucleolar chaperone and proliferation regulator - consistent with actively cycling Early GMP
GAPDH, LDHB: glycolytic/metabolic enzymes - energy production for biosynthesis
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein - mRNA processing in proliferating progenitors
UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport - metabolic support for protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining of CD34+KIT+ Early GMP with puromycin incorporation assay or active protein synthesis reporters; confirm ribosomal biogenesis via NPM1 localization and MKI67 co-expression in Early GMP vs. GMP-Mono to demonstrate functional translation activity correlates with progenitor immaturity rather than lineage commitment.

programme_name: Early GMP translational capacity protein synthesis
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A, EEF1B2) and oxidative metabolism (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH, LDHB) in early GMP progenitors, supporting active protein synthesis during progenitor proliferation. The inclusion of MPO and PRSS57 indicates priming toward myeloid differentiation with azurophil granule preparation, characteristic of early-to-mid GMP stage before lineage commitment deepens.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A: coordinate ribosomal protein upregulation indicating high translational demand in proliferating early GMP
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis capacity
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complex proteins reflecting energetic demands of progenitor expansion
LDHB: anaerobic metabolism support consistent with GMP metabolic flexibility
MPO: early myeloid lineage marker expressed broadly in GMP before monocyte/neutrophil divergence
PRSS57: serine protease with azurophil granule localization, indicating primary granule maturation in GMP
59% Early GMP composition: dominant activating population reflects pre-cycling progenitor state
31.5% GMP-Cycle: secondary enrichment confirms association with proliferative GMP pools
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining of CD34+KIT+ early GMP with RPS24/RPL37A protein levels and MPO expression; confirm that signature is absent in GMP-Mono/ProMono (where MPO declines and CSF1R/CD64 dominate); assess temporal dynamics across sorted GMP substages to confirm association with early rather than late GMP

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive translational capacity driven by ribosomal protein (RPS/RPL) and translation elongation factor expression. The dominance of Early GMP cells (72.5%) with supporting energetic (LDHB, GAPDH) and nucleolar (NPM1) machinery indicates active biosynthetic demands during early myeloid progenitor expansion prior to lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components; consistent high expression required for sustained protein synthesis in proliferative progenitor stages
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity; supports continuous mRNA translation during active cell cycle progression
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating ribosome biogenesis and centrosome duplication; marker of biosynthetic competency in proliferating cells
LDHB, GAPDH: Glycolytic enzymes supporting energetic demands of active translation and rapid cell division
HNRNPA1, HMGN1: RNA-binding protein and chromatin-associated protein; coordinate with open chromatin state required for transcription-coupled translation
HSP90AB1: Heat shock chaperone facilitating protein folding during high-throughput synthesis
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) co-staining Early GMP/GMP-Mono populations for surface CD34/KIT with ribosomal protein immunofluorescence to confirm progenitor-stage expression; (2) assess polysome abundance by fractionation in sorted Early GMP vs mature monocytes; (3) confirm inverse correlation with MPO/ELANE expression to exclude mature granulocytic stages where ribosomal protein synthesis declines.

programme_name: Early ProMono antimicrobial and chromatin remodeling
functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor commitment characterized by activation of antimicrobial effector genes (LYZ, RNASE2) and chromatin remodeling machinery (HMGN1, HMGN2), coupled with cytoskeletal reorganization and stress response pathways supporting progenitor maturation. The dominant Early ProMono composition (58%) with modest Late ProMono (23%) indicates this programme captures the initial phase of monocytic differentiation prior to full surface marker acquisition.
key_evidence: LYZ: Canonical monocyte antimicrobial enzyme, hallmark of mono commitment; lysozyme production marks progression beyond GMP
HMGN2, HMGN1: Chromatin accessibility factors enabling transcriptional reprogramming during ProMono differentiation
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease supporting mono-lineage innate immunity programme
CSTA: Cystatin inhibitor enabling controlled protease activity during mono maturation
TMSB4X: Actin-binding protein facilitating cytoskeletal remodeling for migration/egress competency
HSP90B1: Molecular chaperone supporting protein folding during rapid proteomic remodeling in Early ProMono
ANXA2, PTMA: Calcium-responsive and apoptosis-regulatory proteins supporting progenitor survival during commitment
ENO1, GAPDH: Glycolytic enzymes reflecting metabolic activation of differentiating ProMono cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: LYZ expression with MS4A3 and CSF1R in Early ProMono; quantify MPO/ELANE loss vs LYZ gain; single-cell RNA-seq trajectory analysis from GMP→Early ProMono→Late ProMono validating programme onset timing; ATAC-seq on sorted Early ProMono to confirm HMGN-associated chromatin opening.

functional_description: This signature reflects post-commitment monocyte progenitor differentiation characterized by upregulation of innate immune effector proteins and calcium-binding damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). The programme encompasses bacterial peptidoglycan degradation (LYZ), antimicrobial ribonucleases (RNASE2), and S100 calprotectin components (S100A8/A9) that mediate inflammatory responses and pathogen killing, consistent with late ProMono/early CD14 monocyte maturation prior to tissue extravasation.
key_evidence: LYZ: lysozyme antimicrobial enzyme and canonical monocyte marker; high in Late ProMono and CD14 Mono
S100A8/S100A9: calprotectin heterodimer; DAMP/alarm signals upregulated during mono differentiation and inflammatory priming
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease; myeloid-restricted expression coinciding with effector function acquisition
CSTA/cystatin: cysteine protease inhibitor; balances cathepsin activity (CTSS/CTSL) during lysosomal maturation
MNDA: myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen; granulocyte-monocyte lineage marker reflecting terminal commitment
S100A4/S100A6: S100 family members; calcium signalling and migration priming in differentiating monocytes
ANXA2/VCAN/GRN: extracellular matrix proteins and secreted factors; pre-egress remodelling signatures
PKM/GAPDH/MT-CO3: metabolic reprogramming; shift toward glycolytic/OXPHOS balance characteristic of activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of LYZ, S100A8/A9, and MNDA with ProMono markers (MS4A3, CD34-/CD13+/CD33+) and CD14 onset to confirm Late ProMono enrichment; single-molecule FISH for LYZ/RNASE2 to validate antimicrobial programme heterogeneity within Early vs Late ProMono; functional assay of antimicrobial capacity (bacterial killing, DAMP secretion) in sorted populations.

functional_description: This signature captures the activated state of classical CD14+ monocytes characterized by enhanced antimicrobial granule proteins (S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex), calcium-responsive damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), and oxidative stress response machinery. The predominance of S100 family members and innate immune effectors indicates cells primed for rapid pro-inflammatory response, bacterial sensing, and tissue infiltration.
key_evidence: S100A9: Core component of calprotectin (S100A8/A9 heterodimer), classic DAMP and marker of activated CD14 monocytes; directly linked to inflammatory amplification and bacterial killing
S100A8: Partner protein in calprotectin; critical for monocyte antimicrobial function and recruitment to inflammatory sites
FCN1: Ficolin-1 is a pattern recognition receptor involved in innate immune activation and complement-like pathway triggering; elevated in classical monocytes
S100A12: S100 family member involved in calcium signaling and innate immune activation; secreted DAMP
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor protein essential for immunoreceptor signaling (ITAM-bearing); couples microbial sensing to downstream inflammatory cascades
GRN: Granulin precursor involved in inflammatory regulation and tissue remodeling; secreted by activated monocytes
GPX1: Antioxidant enzyme protecting against ROS generated during oxidative burst; indicates metabolic priming for respiratory burst
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan associated with inflammatory microenvironment and monocyte-endothelial interactions
S100A4: S100 family member involved in cell motility and inflammatory responses
CSTA: Cystatin A protease inhibitor; regulates proteolytic environment in activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate S100A8/A9 protein co-expression via flow cytometry on CD14++CD16- population; confirm calprotectin secretion in LPS-stimulated cultures; assess correlation with CCR2+CX3CR1- phenotype and transcriptional dependency on SPI1/IRF5 via ATAC-seq

programme_name: Early GMP Translation and Metabolic Priming
functional_description: This signature reflects early GMP progenitor cells (89% Early GMP) with robust protein synthesis capacity and metabolic support infrastructure. The dominant ribosomal and translation machinery genes (RPS2, RPS23, RPLP0, RPS24, RPS17, RPL4, EEF1B2) indicate high translational demand characteristic of rapidly proliferating progenitors preparing for myeloid differentiation. Supporting metabolic genes (LDHB, MT-CO2, TXN) and RNA processing factors (HNRNPA1, SNRPE, NPM1, YBX1) enable the biosynthetic capacity required for early lineage priming before overt GMP-Mono commitment.
key_evidence: RPS2/RPS23/RPS24/RPS17/RPL4: Ribosomal proteins indicating high protein synthesis rate in proliferative Early GMP
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting active mRNA translation during progenitor expansion
NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone involved in centrosome duplication and cell proliferation, consistent with GMP cycling
HNRNPA1/YBX1/SNRPE: RNA-binding proteins regulating pre-mRNA processing and splicing in transcriptionally active progenitors
LDHB/MT-CO2: Glycolytic and mitochondrial metabolism supporting energy demands of early myeloid differentiation
TXN: Redox regulation maintaining biosynthetic milieu in proliferating progenitors
89% Early GMP composition: Signature predominantly from undifferentiated GMP stage before GMP-Mono lineage restriction
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal/translation programme expression across Early GMP vs GMP-Mono vs mature monocyte populations; validate with polysome profiling or ribosome occupancy assays (Ribo-seq) to confirm translational activity; interrogate whether this signature precedes or accompanies expression of lineage commitment factors (IRF8, CEBPE, CSF1R) in time-course experiments.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated translational machinery components (40S and 60S ribosomal subunits, elongation factors) and metabolic proteins (GAPDH, mitochondrial oxidoreductases) characteristic of metabolically active, protein synthesis-engaged Early GMP cells. The dominance of ribosomal proteins and translation factors indicates heightened biosynthetic demand consistent with progenitor proliferation and cytoplasmic expansion during monocytic priming.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPS2: 40S ribosomal subunit components—hallmark of translation-intensive progenitors
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—complete ribosomal assembly signature
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity—active protein synthesis execution
NPM1: Nucleolar/cytoplasmic shuttling protein regulating ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme; moonlighting function in transcription/stress—metabolic support for biosynthesis
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic nucleolar protein; supports cell survival during progenitor proliferation
MT-CO3, UQCRH: Mitochondrial OXPHOS components—energy provision for biosynthetic burden
Early GMP dominance (77%): Consistent with GMP-stage elevation in ribosomal biogenesis prior to lineage commitment
suggested_validation: Validate by measuring translation rates (puromycin incorporation) and ribosome content (gradient centrifugation or qRT-PCR of RPS/RPL panels) in sorted Early GMP vs mature monocytes. Confirm via flow cytometry using anti-RPL4 or nucleolar protein markers (NPM1) to stratify GMP subsets by biosynthetic demand.

functional_description: This signature captures the core antimicrobial and lysosomal degradation programme of classical CD14+ monocytes, centred on proteolytic processing, bacterial peptidoglycan sensing, and iron homoeostasis. The dominant genes encode cysteine proteases (CTSS), pattern recognition receptors (CLEC7A, CLEC4E, CLEC4A, FCN1), and the bacterial cell wall-targeting enzyme lysozyme (LYZ), reflecting enhanced capacity for antigen presentation and direct bacterial killing.
key_evidence: CD14: Surface antigen defining classical monocytes; mediates PAMP recognition and innate immunity
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and peptide presentation
LYZ: Lysozyme—direct bactericidal activity against gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens
FCN1: Ficolin—soluble PAMP recognition molecule and complement pathway activator
CLEC7A/CLEC4E/CLEC4A: C-type lectin receptors for fungal and bacterial PAMPs
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor enabling signalling through FcγR and CLRs
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain—iron sequestration to limit bacterial siderophore scavenging
LGALS2: Galectin-2—pattern recognition and lymphotoxin-α binding in inflammation
RGS2: Negative feedback regulator of GPCR signalling; restrains chemokine responsiveness
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis supporting metabolic demands of activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD14, CTSS, and CD64 (FCGR1A) on CD14 Mono subset; quantify CTSS activity ex vivo following TLR4/TLR2 stimulation (LPS/Pam3CSK4); measure LYZ secretion and bactericidal activity in Staphylococcus aureus killing assays; confirm iron homoeostasis via Prussian blue staining and ferritin quantification.

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and innate activation
functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression and mitochondrial bioenergetics in Early ProMono progenitors, coupled with innate immune effector functions. The dominance of Early ProMono cells (86%) with concurrent expression of proliferation markers, chromatin remodelers, and antimicrobial proteins indicates a proliferative progenitor pool poised for monocytic differentiation while maintaining metabolic activity.
key_evidence: PCNA: canonical S-phase marker; direct evidence of active DNA synthesis in Early ProMono
TYMS: thymidylate synthase for dTMP synthesis; confirms robust cell cycle progression
PCLAF: chromatin-associated factor; involved in centrosome function and cell cycle regulation
HMGB1/HMGB2: non-histone chromatin proteins; elevated in proliferating progenitors
STMN1: intracellular relay integrating regulatory signals; marks activated, cycling cells
TUBB/TUBA1B: microtubule components; required for mitotic spindle assembly
MT-CO2/MT-CO3/MT-ND5: OXPHOS complex components; energetic support for rapid proliferation
LYZ: lysozyme expression; monocytic lineage commitment marker and antimicrobial effector
RNASE2: ribonuclease; antimicrobial activity consistent with early innate immune differentiation
S100A8: calcium-binding alarmin; myeloid lineage marker, innate immune activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying Ki67+ (PCNA+ proxy) in MS4A3+/KLF4+ Early ProMono to confirm proliferative state; single-cell RNA-seq trajectory analysis comparing Early vs Late ProMono cell cycle phase distribution; metabolic stress test to validate OXPHOS dependency; immunohistochemistry for LYZ/S100A8 co-expression in bone marrow ProMono zones

functional_description: This signature captures the lysosomal protease and innate immune machinery of monocytes, dominated by cathepsin S (CTSS) and adaptor proteins (TYROBP, FCER1G) that couple pattern recognition to intracellular degradation pathways. The co-expression of calcium-binding proteins (S100A11, S100A4, AIF1) and interferon-induced antiviral factors (IFITM3, IFI6) reflects heightened antimicrobial and intracellular pathogen-handling capacity characteristic of activated CD14 monocytes.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and degradation in activated monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor linking Fc receptors and pattern recognition to downstream signalling
FCER1G: FcγR γ-chain component enabling Fc-mediated phagocytosis and ADCP
AIF1: calcium-binding protein upregulated by IFNγ/TNF in activated macrophages and monocytes
S100A11, S100A4: calcium-signalling intermediates associated with monocyte activation and migration
IFITM3, IFI6: interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) mediating antiviral defence and pathogen restriction
PSAP: saposin precursor supporting lysosomal hydrolase function and lipid antigen processing
FCN1: ficolin lectin pathway component for complement-independent pathogen opsonisation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: co-stain CD14 vs CD16 monocytes for CTSS (intracellular), TYROBP (surface/intracellular), and S100A11 protein; qPCR on FACS-sorted CD14 vs CD16 monocytes ± LPS stimulation to confirm inflammatory priming; immunofluorescence to localise CTSS and S100A4 to lysosomal/phagosomal compartments.

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and antimicrobial maturation
functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor commitment characterized by active proliferation (MKI67, PCLAF, STMN1, HMGB2) coupled with initiation of monocyte-specific antimicrobial programmes (LYZ, RNASE2, RETN). The high representation of Early ProMono cells (76.5%) and elevated mitochondrial genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3) indicate metabolic upregulation supporting differentiation downstream of GMP while retaining proliferative capacity.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte lysozyme production, marker of mono commitment
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease specific to monocyte lineage
MKI67: cell cycle activity consistent with Early ProMono (pre-exit proliferation)
HMGB2, HMGN2: open chromatin architecture supporting differentiation gene expression
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: mitochondrial oxidative metabolism upregulation in committed progenitors
RETN: resistin production associated with activated monocyte progenitors
PCLAF, STMN1: microtubule dynamics and centrosome activity in cycling cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of Early ProMono (MS4A3+KLF4+) with LYZ, RNASE2, and Ki67 to confirm proliferative antimicrobial programme; RNAScope for spatial LYZ/RNASE2 co-expression; comparison with CD14 Mono (which should be LYZ+ but MKI67-low) and GMP-Mono (which should retain MPO/ELANE)

functional_description: This signature reflects monocytic commitment within the GMP-Mono population, characterized by active myeloperoxidase-dependent innate immunity priming (MPO, PRTN3, AZU1, ELANE) alongside enhanced mitochondrial oxidative metabolism (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND5) supporting differentiation energy demands. Elevated stress-response chaperones (HSP90B1, HSPB1), chromatin remodeling factors (HMGB1, HMGN1, H2AFZ), and anti-apoptotic signals (PTMA) indicate active transcriptional reprogramming during monocytic lineage commitment from bipotent GMP precursors.
key_evidence: MPO: Master myeloid enzyme marking early commitment in GMP-Mono (55.5% composition); retained in monocytic trajectory
ELANE: Neutrophil elastase co-expression with MPO indicates dual priming capacity of GMP-stage cells before lineage commitment
PRTN3, AZU1: Azurophil granule serine proteases; GMP-Mono specific antimicrobial priming
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND5: Oxidative phosphorylation upregulation supporting metabolic transition during differentiation
HSP90B1, HSPB1: Heat shock proteins facilitating protein folding during active transcriptional remodeling
HMGB1, HMGN1, H2AFZ: Chromatin accessibility factors enabling monocyte lineage TF (SPI1/IRF8) activity
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic nucleophosmin preventing cell death during commitment stress
GMP-Cycle 30%: Cell cycle activity confirms actively differentiating early GMP-Mono compartment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry (CD14/CD34/MPO/CSF1R) or qPCR validation of IRF8 and KLF4 expression to confirm monocytic commitment; assess SPI1 chromatin accessibility via ATAC-seq to link HMGB1/HMGN1 activity to monocyte-specific enhancers.

programme_name: Monocyte antigen presentation and cytoskeletal remodeling
functional_description: This signature reflects a shared antigen-presenting and cytoskeletal remodeling programme enriched in CD16 monocytes (57%) but also present in CD14 monocytes (37.5%), driven by HLA class II molecules and actin-binding proteins. The programme supports both ADCC-capable CD16 monocyte function and classical antigen presentation, with elevated expression of actin regulators suggesting active cellular migration and morphodynamic surveillance rather than classical patrolling-specific transcription factors.
key_evidence: HLA-DPA1, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DRA, CD74: HLA class II antigen presentation machinery, consistent with both CD16 and CD14 monocyte populations
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain, critical for ADCC signalling via FCGR3A (CD16) and amplification of immune responses in CD16 monocytes
TMSB4X, AIF1, COTL1, S100A4: Actin-sequestering and calcium-binding proteins regulating cytoskeletal dynamics for active migration and patrolling
LST1: Lymphocyte proliferation inhibitor induced by LPS and IFN-γ, marker of monocyte activation and antimicrobial surveillance
S100A11, FTH1, CST3: Iron metabolism and cysteine protease inhibition supporting oxidative and proteolytic immune functions
PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lipid antigen presentation and lysosomal function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of FCER1G, S100A4, LST1 with CD16/CD14/CX3CR1 to distinguish CD16 monocyte-enriched antigen presentation from shared classical monocyte HLA class II expression; validate actin dynamics via live-cell imaging of phalloidin staining during vascular crawling assays.

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodeling and antimicrobial priming
functional_description: This signature reflects early commitment to monocyte fate, dominated by chromatin remodeling proteins (HMGB1/2, HMGN2, H2AFZ/V) that establish transcriptionally permissive states for monocyte-specific genes, coupled with innate antimicrobial effectors (S100A8/A9, LYZ, RNASE2) characteristic of ProMono differentiation. The enrichment of histone variants and chromatin architectural proteins alongside myeloid antimicrobial factors indicates active epigenetic priming of the monocyte transcriptional program in early ProMono cells.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: calcium-binding pattern recognition proteins, hallmark of early myeloid activation and ProMono commitment
HMGB1/2: nucleocytoplasmic shuttling chromatin remodelers driving transcriptional plasticity in differentiating ProMono
HMGN2: nucleosome-binding protein maintaining open chromatin at actively transcribed loci during monocyte specification
LYZ: canonical monocyte antimicrobial marker, indicates loss of neutrophil trajectory and commitment to mono fate
RNASE2: ribonuclease antimicrobial effector consistent with early ProMono innate immune priming
H2AFZ/H2AFV: histone H2A variants mediating chromatin dynamics during monocyte lineage commitment
MNDA: myeloid-restricted nuclear differentiation antigen marking monocyte lineage progression
PTTG1/UBE2C: cell cycle machinery active in proliferating Early ProMono progenitors
suggested_validation: Validate by ChIP-seq for HMGB1/HMGN2 occupancy at mono-specific loci (CSF1R, IRF8, LYZ); assess S100A8/A9 protein localization and calcium signaling; confirm cell cycle activity (PTTG1+/UBE2C+) in sort-purified Early ProMono vs Late ProMono; verify downregulation of MPO/ELANE consistent with neutrophil trajectory loss.

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis machinery and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in GMP-Mono and Early ProMono populations. The dominant ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS26, RPL37A) coupled with metabolic (UQCRH) and cytoskeletal regulators (ACTG1, TMSB4X) indicate heightened translational demand during early monocytic commitment. Presence of MPO and globin transcripts (HBA1/2, HBB) suggests GMP-stage progenitors before full monocytic specialization.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS26, RPL37A: Coordinated 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating active global translation
UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport complex component reflecting elevated oxidative energy demand in proliferating progenitors
MPO: Myeloid peroxidase present in GMP-Mono (41%) and Early ProMono (25.5%), consistent with early lineage commitment before ProMono maturation downregulates MPO
ACTG1, TMSB4X: Actin dynamics and cytoskeletal remodeling during cell migration/differentiation in committed progenitors
HBA1, HBA2, HBB: Globin expression typical of early GMP-stage cells (11% Early GMP in activating population), declines in mature monocytes
PLAC8: Chromatin-associated factor supporting active transcriptional state in proliferating progenitors
Cell composition: 66.5% GMP-Mono + Early ProMono validates progenitor-stage signature
suggested_validation: Sort on ACTG1/MPO/RPS23 co-expression combined with flow-cytometry (CD34+/CD13+/CD33+ GMP markers); confirm MPO+ RPS-high cells are predominantly CD64-low/CSF1R-intermediate (early ProMono), not CD14-high mature monocytes. Single-cell proteomics or immunofluorescence to validate ribosomal protein abundance vs. mature monocyte markers (CD14, CD16).

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis capacity in early myeloid progenitors (67.5% Early GMP), driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). The concurrent elevation of metabolic support genes (GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH) and nucleolar proteins (NPM1) indicates active biosynthetic programs characteristic of proliferating progenitors preparing for lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: Core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components—dominant signature features indicating robust translation in dividing early GMPs
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting rapid protein synthesis rates required for progenitor expansion
NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone and proliferation marker elevated in proliferative progenitor pools
GAPDH, LDHB: Glycolytic and anaerobic metabolism supporting ATP demands of actively translating, dividing cells
UQCRH: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation—energy demand of biosynthetically active progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor and transcription factor cofactor stabilizing progenitor survival during expansion
TXN: Redox homeostasis maintaining protein synthesis fidelity under high translational load
Cell composition: 67.5% Early GMP (peak translational activity phase) with minimal mature mono contamination (1%)
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) co-staining Early GMP-enriched populations (CD34+KIT+CD33+MPO-low) for ribosomal protein translation rates (puromycin-based assay); (2) comparing polysome profiles between Early GMP vs. GMP-Mono (should show increased polysome/monosome ratio in Early GMP); (3) measuring protein synthesis rates via radioactive methionine incorporation or Click-iT assays; (4) confirming inverse correlation with lineage commitment markers (IRF8, CEBPE) in sorted populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein (RPS/RPL) and translation factor expression characteristic of Early GMP and GMP-Cycle progenitors with high biosynthetic demand. The enrichment of ribosomal assembly components, translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar/chromatin-associated proteins (NPM1, HMGN1) indicates active protein synthesis required for rapid proliferation and myeloid progenitor expansion.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins driving translation capacity in proliferative GMP
RPLP0: Acidic ribosomal phosphoprotein required for ribosome stability and translation efficiency
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting rapid protein synthesis during GMP cell cycle progression
NPM1: Nucleolar protein associated with ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation in progenitors
GAPDH, LDHB: Metabolic enzymes supporting glycolytic flux needed for biosynthesis in cycling progenitors
HNRNPA1, HMGN1, PTMA: RNA-binding and chromatin-associated factors enabling coordinated translational control during myeloid progenitor expansion
79% Early GMP composition: validates progenitor state before lineage commitment; 20.5% GMP-Cycle reflects S/G2 phase demand for translation
suggested_validation: Confirm translational activity by polysome profiling or puromycin incorporation assay in sorted Early GMP/GMP-Cycle; validate ribosomal protein stoichiometry via targeted proteomics; compare to ProMono (translation downregulated, commitment phase) to establish translational shutdown as differentiation signal.

functional_description: This signature reflects the core antimicrobial and metabolic competence of mature CD14 classical monocytes, characterized by robust bacterial cell wall degradation capacity, intracellular iron/ROS management, and lysosomal proteolytic machinery. The programme encompasses pattern recognition (FCN1), oxidative stress defence (GPX1, FTH1), and energetic support (NAMPT, GAPDH) essential for sustained inflammatory responses and pathogen containment.
key_evidence: LYZ: Peptidoglycan hydrolysis—direct bacterial cell wall degradation, canonical monocyte antimicrobial function
FCN1: Ficolin-mediated complement activation and pathogen-associated molecular pattern recognition via collagen-like domain
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain—iron storage and detoxification critical for ROS buffering in activated monocytes
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase—H₂O₂ scavenging, essential for oxidative stress tolerance during respiratory burst
S100A9 + S100A6 + S100A4: Calprotectin/S100 family—calcium-binding proteins involved in antimicrobial activity and monocyte activation
CTSS: Cathepsin S—lysosomal cysteine protease required for antigen processing and phagolysosomal degradation
TYROBP (DAP12): ITAM-containing adaptor linking pattern recognition receptors to inflammatory signalling
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis—metabolic support for sustained glycolysis and inflammatory cytokine production
ZFP36L1: mRNA stability regulator—post-transcriptional control of pro-inflammatory mediators
BCL2A1: Anti-apoptotic factor—survival signal in activated, metabolically stressed monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14+FCN1+LYZ+ with intracellular ROS (CellROX) and iron staining (calcein-AM quenching); qPCR validation of LYZ, FCN1, GPX1 in sorted CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono; functional assay of bacterial killing capacity (E. coli opsonized with IgG) in LYZ/FCN1-high monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects robust translation and protein synthesis capacity characteristic of metabolically active early GMP progenitors. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPL4), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and housekeeping metabolism genes indicates high anabolic demand during early myeloid progenitor expansion before lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components indicating active protein synthesis machinery in proliferative progenitors
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor required for efficient ribosomal function during rapid cell division
HNRNPA1: pre-mRNA processing and mRNA stability regulation, supporting high transcriptional output in early GMP
NPM1: nucleolar protein regulating protein chaperoning and centrosome duplication consistent with cell cycle progression in GMP-Cycle subset (10%)
GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH: glycolytic and oxidative metabolism genes reflecting energy demands of proliferating progenitors
YBX1: RNA-binding protein involved in translational control and mRNA stabilization during early differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate by measuring ribosomal biogenesis markers (NPM1 localization, total protein synthesis rate via puromycin incorporation) and correlating with cell cycle phase distributions; compare ribosomal protein abundance between Early GMP vs GMP-Mono to confirm declining translation capacity upon monocytic commitment.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened global protein synthesis and translational capacity in early GMP-stage progenitors, driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation factors. The enrichment of ribosomal machinery alongside metabolic enzymes (GAPDH) and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components (UQCRH, MT-CO3) indicates metabolically active progenitors engaged in rapid biosynthesis required for myeloid differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17: core 40S ribosomal subunit proteins—dominant signature indicating translational upregulation
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: large 60S subunit—coordinated ribosome assembly and protein synthesis capacity
RPLP0: 60S ribosomal stalk protein—facilitates translational elongation and ribosome function
EEF1B2: elongation factor supporting aminoacyl-tRNA delivery—active translation initiation/elongation
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting roles—marks metabolically primed early GMP
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein—mRNA processing during rapid cell cycle and differentiation
PTMA: nucleoplasmically localized, anti-apoptotic—supports progenitor survival during proliferation
UQCRH, MT-CO3: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation—energetic demand of biosynthetically active progenitors
suggested_validation: Validate by FACS sorting Early GMP, GMP-Cycle, and GMP-Mono subsets; assess by polysome profiling or metabolic labeling (e.g., puromycin incorporation); correlate ribosomal protein expression with mRNA and protein synthesis rates via qPCR and flow cytometry for phospho-S6K (mTORC1 axis). Confirm monocyte lineage progression by co-staining CSF1R and IRF8 expression in ribosome-high vs ribosome-low GMP subsets.

programme_name: Early ProMono cytoplasmic maturation and antimicrobial priming
functional_description: This signature reflects early commitment-stage monocyte progenitors acquiring antimicrobial and proteolytic effector capacity while maintaining active translation and actin dynamics. The dominance of Early ProMono (57%) coupled with monocytic hydrolase upregulation (LYZ, RNASE2, CSTA) indicates a pre-egress maturation programme distinct from fully differentiated CD14 monocytes, emphasizing intracellular defence priming over lineage commitment transcription factors.
key_evidence: LYZ: Canonical monocyte bactericidal enzyme; highest t-statistic confirms ProMono-specific expression in committed trajectory
RNASE2: Non-secretory antimicrobial ribonuclease, gained in monocytic differentiation and lost in neutrophils
CSTA: Cystatin superfamily protease inhibitor ensuring controlled proteolytic activity during early maturation
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration regulator supporting migration and progenitor morphogenesis en route to egress
ANXA2: Calcium-dependent phospholipid binding; involved in monocyte membrane dynamics and signal transduction
GPX1: Oxidative stress protection critical for intracellular survival during commitment and pre-egress phase
HMGN2: Chromatin accessibility marker suggesting active transcriptional remodeling in early ProMono
PKM, GAPDH: Glycolytic enzymes reflecting energetic demands of rapidly proliferating progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow sort Early ProMono (CD34+ CD13+ CD14− CSF1R+ MS4A3+) and Late ProMono (CD34− CD13+ CD14+ CSF1R+); validate LYZ, RNASE2, CSTA protein expression by intracellular flow; confirm absence of MPO and ELANE to exclude GMP contamination; qPCR on sorted populations for IRF8 and KLF4 co-expression.

functional_description: This signature defines a classical CD14+ monocyte state characterized by robust antimicrobial effector functions and acute inflammatory activation. The dominant S100A8/A9/A12 calprotectin complex and elevated CXCL8 (IL-8) indicate PAMP-driven innate immune priming with strong neutrophil and inflammatory cell recruitment capacity. Co-expression of phagocytic machinery (FCN1, TYROBP) and metabolic support (NAMPT, FTH1) reflects activated monocytes poised for pathogen clearance and sustained inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9/A12: Calprotectin complex—hallmark of activated CD14 monocytes; DAMP/PAMP sensors secreted during inflammatory response
CXCL8: Pro-inflammatory chemokine driving neutrophil recruitment; signature of classical monocyte activation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (M-ficolin); Pattern Recognition Receptor for bacterial cell wall components; complement-independent opsonization
TYROBP (DAP12): ITAM-bearing co-receptor for TLRs and Fcγ receptors; couples to inflammatory signaling cascades
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis critical for inflammatory cytokine production and metabolic reprogramming of activated macrophages
FTH1: Iron storage support for ROS production and metabolic demands of primed innate immune cells
MAFB: Transcription factor supporting monocyte/macrophage inflammatory differentiation
PLAUR (uPAR): Plasminogen activation receptor; facilitates leukocyte recruitment and ECM remodeling in inflammation
VCAN: Versican; ECM component inducing TLR2/6 responses and monocyte activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: validate CD14+CD16−CCR2+ phenotype with intracellular S100A8/A9 and surface FCGR1A expression; Bulk RNA-seq of sorted CD14 monocytes ± LPS/TNF stimulation to confirm inflammatory priming; Functional assays: measure LPS-induced CXCL8/IL-6 secretion and phagocytic capacity (opsonized bacteria with FCN1 blocking); Compare with tissue-resident macrophages (low S100A8/A9, high CD163/MERTK) and CD16 monocytes (low CCR2, high CX3CR1).

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 Mono-dominant programme characterized by calcium-regulated inflammatory signaling and enhanced innate immune effector functions. The enrichment of S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex, TYROBP-coupled ITAM signaling, and lysosomal proteases (CTSS) indicates priming for rapid bacterial sensing and antimicrobial response, consistent with classical monocyte activation and extravasation.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: Calprotectin heterodimer, hallmark of activated CD14 Mono; Ca2+-dependent DAMP/PAMP sensing and inflammatory amplification
FCN1: Ficolin-1 production links to pattern recognition and complement-like pathway activation in classical monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor couples Fc receptors and TLRs to downstream inflammatory signaling; essential for CD14 Mono effector functions
CD14: Canonical classical monocyte marker; co-receptor for TLR2/TLR4 bacterial LPS sensing
CTSS: Cathepsin S drives antigen processing and pro-inflammatory cytokine maturation in inflammatory monocytes
FCER1G: Fc gamma receptor gamma chain supports phagocytic ITAM signaling and IgG-mediated responses
GRN: Granulin secretion supports inflammatory microenvironment and monocyte recruitment
TMSB4X: Actin-regulatory protein supports rapid monocyte migration and extravasation from bone marrow
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CD14++CD16−CCR2+ gate; measure S100A8/A9 surface expression and intracellular calcium dynamics upon TLR4 stimulation; confirm TYROBP-FCGR1A co-clustering and phagocytic capacity versus CD16 Mono comparator

programme_name: Early ProMono cell cycle and chromatin remodeling
functional_description: This signature reflects active proliferation and chromatin dynamics in Early ProMono progenitors, dominated by cell cycle machinery (UBE2C, TOP2A, CCNB1, PTTG1) and nucleosomal chromatin-associated factors (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2). The concurrent expression of LYZ and RNASE2 indicates early acquisition of monocytic antimicrobial effector functions alongside proliferative capacity, consistent with committed but still-cycling progenitors.
key_evidence: HMGN2: chromatin remodeling in transcriptionally active loci during ProMono transition
HMGB1/HMGB2: nucleosomal DNA binding and transcriptional regulation supporting cell fate specification
UBE2C/TOP2A/CCNB1/PTTG1: mitotic and S-phase machinery indicating active cell cycle (characteristic of Early ProMono, not mature CD14 Mono)
LYZ: canonical monocyte differentiation marker and antimicrobial effector
RNASE2: monocyte-associated antimicrobial ribonuclease
LGALS1: galectin-mediated cell-cell interaction modulation during commitment phase
Cell composition 69.5% Early ProMono validates proliferative progenitor biology
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry on freshly isolated Early ProMono (CD34+CD13+MS4A3+CD14−) confirming Ki67+/cyclin B1+ with simultaneous LYZ and RNASE2 protein co-expression; compare cell cycle gene expression against quiescent Late ProMono and CD14 Mono to confirm proliferative stratification.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP and GMP-Mono populations, indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity during active myeloid progenitor differentiation. The dominance of ribosomal structural components (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4) combined with translation factors (EEF1B2) and nucleolar proteins (PTMA, HMGN1) suggests active translational control supporting proliferation and lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24/RPL37A/RPS23/RPS2/RPS17/RPLP0/RPL7A/RPL4: Large multipart ribosomal signature indicates GMP population maintains elevated basal protein synthesis
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting active mRNA translation during progenitor expansion
PTMA: DNA-binding factor promoting survival and apoptosis resistance in proliferating GMPs
HMGN1: Chromatin remodelling protein associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in differentiating cells
UQCRH/MT-CO3: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components reflecting energy demand of synthetic phase
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing during dynamic gene expression
Cell composition: 78.5% Early GMP + GMP-Mono confirms progenitor-enriched signature; 12% GMP-Cycle supports translation machinery requirement for active cycling
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD34/KIT (GMP markers) with ribosomal protein reporters or polysome profiling; qPCR validation of RPS/RPL transcripts in FACS-sorted Early GMP vs. ProMono to confirm translational capacity divergence. Consider puromycin incorporation assays to quantify active protein synthesis rates in Early GMP vs. more differentiated stages.

programme_name: Monocyte lysosomal proteolysis and iron metabolism
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened lysosomal cysteine protease activity and intracellular iron storage capacity characteristic of activated monocytes engaged in antigen processing and endosomal degradation. The balanced CD16/CD14 composition (52.5%/47.5%) suggests a transitional or intermediate monocyte state with robust protein catabolism rather than canonical patrolling CD16 Mono biology.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine proteinase central to antigen degradation and MHC-II peptide generation
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain indicating elevated intracellular iron sequestration and oxidative stress response
CD68: pan-monocyte lysosomal marker upregulated in activated/intermediate monocytes
IFI30: lysosomal cysteine protease involved in invariant chain processing for MHC-II
FCER1G: Fc gamma receptor signalling adaptor, ADCC-competent phenotype consistent with CD16 Mono
GNLY: granulysin present in cytotoxic monocyte granules, non-classical function
AIF1: allograft inflammatory factor induced by interferon and monocyte activation signals
LST1: lymphocyte inhibitor upregulated by LPS/IFN-γ, marks activated myeloid cells
TMSB4X: actin regulator supporting cellular migration and morphodynamics
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining (CD14/CD16/CTSS/FTH1/FCGR3A) to resolve CD16 Mono vs intermediate Mono; validate antigen processing function via MHC-II peptide loading assays; interrogate lysosomal proteolytic capacity in sorted populations; assess iron metabolism via ferritin release and labile iron pools.

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodelling and metabolic priming
functional_description: This signature reflects early committed monocyte progenitors actively engaged in chromatin remodelling and metabolic reprogramming during the transition from GMP towards monocytic fate. The programme combines nucleosomal organization (HMGN2, HMGB1/2, H2AFZ), translation/RNA processing machinery (HNRNPA2B1, PTMA), and mitochondrial oxidative capacity (MT-CO2, MT-CO3) alongside early monocyte-specific antimicrobial factors (LYZ, RNASE2). This reflects coordinated epigenetic and bioenergetic shifts characteristic of Early ProMono cells establishing commitment before surface marker maturation.
key_evidence: HMGN2: Nucleosomal-binding protein marking transcriptionally active chromatin remodelling in early commitment phase
LYZ: Canonical monocyte antimicrobial enzyme, confirms mono-lineage identity over neutrophil trajectory
RNASE2: Monocyte-restricted antimicrobial ribonuclease, absent in GMP-Neut and mature monocytes
HMGB1/HMGB2: Chromatin architectural proteins driving transcriptional plasticity during early fate commitment
MT-CO2/MT-CO3: Elevated mitochondrial respiration supporting energy demands of monocytic differentiation
TMSB4X: Actin regulation supporting migration priming and cytoskeletal remodelling in Early ProMono
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor stabilizing committed progenitors during differentiation stress
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining with MS4A3 (transient ProMono), CSF1R, and CD14 (absent in Early ProMono) to confirm cell-stage purity. RT-qPCR for KLF4 and IRF8 (mono-commitment TFs) to validate molecular signature. Chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) on HMGN2+ early ProMono should show open chromatin at monocyte loci (LYZ, CSF1R, CCR2) versus closed GMP-neutrophil regions (MPO, ELANE).

functional_description: This signature reflects active transcriptional reprogramming and cell cycle progression in early ProMono progenitors, characterised by chromatin-associated proteins maintaining open chromatin architecture and DNA damage/stress response factors. The programme is driven by nucleosome remodelling factors (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2, H2AFZ/V) coupled with monocyte lineage commitment markers (LYZ) and oxidative metabolism (MT-CO2/3), consistent with proliferative progenitors transitioning toward monocytic differentiation.
key_evidence: HMGN1/2: Maintain open chromatin at actively transcribed loci during lineage specification
HMGB1/2: Chromatin architecture organisers essential for transcriptional plasticity in differentiating progenitors
H2AFZ/H2AFV: Histone variants enriched at active regulatory elements during cell fate commitment
LYZ: Monocyte lineage marker validating ProMono identity within activating population
MT-CO2/3: Oxidative phosphorylation supporting energy demands of proliferating progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic regulator allowing survival during lineage transition
ANP32B: Chromatin remodelling factor facilitating transcriptional changes during differentiation
RNASE2: Antimicrobial effector emerging early in monocytic lineage commitment
suggested_validation: Co-expression analysis of HMGN1/2 with IRF8 and KLF4 in sorted Early ProMono; chromatin accessibility assay (ATAC-seq) on HMGN2+ vs HMGN2− progenitors; validate LYZ expression kinetics against MPO/ELANE loss to confirm neutrophil lineage exit.

functional_description: This signature reflects activated classical monocytes primed for acute inflammatory responses, characterized by calcium-binding damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) sensors, extracellular matrix remodeling capacity, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. The dominance of S100 proteins and metabolic reprogramming genes indicates readiness for rapid effector functions including chemotaxis and tissue infiltration.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin component; canonical DAMP/PAMP-responsive alarmin in inflammatory CD14 monocytes
S100A8: Calprotectin S100A8/A9 heterodimer; TLR4 ligand and neutrophil/monocyte recruitment factor
S100A12: S100 family DAMP; intracellular calcium signaling and inflammation amplification
CXCL8: Pro-inflammatory chemokine; IL-8 drives neutrophil recruitment and monocyte activation
C5AR1: Complement C5a receptor; amplifies inflammatory response to PAMPs and tissue damage
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; supports metabolic reprogramming in activated monocytes
PLAUR: uPA receptor; promotes monocyte migration and tissue invasion during inflammation
VCAN: Versican; ECM component involved in monocyte recruitment and vascular inflammation
THBS1: Thrombospondin; pro-inflammatory matricellular protein enhancing TLR4 signaling
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry (CD14++CD16-CCR2+) combined with intracellular staining for S100A9/A8 and phospho-NF-κB; confirm activation status via TNF/IL-6 production upon LPS/TLR4 stimulation; validate against CD16 monocytes (should show low S100A9, high CX3CR1)

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened ribosomal protein expression and translational capacity in actively cycling GMP-stage progenitors (64% GMP-Cycle), consistent with the anabolic demands of proliferating myeloid precursors. The dominance of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS2, RPS17, RPL7A) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and cofactors (PPIA) indicates robust protein synthesis machinery mobilization rather than lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPS2, RPL7A: coordinate ribosomal subunit expression drives translational output in cycling cells
EEF1B2: elongation factor expression supports high-throughput translation during proliferation
UQCRH, MT-CO2: elevated oxidative phosphorylation capacity fuels energetic demands of protein synthesis
STMN1: microtubule dynamics regulator consistent with mitotic spindle requirements in GMP-Cycle
PTMA: DNA-binding protein with anti-apoptotic function supports survival of proliferating progenitors
PRSS57: serine protease priming reflects early myeloid differentiation trajectory, though not lineage-restricted
suggested_validation: Validate by co-expression analysis of CDK1/MKI67/TOP2A cell-cycle markers with ribosomal signature in sorted GMP-Cycle cells. Confirm inverse correlation with mature monocyte markers (CD14, CD16). Assess whether signature enrichment correlates with S/G2M phase by FACS-gated analysis. Distinguish from GMP-Mono by absence of CSF1R/IRF8 upregulation.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte specialisation in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation coupled with lysosomal protease activity for antigenic peptide generation. The programme emphasises professional antigen-presenting cell (APC) function alongside catabolic capacity, with supporting mitochondrial respiration for sustained effector activity.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: Core HLA class II alpha chain; essential for antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells
HLA-DMB: HLA class II beta chain; MHC-II peptide loading chaperone in endosomal compartments
HLA-DMA: HLA class II alpha partner; HLA-DM co-factor for peptide exchange
HLA-DQB1: Additional HLA class II beta paralogue; broadens peptide-binding repertoire
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine cathepsin; critical for degradation of phagocytosed antigens to peptides
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase; processes antigenic peptides post-proteolysis for optimal MHC binding
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; ECM component involved in leukocyte-endothelium interactions and tissue remodelling
LGALS2: Galectin-2 lectin; pattern recognition via carbohydrate binding; immunoregulatory signalling
MT-CO3, MT-CO2: Mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase subunits; oxidative phosphorylation for energy-intensive APC function
FOSB: AP-1 component; transcriptional regulation of inflammatory and antigen-presentation responses
ENTPD1: Ectonucleotidase; immunomodulation via extracellular ATP/ADP metabolism
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+ monocytes for HLA-DR, CD11c and verify CTSS protein expression by intracellular staining. qPCR validation of HLA-DM, HLA-DQ and CTSS in CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono. Functional assay: measure antigen presentation capacity (peptide-pulsed assay) and lysosomal proteolytic activity in these cells. Confirm absence of this signature in CD16 Mono (which lack robust APC function).

functional_description: This signature reflects GMP-Mono cells (69%) undergoing monocytic commitment, characterized by elevated MPO (myeloid priming) and robust ribosomal protein expression (RPS26, RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0) indicating high protein synthesis capacity. The co-expression of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components (UQCRH, UQCRQ) and redox regulators (TXN) supports metabolic rewiring during monocytic differentiation, with nucleosome remodeling factors (HMGN1) indicating chromatin accessibility for lineage-specific transcription.
key_evidence: MPO: Master myeloid priming marker, present in both monocytic and neutrophilic intermediates but declining in mature monocytes; indicates GMP-Mono/early ProMono developmental stage
RPS26, RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0: Coordinated ribosomal protein upregulation reflecting high translational demand during monocytic differentiation and protein synthesis of commitment factors
UQCRH, UQCRQ: Mitochondrial complex III components indicating enhanced oxidative phosphorylation capacity required for monocyte functional maturation
TXN: Redox homeostasis regulator supporting metabolic transition and protection during monocytic differentiation
HMGN1: Nucleosome-associated protein promoting transcriptionally active chromatin, enabling IRF8/SPI1-driven monocytic gene programs
PPIA, PTMA: Molecular chaperones facilitating protein folding and anti-apoptotic support during differentiation
GMP-Mono dominance (69%) with Early ProMono (14%): Confirms early-to-intermediate monocytic commitment with retained progenitor plasticity
suggested_validation: Validate by co-immunofluorescence of MPO + CD34 (declining) + SPI1/IRF8 expression across FACS-sorted GMP-Mono vs Early ProMono populations; confirm ribosomal translation rates via polysome profiling; assess CSF1R and CD64 upregulation patterns to confirm monocytic lineage trajectory away from neutrophilic progenitors

functional_description: This signature reflects a shared lysosomal-endosomal proteolytic programme active in both CD14 and CD16 monocytes, characterized by cysteine proteases (CTSS, CST3), iron-handling (FTH1), and actin-regulatory proteins supporting phagolysosomal function. The balanced CD14/CD16 composition (51.5%/48.5%) and enrichment of myeloid pan-markers (CD68, TYROBP/DAP12, FCER1G) indicate a core effector state for antimicrobial and tissue remodelling capacity rather than a classical CD14-specific inflammatory programme.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for phagolysosomal degradation and antigen processing in monocytes
CD68: Pan-myeloid marker highly expressed by monocytes; lysosomal-associated glycoprotein
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor enabling Fc receptor and TLR signalling in myeloid cells
FTH1: Iron storage critical for ROS buffering and protection during antimicrobial activation
FCER1G: Fc gamma receptor gamma chain mediating phagocytic opsonin recognition
PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lysosomal lipid degradation and pathogen processing
AIF1: Actin-binding protein induced by cytokine/interferon; promotes myeloid activation
COTL1: Actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics in phagocytosis and migration
LST1: Lipopolysaccharide-inducible membrane protein; responds to bacterial PAMPs
HLA-DPA1: MHC-II antigen presentation capacity characteristic of mature monocytes
suggested_validation: Compare module activation across monocyte subsets using monocyte-specific stimuli (LPS for TLR4, bacterial culture supernatants); assess correlation with CD14/CD16 ratio and surface Fc receptor expression (CD64/FCGR1A); validate CTSS and PSAP activity in functional assays of phagolysosomal degradation capacity to distinguish effector function from inflammatory transcriptional programmes.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened mitochondrial respiratory capacity and oxidative metabolism rather than monocyte commitment biology. The dominant hemoglobin genes (HBA2, HBB, HBA1, HBD, HBM) and mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH) indicate active ATP generation, likely supporting high bioenergetic demand during progenitor expansion. This metabolic programme is dissociated from canonical ProMono differentiation markers (KLF4, IRF8, CSF1R, MS4A3, LYZ).
key_evidence: HBA2/HBA1/HBB/HBD/HBM: Hemoglobin genes dominate signature (5/15 top genes), atypical for monocyte lineage commitment
MT-CO2/MT-CO3/MT-ND1/UQCRH: Mitochondrial respiratory complexes I-IV heavily represented, indicating oxidative phosphorylation dependency
TMSB4X/ACTG1: Actin dynamics for cytoskeletal reorganization during active proliferation
GAPDH/RPS26/ATP5J2: Glycolytic and ribosomal machinery supporting biosynthesis
GMP-Mono (23%) and Early GMP (12.5%) co-enrichment: Suggests metabolic priming in less-committed populations
suggested_validation: Interrogate whether hemoglobin expression represents genuine lineage expression or contamination from erythroid/megakaryocytic cells. Validate ProMono identity via flow cytometry for MS4A3, KLF4 protein, and IRF8 activity. Assess if oxidative metabolism signature correlates with proliferation state (Ki-67) or hypoxic microenvironment exposure. Compare against pure CD14 Mono metabolic signature to confirm this is GMP-Mono/Early ProMono specific.

programme_name: Pro-monocyte chromatin remodelling and RNA processing
functional_description: This signature reflects active chromatin remodelling and nucleosome dynamics in early pro-monocytes, enriched for high-mobility group proteins (HMGB1/2, HMGN2) that facilitate open chromatin states required for lineage-specific transcription. The programme integrates nucleosome assembly (H2AFV, H2AFZ), RNA processing (LSM5, RNASE2), and cell cycle checkpoint control (PTTG1, NUCKS1), consistent with actively differentiating pro-monocyte populations transitioning from GMP with retained proliferative capacity.
key_evidence: HMGB2: Non-histone chromatin protein enabling transcriptional plasticity during lineage commitment
HMGN2: Marks transcriptionally active chromatin, essential for lineage TF accessibility in early pro-monocytes
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease expressed early in monocytic differentiation; marks monocyte-specific innate immunity programme
PTTG1: Securin/separase regulator; indicates active cell cycle checkpoint control in proliferating pro-monocytes
H2AFV/H2AFZ: Histone variants supporting chromatin remodelling during pro-monocyte exit from quiescence
NUCKS1: Phosphorylation target of casein kinase II; involved in chromatin condensation dynamics
LSM5: Small nuclear ribonucleoprotein component; indicates active pre-mRNA splicing during differentiation
PTMA: Nucleoplasmic chaperone preventing apoptosis during metabolically active pro-monocyte expansion
suggested_validation: FACS sort Early ProMono (CSF1R+CD64+MPO+CD34−) vs GMP-Cycle (KIT+CD34+MKI67+), then perform ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq for HMGB1/2 binding and H3K4me3/H3K27ac deposition at monocytic TF loci (SPI1, CEBPA, IRF8). Verify RNASE2 expression elevation as marker discriminating pro-monocytes from neutrophilic commitment (CEBPE+ GMP-Neut).

functional_description: This signature represents activated classical monocytes engaged in acute inflammatory and antimicrobial responses, characterized by prominent expression of S100 alarmin proteins (S100A8/A9/A12), pro-inflammatory cytokine CXCL8, and enhanced lysosomal/phagocytic machinery. The signature reflects calcium-mediated innate immune signaling, oxidative stress response via iron metabolism (FTH1), and protease-dependent antigen processing typical of monocytes responding to bacterial PAMPs.
key_evidence: S100A9: Dominant alarmin; forms heterodimer (calprotectin) with S100A8, induces TLR4 signaling, cardinal inflammatory monocyte marker
S100A8: Calprotectin component; synergizes with S100A9 in DAMP/PAMP sensing and amplification of innate immune response
S100A12: RAGE ligand and TLR4 agonist; amplifies pro-inflammatory cascades in activated monocytes
CXCL8: Canonical pro-inflammatory chemokine; recruits neutrophils; direct evidence of monocyte activation state
CD14: LPS/PAMP recognition, TLR4 co-receptor; confirms classical monocyte phenotype
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; supports ROS buffering and iron homeostasis under inflammatory stress
FCN1: Ficolin; pattern recognition receptor for bacterial and apoptotic cells, enhances phagocytosis
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor; couples phagocytic and pattern recognition receptors to signaling
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease; essential for antigen processing and autophagy in activated phagocytes
VCAN: Versican; ECM remodeling and inflammatory cell migration
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting CD14++CD16- monocytes followed by LPS/TNF stimulation time-course; verify S100A8/A9 co-expression, CXCL8 secretion, and correlation with CD64/FCGR1A upregulation. Orthogonal validation via qPCR of S100A8/A9 dimer formation and functional assays of calprotectin-induced TLR4 signaling.

programme_name: Early GMP ribosomal and translational priming
functional_description: This signature captures the translational machinery expansion and nucleolar/ribosomal biogenesis programme active in early GMP progenitors (77% of activating cells). The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0), translation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar organizing proteins (NPM1, HMGN1) reflects preparation for rapid protein synthesis during GMP expansion and early myeloid differentiation, rather than lineage commitment per se.
key_evidence: RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit protein; housekeeping marker of active protein synthesis capacity
RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL37A: Comprehensive ribosomal subunit coverage indicates coordinate ribosomal biogenesis
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein essential for ribosome assembly and centrosome duplication in proliferating progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; marks cells with elevated translational demand
HNRNPA1, HNRNPH1: RNA-binding proteins regulating mRNA processing; support transcript maturation during active protein synthesis
HSP90AB1: Heat shock chaperone required for protein folding during high translational flux
HMGN1: Nucleosomal protein marking transcriptionally active chromatin; indicates open chromatin state in biosynthetically active GMPs
PTMA: Nucleoplasmic shuttle protein involved in proliferation signalling; consistent with GMP-Cycle activity (13% of cohort)
SET: Protein phosphatase 2A inhibitor; regulates cell cycle and apoptosis in proliferating cells
suggested_validation: Cross-reference with cell-cycle phase annotation (G1/S/G2M) to confirm co-enrichment with GMP-Cycle stage; perform polysome profiling or metabolic labelling (O-propargyl-puromycin) on Early GMP vs GMP-Mono to quantify translational activity; validate with qPCR for ribosomal protein coordinate expression; confirm absence of lineage-specific markers (IRF8, CEBPE, MPO) to exclude ProMono contamination.

functional_description: This signature marks CD14 monocytes with elevated MHC class II antigen presentation capacity (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ, CD74) coupled with enhanced iron storage and management (FTH1). This phenotype reflects antigen-presenting monocytes poised for professional antigen presentation and immune surveillance, distinct from inflammatory monocyte subsets.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: Core HLA class II α-chain component; central to MHC-II assembly and antigen presentation
HLA-DRB1/HLA-DRB5: HLA-DR β-chain paralogs; primary antigen-presenting molecules on monocytes
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer; non-classical but functional MHC-II pathway
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer; complete MHC-II presentation repertoire
CD74: Chaperone for MHC-II assembly and trafficking; marker of professional APCs
HLA-DMA: MHC-II peptide loading factor; indicates active antigen processing
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage linked to oxidative stress tolerance in inflammatory contexts
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adapter; signaling co-receptor for activating immune receptors
CST3: Cystatin; protease inhibitor relevant to antigen processing and inflammation resolution
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ surface expression; functional assay of antigen presentation capacity (allogeneic T cell stimulation); iron staining (Prussian blue) to assess FTH1-linked iron accumulation; distinguish from tissue macrophages (higher CD163) and CD16 monocytes (lower HLA-II expression).

functional_description: This signature reflects activated classical monocytes with prominent calcium-binding S100 proteins (S100A8/A9/A12 calprotectin complex, S100A4/A6) that mediate antimicrobial responses, oxidative stress signaling, and cell migration. The co-expression of CD14, FCN1 (ficolins for pattern recognition), TYROBP (ITAM signaling), and cysteine protease inhibitors (CSTA) indicates priming for bacterial sensing and controlled proteolytic responses characteristic of inflammatory CD14+ monocytes.
key_evidence: S100A9/S100A8: Calprotectin heterodimer (top 2 genes); chelates metal ions, inhibits bacterial growth, induces TLR4/RAGE signaling in inflammation
S100A12: Calprotectin component and alarmin; ligand for RAGE and TLR4; elevated in bacterial/inflammatory stress
S100A4/S100A6: Calcium-dependent regulators of cytoskeleton remodeling and cell motility; support monocyte extravasation
CD14: Canonical classical monocyte marker; LPS co-receptor with TLR4; marks CD14 Mono identity (95% of activating cells)
FCN1: Pattern recognition receptor (ficolin); recognizes bacterial carbohydrates and apoptotic cells; bridges innate immunity
TYROBP (DAP12): Transmembrane ITAM-containing adaptor; couples pattern recognition to immune signaling cascades
CSTA: Cystatin; protease inhibitor; prevents excessive elastase and cathepsin activity in inflammatory milieu
CAPG: Actin regulatory protein; regulates cell shape change and migration during recruitment to inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of S100A8/A9 with CD14/CCR2/CD36 on classical monocytes; correlate expression with TLR4 and NLRP3 inflammasome activation markers; measure calprotectin serum levels in CD14 Mono-enriched inflammation models.

programme_name: Lysosomal protease and innate immune signalling
functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 monocytes with enhanced lysosomal/phagolysosomal capacity and calcium-dependent signalling.
