The coordinated expression of S100 calcium sensors, lysosomal proteases (CTSS), and ITAM-bearing adaptor proteins (TYROBP, FCER1G) indicates priming for antigen processing and pattern recognition receptor signalling.
key_evidence: S100A6, S100A4, S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins driving cytoskeletal dynamics and DAMP sensing in activated monocytes
CTSS, CST3: Lysosomal cysteine proteases essential for phagocytic degradation and antigen presentation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor coupling Fc receptors and pattern recognition receptors to downstream signalling
FCER1G: Gamma chain of Fc receptors and complement receptors; bridges innate immune activation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 lectin pathway activator; constitutive monocyte expression supports complement-mediated phagocytosis
CD74, HLA-DRB1: MHC class II antigen presentation pathway; marks professional APCs
FTH1: Iron storage in context of oxidative stress management during inflammatory activation
TMSB4X, CALM2, AP1S2: Cytoskeletal and vesicular trafficking machinery supporting migration and endocytosis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+ monocytes for CTSS, CD64 (FCGR1A), and S100A4 protein expression; correlate with TLR4/CD14 surface intensity and intracellular ROS (DCFDA). Functional assay: measure phagocytic capacity and lysosomal proteolytic activity in sorted CD14+ cells expressing this signature versus CD16 Mono controls.

functional_description: This signature reflects the assembly of antimicrobial and proteolytic granule cargo characteristic of committed monocyte progenitors transitioning through the ProMono compartment. The enrichment of lysozyme (LYZ), ribonuclease (RNASE2), S100 calgranulins (S100A8/A9), and resistin (RETN) indicates active packaging of bactericidal and immunomodulatory effectors. Concurrent expression of chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN2, HMGB2) and myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA) supports active transcriptional programming during monocyte lineage commitment.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte bactericidal enzyme, high in ProMono/CD14 Mono vs GMP
S100A8/S100A9: calgranulin components of monocyte antimicrobial granules, myeloid maturation markers
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease family member, myeloid-specific expression
RETN: resistin-like antimicrobial factor, monocyte granule component
MNDA: myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen, marks committed granulocyte-monocyte lineage
LGALS1: galectin-1 mediates immune cell interactions, upregulated during monocyte maturation
HMGN2/HMGB2: chromatin accessibility factors supporting differentiation gene expression
CAPG: actin-regulatory protein enabling granule trafficking and cytoskeletal reorganization
Early ProMono dominance (53.5%): signature peaks in early-committed stage before CD14 surface expression
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of LYZ, S100A8, CD33, and CD14 to confirm ProMono enrichment and distinguish from GMP (MPO+) and CD14 Mono (full surface maturation). Single-cell proteomic validation of granule protein co-localization in sorted Early/Late ProMono subsets.

programme_name: Early GMP translational capacity and biosynthesis
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP (85% of activating cells), indicative of high protein synthesis demand during progenitor proliferation and myeloid differentiation. The dominance of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS23, RPS2, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) coupled with stress-response chaperones (HSP90AB1) and nucleolar proteins (NPM1) suggests active anabolic metabolism characteristic of proliferative progenitor states.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS2, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: core ribosomal proteins reflecting sustained protein synthesis in proliferative Early GMP
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor indicating active mRNA translation during myeloid progenitor expansion
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in ribosome biogenesis and centrosome duplication, essential in cycling progenitors
HSP90AB1: heat shock chaperone supporting protein folding during high biosynthetic load in Early GMP
HNRNPA1, PTMA, ANP32B: nucleocytoplasmic RNA-binding and regulatory proteins supporting transcriptional/translational coordination
LDHB: glycolytic enzyme supporting anaerobic metabolism typical of proliferating myeloid progenitors
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein abundance and polysome associations in sorted Early GMP vs. differentiated GMP-Mono by polysome profiling or ribopuromycin incorporation. Cross-validate translation rate via puromycin incorporation assays. Confirm CD34+KIT+early marker expression alongside RPS signature to distinguish Early GMP from non-cycling progenitors.

programme_name: GMP myeloid priming with oxidative metabolism
functional_description: This signature reflects active early-to-intermediate GMP maturation (GMP-Cycle and Early GMP dominant, 83.5%) characterized by MPO upregulation (azurophil granule priming for both lineages), elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5), and robust protein synthesis machinery activation (RPL/RPS genes, SNRPF). The composition skews toward GMP-Cycle cells, indicating cells progressing through S/G2/M phase with concurrent myeloid commitment priming.
key_evidence: MPO: Gold-standard early myeloid progenitor marker; present in azurophil granules of both mono and neutrophil lineages; elevated in GMP priming phase
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Mitochondrial OXPHOS complex subunits; reflect metabolic acceleration during GMP proliferation and granule protein synthesis
RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: Ribosomal proteins; indicator of high translational demand for myeloid-specific proteins (granule enzymes, lineage-determining TFs)
PRSS57: Serine protease family member; encoded and stored in azurophil granules; marks early neutrophil/monocyte differentiation priming
HSPB1, HSP90B1, PPIA: Chaperone/folding machinery; support mass synthesis of granule proteases and myeloid transcription factors
PTMA: Protamine-like protein; involved in nuclear organization during cell cycle; elevated in cycling GMP-Cycle cells
GMP-Cycle dominance (44.5%) + Early GMP (39%): Cell cycle and early maturation phase signatures; MPO rise before lineage bifurcation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD34+/CD13+/CD33+ GMP population for MPO, phospho-S6 (ribosome activity), MitoTracker (OXPHOS capacity), Ki67 (cycle status). qRT-PCR of MPO, PRSS57, mitochondrial genes vs. GMP-committed markers (IRF8, CEBPE). Validate cyclic vs. non-cyclic GMP fractionation by CDK2/PCNA co-expression.

functional_description: This signature represents a lysosomal and phagolysosomal programme in CD14 classical monocytes, characterized by enhanced proteolytic capacity, intracellular vesicle trafficking, and antimicrobial peptidase activity. The programme reflects preparation for pathogen internalization and intracellular degradation, with coordinated expression of cysteine proteases, iron storage, and oxidative stress management.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine proteinase essential for antigen processing and pathogen proteolysis in phagolysosomes
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for Fc receptors and TLRs, critical for phagocytic and inflammatory signalling
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor involved in complement activation and bacterial cell wall recognition
LYZ: Lysozyme bactericidal enzyme targeting peptidoglycan, canonical monocyte antimicrobial effector
AP1S2: Adaptor protein for clathrin-coated vesicle formation, supporting phagolysosomal trafficking
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron storage, protecting against ROS-mediated damage during phagocytosis
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification during respiratory burst
FCGRT: IgG receptor supporting antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis
CD74: MHC II chaperone enabling antigen presentation after proteolytic processing
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor regulating protease activity balance
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry assessing CTSS, LYZ, and FCGR1A (CD64) co-expression in CD14+ monocytes; correlate with functional assays measuring phagocytic capacity and bacterial killing; confirm elevated lysosomal enzyme activity via cathepsin assays in sorted CD14 Mono populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects classical CD14+ monocyte inflammatory priming and antimicrobial effector function, dominated by S100 calprotectin (S100A8/A9) and pattern recognition machinery. The gene programme integrates PAMP sensing (CD14, FCN1, TYROBP/DAP12), iron metabolism for ROS generation (FTH1), and secreted pro-inflammatory mediators (CXCL8), consistent with activation towards bacterial clearance and inflammatory cytokine production.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin component; hallmark of classical monocyte activation and bactericidal function
S100A8: Paired S100 calprotectin; neutrophil recruitment and ROS-mediated antimicrobial responses
CD14: Master PAMP receptor; LPS/TLR4 co-receptor defining CD14+ monocyte identity
FCN1: Complement-pathway opsonin; pattern recognition and innate immune amplification
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor; ITAM signalling coupled to myeloid activation receptors
FTH1: Iron storage; supports NADPH oxidase-dependent ROS synthesis for pathogen killing
CXCL8: Pro-inflammatory chemokine; recruits neutrophils to inflammatory sites
TREM1: Triggering receptor; amplifies PAMP-induced inflammatory responses on myeloid cells
PLAUR: uPAR; facilitates monocyte extravasation and tissue infiltration
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; energetic support for inflammatory cytokine production
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of S100A8/A9 co-expression with CD14high/CCR2+ gate; correlate with intracellular TNF/IL-1β upon LPS stimulation. qPCR analysis of S100A9, FCN1, CXCL8 in sorted CD14 Mono ± TLR4 agonist. Assess iron metabolism crosstalk via FTH1 knockdown impact on ROS production.

functional_description: This signature reflects basal metabolic activity and cytoskeletal dynamics in proliferating Early ProMono cells rather than monocytic commitment. The dominance of mitochondrial respiratory chain components (MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-CO3), actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, ACTG1), and housekeeping factors (PPIA, HMGN2, HMGB2) indicates active oxidative metabolism supporting cell division and migration. Notably absent are monocyte commitment markers (KLF4, IRF8, CD14, CSF1R) and Pro-monocyte differentiation signatures (LYZ, CTSL, CTSS), with hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) suggesting erythroid-lineage contamination or metabolic reprogramming.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-CO3: Oxidative phosphorylation and ATP generation for proliferation
TMSB4X, ACTG1: Actin dynamics supporting motility and cytokinesis in cycling progenitors
LGALS1: Galectin-mediated cell-cell interaction modulation, not monocyte-specific
HMGN2, HMGB2: Active chromatin remodeling in proliferating cells
HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD: Unexpected hemoglobin expression (likely contamination or stress-related)
ABSENT: KLF4, IRF8, CD14, CSF1R, LYZ, CTSL, CTSS (canonical ProMono markers)
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry gating on Early ProMono (CD34+CD13+CD33+MS4A3+KLF4+) vs Late ProMono (CD14 emerging); assess whether TMSB4X/MT-genes correlate with cell cycle phase (Ki67+) or represent contaminating erythroid precursors; cross-check hemoglobin gene expression against erythroid lineage markers (GATA1, GATA2, EPO-R).

programme_name: Monocyte Lysosomal and Innate Immune Activation
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened lysosomal proteolytic capacity and innate immune receptor signaling in CD14 monocytes, with enrichment for antimicrobial and antigen presentation functions. The program is characterized by iron metabolism, calcium-dependent cytoskeletal dynamics, and ITAM-mediated immune cell activation, supporting enhanced phagocytic and degradative capacity typical of classical inflammatory monocytes.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein essential for Fc receptor and TLR signaling in myeloid cells; directly activates downstream immune responses
FCER1G: Gamma chain component of high-affinity Fc receptors (CD64/FCGR1A pathway); critical for antibody-mediated phagocytosis and ITAM signaling
CTSS: Cathepsin S, lysosomal cysteine protease required for antigen processing and MHC-II presentation in professional APCs
PSAP: Prosaposin precursor yields saposins for lysosomal lipid hydrolysis; supports antimicrobial autophagy and pathogen degradation
FCN1: Ficolin-1, pattern recognition receptor for microbial carbohydrates; activates complement and enhances phagocytosis
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage for ROS homeostasis during oxidative burst and NADPH oxidase activation
S100A11/S100A4/S100A6: S100 proteins; calcium-dependent regulators of cytoskeletal dynamics, cell migration, and inflammatory signaling
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein; promotes macrophage activation and inflammatory responses in myeloid cells
CD74: MHC-II chaperone; antigen presentation and immune response initiation in dendritic cells and monocytes
HLA-DRB1: MHC-II beta chain; confirms active antigen presentation capacity of activated CD14 monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+ monocytes for TYROBP/DAP12 and FCER1G (ITAM signaling axis), CTSS activity assay, and surface validation of CD64 (FCGR1A) expression. Confirm enrichment in CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono using qPCR. Assess functional phagocytosis and ROS production in activated CD14 monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects classical monocyte (CD14+) activation characterized by acute inflammatory cytokine production, intracellular iron metabolism for ROS buffering, and lysosomal proteolysis for antigen processing. The programme integrates pattern recognition signalling (TREM1), chemokine secretion (CXCL8, CXCL2, CCL3L3), and metabolic reprogramming supporting sustained inflammatory effector function.
key_evidence: CXCL8: Pro-inflammatory chemokine; sentinel marker of acute monocyte activation and neutrophil recruitment
CXCL2: CXCR2 ligand; amplifies inflammatory cascade
CCL3L3: CCL3 homologue; classical inflammatory cytokine
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage coupled to ROS homeostasis in pro-inflammatory monocytes
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease; MHC-II antigen processing and degradation of inflammatory mediators
TREM1: ITAM-coupled receptor; amplifies TLR/NF-κB signalling in inflammatory monocytes
PLAUR: uPA receptor; cell migration and extracellular matrix remodelling
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; metabolic support for sustained inflammatory response
G0S2: Growth arrest-specific gene; metabolic switching in activated myeloid cells
THBS1: Thrombospondin; matricellular signalling and vascular inflammation
suggested_validation: Co-stain CD14+ sorted cells for FTH1, CXCL8, and TREM1 protein by flow; validate inflammatory cytokine secretion via multiplex ELISA; compare ROS production capacity (DHE/DCFDA) versus CD16 Mono. Cross-reference with LPS/TNF-α stimulation kinetics to confirm acute activation state.

functional_description: This signature reflects late-stage ProMono commitment characterized by robust expression of antimicrobial S100 proteins (S100A8/A9/A12), lysozyme, and ribonucleases that populate secretory granules. The programme marks the transition from early progenitor identity toward mature monocyte effector functions, with simultaneous downregulation of proliferative programmes (CCND3 modest) and actin remodelling (CAPG) supporting cytoskeletal maturation for egress.
key_evidence: S100A8: Calcium-binding antimicrobial protein; dominant in Late ProMono granule content
S100A9: Co-expressed with S100A8 as calprotectin heterodimer; late monocyte maturation marker
LYZ: Lysozyme encodes bactericidal peptidoglycan hydrolase; canonical mono antimicrobial arsenal
RNASE2: Non-secretory ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity; maturation-associated effector
S100A12: S100 family member; monocyte-enriched antimicrobial protein
LGALS1: Galectin-1 regulates cell-cell interactions; supports late-stage maturation and pre-egress signalling
CAPG: Actin-regulatory protein enabling cytoskeletal remodelling for late ProMono morphogenesis
RETN: Resistin-like molecule; innate immune effector expressed in mature monocytes
CCND3: Cell-cycle regulation; modest expression consistent with early cell-cycle exit in Late ProMono
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of S100A8/A9 with CD14, KLF4, IRF8, and CSF1R on sorted ProMono subsets; validate CCR2/S1PR1 expression patterns; quantify azurophil granule content (myeloperoxidase negative) to confirm loss of neutrophil fate.

programme_name: Myeloid Pattern Recognition and Innate Response
functional_description: This signature reflects the activated, inflammatory state of classical CD14 monocytes (91.5% composition) with emphasis on pattern recognition receptor signaling, calcium-dependent antimicrobial responses, and oxidative stress handling. The dominance of S100 calcium-binding proteins and TYROBP-mediated ITAM signaling indicates engagement of innate immune pattern recognition pathways coupled to iron metabolism and antioxidant defenses.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9/A12/A6/A4: Calcium-binding alarmins and DAMPs; S100A8/A9 form calprotectin complex (hallmark of classical monocyte activation and antimicrobial response)
TYROBP: ITAM adaptor linking CLEC7A and other C-type lectin receptors to intracellular signaling (pattern recognition)
FCN1: Ficolin-1 lectin pathway PAMP sensor, highly specific to classical monocytes
CLEC7A: Dectin-1 fungal β-glucan receptor, PRR triggering inflammasome activation
FCER1G: Fc-gamma receptor common γ chain (CD16 component), links FCGR signaling in CD14+ cells
CXCL8: Pro-inflammatory chemokine produced by activated monocytes responding to TLR/PRR engagement
CD36: Scavenger receptor for lipids and apoptotic cells; bridge between PRR and metabolic sensing
FTH1: Iron storage ferritin heavy chain; upregulated during monocyte activation and ROS generation
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase; antioxidant defense against oxidative burst from NADPH oxidase
LGALS3: Galectin-3; lectin mediating pathogen recognition and inflammation; specific to myeloid lineage
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with S100A8/A9 (calprotectin), CLEC7A, and FCER1G surface stains on CD14+ monocytes stimulated with LPS or Candida. Single-cell RNA-seq validation of co-expression with TLR4/MyD88 axis genes. Functional assays: measure IL-1β secretion, ROS production (DCFDA), and phagocytosis of opsonized particles in S100A8/A9+ gated populations.

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and MHC-II
functional_description: This signature reflects iron homeostasis and antigen presentation in CD14 classical monocytes, with FTH1-driven ferritin storage indicating elevated intracellular iron handling, likely supporting oxidative metabolism and ROS generation. Co-enrichment of HLA-DRB1/HLA-DRA and antigen processing machinery (CTSS) suggests concurrent MHC-II-mediated adaptive immune priming, while KLF4 and FOSB indicate activation-associated transcriptional rewiring.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage protein; elevated in metabolically active monocytes requiring ROS-dependent antimicrobial function
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease critical for antigen processing and MHC-II peptide presentation
HLA-DRB1/HLA-DRA: Class II MHC co-expression for professional antigen-presenting cell function
KLF4: Master regulator of monocyte differentiation and pro-inflammatory activation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor supporting CLEC7A and other pattern recognition receptor signaling
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor for fungal/pathogen-associated molecular patterns
FOSB: AP-1 component activated downstream of TLR/inflammatory signaling
HBA1/HBA2/HBB: Globin genes suggest active protein synthesis capacity or metabolic stress response in activated monocytes
CD83: Activation/maturation marker on antigen-presenting cells
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry: co-stain FTH1/ferritin levels with CD14+HLA-DR+ gating; confirm KLF4 nuclear localization in LPS/TNF-activated CD14 monocytes; assess CTSS activity in antigen-processing assays; measure ROS production (DCFDA) in FTH1-high subset to link iron metabolism to oxidative capacity.

functional_description: This signature captures the cytoplasmic and antimicrobial effector programme of Early ProMono progenitors during commitment to monocytic lineage. The dominant S100A family (S100A8, S100A9, S100A4, S100A6) and pattern recognition proteins (FCN1, LGALS1) reflect activation of innate immune functions prior to terminal differentiation. The programme includes cytoskeletal remodelling (TMSB4X, CAPG), proteolytic capacity (CSTA, RNASE2), and myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA, LYZ) consistent with ProMono stage between GMP and CD14 Mono.
key_evidence: S100A8: Calcium-binding cytoplasmic protein marking myeloid differentiation and inflammatory priming in ProMono
S100A9: Co-regulated with S100A8 as calprotectin complex; signature of early monocytic commitment
MNDA: Nuclear myeloid differentiation antigen specific to granulocyte-monocyte lineage; marks committed progenitor state
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor supporting innate immune surveillance function in Early ProMono
LYZ: Core monocyte enzyme marking loss of neutrophil fate and acquisition of mono-specific antimicrobial capability
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein supporting cytoplasmic remodelling during ProMono proliferation and migration
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor supporting intracellular proteolytic regulation in committed progenitor
LGALS1: Galectin supporting cell-cell adhesion and autocrine growth modulation during ProMono transit
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining S100A8/A9 (calprotectin) with MS4A3, KLF4, and CD14 to confirm Early ProMono enrichment; RNA-FISH for S100A8 + LYZ co-expression to distinguish ProMono from CD14 Mono (higher calprotectin in Early ProMono); confirm absence of MPO/ELANE to exclude GMP-Neut contamination

programme_name: Ribosomal and mitochondrial biosynthesis Early GMP
functional_description: This signature represents a translation and oxidative phosphorylation programme dominated by ribosomal protein subunits (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4) and mitochondrial oxidoreductases (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH), indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity and energy metabolism. The 72% Early GMP composition and enrichment in translation factors (EEF1B2, HNRNPA1, NPM1) suggest active ribosomal biogenesis priming cells for rapid myeloid differentiation and proliferation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Multiple 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—hallmark of translational priming in early progenitors preparing for commitment
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain subunits—elevated OXPHOS capacity to support energetic demands of rapidly dividing GMPs
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—essential for efficient protein synthesis during GMP expansion
NPM1: Centrosome duplication and nucleolar protein—cell-cycle relevant for GMP-Cycle subset (21% composition)
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing—consistent with high mRNA turnover in differentiating progenitors
Compositional bias (72% Early GMP, 21% GMP-Cycle, 7% GMP-Mono): signature enriched in proliferative vs committed stages
suggested_validation: Confirm elevated protein synthesis rate via puromycin incorporation or O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) labelling in Early GMP vs GMP-Mono. Validate OXPHOS dependency using seahorse analysis (oxygen consumption rate). Cross-reference with scVI latent space to ensure Early GMP enrichment. Perform ribosomal profiling (Ribo-seq) to directly assess translation dynamics distinguishing GMP stages.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP cells (67.5%), indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity during active myeloid progenitor expansion. The enrichment of ribosomal components (RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4) alongside translation elongation factor EEF1B2 and nucleolar proteins (NPM1, HMGN1) suggests active ribosome biogenesis supporting rapid cell division characteristic of early GMP stage.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating active translational machinery in proliferative Early GMP
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity required for efficient protein synthesis during rapid progenitor expansion
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein essential for centrosome duplication and cell proliferation, abundantly expressed in cycling Early GMP
HMGN1: Open chromatin-associated protein consistent with transcriptionally active early progenitor state
CD74: MHC-II chaperone present in antigen-presenting progenitors; minor accessory marker
Early GMP enrichment (67.5%): Signature predominantly activates in high-proliferation GMP-Cycle cells dependent on robust protein synthetic capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD34+KIT+ early GMP with anti-phospho-S6 (active mTORC1 signalling) and puromycin incorporation assays to quantify protein synthesis rates; qPCR validation of RPS23, RPLP0, NPM1 in sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono populations to confirm translational upregulation during early progenitor expansion phase.

functional_description: This signature captures the monocytic differentiation programme within GMP-stage progenitors (66.5% GMP-Mono), characterised by activation of primary granule proteins (MPO, ELANE, PRTN3, AZU1) and chromatin remodelling factors supporting transcriptional reprogramming. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins and translation machinery alongside nucleosome-associated proteins reflects the proteomic synthesis demands of early monocyte lineage commitment.
key_evidence: MPO: Myeloperoxidase - cardinal primary granule enzyme; highest rank indicates robust monocytic priming in early-stage GMP-Mono
ELANE: Neutrophil elastase - early myeloid priming marker expressed in both mono/neut lineages, consistent with bipotent GMP stage
AZU1: Azurocidin - primary granule serine protease; marks early myeloid commitment upstream of mature mono phenotype
PRTN3: Proteinase-3 - primary granule protease component of antimicrobial arsenal in GMP-Mono
HMGN2 & HMGN1: Nucleosome-binding proteins maintaining open chromatin; support active transcriptional remodelling during lineage priming
HSP90B1: ER chaperone supporting protein folding demands during rapid synthesis of granule proteins and differentiation factors
MS4A3: CD34-related tetraspanin family member - marks immature myeloid progenitor compartment transitioning to committed stage
LGALS1: Galectin-1 - cell-cell interaction mediator; supports autocrine/paracrine differentiation signalling in GMP-Mono microenvironment
Ribosomal proteins (RPL37A, RPS23, LSM5): Elevated translation capacity reflecting protein synthesis demands of lineage differentiation
PLAC8 & PTMA: Transcription factor cofactors; facilitate chromatin accessibility for monocytic lineage-determining factors
suggested_validation: Validate with flow cytometry gating: confirm CD34+/CD14-/CD16- phenotype in activating cells; confirm co-expression of MPO+ELANE+AZU1 in GMP-Mono subset; compare chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) at monocyte lineage TF motifs (SPI1, IRF8, CEBPA binding sites) versus GMP-Neutro signature to quantify mono-biased chromatin remodelling.

functional_description: This signature captures elevated ribosomal protein (RPS26, RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation elongation factor (EEF1B2) expression in Early GMP cells, reflecting high protein synthesis capacity during active progenitor proliferation and differentiation. Co-enrichment of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) and RNA processing factors (HNRNPA1, SNRPE) indicates robust metabolic and biosynthetic activity characteristic of metabolically active, cycling early myeloid progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit structural proteins; dominant signature indicates active protein synthesis in proliferating Early GMP
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor; required for sustained protein synthesis during progenitor expansion
RPLP0: 60S ribosomal protein; consistent with metabolically active progenitors
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components; support energy demands of actively cycling cells
HNRNPA1, SNRPE: pre-mRNA processing and splicing factors; reflect transcriptional and post-transcriptional complexity in differentiating progenitors
71.5% Early GMP composition: signature enriched in least committed GMP stage with highest proliferative demand
suggested_validation: Confirm via polysome profiling or translation rate assays on FACS-sorted Early GMP cells; validate mitochondrial function (oxygen consumption) and ribosomal activity (puromycin incorporation) to distinguish metabolic state from lineage commitment signals (IRF8/CEBPE)

programme_name: CD14 Mono metabolic stress and iron homeostasis
functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic reprogramming in classical monocytes during inflammatory activation, characterized by iron sequestration via ferritin heavy chain (FTH1), NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT) to support glycolytic and poly-ADP-ribose signaling, and antioxidant defense. The enrichment of catabolic enzymes (CTSS, SAT1), stress-response RBPs (ZFP36L1), and survival factors (BCL2A1) indicates active metabolic remodeling under inflammatory/oxidative stress conditions typical of tissue-infiltrating CD14 monocytes.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage protein limiting ferroptosis and ROS in inflammatory monocytes; highly expressed in LPS-activated CD14 Mono
NAMPT: Rate-limiting NAD+ biosynthesis; supports NAD+-consuming ADP-ribosylation and glycolysis in activated innate immune cells
THBS1: Thrombospondin-1; pro-inflammatory matricellular protein involved in tissue remodeling and TLR signaling potentiation
CLEC7A: Dectin-1; C-type lectin receptor for β-glucans; CD14 Mono-restricted PAMP recognition receptor
CTSS: Cathepsin S; lysosomal protease critical for antigen presentation and inflammasome activation in monocytes
BCL2A1: Anti-apoptotic BCL2 family member induced by NF-κB; survival factor in activated monocytes
ZFP36L1: RNA-binding protein stabilizing inflammatory mRNAs (TNF, IL6); feedback regulator of monocyte activation
PLAUR: uPA receptor; promotes monocyte migration and proteolytic activity during inflammation
SAT1: Spermidine/spermine acetyltransferase; polyamine catabolism supporting ROS production and immune function
GPR183: Oxysterol receptor; chemotaxis cue in lipid-rich inflammatory microenvironments
suggested_validation: qPCR/flow validation of FTH1, NAMPT, CLEC7A, CTSS, ZFP36L1 in sorted CD14 vs CD16 monocytes ± LPS stimulation; assess ferroptosis resistance and NAD+ levels in FTH1-high vs FTH1-low populations; correlate with tissue infiltration and inflammatory disease activity.

programme_name: Early ProMono metabolic maturation and antimicrobial
functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic consolidation and innate effector priming in Early ProMono cells, characterized by elevated oxidative phosphorylation capacity (mitochondrial electron transport chain genes MT-CO2/3, MT-ND1/5) coupled with early antimicrobial effector expression (LYZ, RNASE2). The enrichment of chromatin remodelling factors (HMGB1/2, HMGN2, DEK) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPD) supports active transcriptional reprogramming toward monocytic identity.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte antimicrobial lysosomal hydrolase, marks mono commitment
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: oxidative phosphorylation upregulation supporting metabolic transition from progenitor quiescence
RNASE2: non-secretory ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity, early mono effector
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2: chromatin accessibility factors enabling transcriptional plasticity during ProMono specification
PTMA: apoptosis suppression, supporting progenitor survival during commitment
PPIA: PPIase activity supporting protein folding during biosynthetic maturation
Early ProMono dominance (52%): signature enriched in committed stage upstream of surface marker full expression
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of LYZ, MS4A3, CSF1R with MitoTracker to confirm metabolic upregulation in Early ProMono (KLF4+IRF8+); qPCR of MT-encoded genes vs. nuclear-encoded ETC components across sorted Early/Late ProMono and GMP-Mono; ATAC-seq to validate HMGB1/2-associated chromatin accessibility at mono lineage TF loci (PU.1, IRF8, KLF4 targets).

functional_description: This signature reflects mature myeloid cell lysosomal and iron metabolism programmes enriched in CD16 monocytes. The dominance of ferritin heavy chain (FTH1), lysosomal proteases (CTSS), and iron-responsive genes indicates activated iron handling and lysosomal protein degradation capacity characteristic of patrolling monocytes engaged in tissue surveillance and innate immune responses.
key_evidence: FTH1: iron storage and oxidative stress management in patrolling monocytes under metabolic demand
CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen presentation and cytotoxic granule processing
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adapter protein critical for Fc receptor (FCGR3A) and TLR signalling in CD16 monocytes
AIF1: calcium-binding actin-regulatory protein induced by IFN and cytokines, supporting monocyte migration
SPI1: PU.1 master transcription factor driving myeloid differentiation and CD16 monocyte identity
FCER1G: γ-chain subunit of Fcγ receptors (FCGR3A complex), enabling ADCC in CD16 monocytes
COTL1: actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics for crawling and vascular patrolling
CD68: pan-monocyte/macrophage marker and lysosomal LAMP family protein
SAT1: polyamine catabolism associated with macrophage activation and inflammatory licensing
S100A11: calcium-responsive danger signal protein in activated myeloid cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying FTH1, CTSS, and TYROBP protein levels in sorted CD16 Mono (FCGR3A+CX3CR1hi) versus CD14 Mono; functional assay measuring iron uptake and ADCC capacity; assess correlation with oxidative phosphorylation and lysosomal mass in CD16 population using metabolic profiling.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and translational capacity
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal biogenesis and translational machinery in early GMP-stage progenitors, particularly Early GMP (50%) and GMP-Cycle cells (29.5%), consistent with high protein synthesis demands during rapid proliferation. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS2, RPLP0, RPL7A) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and oxidative phosphorylation components (UQCRH, MT-CO2) indicates metabolic activation supporting myeloid progenitor expansion rather than differentiation-specific commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS2, RPLP0, RPL7A: Structural ribosomal proteins enriched in proliferating progenitors (GMP-Cycle 29.5%)
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; elevated in actively dividing cells
UQCRH, MT-CO2: Mitochondrial electron transport chain; supports high ATP demand in cycling GMP
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating centrosome duplication and cell proliferation
PTMA: DNA-binding protein and apoptosis suppressor; antiapoptotic signal in expanding progenitor pool
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA splicing; supports translational regulation
Early GMP + GMP-Cycle composition (79.5%): Proliferation-dominant, not mono-committed (GMP-Mono only 20%)
suggested_validation: Validate via ribosomal profiling or polysome analysis in sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono; confirm translation rate elevation using puromycin incorporation assays; assess whether signature correlates with Ki67+ cycling status and MKI67 expression in raw data to distinguish proliferation from lineage commitment

programme_name: Myeloid antimicrobial response and innate immunity
functional_description: This signature represents a CD14 classical monocyte programme centered on S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A6/A4) that function as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and antimicrobial effectors, coupled with cytoplasmic/granular proteases and innate immune executors. The dominant S100 proteins form heterodimers (calprotectin S100A8/A9) with critical roles in monocyte activation, recruitment, bacterial killing, and inflammatory amplification.
key_evidence: S100A8: DAMP, calprotectin component, TLR4 co-ligand, antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory hallmark of activated CD14 monocytes
S100A9: DAMP, calprotectin partner, NF-κB activator, zinc scavenger limiting bacterial growth
S100A12: DAMP, EN-RAGE protein, RAGE ligand, exacerbates monocyte inflammatory response
S100A6: Calcium-binding regulator of cytoskeletal dynamics and monocyte migration
S100A4: DAMP, pro-metastatic S100, upregulated in inflammatory monocytes
FCN1: Ficolin-1, pattern recognition receptor of innate immunity, complement pathway activation
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear differentiation antigen, lineage marker of monocyte maturation
LYZ: Lysozyme, antimicrobial bactericidal enzyme secreted by monocytes
CAPG: Actin capping protein regulating monocyte migration and extravasation
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein supporting monocyte mobilization
GRN: Granulin precursor, growth factor and antimicrobial molecule
CSTA: Cystatin, cysteine protease inhibitor protecting monocyte integrity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm S100A8/A9 high expression in CD14+CCR2+ classical monocytes; single-cell qPCR or RNA-FISH validation of S100A8/A9/A12 co-expression; functional assay measuring calprotectin secretion and antimicrobial activity in response to TLR agonists (LPS, Pam3CSK4)

functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor commitment with active antibacterial effector programmes and chromatin remodelling. The dominance of Early ProMono (60.5%) combined with elevated LYZ, RNASE2, and AZU1 indicates acquisition of monocytic antimicrobial capacity. Concurrent upregulation of chromatin-associated proteins (HMGN1, HMGN2, H2AFZ, HMGB1) suggests transcriptional priming for terminal monocyte differentiation.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte lysosomal enzyme, peak early ProMono differentiation
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease, monocyte-specific bactericidal activity
AZU1: azurocidin precursor, neutrophil-monocyte bifurcation marker (elevated in ProMono, not mature Mono)
HMGN1/HMGN2: chromatin opening factors associated with active transcriptional programmes during commitment
PTMA: antiapoptotic protein enabling survival during intensive transcriptional remodelling
HSP90B1: ER chaperone supporting protein folding load during secretory pathway maturation
RNASE2/LGALS1: innate immune effectors characteristic of early ProMono vs GMP
Early ProMono enrichment (60.5%) dominant over GMP-Mono (34.0%), confirming committed progenitor state
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry: LYZ+ CD34+ CSF1R+ MS4A3+ in Early ProMono gate; confirm absence of CD14/FCGR1A surface expression typical of Late ProMono; verify MPO/ELANE transcript remains present (distinguishing from CD14 Mono terminal maturation); quantify RNASE2/AZU1 expression difference between ProMono and CD14 Mono monocytes.

functional_description: This signature captures active protein synthesis and ribosomal biogenesis in proliferating GMP-Cycle and GMP-Mono cells. The dominant ribosomal protein genes (RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17) reflect the elevated translational demand of cycling progenitors, while MPO and PRSS57 indicate early myeloid lineage priming with granule protease components.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components; 6 of top 15 genes indicating active protein synthesis in dividing cells
MPO: signature myeloid enzyme marking early differentiation commitment in GMP populations
HMGN1, HMGN2, H2AFZ: chromatin remodeling factors supporting transcriptional activity in cycling progenitors
GMP-Cycle dominance (53.5%): ribosomal signature enriched in S/G2/M phases
UQCRH, PPIA: metabolic and proteostasis support for biosynthetically active cells
PRSS57: azurophil granule serine protease; myeloid lineage maturation marker
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry: co-stain RPS/RPL gene expression (via translating ribosome affinity purification or polysome profiling) with Ki67 and MPO in sorted GMP-Cycle vs Early GMP populations. Compare ribosomal protein abundance between cycling and non-cycling GMP subsets. Confirm myeloid commitment by CD34/CD33/MPO/PRSS57 immunophenotyping.

functional_description: This signature reflects early commitment to monocytic lineage with robust activation of antimicrobial effector proteins and innate immune machinery. The dominance of S100A8/A9 (calprotectin complex), LYZ, and RNASE2 indicates priming of pathogen recognition and bactericidal capacity characteristic of Early ProMono stage, while concurrent expression of chromatin remodelers (HMGB1/2, H2AFZ/V) supports active transcriptional reconfiguration during commitment.
key_evidence: S100A8/S100A9: Calprotectin heterodimer—hallmark of Early ProMono inflammatory priming, peaks before CD14 surface maturation
LYZ: Lysozyme—monocytic antimicrobial marker, elevated in ProMono vs GMP
RNASE2: Ribonuclease—non-secretory antimicrobial effector specific to myeloid commitment
HMGB1/HMGB2: Chromatin architectural proteins driving transcriptional accessibility during ProMono differentiation
H2AFZ/H2AFV: Histone variants enriched in actively remodeling chromatin during lineage commitment
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator—supports active cytoskeletal reorganization in dividing Early ProMono
CSTA: Cystatin—protease inhibitor balancing intracellular proteolysis during monocyte maturation
82% Early ProMono composition: Strong enrichment validates Early ProMono rather than Late ProMono or mature CD14 Mono stage
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: Sort on S100A8/A9 co-expression and MS4A3 to validate Early ProMono identity; confirm absence of CD14 surface and low MPO/ELANE to exclude GMP-Mono; RNA-seq on sorted Early ProMono to verify antimicrobial gene module co-activation with KLF4/IRF8 targets.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte differentiation toward antimicrobial effector function, driven by accumulation of secreted and granular proteins involved in innate immune responses. The dominance of S100 calprotectin components (S100A8/A9/A12) and downstream myeloid differentiation markers indicates maturation of professional phagocytes primed for pathogen recognition and killing.
key_evidence: S100A8: Core calprotectin subunit; canonical CD14 monocyte antimicrobial effector protein
S100A9: Partner subunit of S100A8/A9 heterodimer; DAMP and bactericidal factor
S100A12: S100 family member upregulated in inflammatory monocytes; RAGE ligand
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor for PAMP sensing and complement-mediated phagocytosis
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen; marker of monocyte/granulocyte lineage commitment
VCAN: Versican; ECM remodeling supporting inflammatory infiltration and tissue recruitment
GRN: Granulin precursor; secreted immunomodulatory mediator with phagocytosis-enhancing properties
CSTA: Cystatin A; cysteine protease inhibitor regulating antimicrobial cathepsin activity
GLRX: Glutaredoxin; antioxidant enzyme supporting ROS management during oxidative burst
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry co-staining of S100A8/A9 with CD14/CD64/FCN1; confirm protein localization to granules by immunofluorescence; measure antimicrobial activity (bacterial killing assays, phagocytosis with opsonized pathogens); assess functional dependence on TLR4/CD14/MyD88 signaling using LPS stimulation and receptor blockade.

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation and iron homeostasis
functional_description: This signature reflects a mature CD14 monocyte programme centred on antigen presentation and lysosomal proteolysis for MHC-II processing, coupled with iron storage and oxidative stress management. The dominance of HLA class II genes (HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQB1) and CD74 indicates active antigen-presenting cell function, while FTH1 and ferritin-related iron buffering support metabolic demands under inflammatory conditions.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQB1: core MHC-II heterodimer machinery for antigen presentation
CD74: invariant chain essential for MHC-II assembly and antigen processing
CTSS: lysosomal cathepsin S critical for peptide generation in MHC-II compartments
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for intracellular iron storage and ROS protection in activated monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor for immunoreceptor signalling in antigen-presenting cells
CST3: cystatin for cysteine protease regulation during antigen processing
ZFP36: mRNA stability factor controlling inflammatory response dynamics
COTL1: actin cytoskeleton remodelling supporting phagocytosis and antigen capture
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DR+ CD14+ monocytes; functional assays of antigen presentation capacity (FACS-sorted population with allogeneic T-cell co-cultures); measure labile iron pools and ROS production (DHE/DHF staining); confirm absence of pro-inflammatory cytokine signature (TNF, IL-1β, IL-6 qPCR) to distinguish from classical LPS-activated monocytes.

functional_description: This signature represents classical monocyte (CD14+) antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory effector functions, centered on S100 alarmins, pattern recognition, and innate immune sensing. The dominance of S100A8/A9/A12 (calprotectin components) indicates activated myeloid cells primed for bacterial PAMP responses and neutrophil recruitment. Integration of CD14, FCN1, and CXCL8 supports TLR-mediated inflammatory signaling and monocyte-driven acute inflammation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical inflammatory alarmin and calprotectin component (S100A8/A9 heterocomplex); primary driver of neutrophil recruitment and PAMP-amplification in CD14+ monocytes
S100A8: Calprotectin heavy chain; zinc-sequestering alarmin with antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory properties; elevated in bacterial infection and sterile inflammation
S100A12: Calgranulin C; S100 family alarmin with TLR4-agonist properties; amplifies inflammatory loops in activated monocytes
CD14: LPS co-receptor and TLR4/TLR2 adaptor; essential for endotoxin sensing and LBP-mediated bacterial recognition; defines classical monocyte identity
CXCL8: IL-8 chemokine; primary neutrophil recruiter and angiogenic factor; downstream of NF-κB/AP-1 in TLR-activated monocytes
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition molecule recognizing acetylated PAMPs; complement-independent innate immunity in myeloid cells
PLAUR: uPAR; amplifies TLR signaling and integrin-mediated adhesion; supports monocyte extravasation and tissue infiltration
NAMPT: NAD biosynthesis enzyme; supports energetic demands of activated immune responses and SIRT1-mediated inflammatory regulation
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron homeostasis in inflammatory contexts; protects against ROS-mediated damage during oxidative burst
S100A4/A6: Additional S100 family members; support calcium signaling and cytoskeletal dynamics in activated myeloid cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm CD14++CD16- identity with S100A9+CXCL8+ phenotype. RT-qPCR/immunofluorescence: validate S100A8/A9 as top drivers in isolated CD14 monocytes ± LPS/TNF stimulation. Functional assays: neutrophil recruitment via S100A8/A9 and CXCL8 secretion; TLR4-pathway dependency via CD14 blocking. Spatial transcriptomics: confirm enrichment in inflammatory infiltrates vs. homeostatic bone marrow niches.

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Metabolic Activation and Innate Response
functional_description: This signature captures metabolic reprogramming and innate immune effector functions in classical CD14 monocytes, characterized by enhanced NAD+ biosynthesis, iron metabolism, and inflammatory mediator production. The program reflects metabolic priming for sustained pro-inflammatory responses and antimicrobial activity, consistent with bacterial PAMP-responsive monocyte activation.
key_evidence: NAMPT: NAD+ salvage pathway activation, supporting energy metabolism and inflammatory signaling in activated monocytes
ZFP36L1: Early response gene and TIS11 family member, post-transcriptional regulation of inflammatory mediators (TNF, IL-6)
CXCL8: Pro-inflammatory chemokine directly induced by TLR/NF-κB signaling, key CD14 mono effector cytokine
LYZ: Lysozyme production, bactericidal antimicrobial function characteristic of differentiated CD14 monocytes
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain, iron metabolism and stress response in metabolically active immune cells
S100A12: Damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP), pro-inflammatory amplification in innate immunity
BCL2A1: Anti-apoptotic protein in inflammatory monocytes, extended survival during immune activation
PLIN2: Lipid droplet accumulation, metabolic remodeling in activated macrophage/monocyte lineage
MAFB: Transcription factor for monocyte/macrophage differentiation and inflammatory regulation
HK2: Glycolytic enzyme supporting Warburg-like metabolic shift in activated immune cells
SLC25A37: Mitochondrial iron import for heme synthesis, supporting redox metabolism and ROS generation
suggested_validation: Validate through flow cytometry (CD14+CCR2+ gate) with NAMPT, CXCL8, S100A12 intracellular staining and metabolic assays (Seahorse glyco/mito stress); confirm inflammatory response via LPS stimulation with measurement of IL-8, TNF-α secretion and lysozyme activity

functional_description: This CD14 monocyte signature reflects active lysosomal/phagolysosomal function with prominent cysteine protease activity (CTSS) for antigen processing and bacterial degradation, coupled with iron storage and sequestration (FTH1) to limit microbial iron acquisition and manage oxidative stress. The constellation of genes supports a mature, antimicrobial phagocytic phenotype optimized for pathogen containment rather than inflammatory cytokine production.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease essential for proteolytic degradation of internalized bacterial antigens and phagolysosomal killing
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron sequestration; restricts bacterial siderophore scavenging and buffers ROS-induced iron toxicity
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for Fcγ and complement receptors; bridges phagocytic pattern recognition to downstream signaling
FCN1: ficolin lectin for pattern recognition and complement pathway activation on bacterial surfaces
LYZ: lysozyme for peptidoglycan degradation; bactericidal enzyme highly expressed in mature phagocytes
MNDA: myeloid-restricted nuclear factor marking mature monocyte/granulocyte differentiation state
TMSB4X: actin dynamics regulator supporting phagocytic cup formation and phagolysosomal trafficking
FCER1G: FcγR gamma-chain for high-affinity IgG receptor signaling in immune complex clearance
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14+ monocytes for CTSS and FTH1 protein expression; quantify lysosomal pH and ROS in CTSS-high vs CTSS-low CD14 monocytes; assess phagocytic capacity using opsonized bacteria or beads; RNA-seq validation of TYROBP/FCER1G-dependent signaling pathways in response to IgG-immune complexes.

functional_description: This signature reflects a type I interferon-driven, post-activation state in CD14 monocytes characterized by upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) and calcium-binding proteins. The programme encompasses antiviral defence mechanisms, cytoskeletal remodelling, and cysteine protease inhibition, suggesting monocytes responding to viral PAMPs or secondary type I IFN signalling rather than primary TLR4/LPS stimulation.
key_evidence: ISG15: canonical type I interferon-stimulated gene, marks IFN-α/β signalling axis
IFI6: ISG family member, interferon response effector
IFITM3: interferon-induced transmembrane antiviral protein, restricts viral entry
S100A6, S100A4, S100A11: calcium-binding proteins, cytoskeletal regulation and cell migration
AIF1: allograft inflammatory factor, IFN-γ/cytokine-induced macrophage activation
APOBEC3A: ISG-associated, APOBEC family with antimicrobial nucleic acid editing function
LST1: LPS and IFN-γ-responsive membrane protein, lymphocyte inhibition
CST3: cystatin superfamily cysteine protease inhibitor, immune regulation
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain, amplifies pattern recognition signalling
PSAP: saposin precursor, involved in lipid antigen presentation and cellular homeostasis
MT2A: metallothionein, oxidative stress and metal detoxification response
suggested_validation: Compare ISG signature intensity across CD14 vs CD16 Mono; correlate with type I IFN pathway scores (IRF7, IRF9, STAT1); validate with stimulation experiments (IFN-α vs LPS vs poly(I:C)) and single-cell RNA-seq trajectory analysis to distinguish primary viral sensing from secondary IFN-priming. Assess relationship to CD64 (FCGR1A) expression and oxidative burst capacity.

programme_name: CD14 monocyte lysosomal proteolysis iron metabolism
functional_description: This signature reflects a lysosomal and oxidative stress response programme in classical CD14 monocytes, characterized by robust expression of cysteine proteases (CTSS), iron storage (FTH1), and antimicrobial effectors. The co-expression of TYROBP (DAP12), CLEC7A, and FCN1 suggests pattern recognition receptor signalling coupled to phagocytic and degradative capacity, while elevated NAMPT indicates metabolic rewiring towards NAD+ biosynthesis to support inflammatory and oxidative functions.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and pathogen degradation in monocytes
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron storage and ROS detoxification during immune activation
TYROBP: ITAM adaptor linking C-type lectin receptors to inflammatory signalling in myeloid cells
CLEC7A: Dectin-1 pattern recognition receptor for fungal/bacterial PAMPs on CD14 monocytes
FCN1: ficolin-1 for complement-independent innate opsonization and phagocytosis
LYZ: lysozyme for bacterial cell wall degradation, hallmark of classical monocyte antimicrobial activity
NAMPT: NAD+ salvage pathway supporting NAD+-dependent energy metabolism and immune function
HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB5: antigen presentation capacity of CD14 monocytes
TMSB4X: actin dynamics supporting migration and cell shape changes during recruitment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+ monocytes for CTSS, FTH1, and CLEC7A protein expression; functional assays measuring lysosomal protease activity and iron-dependent ROS production; single-cell RNA-seq trajectory analysis to map this signature to inflammatory/phagocytic monocyte states.

functional_description: This signature defines classical CD14+ monocytes with enhanced antimicrobial and phagocytic capacity, characterized by high expression of pattern recognition receptors (CD14, FCN1, CLEC4E), bactericidal enzymes (LYZ, CTSS), and innate immune activation markers. The programme reflects terminal differentiation of CD14 monocytes towards tissue-resident effector functions with robust bacterial sensing and proteolytic degradation capabilities.
key_evidence: CD14: Master surface marker for classical monocytes; co-receptor for TLR4/LPS sensing
LYZ: Bactericidal lysozyme; direct peptidoglycan degradation of Gram+ bacteria
S100A9: Calprotectin component; antimicrobial, NF-κB activation, myeloid differentiation marker
MNDA: Myeloid-lineage specific nuclear antigen; monocyte/granulocyte differentiation marker
VCAN: Extracellular matrix versican; supports monocyte migration and tissue infiltration
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition lectin; complement pathway activation
CTSS: Lysosomal cathepsin S; antigen processing and bacterial proteolysis
CLEC4E: C-type lectin; PAMP recognition; enhanced in inflammatory monocytes
FPR1: Formyl peptide receptor; bacterial N-formyl peptide sensing; chemotaxis
RGS2: Negative feedback on G-protein signaling; prevents excessive inflammatory response
THBS1: Thrombospondin; ECM remodeling; supports monocyte infiltration into tissues
TMEM176A/B: Lysosomal/phagosomal proteins; support proteolytic function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14++CD16- co-expression with CD64 (FCGR1A), CD11b, and lysozyme intracellular staining. Functional assays: phagocytosis of opsonized bacteria, ROS production post-LPS/LBP stimulation. scRNAseq validation of PAMP receptor co-expression (TLR2/TLR4/CD14/LBP) and inflammasome components (NLRP3, CASP1, GSDMD) in this population.

functional_description: This signature defines non-classical monocytes with elevated iron homeostasis (FTH1), actin-driven cytoskeletal dynamics (COTL1, TMSB4X, AIF1, RHOC), and intrinsic antiviral capacity (IFITM3). The programme integrates Fc-receptor signalling (FCGR3A, FCER1G) for ADCC with stress-response and metabolic reprogramming (SAT1, YBX1), consistent with patrolling CD16 monocyte surveillance and immune activation.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 marker; ADCC and immune complex clearance define non-classical monocytes
IFITM3: Type I IFN-induced antiviral effector; expected in patrolling CD16 subset
FTH1: Iron storage upregulation; CD16 monocytes exhibit elevated oxidative metabolism
COTL1: Actin-binding regulator; supports dynamic crawling and vascular surveillance
AIF1: Cytokine-induced calcium-actin sensor; macrophage activation and endothelial interaction
LST1: Membrane protein enhanced by LPS/IFN-γ; innate immune licensing of CD16 monocytes
TMSB4X: Actin polymerization control; enables rapid migration and vascular patrolling
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain; amplifies ADCC and IgG-dependent activation
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism; metabolic shift in activated vs resting monocytes
S100A11: Calcium-binding protein; stress response and inflammatory priming
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD16+CD14low/- FCGR3A+CX3CR1high co-staining with IFITM3, FTH1 intracellular; ATAC-seq or ChIP for NR4A family (NR4A1/NR4A2) binding to signature loci; RNA-FISH of FTH1/IFITM3 in CD16 vs CD14 monocyte subsets; functional assay of ADCC capacity in FCGR3A+ cells.

programme_name: Lysosomal proteolysis and oxidative stress response
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte state specialised in intracellular antimicrobial defence through lysosomal cysteine protease activity (CTSS, CSTA, CST3) and oxidative stress management (GPX1, FTH1). The combination of TYROBP-mediated ITAM signalling, S100A6/A9 calcium-binding proteins, and iron/ROS homeostasis indicates activated monocytes primed for phagocytosis and intracellular pathogen degradation.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor mediating TLR and Fc receptor signalling in myeloid cells
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and intracellular pathogen degradation
CST3, CSTA: Cystatin family cysteine protease inhibitors controlling lysosomal protease activity
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase detoxifying H2O2 generated during oxidative burst post-phagocytosis
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain buffering iron and ROS in activated monocytes
S100A6, S100A9: Calcium-binding proteins elevated in inflammatory monocyte activation
VCAN: Versican ECM component indicating stromal interaction and inflammatory infiltration
AP1S2, MT-CO3: Supporting vesicular trafficking and mitochondrial oxidative capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying CTSS, GPX1 activity and ROS production (DHE staining) in CD14+CD16- monocytes; immunofluorescence confirming TYROBP and S100A9 co-expression in activated mono; functional assays measuring intracellular bacterial killing post-opsonisation.

functional_description: This signature reflects a metabolically active, proliferative state driven by oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis capacity, coupled with chromatin remodelling that maintains transcriptional competence. The enrichment of mitochondrial respiratory chain components and ribosomal proteins indicates Early ProMono cells are energetically prepared for rapid differentiation and effector function acquisition, while HMGB family proteins and PTMA suggest active chromatin reorganisation supporting monocytic gene activation programmes.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Oxidative phosphorylation capacity and ATP generation required for metabolically demanding monocyte commitment and proliferation
RPS24, PPIA: Ribosomal protein and protein folding machinery supporting sustained biosynthesis during differentiation
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2: Chromatin-associated proteins maintaining open chromatin state for promonocytic transcriptional programmes
S100A8: Antimicrobial calcium-binding protein with high expression in activated myeloid lineage, consistent with early monocyte identity
STMN1: Cell-cycle regulator and microtubule dynamics modulator supporting proliferation in Early ProMono compartment
Early ProMono enrichment (40.5%): Dominant cell-type composition aligns with metabolic priming preceding final monocytic differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate by metabolic flux analysis (Seahorse) and FACS-sorted Early ProMono (CD34+CD38+CD123-CD45RA-) vs Late ProMono (CD34-CD14lo), measuring OXPHOS dependency and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) at monocytic transcription factor binding sites (KLF4, IRF8, PU.1 targets). Cross-reference with IRF8-target genes to confirm commitment phase.

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis and ribosomal biogenesis in early GMP-stage progenitors (Early GMP 46%, GMP-Mono 35%), marking a metabolically active, proliferative precursor state. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A) coupled with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and MPO indicates concurrent active myeloid differentiation commitment with high translational demand during GMP expansion.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A: Ribosomal structural proteins indicating active protein synthesis capacity in proliferating progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis during GMP differentiation
MPO: Myeloid peroxidase marker of myeloid lineage priming, consistent with Early GMP/GMP-Mono composition (81% combined)
PTMA: Nucleoplasmic protein with anti-apoptotic function, supporting survival of metabolically active progenitors
HMGN1: Chromatin-associated protein enabling transcriptionally active chromatin landscape during myeloid commitment
PPIA, EEF1B2: Protein folding and translation efficiency factors reflecting elevated biosynthetic demands
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry sorting for CD34+KIT+MPO+ Early GMP and CD34+/−KIT−MPO+ GMP-Mono, followed by qRT-PCR quantification of ribosomal protein cluster expression. Perform polysome profiling to confirm elevated translation rate. Compare 80S/40S ribosomal subunit ratios between GMP stages and mature monocytes to confirm progenitor-specific translational activity.

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14+ classical monocyte state characterised by high expression of S100 alarmin proteins (S100A8/A9/A6/A12) involved in PAMP sensing and inflammation, coupled with enhanced mitochondrial oxidative metabolism (MT-CO2/CO3) supporting inflammatory effector functions. The programme is dominated by myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA, FCN1) and innate immune pattern recognition (CD14, CD36), consistent with activated pro-inflammatory monocyte biology.
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical DAMP/PAMP sensor; primary driver of CD14 Mono inflammation and neutrophil recruitment
S100A8: Heterodimerises with S100A9 (calprotectin complex); critical for TLR4 and RAGE signalling
S100A12: S100 family alarmin; potent RAGE ligand amplifying pro-inflammatory cascades
CD14: Master PAMP receptor for LPS/TLR4 cooperation; defines classical monocyte identity
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen; marker of monocyte-granulocyte lineage maturation
FCN1: Ficolins; pattern recognition molecule for innate immunity and complement activation
MT-CO2/MT-CO3: Elevated mitochondrial electron transport; supports energetic demands of pro-inflammatory cytokine production
FOSB: AP-1 component; immediate early transcription factor in response to inflammatory signals
CD36: Scavenger receptor; recognises apoptotic cells and lipid antigens in innate immunity
VCAN: Versican ECM proteoglycan; remodels inflammatory microenvironment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirmation of CD14++CD16- phenotype with elevated S100A8/A9 protein expression (intracellular staining); validate pro-inflammatory potential via LPS stimulation and TNF-α/IL-6/IL-1β secretion; assess mitochondrial OXPHOS activity by seahorse analysis.

programme_name: Early ProMono metabolic and antimicrobial priming
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ribosomal protein synthesis in Early ProMono cells, coupled with upregulation of the antimicrobial effector RNASE2 and the monocyte lineage marker LYZ. The enrichment of metabolic and biosynthetic machinery, along with chromatin remodeling factors (HMGB2, HMGN2), supports the metabolic demands and transcriptional reprogramming of committed monocyte progenitors transitioning away from multipotency.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1: Early ProMono cells exhibit elevated mitochondrial respiratory chain activity required for increased ATP production during differentiation
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease upregulated in committed monocyte progenitors, consistent with pre-egress monocytic identity
LYZ: Lysozyme is a canonical monocyte lineage marker and appears in Early ProMono as commitment marker, distinguishing from GMP
RPS26, PPIA: Enhanced protein synthesis machinery supporting rapid transcriptional/translational reprogramming of ProMono stage
HMGB2, HMGN2, PTMA, HIST1H1E: Chromatin remodeling and histone modifications facilitating ProMono-specific transcriptional programmes
GSTP1: Oxidative stress detoxification supporting increased metabolic flux in differentiating progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: confirm MS4A3+/CSF1R+ Early ProMono signature; RT-qPCR for LYZ, RNASE2, KLF4, IRF8 in FACS-sorted Early ProMono vs GMP; assess mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM) and ROS levels in Early ProMono to validate metabolic activation state.

programme_name: Monocyte Innate Immunity and Antimicrobial Response
functional_description: This signature reflects the antimicrobial effector and damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) response programme of classical CD14+ monocytes. The dominant S100A family genes (S100A8, S100A9, S100A12, S100A4, S100A6) encode alarmin-like calcium-binding proteins that function as potent pro-inflammatory DAMPs and antimicrobial effectors, supporting bacterial killing and inflammatory recruitment. Supporting genes including FCN1 (ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor), CSTA (cysteine protease inhibitor), and VCAN (extracellular matrix proteoglycan) indicate active engagement in innate immune sensing and tissue remodelling during infection or inflammation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical DAMP and antimicrobial alarmin; elevated in inflammatory monocytes; forms heterodimers (S100A8/A9) with TLR4 ligand activity
S100A8: Co-expressed alarmin and PAMP-associated molecule; amplifies pro-inflammatory signalling in classical monocytes
S100A12: RAGE ligand and DAMP; contributes to monocyte recruitment and activation during infection
S100A4: Calcium-binding alarmin involved in monocyte migration and inflammatory response
FCN1: Pattern recognition receptor (ficolin-1); activates complement and supports bacterial opsonisation
CSTA: Cystatin; regulates cysteine proteases in antimicrobial and inflammatory contexts
VCAN: Extracellular matrix versican; involved in monocyte extravasation and tissue inflammation
MAFB: Lineage-determining transcription factor for monocyte/macrophage differentiation; supports CD14+ identity
CD14 Mono composition 79%: Confirms classical monocyte activation state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: S100A8/A9 protein surface/intracellular staining on gated CD14+ CD16- monocytes; measure FCN1 and FCGR1A co-expression; TLR4 stimulation assays to confirm IL-1β and TNF-α production from S100A-high monocytes; assess calcium flux responses and phagocytic capacity in this population

programme_name: Myeloid lysosomal proteolytic and innate immune machinery
functional_description: This signature represents a core myeloid differentiation and activation programme centred on lysosomal proteolysis, calcium signalling, and innate immune receptor-mediated effector functions. The dominance of FCER1G, TYROBP (DAP12), and CTSS indicates a differentiated, phagocytically and proteolytically active monocyte subset with capacity for antigen processing and Fc receptor-driven activation, whilst S100 proteins and actin-regulatory factors (TMSB4X, AIF1) support cytoskeletal remodelling required for migration and immune surveillance.
key_evidence: FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma-chain subunit essential for ITAM-dependent signalling in both CD16 (FCGR3A-paired) and CD14 monocytes; ranks #1
TYROBP: DAP12 scaffolding adaptor protein co-associates with FCGR3A and activating receptors; critical for antibody-dependent cellular activation
CTSS: Lysosomal cathepsin S required for antigen processing and presentation; hallmark of differentiated myeloid cells
LST1: LPS and IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein; marks activated, pathogen-responsive monocytes
S100A6, S100A11, S100A4: Calcium-binding proteins supporting cytoskeletal dynamics and cell migration in activated monocytes
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration protein enabling cytoskeletal flexibility for patrolling and extravasation
AIF1: IFN- and cytokine-inducible actin-binding protein promoting macrophage activation
PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lysosomal hydrolase trafficking and innate immune responses
suggested_validation: Validate CD16 Mono enrichment (48% of top 200) by flow cytometry quantification of FCER1G, TYROBP co-expression with FCGR3A (CD16) and CX3CR1; confirm absence of classical monocyte markers (CCR2, high CD14); assess functional capacity for ADCC and lysosomal protease activity in sorted FCER1G+TYROBP+ CD16 Mono versus CD14 Mono baseline

functional_description: This signature reflects robust protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP cells, characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and RNA processing machinery. The dominance of ribosomal and translational components indicates high biosynthetic demand consistent with active progenitor proliferation and differentiation priming.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins—core translational machinery elevated in biosynthetically active Early GMP
RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—large subunit components required for translation elongation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor with GTPase exchange activity—directly facilitates aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to ribosome
HNRNPA1: Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein regulating pre-mRNA processing and splicing—supports myeloid differentiation transcriptome remodelling
NPM1: Nucleophosmin involved in ribosome biogenesis and protein chaperoning—marks proliferative progenitor state
GAPDH, LDHB: Glycolytic and anaerobic metabolism enzymes—energy supply for biosynthetically demanding progenitor stage
SNRPE: spliceosomal component—active pre-mRNA processing during differentiation priming
suggested_validation: Confirm Early GMP identity via flow cytometry (CD34+/KIT+/CD13+/CD15lo); assess ribosomal protein co-expression by qPCR across GMP substages; verify distinction from GMP-Cycle via Ki67/PCNA scoring; correlate ribosomal signature intensity with proximity to lineage commitment markers (IRF8, CEBPE, KLF4 onset)

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 classical monocyte activation focused on antimicrobial effector functions and innate immune sensing. Dominated by S100A8/A9 (calprotectin), a hallmark of activated myeloid cells with bactericidal and immunomodulatory properties, alongside lysozyme (LYZ), ficolin-1 (FCN1), and cystatin A (CSTA) that comprise the antimicrobial arsenal. Supporting metabolic and oxidative stress responses through glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, PKM), antioxidant defense (GPX1), and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (NDUFB9).
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical CD14 monocyte activation marker; forms S100A8/A9 heterodimer (calprotectin) with potent antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory signaling via TLR4/RAGE
S100A8: Partner protein in calprotectin complex; elevated in inflammatory monocyte responses to bacterial PAMPs
LYZ: Bacterial cell wall degradation (peptidoglycan); key monocyte antimicrobial protein secreted upon activation
FCN1: Ficolin family PAMP recognition receptor; complement pathway activation and bacterial opsonization
CSTA: Cystatin A cysteine protease inhibitor; regulates granule proteases during antimicrobial responses
GPX1: Antioxidant defense against ROS generated during oxidative burst via NADPH oxidase activation
GAPDH, PKM: Glycolytic enzymes supporting energy demands of activated monocyte immune functions
NDUFB9: Complex I mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation; supports ATP production in activated states
GRN: Granulin precursor; pro-inflammatory mediator involved in immune cell recruitment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm S100A8/A9 co-expression in CD14++CD16- monocytes; RNAseq validation of calprotectin signature in response to TLR4/TLR2 stimulation; functional assay of antimicrobial capacity (bacterial killing, phagocytosis) in S100A8/A9-high subset

functional_description: This signature represents a late-stage monocyte progenitor and early CD14+ monocyte programme characterized by upregulation of antimicrobial proteins, calcium-binding S100 family members, and metabolic reprogramming. The dominance of S100A8/A9 paired with LYZ, MNDA, and CSTA indicates terminal differentiation toward an innate immune effector state rather than active ProMono commitment.
key_evidence: S100A8: Sentinel marker of mature monocyte/early CD14+ mono activation; calcium-mediated inflammatory signaling
S100A9: Functional partner of S100A8 in neutrophil-like antimicrobial response; abundant in circulating CD14+ mono
LYZ: Core monocyte marker; bactericidal function consistent with post-commitment maturation
MNDA: Myeloid-lineage specific nuclear antigen; marks granulocyte-monocyte differentiation completion
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor supporting intracellular proteolysis control in mature myeloid cells
FCN1: Pattern recognition receptor for complement-mediated immunity; elevated in CD14+ versus progenitors
S100A12: S100 calprotectin component; pro-inflammatory alarmin in mature monocytes
CAPG: Actin-regulatory protein enabling cytoskeletal dynamics required for mature myeloid motility
suggested_validation: Confirm via flow cytometry co-expression of S100A8/A9 with CD14 and CD11b to distinguish Late ProMono/Early CD14+ Mono from GMP; validate absence of MPO and ELANE; assess CCR2/S1PR1 expression to confirm egress-competent state rather than early commitment phase.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis capacity and translational activity in early-stage GMP progenitors, particularly those undergoing proliferation. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0), translation factors (EEF1B2), and mitochondrial OXPHOS components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, NDUFS5) indicates metabolic preparation for rapid cell division and differentiation, characteristic of the GMP-Cycle and Early GMP compartments.
key_evidence: RPS24/RPS23/RPL37A/RPLP0/RPS17/RPS2: Consensus ribosomal subunit proteins dominating signature—hallmark of progenitors with high translational demand
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis during active GMP proliferation
MT-CO2/MT-CO3/NDUFS5: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components reflecting elevated oxidative metabolism in cycling progenitors
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator associated with cell cycle checkpoint control
MPO: Single myeloid differentiation marker present but minor—indicates early GMP before full myeloid priming
PTMA: Nuclear/cytoplasmic anti-apoptotic factor supporting survival of metabolically active progenitors
HMGN1: Chromatin remodeling protein associated with transcriptionally active, open chromatin typical of GMP
Cell composition: 73% Early GMP + GMP-Cycle dominance confirms progenitor proliferative state rather than differentiated mono compartment
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry co-expression of CD34+KIT+CD13+ (GMP) with high MitoTracker/TMRM (OXPHOS activity) and BrdU incorporation (S-phase). Confirm by qPCR that this signature is enriched in sorted Early GMP vs mature CD14+ monocytes. Assess whether MPO remains suppressed (ruling out late GMP/ProMono transition).

programme_name: Ribosomal and translational capacity early GMP
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein (RPS/RPL family) and translation elongation factor expression in Early GMP-stage progenitors, coupled with mitochondrial respiratory chain activity. The dominant early GMP composition (74.5%) and enrichment of protein synthesis machinery indicates heightened biosynthetic demand during early myeloid progenitor expansion, prior to terminal monopoiesis-specific differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPS26, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components; consistent coordinate upregulation in high-proliferation progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity; marks active protein synthesis capacity
RPLP0: 60S ribosomal stalk protein; essential for translation initiation and elongation
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation; elevated in cycling progenitors
HNRNPA1: Pre-mRNA processing and RNA stability; supports mRNA availability during biosynthetic phase
MT-ND1, UQCRH: Mitochondrial Complex I and III components; ATP/NADH provision for anabolic demand
SNRPE: Spliceosomal U snRNP core component; marks active pre-mRNA processing in proliferating cells
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry: CD34+ early GMP should show elevated ribosomal protein content and MitoTracker intensity versus CD34− monocytes. Confirm GMP-Cycle fraction has higher expression of ribosomal genes (RPL/RPS) and PCNA/MKI67 co-expression. Check that monocytic commitment (CSF1R/CD64 upregulation, MPO priming) occurs with relative downregulation of this ribosomal signature.

programme_name: Myeloid antimicrobial granule and damage-associated molecular pattern
functional_description: This signature captures the innate immune effector state of classical CD14 monocytes, dominated by S100 alarmin proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A4/A6) and antimicrobial granule components (FCN1, CSTA).
