The coordinated upregulation of calcium-binding S100 family members and cysteine protease inhibitors reflects activated monocyte degranulation, pathogen-associated molecular pattern sensing, and cytokine/chemokine production in response to infection or sterile inflammation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical alarmin and DAMP; forms S100A8/A9 heterodimer (calprotectin) with potent pro-inflammatory and antimicrobial activity
S100A8: Co-partner in calprotectin complex; elevated in monocyte activation and bacterial infection
S100A12: S100 family member with RAGE-binding capacity; monocyte-specific alarmin
FCN1: Ficolin-1 pattern recognition receptor in monocyte granules; lectin-complement pathway activation
CSTA: Cystatin A; cysteine protease inhibitor regulating cathepsin activity in phagocytic cells
S100A4: S100 protein involved in cell motility and TLR4 signaling amplification
S100A6: Intracellular calcium-regulated protein; monocyte differentiation marker
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear differentiation antigen; indicator of monocyte lineage maturation
TMSB4X: Actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal remodeling for phagocytosis and migration
VCAN: Versican extracellular matrix component; monocyte-macrophage matrix interactions
HBA1/HBA2/HBB: Hemoglobin subunits; consistent with iron metabolism in inflammatory monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: CD14+CCR2+ monocytes should show elevated S100A8/A9 (MFI), FCN1 surface expression, and MNDA nuclear staining. Functional assays: measure calprotectin (S100A8/A9) secretion upon LPS/TLR4 stimulation; assess phagocytic capacity (IgG opsonized particles) and ROS production. Compare S100A8/A9 expression between steady-state and lipopolysaccharide-activated monocytes via qPCR and intracellular flow cytometry.

programme_name: CD14 Mono Iron Metabolism Stress Response
functional_description: This signature defines a CD14 monocyte state characterized by iron homeostasis, oxidative stress management, and metabolic reprogramming. The program couples ferritin-mediated iron storage (FTH1) with antioxidant defenses (GPX1) and NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT), supporting sustained inflammatory capacity under metabolic constraint. Co-expression of lysozyme (LYZ) and cathepsin S (CTSS) indicates active antimicrobial and antigen-processing functions.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron accumulation and ROS buffering capacity in activated CD14 monocytes
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification during inflammatory oxidative burst
NAMPT: NAD+ salvage pathway supporting mitochondrial function and inflammatory metabolism
LYZ: Canonical monocyte lysosomal enzyme for bacterial peptidoglycan degradation
CTSS: Cathepsin S in MHC-II antigen processing and inflammasome regulation
CEBPD: CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein delta supporting myeloid differentiation
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor coupling Fc receptors and TLR signaling
ZFP36L1: Post-transcriptional stabilization of inflammatory cytokine mRNAs
MAFB: v-maf musculoaponeurotic fibrosarcoma oncogene ortholog B in myeloid maturation
HLA-DRA: MHC class II expression for antigen presentation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+ monocytes for FTH1 (iron), ROS (DHE/CM-H2DCFDA), and phospho-STAT1/STAT3 to confirm metabolic/stress state. RNA-seq on sorted CD14hi FTH1hi vs FTH1lo monocytes to validate iron-linked inflammatory signatures. Test LPS/TNF stimulation kinetics of FTH1, GPX1, NAMPT induction.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in early GMP and GMP-Mono populations (68% of activating cells). The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0), mitochondrial electron transport genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH), and metabolic enzymes (PPIA, GSTP1) indicates active anabolic capacity and ATP generation supporting rapid myeloid progenitor expansion. Inclusion of MPO and STMN1 confirms early myeloid lineage commitment with active cytoskeletal remodelling.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0: ribosomal structural proteins driving protein synthesis in proliferating early GMP
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: oxidative phosphorylation machinery supporting energy demands of progenitor amplification
PTMA: DNA-binding factor and apoptosis antagonist promoting progenitor viability during differentiation
GSTP1: detoxification enzyme protecting rapidly dividing cells from oxidative stress
STMN1: microtubule dynamics regulator essential for cell cycle progression in GMP-Cycle (10% of cohort)
MPO: early myeloid lineage marker confirming GMP-Mono and GMP differentiation trajectory
HMGN1: open chromatin architecture supporting active transcriptional programmes in proliferating progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD34+KIT+CD33+ GMP with CD71 (transferrin receptor) and mitotracker dyes to confirm elevated translation and mitochondrial mass; qPCR validation of MPO, STMN1 expression in FACS-sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono subsets; polysome profiling to quantify active translation in these populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein production and translational capacity in Early GMP cells, with supporting roles for RNA-binding proteins and nucleolar/centrosomal factors. The enrichment of RPS and RPL family members alongside YBX1, HNRNPA1, and NPM1 indicates active protein synthesis required for progenitor self-renewal and rapid proliferation before lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS2, RPS24, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components—hallmark of translational machinery upregulation in metabolically active Early GMP
YBX1: cold shock domain RNA-binding protein regulating translation and mRNA stability; elevated in proliferative progenitors
HNRNPA1: heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein involved in pre-mRNA processing and translation regulation; consistent with active transcription in Early GMP
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating centrosome duplication and cell proliferation; marker of actively cycling Early GMP (70.5% composition)
HMGN1: nucleosomal DNA-binding protein associated with transcriptionally active chromatin; reflects open chromatin in multipotent progenitors
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor; essential for protein synthesis scaling in expanding progenitor pools
LDHB, UQCRH: metabolic enzymes supporting glycolytic and oxidative phosphorylation flux in proliferative cells
PTMA: anti-apoptotic nucleolar protein promoting progenitor survival during expansion
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry sorting Early GMP (CD34+KIT+CD14-CD15-) vs. committed progenitors and measuring ribosome biogenesis markers (UBF, RRN3, fibrillarin); confirm by qRT-PCR on bulk RPS/RPL genes; assess correlation with cell cycle (Ki67/PCNA) and MYB/CEBPA expression in Early GMP subset.

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte state specializing in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation coupled with intracellular iron storage and management. The coordinated upregulation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ complexes with CD74 (invariant chain) indicates enhanced professional antigen presentation capacity, while FTH1 expression suggests active iron metabolism necessary for oxidative stress buffering in inflammatory contexts.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: core HLA class II α-chain; central to antigen presentation in CD14 monocytes
HLA-DRB5: HLA class II β-chain; forms functional heterodimer with HLA-DRA
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP class II complex; independent antigen presentation pathway
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ class II complex; complete MHC-II repertoire
CD74: invariant chain chaperone; essential for MHC-II biogenesis and trafficking
FTH1: heavy-chain ferritin; iron sequestration and ROS detoxification
CST3: cystatin C; protease inhibitor; modulates antigen processing
IFI30: lysosomal thiol reductase; facilitates MHC-II processing in endosomal compartments
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor; pattern recognition supporting antigen uptake
ZFP36L1: mRNA stability regulator; post-transcriptional inflammatory control
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm HLA-DR/DP/DQ surface expression with functional assay of antigen presentation capacity (e.g., allogeneic T-cell proliferation). Iron metabolism validation: measure FTH1 protein and labile iron pools using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. RNAseq: validate coordinated expression of complete MHC-II genes and compare antigen presentation markers between CD14 Mono subsets.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Cytoskeletal and Immune Activation
functional_description: This signature defines non-classical CD16 monocytes (74.5% of activating cells) with enhanced cytoskeletal dynamics, Fc-receptor signalling, and calcium-responsive immunity. The programme emphasizes actin remodelling for vascular patrolling, ADCC capability via FCGR3A, and innate immune activation through ITAM-bearing adaptor proteins.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 marker; defines non-classical monocyte identity and enables antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity
LST1: CD16 Mono-enriched; lymphocyte inhibition and IFN-γ-responsive antimicrobial immunity
AIF1: Interferon-induced, macrophage activation marker; promotes inflammatory responses in patrolling monocytes
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein; critical for cytoskeletal remodelling during vascular crawling and migration
COTL1: Actin-binding protein linked to 5-lipoxygenase; supports migration and eicosanoid signalling
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor; associates with FCGR3A and FcεRI-γ for integrated immune signalling
FCER1G: FcγR and FcεR common γ-chain; essential for Fc-receptor clustering and ADCC activation
S100A11, S100A4: Calcium-binding proteins; regulate cell motility and inflammatory responses
FTH1: Iron storage; indicates oxidative stress handling in activated monocytes
RHOC: GTPase regulating actin dynamics and cell motility during patrolling
MS4A7: MS4A family membrane protein; CD16 Mono-associated immunomodulation
PSAP: Lysosomal saposin precursor; supports antimicrobial autophagy and phagocytosis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry (FCGR3A+CD14-/low CX3CR1+) with functional assays: ADCC killing via FCGR3A engagement, transendothelial migration assays, and live-cell imaging of F-actin dynamics during crawling. RNA-seq validation of actin regulators (TMSB4X, COTL1, RHOC) and interferon-responsive genes in sorted CD16 Mono vs CD14 Mono.

functional_description: This signature reflects activated classical monocytes (CD14 Mono, 80%) engaged in acute innate immune response, characterized by S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex expression—hallmark danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) released during inflammation. The dominance of S100 family members (S100A9, S100A8, S100A6, S100A4) and cytoskeletal regulators (TMSB4X) suggests enhanced cell migration and pro-inflammatory activation, with minor contamination from monocyte progenitors indicating enrichment for activated differentiated monocytes.
key_evidence: S100A9: Core DAMP and myeloid activation marker; S100A8/A9 heterodimer (calprotectin) is quintessential signature of classically activated CD14 monocytes and acute inflammation
S100A8: Partner protein in calprotectin complex; synergistic TLR4 agonist activity with LPS; strongly induced by NF-κB and IRF5 downstream of PAMP sensing
S100A6: S100 family member contributing to cytosolic calcium signaling and inflammation amplification in myeloid cells
S100A4: Migration-associated S100 protein; upregulated in inflammatory monocyte subset; facilitates cell motility during recruitment to inflamed tissues
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein essential for monocyte migration and extravasation; supports chemotaxis toward CCL2 and tissue recruitment
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (M-ficolin); pattern recognition receptor expressed on monocytes; promotes complement activation and bacterial opsonization
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; upregulated in activated monocytes; facilitates cellular adhesion and tissue infiltration during inflammatory response
CSTA: Cystatin-A; cysteine protease inhibitor; expressed in activated myeloid cells to regulate protease activity during inflammation
HBA/HBB/MT-CO2: Elevated metabolic markers indicating enhanced aerobic respiration and ATP production supporting inflammatory effector functions
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+CD16− monocytes with S100A8/A9 and CCR2 to confirm classical monocyte identity; qPCR validation of S100A8/A9 expression in sorted CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono; functional assay measuring TLR-induced cytokine production (IL-1β, TNF-α) in S100A8/A9-high cells to confirm inflammatory activation state.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened translation capacity and protein synthesis machinery in early myeloid progenitors, particularly Early GMP cells (60.5% of activating population). The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and RNA processing components (HNRNPA1, SNRPE, FBL) indicates active ribosome biogenesis supporting rapid proliferation and differentiation demands characteristic of GMP-stage progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins—essential for translation capacity in proliferating progenitors
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor GEF—enables aminoacyl-tRNA delivery during active protein synthesis
NPM1: nucleolar protein with dual roles in ribosome biogenesis and cell cycle progression—elevated in cycling GMP populations
FBL: U3 snRNP component—participates in pre-rRNA processing critical for ribosome assembly
HNRNPA1, SNRPE: RNA-binding proteins in splicing/pre-mRNA processing—support transcriptome plasticity during lineage commitment
HMGN1: nucleosomal DNA-binding protein—marks transcriptionally active chromatin associated with high biosynthetic demand
Early GMP enrichment (60.5%): signature activation in progenitor population requires maximal translation capacity for rapid proliferation and differentiation
suggested_validation: Assess ribosomal protein expression via flow cytometry (S6 phosphorylation as proxy for translation activity) or polysome profiling in sorted Early GMP vs. differentiated monocyte populations. Cross-validate with bulk RNA-seq of GMP-stage cells under FLT3 stimulation to confirm translation machinery upregulation during progenitor expansion versus differentiation-associated downregulation.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal and translational machinery in Early GMP and GMP-Cycle populations, consistent with active protein synthesis demands during progenitor expansion and myeloid commitment. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPL4) and translation factors (EEF1B2) indicates heightened biosynthetic capacity characteristic of proliferating progenitors preparing for lineage-restricted differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components driving translation in proliferating GMP
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, essential for efficient protein elongation
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating centrosome duplication and cell proliferation checkpoints in progenitors
HNRNPA1: pre-mRNA processing and alternative splicing regulation supporting myeloid differentiation programming
HSP90AB1: molecular chaperone enabling signal transduction stability during FLT3/CSF1R pathway activation
YBX1: DNA/RNA binding protein regulating transcription and translation in cycling progenitors
HMGN1: nucleosome remodelling protein associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in Early GMP (61%)
suggested_validation: Validate via ribosomal biogenesis/translation assay (polysome profiling or puromycin labelling) in sorted Early GMP/GMP-Cycle vs mature mono; confirm coordinate upregulation with cell cycle markers (MKI67, CDK1) and early myeloid priming (MPO, ELANE) in the same populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic reprogramming and iron homeostasis in activated CD14 monocytes under inflammatory stress. The programme integrates iron storage (FTH1), NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT), polyamine catabolism (SAT1), and MHC-II antigen presentation machinery, coupled with lysosomal proteolysis for antigenic peptide generation.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage protein; ferritin upregulation indicates oxidative stress response and ROS management in activated CD14 monocytes
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis rate-limiting enzyme; essential for energetic demands and SIRT-dependent metabolic adaptation during inflammation
MAFB: Monocyte master TF (RUNX family ortholog); critical for CD14 monocyte maturation and alternative activation
SAT1: Polyamine metabolism regulator; acetylates spermidine in catabolic pathway supporting cell proliferation control
ZFP36L1: Early response TF (TIS11 family); immediate early gene induced by PAMPs/inflammatory signals; post-transcriptional regulator of cytokine mRNAs
HLA-DRA/HLA-DMA: MHC-II machinery; antigen presentation capacity characteristic of professional APCs (CD14+ monocytes)
CTSS: Lysosomal cathepsin; proteolytic processing of antigens for MHC-II presentation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor; signaling amplification in Fc receptor and TLR complexes during phagocytosis
BCL2A1: Anti-apoptotic factor; survival signal in inflammatory monocytes
CEBPD: C/EBP family member; cooperates with CEBPB/SPI1 in monocyte lineage commitment
CLEC7A: Dectin-1; fungal PAMP pattern recognition receptor on myeloid cells
G0S2: Growth arrest/lipid storage gene; metabolic reprogramming marker
SGK1: Serine/threonine kinase; osmotic stress and nutrient sensing in inflammatory conditions
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: confirm CD14++CD16- phenotype and co-expression of FTH1, CTSS with TLR2/TLR4 stimulation. Functional assays: measure antigen presentation capacity (MHC-II FITC), iron-catalyzed ROS production (DHE), and NAD+ levels under LPS/TNF stimulation. Phospho-flow for TYROBP/ITAM signaling downstream of Fc receptors.

functional_description: This signature reflects classical CD14 monocytes in acute inflammatory activation, characterized by S100A8/A9/A12 calprotectin complex upregulation—canonical damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) sensors and neutrophil chemoattractants. The co-expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISG15, IFI6, IFI44L) alongside CD14 and metabolic reprogramming (NAMPT, TYMP) indicates dual TLR/interferon pathway activation typical of bacterial or endotoxin-driven emergency myelopoiesis.
key_evidence: S100A9/S100A8/S100A12: Calprotectin complex—hallmark of activated CD14 Mono; released during inflammation and bind TLR4/RAGE
CD14: High surface expression on 92% CD14 Mono; LPS co-receptor and PAMP recognition
ISG15/IFI6/IFI44L: Type-I interferon-stimulated genes indicating dual TLR→IRF7 or IFN-β autocrine signaling
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; induced in inflammatory monocytes via NF-κB; facilitates cell-cell and ECM interactions
NAMPT/TYMP: NAD+ salvage and nucleotide metabolism supporting rapid ATP demand in activated pro-inflammatory cells
APOBEC3A: Innate restriction factor; upregulated in inflammatory myeloid cells
CST3: Cystatin—protease inhibitor balancing inflammatory protease milieu
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14++ HLA-DR+ cells sorted for S100A8/A9 protein by intracellular staining. qPCR validation of S100A9, ISG15, NAMPT in FACS-purified CD14 Mono ± LPS/IFN-β stimulation. CITE-seq or protein array profiling of calprotectin complex release in supernatant. Mechanistic: test TLR4 antagonism effect on signature suppression.

functional_description: This signature captures the core inflammatory and antimicrobial programme of CD14+ classical monocytes, dominated by S100 alarmin proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A6) that mediate DAMP/PAMP sensing and innate immune activation. The co-expression of CD14, FCN1 (pattern recognition), MNDA (myeloid differentiation), and TYROBP (ITAM signalling) indicates active bacterial sensing and pro-inflammatory priming characteristic of tissue-infiltrating inflammatory monocytes.
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical alarmin; binds TLR4 and RAGE; drives sterile and microbial inflammation
S100A8: Partners S100A9 in calprotectin heterodimer; neutrophil recruitment; antimicrobial activity
S100A12: S100 family member; elevated in bacterial infection and inflammatory states
CD14: Monocyte lineage marker and LPS co-receptor; essential PAMP sensing
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor; complement activation pathway
MNDA: Myeloid-specific transcriptional regulator; marks granulocyte-monocyte differentiation
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor; couples pattern recognition to inflammatory signalling
CSTA: Cystatin A; protease regulator in inflammatory secretome
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: S100A8/A9 co-expression on CD14++CD16- cells; measure alongside TLR4/CD64 expression. RNA-seq validation of S100A8/A9 ratio in LPS-stimulated CD14 monocytes vs resting baseline. Functional assay: assess calprotectin secretion and ROS production in S100A9-high vs S100A9-low CD14 monocyte subsets.

programme_name: OXPHOS and metabolic priming in monopoiesis
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated oxidative phosphorylation and metabolic capacity across CD14 monocytes and early progenitor subsets, coupled with antigen presentation machinery priming. The programme integrates mitochondrial respiratory chain assembly with glycolytic checkpoint control and cytoprotective responses, suggesting metabolic reprogramming during monocyte specification and maturation.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Coordinate OXPHOS complex I and IV assembly and electron transport chain function
SLC25A5: Mitochondrial ADP/ATP antiporter coupling OXPHOS to ATP export
GPX1, GSTP1: Redox buffering and detoxification supporting high metabolic flux
TPI1: Glycolytic enzyme bridging glycolysis to gluconeogenesis
CD74: MHC-II invariant chain for antigen presentation pathway priming
TMSB4X: Actin regulation supporting cytoskeletal dynamics in differentiating monocytes
YBX1, PTMA: RNA/DNA binding proteins with roles in proliferation and stress response
CD63: Tetraspanin with roles in exosomal trafficking and immune signalling
suggested_validation: Measure oxygen consumption rate and ATP/ADP ratio in CD14 vs CD16 monocytes and progenitor subsets; validate MHC-II-CD74 complex assembly via immunoprecipitation; assess reactive oxygen species buffering capacity via GPX1/GSTP1 activity assays in metabolically sorted populations

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and Antigen Presentation
functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic reprogramming and immunological activation in classical CD14 monocytes, centered on iron homeostasis (FTH1), NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT), and HLA Class II-mediated antigen presentation (HLA-DRA). The signature integrates antimicrobial functions (LYZ lysozyme, CLEC7A C-type lectin recognition) with oxidative stress management (GPX1, SAT1 polyamine catabolism) and post-transcriptional regulation of inflammatory responses (ZFP36L1).
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage critical for monocyte metabolic fitness and ROS management in activated state
NAMPT: NAD+ salvage pathway supports metabolic demands of inflammatory monocytes and SIRT-dependent processes
HLA-DRA: Class II antigen presentation hallmark of CD14 mono, distinguishes from CD16 mono and progenitors
LYZ: Antimicrobial effector function via bacterial cell wall degradation (PAMP response)
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adapter for TLR and C-type lectin signaling integration
CLEC7A: Pattern recognition receptor for fungal/bacterial PAMPs, synergizes with TLR pathways
MAFB: Transcription factor essential for late-stage monocyte differentiation and activation
CEBPD: CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein supporting inflammatory monocyte gene expression
ZFP36L1: Early response gene encoding ARE-binding protein for cytokine mRNA stability control
GPX1: Antioxidant defense against ROS generated during NADPH oxidase activation
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism supports sustained metabolic activity and prevents polyamine toxicity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of FTH1, MAFB, and HLA-DRA expression in CD14 Mono (CD14+CD16−CCR2+) vs CD16 Mono (CD14+CD16+CX3CR1+); qPCR confirmation of NAMPT and CEBPD in sorted CD14 monocytes stimulated with LPS (TLR4 agonist); functional assays measuring iron uptake (FTH1) and phagocytic capacity (TYROBP/CLEC7A signaling) in activated CD14 monocytes.

programme_name: Monocyte Metabolic Priming and Antimicrobial Effector
functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic activation and antimicrobial effector functions in CD14 classical monocytes, characterized by elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) capacity and antimicrobial peptide production. The enrichment of mitochondrial complexes I and IV components indicates heightened energy demand for inflammatory and phagocytic functions, complemented by lysozyme and ribonuclease production for bacterial cell wall degradation and nucleic acid targeting.
key_evidence: MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Respiratory chain complexes I and IV subunits indicating enhanced OXPHOS for energy-demanding immune functions
LYZ: Lysozyme encoding antibacterial peptidase targeting bacterial peptidoglycan; canonical monocyte antimicrobial effector
RNASE2: Ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity against bacterial and viral nucleic acids
FLNA: Actin-crosslinking protein essential for cytoskeletal remodeling during phagocytosis and cell migration
PPP1R14B: Serine/threonine phosphatase inhibitor predicted role in innate immune signaling
50% CD14 Mono composition in top activators confirms classical monocyte identity despite progenitor contamination
suggested_validation: Compare metabolic flux analysis (seahorse OXPHOS) between CD14 and CD16 monocytes; validate LYZ/RNASE2 protein secretion via ELISA in response to TLR ligands; confirm FLNA phosphorylation status during phagocytosis assays; assess whether signature correlates with SPI1/CEBPB ChIP peaks at these loci

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic adaptation of CD14 monocytes to oxidative stress through coordinated upregulation of antioxidant defenses (GPX1, FTH1) and iron storage capacity. The signature indicates activation of early response and stress-response transcriptional programs (ZFP36L1, ZFP36, CEBPD) alongside enhanced antimicrobial effector function (LYZ, TYROBP), consistent with inflammatory monocyte priming in response to PAMP or inflammatory signals.
key_evidence: FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron storage and ROS buffering in activated monocytes
GPX1: glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification, critical ROS defense mechanism
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM-containing adaptor for TLR/lectin receptor signaling in myeloid cells
LYZ: lysozyme production for antimicrobial activity in inflammatory monocytes
ZFP36/ZFP36L1: ARE-binding proteins for TNF/IL6 mRNA stability regulation
CEBPD: C/EBP family member induced by inflammatory stimuli, distinct from CEBPB
LGALS3: galectin-3 for pattern recognition and pro-inflammatory signaling
HLA-DRA: MHC-II presentation capability of activated CD14 monocytes
SAT1: polyamine catabolism, metabolic signature of inflammatory activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantification of ferritin and ROS (DHE staining) in CD14 monocytes; qPCR validation of GPX1, FTH1, ZFP36/L1 and CEBPD in sorted CD14 vs CD16 monocytes; functional assessment of lysozyme secretion and oxidative burst capacity in response to TLR2/4 agonists

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and translation machinery
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation factor activity, characteristic of Early GMP cells with active protein synthesis capacity. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation support (UQCRH, MT-CO2) indicates metabolically active progenitors poised for rapid proliferation and differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS23/RPS24/RPS17/RPL37A/RPLP0/RPL7A: core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins driving translation capacity
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, essential for translation elongation
PTMA: DNA-binding co-factor and apoptosis repressor supporting progenitor survival during proliferation
STMN1: microtubule dynamics regulator facilitating cell cycle progression in GMP-Cycle subset
UQCRH and MT-CO2: mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicating oxidative metabolism in cycling progenitors
HMGN1: nucleosomal DNA binding protein associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in Early GMP
SNRPE: spliceosomal component supporting mRNA processing for differentiation-related genes
suggested_validation: Quantify polysome density and global translation rates in Early GMP vs. mature monocytes using polysome profiling or O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) incorporation assays. Verify PTMA, STMN1, and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism correlate with cell cycle entry and progenitor proliferation capacity using qPCR and oxygen consumption measurements.

programme_name: Early GMP basal translation and protein synthesis
functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP cells (82.5% composition), supporting active but non-proliferative protein synthesis capacity. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, SNRPE) indicates baseline translational competence required for GMP homeostasis and early myeloid differentiation priming, rather than a proliferation-specific programme.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins establishing translation capacity
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting steady-state protein synthesis
HNRNPA1, SNRPE: RNA-binding and splicing cofactors indicating active mRNA processing
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in ribosome biogenesis and protein chaperoning
GAPDH, UQCRH: Metabolic cofactors supporting basal energetic state
Early GMP 82.5%: Signature predominantly marks quiescent/G0-G1 phase progenitors, not cycling GMP-Cycle (10.5%)
suggested_validation: Distinguish this GMP basal translation programme from proliferation-driven signatures by co-staining FACS (CD34+CD38−/low vs cycling Ki67+ populations) and comparing ribosomal protein expression against cell-cycle markers (CDK1, MKI67, TOP2A). Validate that translation capacity precedes lineage commitment TF activation (CEBPE, IRF8) using temporal RNA-seq or protein synthesis assays (puromycin incorporation) across GMP substages.

functional_description: This signature represents constitutive protein synthesis machinery predominantly active in early GMP-stage progenitors, characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPL/RPS), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH). The dominance of translation and metabolic housekeeping genes with minimal lineage-specific signals indicates this captures a proliferative, biosynthetically-active progenitor state rather than differentiation commitment.
key_evidence: RPL37A, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL7A, RPLP0: Coordinate ribosomal subunit components indicating active protein synthesis capacity
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting high translational throughput in proliferating cells
GAPDH, MT-CO2, UQCRH: Glycolytic and oxidative phosphorylation enzymes supporting energy demands of protein synthesis
H3F3A, HMGN1, PTMA: Chromatin-associated proteins enabling open, transcriptionally-active chromatin architecture in early progenitors
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in mRNA processing and export, supporting transcriptome turnover
59.5% Early GMP composition: Signature enriched in least-committed GMP stage before monocyte/neutrophil bifurcation
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression across GMP substages (Early GMP vs GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono) and ProMono; validate that signature activity declines during monocyte commitment (ProMono→CD14 Mono) where translational demands shift; assess correlation with cell cycle phase and MKI67/PCNA to confirm biosynthetic activity is proliferation-associated rather than lineage-specific.

functional_description: This signature reflects mature CD14 classical monocyte antimicrobial and oxidative stress response capacity, centered on lysozyme-mediated bacterial killing, antioxidant defense via glutathione peroxidase, and metabolic support for effector functions. The dominance of housekeeping genes (GAPDH, ribosomal proteins) alongside LYZ and GPX1 indicates a transcriptionally active, metabolically primed state characteristic of inflammatory monocytes poised for pathogen engagement.
key_evidence: LYZ: Encodes lysozyme, canonical monocyte antimicrobial enzyme for peptidoglycan degradation; top-ranked discriminator of CD14 Mono maturity
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification; essential for managing ROS generated during phagocytosis and NADPH oxidase activity
CEBPD: bZIP transcription factor co-regulating myeloid differentiation and inflammatory gene expression alongside CEBPB
ZFP36L1: Early response gene induced by TPA/mitogens; involved in inflammatory cytokine mRNA stabilization and decay control
PLIN2: Lipid droplet protein; correlates with metabolic reprogramming and lipid accumulation in activated monocytes
NAMPT: NAD biosynthesis enzyme supporting ATP generation and sirtuin-mediated metabolic flexibility during immune activation
CD63: Tetraspanin involved in vesicle trafficking and exocytosis; marker of monocyte secretory/phagocytic capacity
PLEK: Phosphoinositide-binding protein; regulates PKC signaling downstream of TLR engagement and Fcγ receptor clustering
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+CD16- monocytes for LYZ intracellular expression and GPX1 activity; RNAseq comparison with CD16 monocytes (high CX3CR1, low CCR2) to confirm antimicrobial skewing; functional assay measuring phagocytic capacity and ROS production in LYZ+ vs LYZ- CD14 Mono subsets

programme_name: Monocyte cytoplasmic calcium signaling and lysosomal proteolysis
functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced intracellular calcium handling and lysosomal cysteine protease activity in CD14 monocytes, dominated by S100 calcium-binding proteins and cathepsin machinery. The gene expression pattern suggests activation of cytoskeletal remodeling and antigen processing functions characteristic of inflammatory monocytes engaged in phagocytic and proteolytic activities.
key_evidence: S100A6: Calcium-binding EF-hand protein mediating cytoplasmic calcium signaling in activated monocytes
S100A4: Calcium-binding protein regulating actin polymerization during monocyte migration and inflammatory response
S100A11: EF-hand calcium sensor supporting inflammatory monocyte cytoskeletal dynamics
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine cathepsin essential for antigen processing and phagolysosomal degradation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein linking Fc receptor and integrin signaling in phagocytes
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain component required for antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis via FCGR1A
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics during migration and phagocytosis
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor modulating lysosomal protease activity
HBA2/HBA1/HBB: Hemoglobin components retained from erythrophagocytosis substrate
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring intracellular calcium flux (Fluo-4) and lysosomal protease activity (cathepsin L/S) in CD14 vs CD16 monocytes; confirm TYROBP-FCER1G complex expression by immunoprecipitation; assess S100A4/A6 expression via immunofluorescence in response to TLR4 stimulation.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte activation centered on MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation, coupled with pro-inflammatory priming. The dominant HLA class II gene ensemble (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) and CD74 (invariant chain) establish antigen presentation capacity, while IL1B and FOSB indicate early innate immune activation and transcriptional rewiring toward inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB5: canonical class II presentation machinery; hallmark of activated professional APCs
HLA-DPB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: additional class II heterodimer components ensuring broad peptide binding repertoire
CD74: essential chaperone for class II assembly and trafficking; marks functional APC capacity
IL1B: pro-inflammatory cytokine central to monocyte innate response; absent in CD16 mono and progenitors
FOSB: immediate-early transcription factor indicating rapid activation kinetics and inflammatory pathway engagement
FTH1: iron storage reflecting metabolic remodeling during activation; supports pro-inflammatory macrophage phenotype
TMSB4X: actin regulation supporting enhanced migration and extravasation required for tissue recruitment
CST3: cysteine protease inhibitor supporting protease balance during activated state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: HLA-DR+ CD14+ with IL-1β intracellular staining, phospho-p65, and CCR2 to confirm inflammatory monocyte subset. qPCR validation of IL1B, FOSB, and HLA-DRA. Functional assay: assess antigen presentation capacity via mixed lymphocyte reaction and measure TNF-α/IL-6 secretion upon TLR4 stimulation.

functional_description: This signature represents classical CD14+ monocyte inflammatory priming and antimicrobial effector function, centered on S100 alarmin/DAMP sensing and intracellular proteolytic capacity. The coordinated expression of S100A8/A9/A12 (calprotectin complex), TYROBP (DAP12 adaptor), and lysosomal proteases (CTSS, CSTA) indicates activated inflammatory monocytes poised for pathogen recognition and intracellular killing.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9/A12: Calcium-binding alarmins marking inflammatory monocyte activation; secreted or DAMP-associated; high F-stat indicates robust CD14 Mono enrichment
CD14: Canonical classical monocyte marker; LPS/PAMP co-receptor supporting TLR4 signaling
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor linking pattern recognition receptors to intracellular signaling cascades in myeloid cells
FCN1: Ficolin-1 recognition receptor for pathogen-associated molecular patterns; monocyte-associated lectin innate immune sensor
CTSS/CSTA: Lysosomal cysteine proteases essential for phagolysosomal antigen processing and intracellular killing
FTH1: Iron storage/detoxification supporting metabolic reprogramming during inflammatory activation
VCAN/GRN: Extracellular matrix remodeling and granule proteins supporting migration and tissue infiltration
TYMP/VCAN: Bone marrow emigration-associated gene expression consistent with mobilized inflammatory monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+CD16- population for S100A9, TYROBP cell surface expression and/or intracellular staining; compare to CD16+ monocytes and progenitors. Functional assay: measure LPS-induced TNF/IL-1β secretion and ROS production in sorted CD14 Mono; assess TLR4/MyD88 dependency. Spatial transcriptomics: localize signature to inflamed bone marrow microenvironments or peripheral blood during infection/inflammatory stimulus.

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Antigen Presentation Myeloid Program
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14+ classical monocyte state centered on MHC class II antigen presentation machinery and myeloid differentiation, with strong expression of HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA, and CD74. The co-expression of TYROBP (DAP12), MNDA, and AIF1 indicates activated myeloid identity with enhanced pattern recognition and immune response capacity, while LGALS2, FCN1, and CST3 suggest lectin-mediated pathogen sensing and proteolytic remodeling.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA, CD74: MHC class II antigen presentation axis—hallmark of professional APCs in CD14+ monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor critical for FcγR and TLR signaling integration in myeloid cells
MNDA: Myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen—monocyte/granulocyte lineage marker
FCN1: Ficolin—PAMP recognition via complement lectin pathway; typical of inflammatory monocytes
LGALS2: Galectin-2—soluble lectin for glycan-mediated pathogen and danger-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) recognition
AIF1: Allograft inflammatory factor—calcium-binding protein supporting macrophage activation and cytokine responses
CST3: Cystatin C—cysteine protease inhibitor; involved in immune homeostasis and protease regulation
RGS2: Regulator of G protein signaling—negative feedback on GPCR signaling (e.g., CCR2-mediated migration)
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DR, CD74, and FCN1 co-expression on CD14++CD16– classical monocytes; confirm TYROBP+ activation state and assess phagocytic capacity via Fc-receptor clustering assays.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein (RPS/RPL), translation elongation (EEF1B2), and nucleolar/nuclear shuttling proteins (NPM1, HNRNPA1, PTMA) characteristic of Early GMP progenitors maintaining high translational machinery output. The enrichment of glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, LDHB) and HSP90AB1 supports active anabolic metabolism requisite for sustained proliferative capacity and protein synthesis during early myeloid commitment.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4: Multiple ribosomal structural proteins indicating elevated protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP (96% composition)
RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit component; core translational machinery marker
NPM1: Nucleolar protein involved in ribosome biogenesis and centrosome duplication; supports progenitor self-renewal
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; direct mediator of amino-acyl tRNA delivery
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing; supports transcriptional/translational coordination
GAPDH, LDHB: Glycolytic enzymes; metabolic signature of active progenitors
HSP90AB1: Heat shock protein supporting protein folding during anabolic stress
PTMA: Nucleolar/cytoplasmic protein with anti-apoptotic function; preserves progenitor viability
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry measuring CD34+/CD33+ Early GMP expression of ribosomal proteins (RPL7A, RPS24) and translation factors (EEF1B2) relative to CD14+CD16− mature monocytes. Confirm functional translational capacity using O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) incorporation assay. Integrate with MYB/CEBPA/SPI1 expression to confirm early progenitor identity and exclude cycling GMP-Cycle contamination (CDK1, PCNA absent from signature).

functional_description: This signature reflects robust protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP progenitors, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation factors. The co-enrichment of RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, YBX1, NPM1) and metabolic enzymes (LDHB) suggests active translation coupled with anabolic metabolism supporting rapid GMP proliferation and differentiation priming.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17: core 40S ribosomal subunit proteins defining translational capacity
RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit assembly and function
EEF1B2: elongation factor supporting ribosome-catalysed protein synthesis
NPM1: nucleolar protein regulating ribosome biogenesis and centrosome duplication; marks cycling progenitors
HNRNPA1, YBX1: RNA-binding proteins controlling mRNA processing and stability during GMP activation
LDHB: glycolytic enzyme supporting metabolic demands of proliferative progenitors
HSP90AB1: chaperone stabilising signalling proteins (MYB, CEBPA, IRF8) during lineage commitment
83% Early GMP composition: validates progenitor-specific translational programme distinct from mature monocytes
suggested_validation: Cross-validate against bulk RNA-seq of FACS-sorted Early GMP (CD34+KIT+) vs CD14 monocytes; confirm downregulation of this ribosomal/translation signature in ProMono (CSF1R+MPO-); assess correlation with cell-cycle phase (GMP-Cycle) and SPI1/CEBPA co-expression patterns.

functional_description: This signature reflects a metabolically active, iron-sequestering monocyte state with enhanced oxidative stress management and tissue remodeling capacity. The enrichment of ferritin heavy chain (FTH1), NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT), and matrix remodeling inhibitors (TIMP1) suggests preparation for sustained inflammatory responses whilst mitigating iron-dependent ROS toxicity. The inclusion of CEBPD and MAFB indicates alternative C/EBP pathway engagement distinct from canonical pro-inflammatory transcription.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage and sequestration; critical for ROS protection in activated monocytes undergoing oxidative burst
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; supports metabolic reprrogramming and SIRT-dependent signaling in inflammatory myeloid cells
TIMP1: MMP inhibition; prevents excessive ECM degradation during monocyte infiltration and tissue inflammation
CEBPD: Alternative C/EBP TF; balances CEBPB-driven pro-inflammatory response with metabolic adaptation
MAFB: Monocyte maturation TF; marks intermediate/activated monocyte differentiation state
COTL1: Actin dynamics and 5-LO interaction; supports cytoskeletal reorganization and lipid mediator signaling
CLEC7A: Dectin-1; fungal/damage-associated pattern recognition complementary to TLR signaling
CXCL16: Transmembrane chemokine; monocyte recruitment and trans-endothelial migration
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein; cytoskeletal dynamics and inflammatory signaling amplification
HMOX1: Heme oxygenase-1; oxidative stress resolution and anti-inflammatory metabolite (bilirubin) generation
suggested_validation: Sort CD14+ monocytes by FTH1 and NAMPT expression; validate iron content (Prussian blue), NAD+/NADH ratio, and mitochondrial ROS production. Confirm TIMP1 activity by gelatin zymography. Test whether signature enrichment correlates with ex vivo LPS+IFN-γ priming response and sustained TNF production.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein synthesis capacity and oxidative metabolism in Early GMP and GMP-Mono populations, consistent with active protein production during myeloid progenitor expansion. The enrichment of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS2, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPS26, RPLP0) and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components (MT-CO2, UQCRH) indicates heightened anabolic and energetic demands characteristic of proliferating progenitors preparing for lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS2/RPS23/RPS24/RPS17/RPS26/RPLP0: ribosomal proteins driving protein synthesis capacity in proliferating Early GMP/GMP-Mono (51.5% + 27% = 78.5% of activating cells)
MT-CO2/UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain components supporting oxidative ATP generation in metabolically active progenitors
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating centrosome duplication and ribosome biogenesis, consistent with G1/S checkpoint activity
LDHB: lactate dehydrogenase subunit supporting glycolytic-oxidative metabolic flexibility during myeloid expansion
SNRPE/LSM5: spliceosomal components enabling dynamic gene expression remodeling during lineage specification
TXN: thioredoxin managing redox homeostasis under elevated metabolic demand
MIF: cytokine with known role in myeloid differentiation and macrophage/monocyte function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD34+KIT+ Early GMP with anti-phospho-S6 (ribosomal biogenesis) and Mitotracker (mitochondrial membrane potential) to confirm enhanced translation and OXPHOS. RT-qPCR validation of ribosomal protein mRNA in sorted Early GMP vs. mature monocytes. Consider that signature may partially reflect technical artifact of high RNA content in progenitors rather than lineage-specific commitment signals.

functional_description: This signature captures the mature CD14 classical monocyte inflammatory state, characterized by robust antimicrobial and damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) sensing through S100 calprotectin (S100A8/A9) and pattern recognition receptors (FCN1, LYZ). The signature reflects heightened innate immune effector function via bacterial cell wall degradation and oxidative stress responses, consistent with pro-inflammatory monocyte activation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin component; central DAMP and neutrophil chemoattractant in monocyte-driven inflammation
S100A8: Calprotectin heterodimer partner; S100A8/A9 complex triggers TLR4 signalling independent of LPS
LYZ: Lysozyme; bactericidal enzyme marking antimicrobial effector state in CD14 Mono
CD14: Monocyte surface marker and LPS co-receptor; validates CD14 Mono enrichment (64.5%)
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition molecule for bacterial acetyl groups and apoptotic cells
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen; marker of monocyte/granulocyte lineage maturation
S100A6, S100A4, S100A12: S100 family calcium sensors; amplify inflammatory signalling cascades
VCAN: Versican; ECM proteoglycan remodelling during monocyte extravasation and tissue infiltration
CSTA: Cystatin A; cathepsin inhibitor regulating protease balance in inflammatory monocytes
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation; energetic demand of activated monocytes
RETN: Resistin; adipokine with pro-inflammatory properties enriched in activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of S100A8/A9 calprotectin with CD14, CD16, and CD64 (FCGR1A) to confirm CD14 Mono enrichment; RNA-ISH of S100A8/A9 in bone marrow sections to localize inflammatory monocyte niche; measure plasma calprotectin and correlate with CD14 monocyte frequency in inflammatory conditions.

functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor differentiation characterized by upregulation of antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, S100A8/A9, RNASE2) and oxidative stress defence (GPX1), coupled with chromatin remodelling activity (HMGN2, HMGB1/2) supporting transcriptional reprogramming. The programme marks transition from GMP to committed ProMono fate with acquisition of bactericidal capacity before full CD14 surface marker expression.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte lysozyme, antibacterial peptidoglycan hydrolase essential for mono function
S100A8/S100A9: calprotectin complex, transient ProMono marker and neutrophil-like antimicrobial alarm protein
RNASE2: monocyte-enriched RNase with antimicrobial activity, marks departure from GMP
GPX1: antioxidant defence against reactive oxygen species during monocyte maturation
CEBPD: C/EBP family TF supporting myeloid differentiation, cooperative with C/EBPα in ProMono
HMGN2/HMGB1/HMGB2: chromatin-associated factors enabling transcriptional remodelling during commitment
PTMA/ANP32B: nucleosome dynamics and apoptosis regulation, supporting developmental transitions
CSTA: cysteine protease inhibitor, protective during myeloid maturation
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry: co-express LYZ+S100A9+ with MS4A3-high, MPO-low, IRF8-intermediate in Early ProMono gates. Confirm CEBPD/C/EBPα co-occupancy at LYZ/S100A8 promoters via ChIP-seq. Assess chromatin accessibility at antimicrobial loci via ATAC-seq in sorted Early ProMono vs GMP.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened translational capacity and metabolic activity in GMP-Mono cells committed toward monocytic differentiation. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS26, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS24) and spliceosomal components (SNRPE, SNRPF) indicates active protein synthesis machinery coupled with pre-mRNA processing, consistent with progenitors actively translating monocyte-lineage proteins. Co-expression of mitochondrial OXPHOS genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRQ, UQCRH) and MPO marks metabolic repriming and early myeloid differentiation commitment.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS24: 40S and 60S ribosomal protein enrichment indicates translational upregulation characteristic of GMP-Mono actively synthesizing monocyte-lineage proteins
SNRPE, SNRPF: spliceosomal snRNP components suggest elevated splicing capacity accompanying lineage-specific transcriptome remodeling
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRQ, UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain subunits indicate metabolic transition from quiescent HSC/early GMP toward more energetically demanding monopoiesis
MPO: myeloperoxidase presence confirms early myeloid lineage priming in GMP-Mono stage
PTMA, ANP32B: nuclear factors suggest active chromatin remodeling and apoptosis regulation during monocytic commitment
Cell composition: 36.5% GMP-Mono + 28.5% Early GMP indicates feature enriched in early monopoietic progenitors, not mature monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate translational activity via polysome profiling or puromycin incorporation in sorted GMP-Mono vs Early GMP populations. Confirm metabolic shift using seahorse mito stress assays. Correlate ribosomal protein expression with CSF1R and CD64 upregulation (monocytic commitment markers) to distinguish from neutrophilic GMP-Cycle counterpart.

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte state emphasizing intracellular protein quality control, cytoskeletal homeostasis, and tissue remodeling rather than acute inflammation. The enrichment of proteases inhibitors (TIMP1, CST3, CAST), S100 calcium-sensors (S100A6, S100A4), and interferon-response proteins (IFITM3, IFI6) suggests activated but not hyperinflammatory monocytes managing oxidative stress and matrix integrity during steady-state or resolution phases.
key_evidence: TIMP1: matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor, restrains excessive tissue degradation in activated monocytes
S100A6, S100A4: calcium-binding proteins regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and stress responses in myeloid cells
CST3, CAST: cysteine/calpain protease inhibitors controlling intracellular proteolysis
IFITM3, IFI6: interferon-stimulated genes indicating antiviral/tissue-protective rather than classical LPS-TNF axis activation
LGALS1, LGALS2: galectins mediating cell-matrix interactions and negative feedback on monocyte activation
HLA-DRB1: antigen presentation capacity typical of resident/tissue-associated CD14 mono
PSAP, TYMP: lysosomal/catabolic enzymes supporting autophagy and intracellular pathogen control
CD14 Mono dominance (87%): validates CD14 classical monocyte phenotype, not CD16 non-classical
suggested_validation: Compare this signature against transcriptomics of LPS-activated (TNF, IL1B, CXCL8 high) vs. resting CD14 monocytes and tissue macrophages; validate S100A4/A6 and TIMP1 protein expression by flow cytometry or immunofluorescence in steady-state vs. acute inflammatory conditions; assess functional capacity for phagocytosis and ROS production to confirm non-hyperinflammatory state.

functional_description: This CD14 monocyte-enriched signature reflects a calcium-responsive inflammatory state driven by S100 alarmin family proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A4/A6) that serve as danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) amplifying innate immune activation. The programme coordinates antibacterial effector functions including pattern recognition (FCN1, CD14), proteolytic activity (CSTA, MNDA), and microbicidal capacity (LYZ, CAPG), consistent with acute myeloid inflammatory response to bacterial PAMPs.
key_evidence: S100A8: Master DAMP and alarmin; TLR4 ligand amplifying monocyte inflammatory activation and recruitment
S100A9: Heterodimer partner of S100A8 (calprotectin complex); establishes pro-inflammatory myeloid state
S100A12: Calcium-binding alarmin; TLR4/RAGE agonist driving monocyte activation independent of pathogen recognition
FCN1: Pattern recognition molecule (ficolin); complement-independent phagocytic priming and bacterial opsonisation
CD14: Primary LPS co-receptor and PAMP sensor; required for TLR4/TLR2 signalling in monocytes
LYZ: Lysozyme; direct antibacterial effector targeting peptidoglycan in bacterial cell walls
MNDA: Myeloid differentiation antigen; marker of mature monocyte inflammatory polarisation
CSTA: Cystatin; protease regulator balancing inflammatory proteolysis during immune response
CAPG: Actin-binding protein; enables phagocytic cup formation and chemotaxis to inflammatory sites
VCAN: Versican; ECM component modulating monocyte retention and inflammatory signalling in microenvironments
suggested_validation: Co-staining for S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex with CD14 and CD64 in classical monocytes; assess TNF-α and IL-6 production following LPS stimulation; quantify FCGR1A expression and phagocytic capacity in S100A8/A9-high monocytes; validate elevated lysozyme activity in serum/plasma of activated monocyte donors

functional_description: This signature defines CD14+ classical monocytes with a prominent antimicrobial effector state, characterized by abundance of S100 alarmins (S100A8/A9/A12/A6/A4), pattern recognition molecules (FCN1, CD14), and antimicrobial proteases (LYZ, CSTA). The programme reflects pre-activated/primed monocytes poised for rapid bacterial sensing and innate immune response with cytoplasmic calcium-signalling ready state.
key_evidence: S100A8: Myeloid alarmin and damage-associated pattern for monocyte/neutrophil recruitment and antimicrobial priming
S100A9: Heterodimerizes with S100A8 (calprotectin complex); hallmark of activated CD14 Mono inflammatory state
S100A12: S100 family member enriched in myeloid cells; amplifies TLR4 signalling and NF-κB activation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 pattern recognition receptor for bacterial PAMP sensing; classical monocyte-specific
CD14: Co-receptor for TLR4/LPS sensing; surface marker confirming CD14 Mono identity
LYZ: Lysozyme antimicrobial peptidoglycan hydrolase; secreted bacterial killing factor in monocytes
MNDA: Myeloid differentiation antigen restricted to monocyte/granulocyte lineage; marker of terminal myeloid commitment
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor; anti-apoptotic in activated monocytes; immune homeostasis
CAPG: Actin-regulating protein essential for phagocytic cup formation and bacterial uptake
VCAN: Versican; ECM proteoglycan involved in monocyte adhesion and extravasation during inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain S100A8/A9 (alarmins) with CD14/CD64 to confirm classical monocyte inflammatory state; qPCR validation of FCN1 and LYZ in FACS-sorted CD14+CCR2+ monocytes vs CD16+CX3CR1+ non-classical monocytes; functional assay: measure phagocytic capacity and ROS production in S100A8/A9-high vs S100-low CD14 monocytes

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte state characterized by robust MHC class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ, HLA-DM) coupled with iron storage capacity and metabolic adaptation. The co-expression of TYROBP (DAP12)-dependent signaling, pattern recognition receptors (CLEC7A), and iron metabolism (FTH1) suggests activated antigen-presenting monocytes engaged in tissue surveillance and immune regulation rather than acute inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB5/HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1/HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: Comprehensive MHC class II molecule expression defining professional antigen-presentation program
HLA-DMA: Peptide loading factor for MHC class II, essential for functional antigen presentation
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain indicating iron storage; critical for controlling oxidative stress in surveillance monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor protein coupling pattern recognition receptors to downstream signaling
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor (Dectin-1) for fungal PAMP sensing; marker of tissue-resident/activated monocytes
MAFB: Transcription factor regulating myeloid differentiation and alternative activation programs
CXCL16: Chemokine involved in T cell recruitment and IFN-γ response; suggests immunoregulatory context
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis supporting metabolic demands of antigen presentation
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism regulating cellular stress responses during immune activation
ZFP36L1: Post-transcriptional regulator of inflammatory mediators (mRNA decay); suggests controlled inflammatory state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming CD14+HLA-DR++TYROBP+CLEC7A+ phenotype; functional assays measuring MHC class II-restricted antigen presentation capacity and iron-dependent ROS regulation; RNA-seq of sorted cells to verify antigen presentation vs. pro-inflammatory program distinction from classical M1 signatures

functional_description: This signature represents a CD14 monocyte programme dominated by lysosomal cysteine protease activity (CTSS) and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (ATP5F1, ATP5A1, MT-CO2, ATP5C1), supporting antigen processing and intracellular killing capacity. The signature integrates actin dynamics (TMSB4X) with myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA) and cytotoxic granule proteins (GNLY), consistent with activated classical monocytes engaged in phagocytic and proteolytic effector functions.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine proteinase essential for antigen presentation and intracellular pathogen degradation in monocytes
ATP5F1, ATP5A1, ATP5C1, MT-CO2: mitochondrial ATP synthase and electron transport chain components supporting high-energy demands of oxidative burst and proteolytic activity
MNDA: myeloid-lineage restricted nuclear antigen marking differentiated monocytic cells
TMSB4X: actin sequestering protein enabling cytoskeletal remodelling during phagocytosis and migration
GNLY: cytotoxic granule protein present in monocytes with NK-like killing capacity
89% CD14 Mono composition: strong enrichment in classical monocytes with intact lysosomal and metabolic programmes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CTSS+ CD14+ monocytes co-expressing mitochondrial markers; functional assays measuring intracellular proteolysis capacity and oxidative burst (DCF-DA assay); RNA-seq of CTSS-sorted monocyte subsets to confirm lysosomal protease programme independence from pro-inflammatory cytokine activation

functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 classical monocytes with enhanced calcium-responsive innate immune function. The dominant S100A8/A9 calprotectin heterodimer and S100A6/A4 members drive antimicrobial responses, leukocyte recruitment, and damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) sensing. Co-expression of FCN1 (ficolin-1), VCAN (versican), and CSTA indicates enhanced phagocytic capacity and extracellular matrix remodelling supporting inflammatory niche establishment.
key_evidence: S100A9: Core DAMP alarmin and neutrophil chemoattractant; marker of activated monocytes in inflammation
S100A8: Calprotectin partner; antimicrobial and TLR4 ligand; released upon monocyte activation
S100A6: Calcium-binding regulator of monocyte differentiation and pro-inflammatory responses
S100A4: Cytokine-induced calcium sensor; promotes monocyte migration and tissue infiltration
FCN1: Pattern recognition molecule; enhances complement-mediated bacterial opsonisation and phagocytosis
VCAN: ECM proteoglycan supporting monocyte adhesion and chemokine retention in inflamed tissues
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor enabling controlled inflammatory proteolysis
BLVRB: Heme catabolism enzyme; indicates heightened metabolic activity in activated monocytes
LGALS1: Galectin-1; immunomodulatory feedback regulator in activated myeloid cells
HBA/HBB: Residual haemoglobin transcripts suggest recent erythroid contact or phagocytosis of RBCs
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry for S100A8/A9 protein co-expression (Calprotectin) and FCN1 surface in CD14+ CD16- subsets; qPCR validation of S100 family members in FACS-sorted classical monocytes stimulated with LPS or TNF-α; assess correlation with CD64 (FCGR1A) expression and intracellular ROS production via dihydrorhodamine assay.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein translation and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened ribosomal biogenesis and protein synthesis capacity coupled with active oxidative phosphorylation, characteristic of metabolically active GMP-stage progenitors undergoing differentiation commitment. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal structural proteins alongside mitochondrial electron transport components suggests cells engaged in anabolic biosynthesis and energy production during the transition from proliferative GMP to early monocytic commitment.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A: coordinate 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating elevated translation demand during GMP differentiation
MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components reflecting metabolic shift from glycolytic progenitors to energy-demanding early committed monocytes
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis during early monocytic priming
HMGN1: chromatin remodelling protein associated with transcriptionally active regions, consistent with active differentiation programme
SNRPF: spliceosomal component involved in dynamic RNA processing during lineage commitment
Cell composition 48% Early GMP + 31.5% GMP-Mono: signature enriched in earliest monocytic commitment stages
suggested_validation: Validate metabolic shift via OXPHOS assays (seahorse) and ribosome profiling in sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono populations; confirm translation rates correlate with commitment; assess whether signature predicts differentiation capacity in single-cell functional assays; compare against committed monocytes (CD14+CD16+) where MPO/ELANE typically downregulate.

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte population specializing in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation coupled with iron metabolism regulation. The coordinated upregulation of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ molecules alongside CD74 (invariant chain) and FTH1 suggests monocytes engaged in professional antigen-presenting cell function with active intracellular iron storage, consistent with tissue-resident or inflammatory-primed classical monocytes.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRB5: Core HLA class II alpha/beta chains; foundational for peptide-MHC presentation
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer components; redundant class II presentation pathway
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ class II molecules; tertiary presentation pathway activation
CD74: Invariant chain chaperone for class II loading and trafficking; essential for functional MHC-II complexes
HLA-DMA: Non-classical MHC-II molecule; peptide exchange factor for class II optimization
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron sequestration and ROS protection in activated monocytes
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor; ITAM signaling from myeloid receptors including TREM-1/2
CST3: Cystatin C; cysteine protease inhibition and antigen processing regulation
YBX1, RPS2, RPS24: RNA/ribosomal proteins; housekeeping but elevated in metabolically active cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: HLA-DR+CD74+ gating in CD14++CD16- monocytes; assess iron staining (Perl's Prussian blue or ferritin IF). Functional assays: autologous or allogeneic T cell proliferation assay with sorted cells. RNA-seq confirmation of coordinated HLA-II vs. pro-inflammatory modules (TNF, IL-1β, IL-6 expression levels) to distinguish from classical LPS-activated signature.

functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced lysosomal proteolytic capacity and MHC class II antigen presentation machinery in classical CD14 monocytes. The programme is driven by cathepsins (CTSS), saposin processing (PSAP), and coordinated HLA-DR/DP expression with the invariant chain (CD74), supporting professional antigen-presenting cell function rather than inflammatory effector response.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and peptide generation for MHC-II presentation
PSAP: encodes saposins required for lysosomal degradation and lipid antigen processing
CD74: MHC-II chaperone and invariant chain regulating antigen loading and presentation
HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: complete MHC-II heterodimer components for antigen presentation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor linking Fc receptors and pattern recognition receptors to antigen uptake
AIF1: calcium-binding protein mediating macrophage activation and antigen handling
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain component of FcγR cluster required for antibody-mediated antigen uptake
TMSB4X, CALM2: actin regulation and calcium signaling supporting endocytic antigen uptake
FTH1, CST3: iron metabolism and cystatin-based protease regulation in lysosomal compartments
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry for HLA-DR/DP/DQ surface expression and CD74 intracellular staining; functional assay measuring antigen presentation capacity using peptide-pulsed dendritic cell co-culture; quantify CTSS and PSAP enzyme activity in lysosomal fractions from sorted CD14 monocytes versus CD16 monocytes.

functional_description: This signature captures metabolically primed CD14 classical monocytes with elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity and active protein synthesis machinery. The enrichment of OXPHOS genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5) coupled with ribosomal proteins reflects heightened energetic demands of pro-inflammatory monocyte differentiation and inflammatory effector function.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Complex I and IV components driving NADH oxidation and ATP synthesis for inflammatory activation
RPS24, RPS26, RPL37A: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins supporting accelerated protein synthesis during monocyte activation
S100A9: Canonical CD14 monocyte marker; calcium-binding protein amplified in inflammatory states
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease consistent with neutrophil elastase-like effector function in mature monocytes
SERPINB1: Protease inhibitor reflecting antimicrobial and tissue-remodeling capacity of classical monocytes
CES1: Carboxylesterase implicated in lipid sensing and metabolism of inflammatory lipid mediators
Cell composition: 53.5% CD14 Mono with substantial Late ProMono (14%), indicating active monocytopoiesis maturation pathway
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+CCR2+ monocytes for mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker) and protein synthesis activity (puromycin incorporation); confirm enhanced oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse) relative to CD16 Mono and progenitors. Quantify OXPHOS gene expression by qPCR in sorted classical monocytes stimulated with LPS/TNF.

programme_name: Classical Monocyte Granule and Antimicrobial Programme
functional_description: This signature captures the hallmark granular protease and S100 calcium-binding protein programme of classical CD14+ monocytes, reflecting their role as professional phagocytes primed for antimicrobial defence. The coordinated expression of S100A8/A9 (calprotectin heterodimer), S100A12, and proteolytic enzymes (FCN1, CSTA) underpins neutrophil-like granule biogenesis and pathogen-associated molecular pattern sensing, while VCAN and PLBD1 support extracellular matrix remodelling during inflammatory recruitment and infiltration.
key_evidence: S100A8: Calprotectin (S100A8/A9 dimer)—canonical classical monocyte antimicrobial granule protein; elevated in systemic inflammation and bacterial sensing
S100A9: Calprotectin partner; co-released DAMPs; MyD88/TLR-responsive in classical monocyte activation
S100A12: Calcium-binding alarmin; classical monocyte-enriched; amplifies innate immune signalling
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor for acetylated LPS and bacterial carbohydrates; marks inflammatory monocytes
CD14: LPS co-receptor with TLR4; defining classical monocyte marker; PAMP sensing hub
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; extracellular matrix support for monocyte infiltration and inflammatory licensing
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen; granulocyte-monocyte lineage marker; reflects terminal classical monocyte maturation
CSTA: Cystatin A protease inhibitor; granule component; anti-inflammatory regulation of serine proteases
CAPG: Gelsolin-family actin regulator; critical for monocyte shape change and transendothelial migration
PLBD1: Phospholipase B-like; extracellular mediator of inflammation and matrix degradation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantification of S100A8/A9 surface expression and intracellular granule content in CD14++CD16− classical monocytes; LPS/TLR4 stimulation to confirm rapid upregulation; comparison with CD16+ non-classical monocytes (expected CCR2-low, CX3CR1-high phenotype lacking this programme).

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis and oxidative metabolism capacity, driven primarily by ribosomal protein upregulation (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS26, RPL7A) and mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH). This metabolic state supports the elevated biosynthetic and energetic demands of early monocytic differentiation from GMP-stage progenitors, particularly in GMP-Mono and Early GMP cells (68% of activating cells).
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS26, RPL7A: ribosomes require substantial upregulation to support rapid protein synthesis during myeloid lineage commitment
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH: oxidative phosphorylation and electron transport drive ATP production for biosynthesis and cellular processes during differentiation
HMGN1: marks transcriptionally active chromatin, consistent with active transcriptional remodelling during GMP-to-monocyte transition
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supports sustained protein synthesis capacity
TMSB4X, ACTG1: actin dynamics enable cytoskeletal remodelling required for cell morphogenesis and migration during monocyte differentiation
Cellular composition: 68% GMP-Mono + Early GMP indicates signature enriched in early monocytic commitment stage, before mature markers fully activate
suggested_validation: Validate through flow cytometry measuring mitochondrial content (MitoTracker) and protein synthesis capacity (puromycin incorporation) in sorted GMP-Mono vs. mature CD14/CD16 monocytes. Correlate ribosomal protein expression with CSF1R and loss of early GMP markers (CD34, KIT). Perform polysome profiling to confirm translation activity, and measure metabolic parameters (ECAR, OCR) to confirm elevated OXPHOS dependency in this differentiation stage.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ribosomal protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP and GMP-Mono stages, indicating heightened metabolic demand during early myeloid priming before lineage commitment. The dominance of mitochondrial complex genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH) coupled with ribosomal proteins suggests rapid biosynthetic activity characteristic of proliferating progenitors preparing for differentiation.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1: Complex I-IV electron transport chain components—elevated in metabolically active early GMP undergoing proliferation and lineage priming
RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPS2: Coordinated ribosomal protein enrichment—hallmark of high translational capacity in proliferating progenitors
UQCRH: Ubiquinol-cytochrome c reductase complex III component—consistent with oxidative metabolism in early GMP before monocytic differentiation suppresses OXPHOS
PTMA, HMGN1, HNRNPA1: Nuclear/nucleolar factors supporting transcriptional activation and rRNA processing—enable rapid biosynthesis during progenitor expansion
FBL: Nucleolar snRNP component for rRNA maturation—supports elevated ribosome biogenesis in proliferative GMP-Mono
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) flow cytometry measuring mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker) and membrane potential (TMRM) in CD34+KIT+CD13+ Early GMP vs. CD14+ mature monocytes; (2) metabolic flux analysis (Seahorse) confirming OXPHOS dependency in Early GMP/GMP-Mono; (3) single-cell RNA-seq integration with surface markers (CD34, KIT, CSF1R) to confirm enrichment in GMP-stage rather than ProMono; (4) confirm signature absence in mature CD14 monocytes where OXPHOS diminishes.

functional_description: This signature defines CD14 monocytes with elevated antigen-presenting capacity and lysosomal hydrolase activity, characteristic of cells poised for pathogen-derived peptide presentation via MHC-II. The coordinated upregulation of HLA class II molecules (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP) with their chaperone CD74, combined with lysosomal proteases (CTSS, CPVL) and pattern recognition receptors (TYROBP, CLEC7A, FCN1), indicates a phagocytic and antigen-processing phenotype consistent with mononuclear phagocyte specialisation.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for Fcγ and C-lectin receptors, critical for phagocytic signalling in monocytes
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for MHC-II-mediated antigen processing and peptide generation
CD74: MHC-II chaperone and antigen presentation regulator, marker of professional APCs
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRB5, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DPA1: Comprehensive MHC-II alpha and beta chains enabling broad peptide presentation
HLA-DMA: MHC-II peptide loading catalyst, facilitates antigen presentation pathway
FCN1: Ficolin-1, C-type lectin family member recognising microbial carbohydrate patterns
CLEC7A: Dectin-1, β-glucan receptor for fungal/bacterial PAMP sensing
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain supporting iron homeostasis in phagocytic cells handling haem-iron from pathogens
AIF1: Actin-binding protein supporting cytoskeletal remodelling during phagocytosis and immune activation
CST3: Cystatin inhibiting cathepsins, regulating proteolytic balance in antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14+ monocytes for HLA-DR surface expression, CD74 intracellular staining, and CTSS activity via DQ-ovalbumin assay. RNAseq confirmation in sorted CD14 Mono with elevated MHC-II transcripts. Functional validation: measure antigen presentation capacity using peptide-loaded autologous T-cell proliferation assays. Verify absence of CD16 and CX3CR1 (discriminating from CD16 subset) and absence of progenitor markers (CD34, MPO).

functional_description: This signature reflects the terminal differentiation and antimicrobial effector programme of classical CD14+ monocytes, dominated by S100A8/A9 calprotectin and antimicrobial proteases. The programme emphasizes intracellular bacterial killing capacity, calcium-responsive innate immune signalling, and metabolic support for inflammatory function rather than classical TLR-driven cytokine production.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin component, primary biomarker of monocyte maturation and bacterial-killing capacity; Ca2+-signalling hub for antimicrobial response
S100A8: Calprotectin dimer partner with S100A9; cytoplasmic danger-associated molecular pattern and pathogen-associated pattern sensor
LYZ: Lysozyme, direct bacterial peptidoglycan degradation; canonical antimicrobial effector of mature myeloid cells
FCN1: Ficolin-1; complement-independent pattern recognition and opsonization for phagocytosis
CSTA: Cystatin A; protease inhibitor balancing antimicrobial serine proteases during phagocytic burst
S100A6: Calgranulin C; Ca2+-binding protein supporting cell migration and antimicrobial granule function
