VCAN: Versican; extracellular matrix component supporting monocyte retention in inflammatory microenvironments
PKM: Glycolytic enzyme supporting ATP production for phagocytic and oxidative burst energy demands
ANXA2: Annexin A2; phospholipid-binding protein regulating membrane dynamics during phagocytosis and microbial interaction
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming CD14++CD16− phenotype with S100A8/A9 and LYZ protein expression; functional assays measuring bacterial killing (e.g., opsonized E. coli phagocytosis/ROS production); in situ measurement of calprotectin release in inflammatory conditions

functional_description: This signature captures the early-to-intermediate monocyte differentiation programme characterized by calcium-binding S100 proteins (S100A8/A9/A4/A6) and innate immune effector molecules. The dominant representation of Early and Late ProMono cells (57% combined) alongside CD14 Mono (43%) indicates a Pro-inflammatory myeloid maturation state with active antimicrobial and cytokine responses.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: Canonical calprotectin components (S100A8/A9 heterodimer); neutrophil/monocyte damage-associated molecular patterns; mark activated myeloid differentiation
LYZ: Lysozyme hallmark of monocyte/macrophage lineage; antibacterial effector upregulated during ProMono-to-CD14 Mono transition
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor expressed in monocytes; innate immune activation marker
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen; lineage-restricted to granulocyte-monocyte compartment; present across ProMono and CD14 Mono
MS4A6A: Monocyte-associated tetraspanin; membrane protein upregulated in monocytic lineage; marks differentiation state
TMSB4X/CAPG: Actin-regulatory proteins; support cytoskeletal remodelling during monocyte maturation and migration
CSTA/GRN: Cysteine protease inhibitor and granulins; lysosomal/granule maturation consistent with ProMono→Mono transition
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: S100A8+S100A9+ with CSF1R+MS4A3+ (Early ProMono) vs CSF1R+CD14+ (Late ProMono/CD14 Mono); confirm loss of MPO/ELANE vs GMP; RNA-FISH for spatial arrangement of S100 proteins relative to monocyte commitment TFs (KLF4, IRF8)

functional_description: This signature represents active protein synthesis machinery, dominated by ribosomal protein subunits (40S: RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24; 60S: RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), alongside nucleolar/chromatin-associated proteins (NPM1, HMGN1) supporting ribosome biogenesis. The enrichment in Early GMP and GMP-Mono cells reflects high translational demand during myeloid progenitor expansion and lineage commitment, consistent with increased protein synthesis during differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS2, RPS23, RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins—core translational machinery
RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—large subunit function
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor—aa-tRNA delivery to ribosome
NPM1: nucleolar protein regulating ribosome assembly and cell proliferation
HMGN1: chromatin-associated protein supporting transcriptional activity
CD74: MHC-II chaperone, marks monocyte lineage commitment
HNRNPA1, PTMA: RNA/DNA-binding proteins supporting active transcription
Cell composition: 48.5% Early GMP, 25% GMP-Mono, 20% CD14 Mono—progenitor-skewed
suggested_validation: Perform ribosomal profiling or polysome analysis on sorted Early GMP and GMP-Mono to quantify translation rates; validate CD74 co-expression as monocytic lineage marker; compare ribosomal protein expression between GMP-Mono and neutrophil-committed GMP-Cycle to confirm mono-biased translational activation.

functional_description: This signature reflects mature monocyte antimicrobial effector functions and innate immune activation, dominated by bactericidal/proteolytic enzymes (LYZ, RNASE2, RNASE6, CSTA) and calcium-binding S100 proteins (S100A8, S100A9, S100A4, S100A6) critical for inflammatory responses and pathogen sensing. The enrichment in Early/Late ProMono (53% combined) alongside CD14 Mono (45.5%) indicates this programme activates during terminal monocyte commitment and maturation, reflecting the transition to functional antimicrobial competency rather than stage-specific commitment biology.
key_evidence: LYZ: Canonical bactericidal lysozyme, hallmark of monocyte/macrophage differentiation
S100A8/S100A9: Calprotectin complex (MRP8/14), neutrophil-monocyte shared calcium sensors and inflammatory mediators, not ProMono-stage-specific
RNASE2/RNASE6: Antimicrobial ribonucleases, monocyte effector enzymes
CSTA: Cystatin A, cysteine protease inhibitor protecting cytoplasmic proteases in antimicrobial response
MNDA: Myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen, granulocyte-monocyte lineage marker but not commitment-stage-specific
GRN: Granulins support antimicrobial and tissue remodeling functions
S100A4/S100A6: Calcium-binding proteins involved in cell migration and inflammatory signaling
suggested_validation: Distinguish ProMono-stage-specificity from monocyte maturation/activation using stage-stratified analysis: examine if this signature peaks in Late ProMono vs CD14 Mono or if it represents shared committed-monocyte functions. Compare against KLF4/IRF8-driven transcriptional commitment signatures and GMP-Mono contrasts to confirm whether this reflects ProMono identity or downstream effector maturation independent of commitment stage.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened translational capacity and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in Early GMP progenitors, characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and respiratory chain complexes. The co-expression of splicing machinery (SNRPE) and nucleolar factors (NPM1, HMGN1) suggests active protein synthesis coupled with cell cycle progression and chromatin remodelling typical of proliferative progenitors.

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor primes the ribosome for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, supporting high-throughput protein synthesis demand
MT-ND1, MT-CO2, UQCRH: Mitochondrial respiratory chain components enable oxidative ATP production required for anabolic progenitor metabolism
NPM1: Nucleolar protein involved in centrosome duplication and protein chaperoning, hallmarks of cycling progenitors (12.5% GMP-Cycle co-enrichment)
HMGN1: Chromatin-associated factor facilitating transcriptional access during proliferation; consistent with active myeloid differentiation programme priming
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing; supports splicing demands during lineage commitment transitions
suggested_validation: Validate by co-staining Early GMP for CD34+/KIT+ with phospho-S6 or 4E-BP1 phosphorylation (mTORC1 activity readout) and MitoTracker Deep Red for mitochondrial mass; confirm downregulation of this signature in mature monocytes (CD14+CD16+) where translational demand plateaus and metabolic profile shifts toward OXPHOS quiescence.

functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor maturation centred on cytoplasmic protein accumulation and cysteine protease activity. The programme is dominated by S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A9, S100A8, S100A6, S100A4) characteristic of committed monocytic lineage, coupled with lysosomal hydrolase expression (LYZ, CST3, CSTA) and glycolytic enzymes, supporting metabolic transition from proliferative GMP to functional ProMono.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calcium-binding myeloid protein family marker; S100A8/A9 heterodimer central to monocyte antimicrobial function
LYZ: Canonical monocyte hydrolytic enzyme; lost in GMP-Neut, gained in ProMono commitment
S100A8, S100A6, S100A4: S100 family calcium sensors enriched in committed monocytic lineage, not neutrophil
CSTA, CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitors supporting lysosomal maturation and antigen processing capacity
GRN: Granulin precursor; secreted danger-associated molecule elevated in activated monocytes
ANXA2: Annexin involved in exocytosis and cell surface redistribution during monocyte maturation
PKM, GAPDH: Glycolytic programme shift supporting metabolic demands of ProMono vs quiescent GMP
LGALS1: Galectin-1; cell–cell interaction mediator enriched in monocytic lineage
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain S100A9+/CD14+/CD64+ in Early ProMono gate; confirm absence of MPO/ELANE; RNA-FISH for S100A8, LYZ on sorted Early ProMono vs GMP-Mono; proteomics validation of S100/cystatin abundance; functional assay of lysosomal enzyme activity in this population.

functional_description: This signature captures the granule protein and antimicrobial effector programme of classical CD14+ monocytes and their precursors. The dominant S100A8/A9 calprotectin heterodimer, lysozyme, and ficolin-1 reflect constitutive antimicrobial granule loading and pathogen recognition capacity characteristic of myeloid cells poised for rapid bacterial killing.

S100A8: Calprotectin partner, EF-hand calcium sensor in phagocyte granules, released upon activation
LYZ: Lysozyme (muramidase), quintessential monocyte antimicrobial hydrolase targeting bacterial peptidoglycan
FCN1: Ficolin-1, pattern recognition molecule in monocyte granules mediating complement-like activation
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen, monocyte/granulocyte lineage-restricted nuclear marker
S100A6: Calgranulin C, S100 protein co-localized with A8/A9 in myeloid granules
CSTA: Cystatin A, endogenous cysteine protease inhibitor protecting monocyte granule integrity
CAPG: Gelsolin family actin regulator supporting monocyte cytoskeletal dynamics for phagocytosis
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase, ROS detoxification enzyme in activated monocytes
RNASE2: Non-secretory ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity in myeloid cells
suggested_validation: FACS: Sort CD14+ CD64+ S100A8/A9-high cells and validate antimicrobial function via CFU killing assay and ROS production (DHE/DCFDA). RNA-seq comparison with CD16 Mono (low S100A8/A9) and progenitors would confirm lineage specificity. Microscopy: Confirm S100A8/A9 granule co-localization with LYZ and FCN1 in early ProMono differentiation stages.

functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte population specialized in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation and immune activation. The dominant enrichment of HLA class II loci (DR, DQ, DP) alongside CD74 (invariant chain/CLIP) indicates active processing and presentation of exogenous antigens. Elevated FTH1 and iron metabolism genes suggest metabolic priming for inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: HLA class II α-chain core component of antigen presentation machinery
HLA-DRB1/DRB5: HLA class II β-chains essential for peptide loading and TCR engagement
HLA-DPA1/DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimerization for alternative antigen presentation pathway
HLA-DQA1/DQB1: HLA-DQ complex formation for diverse peptide repertoire presentation
CD74: Invariant chain chaperone and CLIP-peptide loading catalyst in endosomal compartments
HLA-DMA: MHC-II peptide exchange catalyst in specialized presentation pathway
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain reflecting iron metabolism and oxidative stress preparedness
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM-containing adaptor for phagocytic receptors and TLR-induced signaling
CST3: Cystatin for protease regulation during antigen processing
CLEC7A: Dectin-1 C-type lectin receptor for pathogen recognition and presentation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of HLA-DR/DP/DQ surface expression on CD14+ monocytes with intracellular CD74 staining; RNA-seq comparison with CD16 Mono and progenitors to confirm MHC-II dominance; functional assay of antigen presentation capacity to autologous T cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein synthesis and oxidative phosphorylation capacity, characteristic of metabolically active GMP-Mono progenitors preparing for rapid differentiation. The enrichment of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPS2, RPL7A) combined with mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) and translation factors (EEF1B2, PPIA) indicates heightened anabolic demand consistent with committed monocytic progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS24/RPS23/RPL37A/RPS17/RPLP0/RPS2/RPL7A: Ribosomal structural proteins—dominant signature indicating translational machinery upregulation in metabolically demanding differentiation stage
MT-CO2/MT-CO3/UQCRH: Mitochondrial Complex III/IV subunits—elevated OXPHOS capacity supports ATP demand of committed progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—facilitates rapid protein synthesis during GMP-to-monocyte transition
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase—protein folding capacity during differentiation
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic and transcription factor interaction—survival signal in committed progenitors
HMGN1: Chromatin remodeling—accessible chromatin for lineage-specific gene expression
TXN: Redox homeostasis—supports high metabolic activity and monocytic differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD34/CD33/CD14/CD16 combined with measurement of mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1) and ribosomal protein content (RPS24 by intracellular flow) to confirm elevated translation and OXPHOS in GMP-Mono vs Early GMP and early ProMono populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects a metabolically active, antimicrobially competent CD14 monocyte state characterized by robust bacterial sensing and degradation capacity alongside elevated intracellular iron management and oxidative stress resilience. The programme centres on innate immune effector functions (lysozyme-mediated peptidoglycan lysis, phagocytic priming) coupled with metabolic reprogramming to support pro-inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: LYZ: Direct bacterial cell wall degradation (peptidoglycan cleavage); canonical CD14 monocyte antimicrobial factor
S100A9, S100A12, S100A6: Alarmin/DAMP-associated proteins; CD14 monocyte hallmarks reflecting inflammatory/antimicrobial priming
FTH1: Iron storage for Fenton chemistry and ROS generation; critical for antimicrobial oxidative burst
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification; balances NADPH oxidase-driven ROS production
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis enzyme; supports metabolic reprogramming and glycolytic capacity in activated monocytes
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme (moonlighting protein); glycolytic shift is hallmark of CD14 monocyte activation
MAFB, CEBPD: Myeloid TFs driving CD14 monocyte-specific identity and inflammatory competence
ZFP36L1: Early response gene/RNA-binding protein regulating pro-inflammatory cytokine mRNA stability
BCL2A1: Anti-apoptotic protein; maintains monocyte survival during inflammatory activation
PLEK: PKC signalling adaptor; supports TLR-downstream signalling in innate immune activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of LYZ, S100A9, CD14 (high), CCR2 on classical monocytes; correlate with CD64 (FCGR1A) and TLR4/CD14 expression; confirm metabolic state via intracellular iron (Prussian blue) and NADPH oxidase activity (dihydrorhodamine assay); RNA-seq on FACS-sorted CD14+ S100A9+ cells; test antimicrobial capacity via opsonized bacterial killing assays.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal biogenesis and translational capacity in early-to-mid stage GMP progenitors (Early GMP 41%, GMP-Cycle 32%), consistent with the high protein synthesis demands of proliferating myeloid progenitors. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal protein subunits (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) coupled with translation factors (EEF1B2) and nucleolar chaperones (NPM1, PTMA) indicates active ribosome assembly and active translational machinery during GMP expansion.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPL4: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunits defining translational capacity
EEF1B2: elongation factor essential for tRNA delivery to ribosome during active protein synthesis
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein required for ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation
PTMA: anti-apoptotic factor and transcription co-regulator supporting progenitor survival during active cycling
UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain, supporting ATP supply for anabolic demands
HSPB1: chaperone protein managing proteostasis under synthetic stress of high translation rates
Cell composition: 73% Early GMP + GMP-Cycle indicating proliferative progenitor stage
MPO: present at detectable levels consistent with early myeloid priming but not yet downregulated as in ProMono
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring CD34/KIT expression and Ki67 in RPS24+ cells; confirm ribosomal biogenesis by polysome profiling in Early GMP/GMP-Cycle subsets; assess translational activity via puromycin incorporation; contrast with ProMono (should show RPS downregulation and MPO decrease marking lineage commitment)

functional_description: Feature 167 captures a translational machinery signature dominated by ribosomal proteins (40S: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2; 60S: RPL7A, RPL37A, RPL4) and translation factors (EEF1B2), reflecting high protein synthesis demand in early GMP progenitors. This signature is enriched in early/committed myeloid progenitors with elevated metabolic activity (GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH) and RNA processing capacity (HNRNPA1, NPM1), consistent with active cell division and biosynthetic capacity of early GMP rather than differentiation-specific programs.
key_evidence: RPS24/RPS23/RPS17/RPS2/RPL7A/RPL37A/RPL4: 7/15 top genes are canonical ribosomal subunit proteins, indicating robust translation initiation/elongation machinery
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting high-capacity protein synthesis
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein associated with ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation
HSP90AB1: chaperone supporting protein folding during elevated synthesis
GAPDH/LDHB/UQCRH: glycolytic and oxidative phosphorylation enzymes supporting energetic demand of anabolic progenitors

suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein/translation factor expression (flow: anti-RPL7A, anti-RPS2) and protein synthesis rate (puromycin incorporation) across Early GMP vs GMP-Mono vs mature CD14+ monocytes. Validate translation dependency via FT671 (translation inhibitor) or CHX treatment on sorted GMP populations. Cross-reference with polysome profiling or ribosome-associated proteomics.

functional_description: This signature reflects acute myeloid inflammatory activation dominated by S100A family calprotectin components (S100A8/A9/A12) and neutrophil-associated proteins, indicating CD14 monocyte engagement in emergency myelopoiesis and acute phase responses. The enrichment of early and late progenitor monocytes (35% of activating cells) alongside classical CD14 monocytes suggests coordinated emergency granulopoiesis coupled with monocyte inflammatory priming, characteristic of severe infection or sterile injury.
key_evidence: S100A8: Core calprotectin heterodimer component; hallmark of emergency myelopoiesis and acute monocytic inflammation
S100A9: Calprotectin partner; secreted DAMP/PAMP sensor released during intense innate activation
S100A12: Extended calprotectin family; RAGE ligand amplifying inflammatory circuits in acute crisis
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen; marks mature granulomonocytic lineage engagement
FCN1: Ficolins mediate complement-independent pathogen recognition; elevated in emergency myelopoiesis
CAPG: Calcium-regulated actin capping protein; enables rapid cytoskeletal remodeling during migration and phagocytosis
S100A6: Accessory S100 family member amplifying calcium signaling in inflammatory state
CSTA: Cystatin protease inhibitor; balances proteolytic activity during myeloid mobilization
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying S100A8/A9 protein surface/intracellular expression in CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono; qPCR of S100A8/A9 in sorted CD14 Mono from LPS-stimulated vs resting bone marrow cultures; assess progenitor cell cycle status and myeloid maturation markers (CD34, CD13, CD15) to confirm emergency granulopoiesis contribution.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated translational machinery in Early GMP progenitors, marking a transition state characterized by active protein synthesis capacity. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation factors indicates preparation for rapid proliferation and lineage-specific differentiation, consistent with GMP-stage progenitors engaged in biosynthetic upregulation before commitment.

RPS24: 40S subunit protein, part of core ribosomal translation machinery
RPLP0: 60S subunit acidic phosphoprotein, structural component of mature ribosome
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor, directly involved in aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to ribosome
NPM1: Nucleophosmin, cell proliferation marker and ribosome biogenesis coordinator in progenitors
PTMA: Nucleoprotein with antiapoptotic function, elevated in metabolically active progenitor states
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in mRNA processing during active gene expression programs
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling or pulse-chase puromycin incorporation assays on FACS-sorted Early GMP vs mature monocytes to quantify translation rates. Confirm elevated ribosomal biogenesis via NPM1 localization and nascent ribosomal RNA synthesis (BrU incorporation). Cross-validate with proteomics to confirm elevated protein synthesis flux in Early GMP compared to differentiated mono populations.

programme_name: Mitochondrial Oxidative Metabolism and Protein Synthesis
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated mitochondrial respiration (Complex I and IV components) and active protein synthesis machinery, consistent with metabolic demands of early ProMono progenitors during commitment. The enrichment of nuclear organization factors (HMGN1/2, HMGB1) and histone variants suggests open chromatin and transcriptional activity during monocytic differentiation.
key_evidence: MT-CO3: Core respiratory chain complex IV subunit; elevated in metabolically active early ProMono cells
MT-CO2: Cytochrome c oxidase; indicates heightened oxidative phosphorylation
MT-ND1: Respiratory complex I NADH dehydrogenase; OXPHOS dependence of committing progenitors
RPS23/RPS24/RPL37A: Ribosomal proteins; sustained protein synthesis during commitment phase
HMGN1/HMGN2: Nucleosome-binding chromatin remodellers; mark transcriptionally active regions during differentiation
HMGB1: Non-histone architectural protein; facilitates transcriptional remodelling of monocytic TFs
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic and TF-binding; supports survival during ProMono differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantification of mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker) and ROS production in sorted Early/Late ProMono vs GMP-Mono populations; validate against bona fide monocyte commitment markers (KLF4, IRF8, CSF1R) to confirm this reflects the energetic demands of commitment rather than a cycling or stress state.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal biogenesis and translational capacity in Early GMP progenitors, dominated by structural ribosomal proteins (RPS/RPL families) and translation machinery components. The enrichment of these housekeeping genes in Early GMPs relative to mature monocytes indicates high protein synthetic demand during active progenitor proliferation and myeloid differentiation.

RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit structural protein; component of rRNA processing machinery
RPL7A: 60S ribosomal subunit; parallels RPL4, RPL37A in signature
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein; master regulator of ribosome biogenesis and centrosome duplication—marks proliferative stage
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein; regulates mRNA processing and stability in actively transcribing cells
PTMA: nucleolar/cytoplasmic shuttling protein; cell proliferation regulator
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor; indicates active protein synthesis
LDHB: glycolytic enzyme; supports biosynthetic ATP demands of progenitor proliferation
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme and moonlighting protein; general bioenergetic marker
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein and NPM1 expression across Early GMP vs. GMP-Cycle vs. GMP-Mono by qPCR or flow cytometry (NPM1 protein); validate with puromycin incorporation assays to confirm elevated active translation in Early GMP stage

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte specialization in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation coupled with lysosomal cysteine protease activity. The coordinated expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ molecules alongside CD74 (invariant chain) and peptide-processing enzymes (CTSS, CPVL) indicates active antigen processing capacity. This represents a professional antigen-presenting cell phenotype distinct from classical inflammatory or patrolling monocyte functions.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: Complete MHC class II molecular assembly (DR, DP, DQ heterodimers)
CD74: Invariant chain essential for MHC II trafficking, loading, and immune synapse formation
HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB: Peptide-exchange machinery within endosomal-lysosomal compartments
CTSS: Cathepsin S—primary lysosomal cysteine protease for antigenic peptide generation
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase for C-terminal trimming of MHC II-presented peptides
TYROBP: DAP12 adapter for ITAM signaling (associates with KIRs, TLRs on APC)
CST3: Cystatin C—endogenous cysteine protease inhibitor regulating antigen processing balance
MS4A6A: Membrane scaffold potentially involved in receptor clustering during antigen presentation
LGALS2: Galectin-2—lectin for immune modulation and lymphocyte binding

Functional assay: measure antigen uptake and processing via fluorescent antigen or OVA-peptide presentation to CD4+ T cells. Compare to CD16 Mono (lower MHC II) and progenitors (absent).

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis and oxidative metabolism in Early GMP cells transitioning toward monocytic commitment. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPL37A), translation factors (EEF1B2), and RNA-binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPA1) coupled with mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-ND1, MT-CO2) and the ADP/ATP transporter (SLC25A5) indicates elevated anabolic capacity required for biosynthetic demand during myeloid commitment.

EEF1B2: Elongation factor critical for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery during sustained protein synthesis
YBX1: Cold shock domain protein with dual DNA/RNA binding activity; supports translational regulation and mRNA stabilization
HNRNPA1: Pre-mRNA processing and RNA metabolism; modulates splicing patterns during lineage commitment
MT-ND1, MT-CO2: Complex I and IV components indicating elevated oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production
SLC25A5: Mitochondrial ADP/ATP translocase; essential for bioenergetic homeostasis during metabolically active progenitor state

suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry for CD34+/KIT+/CD33+ Early GMP co-expressing ribosomal protein markers; correlate with MPO/CSF1R expression gradient. Single-cell metabolic profiling (seahorse or SCENITH) to confirm elevated OXPHOS and protein synthesis rates. ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq for SPI1/CEBPA occupancy at ribosomal and metabolic gene loci.

functional_description: This signature reflects the lysosomal cysteine protease and antimicrobial effector programme of classical CD14 monocytes, centred on antigen processing (CTSS), bacterial cell wall degradation (LYZ), and danger-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) sensing via ficolin (FCN1). The co-expression of S100A9/A6 calprotectins, iron storage (FTH1), and oxidative stress defence (GPX1) indicates a primed, pro-inflammatory state optimised for intracellular pathogen containment and extracellular tissue remodelling.

LYZ: lysozyme cleaves bacterial peptidoglycan—archetypal monocyte antimicrobial enzyme
FCN1: ficolin mediates complement-independent innate immune recognition of acetylated PAMPs; highly CD14 Mono-specific
S100A9/S100A6: calprotectins are danger-associated alarmins and neutrophil-recruiting factors; hallmark of inflammatory monocytes

AP1S2: clathrin adaptor supports vesicular trafficking required for secretory pathway during cytokine/granule release
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: validate CD14+CD16− (classical monocyte) gate; confirm CTSS, FCN1, S100A9, LYZ protein co-expression by intracellular staining. Functional assay: measure phagocytosis of opsonised bacteria and intracellular CTSS-dependent proteolysis. Compare ZFP36 expression dynamics in LPS-stimulated CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono to confirm post-transcriptional brake. ROS assay: confirm GPX1-dependent H₂O₂ scavenging capacity.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte activation of HLA class II-mediated antigen presentation machinery, coordinated with accessory lysosomal and iron metabolism pathways. The dominance of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ alpha/beta chains alongside CD74 (invariant chain) indicates professional antigen-presenting cell (APC) capacity. Co-expression of TYROBP (DAP12), AIF1, and iron storage (FTH1) supports activated monocyte phenotype engaged in inflammatory antigen presentation rather than innate immune sensing.

HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP presentation pathway, secondary to HLA-DR in monocytes
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ presentation pathway, all three HLA-II types co-activated
CD74: Chaperone for MHC-II assembly and recycling; essential for class II function
HLA-DMA: Peptide editor for HLA-DP/DQ; indicates active antigen processing
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor; bridges TLR and Fc receptor signaling in inflammatory contexts
AIF1: Calcium-responsive actin-binding protein; marker of monocyte activation and migration
FTH1: Iron storage; elevated in activated monocytes with oxidative metabolism
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor; supports lysosomal proteolysis control during antigen processing
FCGRT: IgG Fc receptor; supports antibody-mediated cellular responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: HLA-DR+CD74+CD14++ cells for APC maturation; intracellular staining of HLA-DP/DQ; correlate with phagocytic load and inflammatory cytokine production (TNF, IL-6) to confirm inflammatory APC state vs. steady-state antigen presentation.

programme_name: Monocyte translational activity and myeloid maturation
functional_description: This signature captures active protein synthesis and metabolic activity in differentiating monocytes, particularly in the CD14 Mono and GMP-Mono compartments. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPS26, RPLP0) and hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) reflects high translational demand during myeloid differentiation. FOSB and EGR1 suggest concurrent immediate-early transcriptional responses to maturation signals, while UQCRH indicates elevated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism supporting biosynthetic capacity.

HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD: Globin gene expression typical of early myeloid progenitors with retained erythroid transcriptional memory

UQCRH: Complex III component indicating elevated mitochondrial respiration supporting biosynthetic demand

Confirm hemoglobin gene expression is progenitor-specific (not mature monocyte artifact). Use miRNA-seq or metabolic flux analysis to confirm elevated OXPHOS in this population. Cross-reference FOSB/EGR1 activity with TCF1/mTORC1 pathway components to characterize maturation stimulus.

functional_description: This signature represents a cytoplasmic and nuclear remodelling programme in Early ProMono cells (62% composition) characterized by antimicrobial effector expression (LYZ, RNASE2), calcium-responsive cytoskeletal regulation (TMSB4X, CAPG, S100A8/A9), and chromatin accessibility marking active differentiation (HMGN2, HMGB1/2). The constellation reflects heightened innate defence capacity and cytoplasmic organisation during committed monocyte progenitor maturation, distinct from GMP-stage myeloid multipotency.

S100A8/A9: myeloid-restricted calprotectin complex, inflammation and cell-cell communication
LGALS1: galectin-mediated autocrine regulation, cell differentiation checkpoint

functional_description: This signature marks early GMP-stage progenitors with elevated translational machinery and protein synthesis capacity. The predominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS/RPL genes), translation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar proteins (NPM1, PTMA) indicates active biosynthetic demand characteristic of proliferating myeloid progenitors before terminal differentiation.

programme_name: Early GMP translational capacity and metabolism
functional_description: This signature reflects high ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression, indicating robust protein synthesis capacity in early GMP progenitors. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and mitochondrial respiratory chain genes (MT-ND1, UQCRH) defines metabolically active, proliferating early myeloid progenitors poised for rapid differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins—hallmark of translational demand in rapidly dividing progenitors
RPLP0: P0 ribosomal protein, housekeeping ribosomal component indicating sustained protein synthesis
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity required for efficient peptide elongation during high-throughput protein production
MT-ND1, UQCRH: Mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase and cytochrome c reductase—oxidative phosphorylation engagement supporting biosynthetic metabolism
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein facilitating pre-mRNA processing, required during high transcriptional demand
ACTG1: Cytoskeletal actin supporting cell division and morphological changes in progenitors
PRSS57: Serine protease stored in azurophil granules—early myeloid differentiation priming marker
Cell composition: 41.5% Early GMP + 29.5% GMP-Mono dominance indicates signature captures early commitment phase with bioenergetic acceleration
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosome biogenesis capacity via RPS/RPL qPCR and flow sorting of sorted Early GMP (CD34+KIT+) vs mature monocytes; correlate with polysome profiling and mitochondrial function assays (MitoTracker, Seahorse). Validate PRSS57 azurophil granule storage using immunofluorescence in Early GMP.

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Myeloid Differentiation and Inflammatory Priming
functional_description: This signature reflects terminal myeloid differentiation and innate immune activation of classical CD14+ monocytes, characterized by abundant S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A6/A4) that function as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and potent pro-inflammatory mediators. The co-expression of FCN1 (pattern recognition receptor), CD14 (LPS co-receptor), MNDA (myeloid maturation marker), and actin-regulatory proteins (CAPG, CSTA) indicates cells primed for rapid phagocytic and inflammatory responses. This signature distinguishes mature CD14 Mono from progenitors and CD16 Mono, marking cells at peak inflammatory competence in steady-state bone marrow.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9/A12: Canonical pro-inflammatory alarmins and DAMP effectors; hallmark of activated classical monocytes
S100A4/A6: Calcium-binding proteins regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and inflammatory amplification
CD14: TLR4/LPS co-receptor; confirms CD14 Mono identity and innate sensing capacity
FCN1: Pattern recognition lectin; complement pathway activation and bacterial opsonization
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear antigen; marker of terminal granulomonocytic differentiation
CAPG: Gelsolin-family actin regulator; essential for cytoskeletal remodeling during phagocytosis
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor; regulates cathepsin activity in myeloid cells during inflammation
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; ECM interaction and cell migration in inflammatory niches
Composition 77% CD14 Mono: Robust enrichment in target population; 19% Late ProMono reflects differentiation continuum
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: S100A8/A9 co-staining with CD14/CD16/CCR2; RT-qPCR of S100A8, FCN1, MNDA in sorted CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono and progenitors; immunofluorescence for S100A8/A9 protein in bone marrow sections; functional assay of DAMP release and phagocytic capacity in high-scoring cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein synthesis and nucleolar function in early GMP-stage progenitors, driven by high translational demand during rapid proliferation. The dominance of RPS/RPL genes with accessory nucleolar proteins (NPM1, HMGN1) indicates active ribosomal biogenesis coinciding with GMP cell-cycle priming, rather than lineage-specific commitment signals.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins, reflecting polysome abundance in proliferating Early GMP (72.5%)
NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone and centrosome regulator, marks actively dividing progenitors with elevated protein synthesis
HMGB1, HMGN1: Chromatin-associated proteins promoting open transcription state in cycling GMP
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic nucleolar protein supporting survival during proliferative GMP phase
GMP-Cycle enrichment (20%): Cell-cycle component GMP cells show maximal ribosomal capacity
Absence of lineage markers: No IRF8, CEBPE, CSF1R, MPO, or CD64 suggest pre-commitment state
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression (Western blot for RPS23/RPL37A, qPCR for RPS2) and nucleolar activity (NPM1 immunofluorescence, ribosomal RNA quantification) between sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono vs ProMono to confirm proliferation-driven rather than lineage-driven signature. Correlate with Ki-67/EdU incorporation rates.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression in Early GMP cells, supporting the high protein synthesis demands of early myeloid progenitors during active proliferation and lineage priming. The enrichment of hnRNPs and nucleosome-associated factors suggests active chromatin remodelling and RNA processing accompanying translational activation before lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL4, RPL7A: Multiple ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) indicate elevated translational capacity characteristic of proliferative Early GMP
RPLP0: Large subunit ribosomal protein; core ribosomal component supporting protein synthesis in undifferentiated progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor (guanine nucleotide exchange factor); essential for efficient mRNA translation in proliferating cells
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing and splicing; associated with dynamic gene expression in progenitors undergoing lineage priming
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in centrosome duplication and cell proliferation; abundant in cycling Early GMP
HMGN1: Chromatin-associated protein marking transcriptionally active regions; consistent with open chromatin of actively differentiating progenitors
HSP90AB1: Heat shock protein supporting protein folding during high translational activity and stress responses in proliferating progenitors
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase supporting glycolytic metabolism; energetic demand of early myeloid progenitor cell divisions
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) RNA-seq or qPCR comparing ribosomal protein expression across Early GMP vs. committed ProMono/Monocyte stages; (2) Polysome profiling to confirm active translation in Early GMP; (3) Ribosome biogenesis flux assays (47S pre-rRNA levels) to confirm elevated ribosome production; (4) Cross-reference with protein synthesis reporters (SUnSET assays) in FACS-sorted Early GMP subpopulations.

functional_description: This signature reflects the mature CD14 classical monocyte state characterized by oxidative stress response (GPX1), antimicrobial proteolysis (CST3, CSTA, FCN1), and calcium-mediated inflammatory signaling (S100A8/A9 calprotectin). The module integrates innate immune effector functions including pattern recognition (TYROBP ITAM signaling), antigen presentation (CD74), and myeloid differentiation commitment (MNDA), consistent with primed pro-inflammatory monocytes poised for rapid microbial response.
key_evidence: S100A8/S100A9: Canonical calprotectin complex—damage-associated molecular patterns and microbial PAMPs, abundant in activated CD14 monocytes
GPX1: Antioxidant defense against ROS generated during respiratory burst and inflammatory responses
CST3/CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitors regulating endocytic and proteolytic pathways central to bacterial killing
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor for acetylated PAMPs; CD14 monocyte-enriched lectin pathway opsonin
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor coupling Fc and TLR signaling to downstream inflammatory transcription
CD74: MHC-II chaperone enabling antigen presentation by classical monocytes
MNDA: Myeloid-lineage-restricted nuclear antigen marking committed monocytic differentiation
TMSB4X/AP1S2: Cytoskeletal and vesicular trafficking supporting phagocytosis and degranulation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining S100A8/A9, CD14, CD16 to confirm CD14 Mono enrichment; compare calprotectin secretion and ROS production (DHE/DCFDA) upon LPS/Phorbol stimulation between CD14 vs CD16 monocytes; validate FCN1 surface expression and complement C3b opsonization capacity.

functional_description: This signature defines activated CD14 classical monocytes engaged in acute antimicrobial and inflammatory response, characterized by upregulation of S100 alarmins (S100A8/A9 calprotectin heterodimer, S100A6, S100A12) that promote pathogen sensing, recruitment, and ROS-independent bactericidal activity. The programme integrates pattern recognition (FCN1 ficolin, CD14 LPS co-receptor), myeloid differentiation (MNDA), actin dynamics for migration/phagocytosis (CAPG), and metabolic remodeling (BLVRB heme catabolism, RBP7 lipid metabolism) consistent with pro-inflammatory monocyte activation.
key_evidence: S100A8: Core component of calprotectin; neutrophil/monocyte-derived DAMP with potent antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory activity via RAGE/TLR4
S100A9: S100A8 heterodimer partner; zinc-sequestration antimicrobial function; serum marker of monocyte activation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 pattern recognition receptor; enhances complement-mediated bacterial killing; elevated in CD14 Mono subset
CD14: LPS/LBP co-receptor and master PAMPs sensor; essential for TLR4 signalling and monocyte recruitment
MNDA: Myeloid-restricted nuclear antigen; marker of granulomonocytic differentiation and activated state
S100A6: Calgranulin C; S100 family member supporting antimicrobial responses and calcium signalling
S100A12: Calgranulin C; inflammatory alarm signal; promotes monocyte recruitment and ROS generation
CAPG: Gelsolin-family actin-binding protein; regulates cytoskeletal dynamics essential for chemotaxis and phagocytosis
CSTA: Cystatin A; endogenous cysteine protease inhibitor balancing proteolytic activity during inflammation
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; ECM remodelling during inflammatory monocyte extravasation and tissue infiltration
BLVRB: Biliverdin reductase B; heme catabolism and anti-inflammatory metabolite generation (bilirubin)
RBP7: Retinol-binding protein; lipid metabolism supporting inflammatory metabolic reprogramming
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: S100A8/A9 (calprotectin) co-expression with CD14++CD16- surface phenotype and CCR2+CX3CR1low; single-cell qPCR validation of S100 cluster membership; LPS stimulation time-course to confirm rapid upregulation of S100A8/A9 and MNDA in classical monocytes; spatial transcriptomics to localize signature to bone marrow monocytic compartment

programme_name: Monocyte metabolic maturation and antimicrobial priming
functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic consolidation and antimicrobial effector function in Early ProMono-enriched populations. The dominance of ATP synthase subunits (ATP5B, ATP5F1, ATP5G3, ATP5J2) indicates heightened oxidative phosphorylation to support monocyte energy demands, while LYZ and CSTA encode canonical bactericidal and protease-inhibitory proteins essential for monocyte antimicrobial defence. The concurrent expression of actin-binding (TMSB4X) and galectin proteins (LGALS1) supports cell migration and adhesion during the transition from committed progenitor to pre-egress state.
key_evidence: LYZ: Hallmark monocyte antimicrobial protease, robustly upregulated during ProMono → mature mono transition
ATP5B/ATP5F1/ATP5G3/ATP5J2: ATP synthase components indicating activated OXPHOS; metabolic shift from proliferation to bioenergetic fitness
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration regulator supporting cytoskeletal remodelling and migratory capacity in committed progenitors
LGALS1: Galectin-1 mediates cell–cell interactions and negative feedback on proliferation, consistent with Exit cell-cycle priming
CSTA: Cystatin-family cysteine protease inhibitor supporting proteolytic homeostasis in antimicrobial compartments
Early ProMono dominance (50.5%): Signal is enriched in earliest committed stage before full CD14 surface maturation
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry for LYZ + CSTA + ATP5B in CSF1R+ MS4A3+ CD14-/low and CD14+ gates to confirm Early ProMono specificity; confirm OXPHOS dependency via Seahorse metabolic assay on sorted Early ProMono vs GMP-Mono populations; assess correlation of ATP synthase expression with cell-cycle exit markers (CDKN1A) to confirm pre-egress timing.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 classical monocyte antimicrobial and oxidative burst capacity, featuring constitutive expression of lysozyme (LYZ) for bacterial cell wall degradation and oxidative stress response genes (GPX1, mitochondrial OXPHOS). The program integrates neutrophil elastase inhibition (CSTA), damage-associated alarmin secretion (S100A8/A9, GRN), and immediate early transcription factor activity (FOSB) characteristic of activated inflammatory monocytes primed for pathogen encounter.
key_evidence: LYZ: Direct bactericidal peptidoglycan degradation activity, hallmark of CD14 Mono antimicrobial arsenal
S100A8/S100A9: Calcium-binding alarmin proteins; DAMPs and monocyte granule constituents marking pro-inflammatory state
GPX1: Catalase-independent antioxidant for ROS detoxification post-respiratory burst in phagocytosis
MT-ND1/MT-CO2/MT-CO3: Mitochondrial respiratory chain genes supporting high-energy oxidative phosphorylation for sustained inflammatory activation
FOSB: AP-1 component enabling rapid transcriptional response to TLR and cytokine signaling in activated monocytes
CSF3R: G-CSF receptor mediating myeloid differentiation and emergency monocytopoiesis signals
GRN: Secreted granulin peptides with immunomodulatory and tissue remodeling functions in inflammation
VCAN: ECM proteoglycan involved in inflammatory cell recruitment and tissue migration
CSTA: Cystatin family cysteine protease inhibitor protecting monocyte granule proteins during trafficking
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of S100A8/A9 and LYZ co-expression in CD14+CD16-CCR2+ monocytes; single-cell transcriptomics correlation with antimicrobial module scores; functional assay of bactericidal capacity and ROS production in sorted FOSB+ monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects early monocytic differentiation with dominant innate immune effector functions, characterized by strong S100A8/A9 calcium-binding protein expression and enhanced antimicrobial/proteolytic capacity. The composition (42% CD14 Mono, 39% Early ProMono, 19% Late ProMono) indicates this programme captures the transition from committed progenitors through early monocyte maturation, driven by myeloid differentiation and inflammatory conditioning rather than late-stage commitment factors.
key_evidence: S100A8/S100A9: Calprotectin complex—hallmark of activated myeloid cells; dramatically upregulated in Early ProMono→CD14 Mono transition; calcium-dependent inflammatory mediators
LYZ: Lysozyme—canonical monocyte antimicrobial enzyme; core component of mono lysosomal arsenal; marks departure from neutrophil-biased GMP
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen—granulocyte-monocyte lineage marker; nuclear factor indicating active myeloid identity establishment
FCN1: Ficolin-1—innate immune pattern recognition receptor; monocyte-enriched immune surveillance marker
S100A6/S100A12/S100A4: S100 family expansion—calcium signalling and inflammatory cytokine production; indicates inflammatory monocyte priming
CAPG: Actin-regulatory protein—supports cytoskeletal remodelling required for monocyte migration and extravasation programmes
CSTA/PKM: Protease inhibition and glycolytic commitment—supports metabolic rewiring from progenitor state to effector monocyte metabolism
suggested_validation: Cross-validate against published Early ProMono and CD14 Mono bulk RNA-seq signatures; confirm S100A8/A9 and LYZ elevation by flow cytometry protein levels across ProMono developmental stages; assess whether IRF8 and KLF4 targets are enriched via motif analysis to confirm transcriptional commitment driver engagement.

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and Antigen Presentation
functional_description: This signature represents mature CD14 classical monocytes with elevated iron homeostasis (FTH1-mediated ferritin storage) and robust antigen-presenting cell (APC) function via HLA class II molecules. The co-expression of lysosomal proteases (CTSS, LYZ) and iron metabolism genes indicates preparation for phagocytic degradation of pathogens, while TYROBP (DAP12) signaling supports pattern recognition receptor activation characteristic of inflammatory monocytes.
key_evidence: FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain—iron storage critical for myeloid cell oxidative metabolism and ROS handling; elevated in activated inflammatory monocytes
HLA-DRA, HLA-DMA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DQB1: MHC class II presentation machinery—hallmark of professional APCs; CD14 Mono >> CD16 Mono
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM-containing adaptor—bridges pattern recognition receptors (CLEC7A, TLRs) to inflammatory signaling; essential for monocyte activation
CTSS: Cathepsin S—lysosomal cysteine proteinase for antigen processing; elevated in activated APCs
LYZ: Lysozyme—bacterial peptidoglycan degradation; marks bactericidal and phagocytic capacity
ZFP36L1: TIS11 family zinc finger—early response gene to inflammatory stimuli (TPA, cytokines); mRNA stability regulator
CLEC7A: Dectin-1—fungal/bacterial PAMP receptor; signals through Syk-TYROBP axis
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis—critical for NAD+-dependent metabolism in activated innate immune cells
MAFB: MAF bZIP transcription factor—regulates inflammatory cytokine and MHC II expression in macrophages/monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining: CD14+HLA-DR+FTH1+ population; confirm iron metabolism dependence via ferric iron uptake assays; assess antigen presentation capacity (phagocytosis + peptide-MHC II display); correlate ZFP36L1 upregulation with inflammatory cytokine mRNA turnover under LPS/TLR stimulation

functional_description: This signature represents the lysosomal-endosomal compartment maturation programme in CD14 monocytes, characterized by cysteine protease activity (CTSS, CPVL), iron storage (FTH1), saposin-mediated lipid degradation (PSAP), and MHC-II antigen presentation machinery (CD74). The programme reflects active intracellular degradative capacity coupled with professional antigen-presenting cell (APC) differentiation, distinct from the pro-inflammatory or PAMP-sensing programmes.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine proteinase essential for antigen processing and peptide presentation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor enabling Fc receptor and innate immune signalling in phagocytes
FCN1: Innate immune lectin (ficolin) for pattern recognition and complement activation
FTH1: Iron storage capacity indicating high metabolic and degradative flux
PSAP: Saposin-mediated lipid hydrolysis for lysosomal function and autophagy
CD68: Pan-monocyte/macrophage marker; lysosomal-associated membrane glycoprotein
CD74: MHC-II chaperone for Class II antigen presentation pathway
COTL1: Actin dynamics regulating phagocytic cup formation and cell migration
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain enabling antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis
LGALS3: Galectin-3 bridging innate recognition and inflammasome priming
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: Sort CD14+CTSS+CD74+ monocytes and assess lysosomal content (LysoTracker), antigen uptake capacity, and FITC-dextran degradation kinetics. Compare with CD16 Mono (lower CD74) and GMP controls. Functional assay: Measure protease activity (cathepsin S/L) and MHC-II-restricted antigen presentation using model peptides.

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic stress and cytoplasmic calcium-binding activity in differentiating CD14 monocytes, characterized by prominent S100A8/A12 (calprotectin components) expression and hemoglobin gene carryover from erythroid progenitor contamination. The signature lacks canonical inflammatory (TNF, IL1B, IL6) and PAMP-sensing (TLR2, TLR4, CD14) markers, instead representing post-transcriptional remodeling during monocytic maturation with active protease inhibition.
key_evidence: S100A8: Calcium-binding alarmin with strong CD14 Mono enrichment (86% of top activators); calprotectin component induced during myeloid stress
S100A12: Partner S100 protein in calprotectin heterodimer; parallel elevation indicates inflammation-independent differentiation signal
MNDA: Myeloid-lineage-restricted nuclear antigen marking granulomonocytic differentiation; confirms monocyte maturation trajectory
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor suggesting proteolytic remodeling during monocyte maturation
HBA1/HBA2/HBB/HBD: Hemoglobin genes indicate erythroid progenitor carryover (Early/Late ProMono = 14% of activators); not functionally relevant to CD14 Mono
ATP5J2/ATP5F1: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components reflecting metabolic demands of monocyte maturation
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein involved in cytoskeletal remodeling during cell differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry (CD14+CD16− with S100A8/A12 median fluorescence intensity); compare against inflammatory monocyte signature (TNF+IL1B+). Assess whether hemoglobin gene expression correlates with progenitor contamination or genuine CD14 Mono redox state. Single-cell proteomics recommended to distinguish calprotectin secretion from intracellular accumulation.

functional_description: This signature captures the classical CD14+ monocyte differentiation and activation state, characterized by myeloid lineage commitment markers (MNDA), pattern recognition receptor signaling (FCN1, TYROBP/DAP12), and calcium-responsive innate immune effector proteins (S100A8/A9/A11/A4/A6). The enrichment of lysosomal proteases (CTSS) and actin-binding proteins (AIF1) indicates active phagocytic and migratory capacity typical of inflammatory classical monocytes.
key_evidence: FCN1: Ficolin-1 is a soluble pattern recognition receptor for bacterial PAMPs and apoptotic cells; marker of activated innate immunity
MNDA: Myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen—lineage-restricted marker of granulocyte-monocyte differentiation, nuclear localization indicates active myeloid commitment
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM-containing adaptor mediates signaling downstream of TREM and Fc receptors; couples to inflammatory responses
CD14: Canonical LPS co-receptor and monocyte identity marker; essential for TLR4-MyD88 bacterial sensing pathway
S100A8/A9: Calprotectin heterodimer; neutrophil and monocyte alarmin with pro-inflammatory activity and leukocyte recruitment function
S100A4/A6/A11: S100 calcium-binding proteins implicated in monocyte migration, cytoskeletal dynamics, and inflammatory responses
CTSS: Cathepsin S lysosomal protease; essential for antigen processing and phagocytic degradation in myeloid cells
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain component of FCGR1A (CD64) signaling; mediates antibody-opsonized pathogen recognition
AIF1: Allograft inflammatory factor-1; actin-binding protein promoting macrophage activation and vascular inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: co-expression of CD14++, FCGR1A+, CCR2+ on classical monocytes; confirm absence of CD16 and CX3CR1. Single-cell RNA-seq differential expression analysis against CD16 mono and progenitor clusters. Functional assay: LPS-stimulation with measurement of TNF/IL-6 production and phagocytic capacity via S. aureus opsonization.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and metabolic priming
functional_description: This signature represents a metabolically active, protein synthesis-dominant programme enriched in early GMP progenitors. The preponderance of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0), mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-CO2, UQCRH), and glycolytic enzymes (TPI1) indicates heightened translational capacity and ATP production required for rapid myeloid differentiation and proliferation.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins—signature of high protein synthesis demand in proliferating early GMP
MT-CO2, UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain components—reflect increased oxidative metabolism supporting energy-intensive myeloid progenitor expansion
TPI1: glycolytic enzyme—priming cells for rapid ATP generation during GMP proliferation
TXN: redox homeostasis regulator—protects metabolically active progenitors from oxidative stress during differentiation
PTMA, NPM1: nucleolar/centrosomal proteins—coordinate protein biogenesis and cell cycle progression in cycling GMP
HMGN1, YBX1, HNRNPA1: chromatin remodelling and RNA-binding proteins—maintain open chromatin for active myeloid differentiation transcription
Cell composition 45% Early GMP + 17% GMP-Mono + 4.5% GMP-Cycle: programme peaks in cycling/early-committed progenitors, not mature monocytes
suggested_validation: Measure ribosomal protein expression (Western blot or flow cytometry) and global protein synthesis rate (e.g. puromycin incorporation assay) across Early GMP vs. Late ProMono vs. mature monocyte stages. Confirm metabolic state by seahorse analysis (OXPHOS vs. glycolysis) to validate oxidative metabolism signature.

functional_description: This signature captures a core translational machinery programme dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS/RPL subunits) and translation elongation factors, reflecting heightened protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP progenitors. The enrichment of RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, YBX1) and nucleolar factors (NPM1) suggests active ribosome biogenesis and robust anabolic metabolism characteristic of proliferative progenitor states.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit structural proteins—core translation machinery
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit components—essential for peptide bond formation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to ribosome
HNRNPA1, YBX1: RNA-binding proteins regulating mRNA processing and stability during active synthesis
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein coordinating ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation
GAPDH, HMGN1, H3F3A: Metabolic and chromatin remodelling support for anabolic GMP state
69% Early GMP composition: signature reflects progenitor proliferation state, not lineage commitment
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein abundance by flow cytometry (anti-RPS2, anti-RPL7A) across Early GMP vs CD14 Mono; confirm elevated protein synthesis rate via puromycin incorporation assay; cross-reference with ribosome profiling or polysome fractionation in sorted GMP subsets to validate translational capacity gradient.

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis machinery in Early GMP progenitors, characterized by abundant ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation factors (EEF1B2). The co-expression of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1) indicates high metabolic activity supporting biosynthetic demand during early myeloid progenitor expansion.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit composition—translational capacity in actively differentiating GMP
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1: Complex I/IV OXPHOS components—energetic support for anabolic processes in early progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—active protein synthesis during GMP commitment
HNRNPA1, PTMA: RNA-binding and anti-apoptotic functions—post-transcriptional regulation in viable, expanding progenitors
HSP90AB1: Heat shock protein—proteostasis during rapid differentiation
Early GMP dominance (66.5%): Signature enriched in GMP-Mono transition stage, not mature monocytes
suggested_validation: Confirm ribosomal biogenesis activity via polysome profiling or 3H-leucine incorporation assays in sorted Early GMP vs mature CD14 monocytes. Validate mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/TMRE) and oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse) to confirm metabolic coupling. Cross-reference with ribosome biogenesis TFs (e.g., NPM1, MYBL2 expression) in Early GMP compartment.

functional_description: This signature represents elevated ribosomal and translation machinery components in Early GMP progenitors, reflecting high protein synthesis capacity during active proliferation and progenitor maintenance. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS, RPL), translation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar/RNA-binding proteins (NPM1, HNRNPA1, YBX1) indicates robust translational activity characteristic of metabolically active, cycling progenitors prior to terminal myeloid differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS17, RPS24, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating high translation capacity
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to ribosome
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating cell proliferation and protein chaperoning
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing and translation regulation
YBX1: Cold shock domain protein with DNA/RNA binding activity; supports progenitor maintenance
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor and transcription factor co-regulator supporting progenitor survival
GAPDH, UQCRH: Glycolytic and mitochondrial metabolic enzymes supporting energy demands
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry measuring ribosomal protein (RPS23, RPL7A) expression across CD34+/KIT+ Early GMP vs. GMP-Mono; correlate with Ki67 proliferation markers and metabolic profiling (glucose/amino acid uptake). Confirm distinction from mature monocytes by CD14/CD16 gating.

functional_description: This signature represents a translational capacity programme dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPS17, RPS2) and translation factors (EEF1B2), coupled with nucleosome remodelling factors (HMGN1/2) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1). The enrichment in Early GMP (42.5%) and GMP-Mono (18.5%) suggests priming of protein synthesis machinery during early monocytic commitment, while the presence of PTMA (apoptosis suppression) and ANP32B (chromatin dynamics) indicates active transcriptional remodelling alongside translational preparation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPS17, RPS2: core 60S/40S ribosomal subunit proteins establishing global translational capacity
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor indicating active protein synthetic flux
HMGN1/2: nucleosome binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin, supporting active gene expression during GMP differentiation
HNRNPA1: pre-mRNA processing and splicing factor indicating coordinated transcriptional-translational coupling
PTMA: inhibitor of apoptosis protecting metabolically active progenitors
Early GMP dominance (42.5%): signature captures early commitment stage requiring protein synthesis capacity before lineage-specific programmes
UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport suggesting energy demand matching anabolic translation activity
suggested_validation: Validate with bulk polysome profiling or ribosome footprinting on Early GMP vs mature monocytes to confirm elevated translation initiation/elongation; assess correlation with cell cycle entry markers (CDK1, PCNA) to determine if translational priming precedes or accompanies S-phase; use RT-qPCR for RPS24, EEF1B2, HMGN1 on flow-sorted Early GMP populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive ribosomal protein and translation factor expression in Early GMP progenitors, indicating active protein synthesis required for rapid cell division and differentiation. The dominance of RPS and RPL components (40S and 60S subunits) with supporting elongation factors (EEF1B2) and nucleolar proteins (NPM1) is consistent with high translational demand in proliferating early myeloid progenitors prior to lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins—core translation machinery
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—large subunit structural components
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor GEF activity—facilitates aminoacyl-tRNA delivery
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein with centrosome duplication and cell proliferation roles—consistent with cycling Early GMP
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein for pre-mRNA processing—active transcriptional landscape
GAPDH, LDHB, UQCRH: glycolytic and mitochondrial metabolism—energy supply for biosynthesis
PTMA: anti-apoptotic function—progenitor survival during differentiation priming
79.5% Early GMP composition: signature peaks in non-cycling but metabolically active progenitors
suggested_validation: Confirm elevated ribosomal biogenesis by quantifying 40S/60S subunit ratios and NPM1 nucleolar localization in sorted Early GMP vs. committed GMP-Mono by flow cytometry and immunofluorescence. Assess protein synthesis rates using puromycin incorporation or O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) labeling. Correlate with absence of commitment-associated TF signatures (IRF8, CEBPE) to exclude ProMono state.

programme_name: CD14 Mono Iron Metabolism Oxidative Stress
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 classical monocyte state characterized by elevated iron homeostasis (FTH1), NAD+ metabolism (NAMPT), and myeloid activation markers, coupled with stress-response transcription factors and innate immune signaling. The program integrates metabolic reprogramming for ROS generation capacity with post-transcriptional regulation of inflammatory mediators.
key_evidence: FTH1: Heavy-chain ferritin for iron storage, critical cofactor for NADPH oxidase-dependent ROS generation in activated monocytes
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis enzyme supporting glycolytic/oxidative metabolism and CD14+ monocyte inflammatory activation
ZFP36L1: mRNA stability/decay factor regulating TNF, IL6, and other pro-inflammatory cytokine transcripts in TLR-activated monocytes
MAFB: Master transcription factor for monocyte/macrophage lineage identity and maturation
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor protein in FcγR signaling and TLR/DAP12 complexes, core to phagocyte activation
PLEK: Phosphoinositide binding protein in PKC signaling downstream of pattern recognition receptors
MAP3K8: TPL2 kinase mediating TNF/IL-1 signaling through NF-κB and MAPK pathways in myeloid cells
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism enzyme, marker of metabolic stress and immune activation in inflammatory monocytes
BCL2A1: Anti-apoptotic factor sustaining activated monocyte survival during inflammatory responses
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor Dectin-1 for β-glucan recognition, complementary to TLR signaling
suggested_validation: RT-qPCR validation of FTH1, NAMPT, ZFP36L1, TYROBP in sorted CD14+ Mono from inflammatory vs. steady-state bone marrow; flow cytometry co-staining for CD14, CD64, and intracellular iron/ROS markers; assess correlation with TLR2/TLR4 activation status and CCR2 expression for egress-primed classical monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects early GMP differentiation toward monocytic lineage with prominent metabolic and translational machinery activation. The predominance of ribosomal proteins, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components, and antioxidant enzymes indicates metabolic reprogramming during GMP-to-monocyte transition, coupled with cell survival signals suppressing apoptosis.
key_evidence: MPO: Myeloperoxidase - critical early myeloid marker present in GMP-Mono and GMP-Cycle, priming for both monocytic and neutrophilic differentiation
RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A: Ribosomal proteins - elevated translational capacity supporting rapid protein synthesis during GMP proliferation and differentiation
UQCRH, UQCRQ, MT-CO2: Mitochondrial OXPHOS subunits - indicating increased ATP production and metabolic maturation in early GMP stages
GSTP1: Glutathione S-transferase - antioxidant enzyme protection during active myeloid differentiation and metabolic stress
PTMA: Apoptosis inhibitor - survival signal maintaining GMP and early ProMono populations during lineage commitment
HMGN1: Active chromatin architecture regulator - facilitating transcriptional plasticity during GMP differentiation
TXN: Thioredoxin - redox homeostasis supporting metabolic reprogramming and cell viability
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry co-staining: MPO+CD34+CD13+ (early GMP signature) vs MPO+CD34-CSF1R+ (Early ProMono signature). Measure mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1) and oxidative phosphorylation capacity (seahorse) across sorted GMP substages. Confirm PTMA and GSTP1 expression by qRT-PCR in FACS-sorted GMP-Cycle vs Early ProMono populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein synthesis and nucleosomal chromatin remodelling in early GMP and early ProMono cells. The dominance of ribosomal components (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17) combined with chromatin-associated proteins (HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1) indicates active transcriptional engagement and protein synthesis capacity characteristic of metabolically active progenitors primed for lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17: Ribosomal structural proteins indicating high translational machinery abundance in actively differentiating progenitors
HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1: Nucleosomal DNA-binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin required during GMP lineage priming
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic and transcription factor binding activity supporting progenitor viability during commitment decisions
YBX1, ANP32B: RNA/DNA binding proteins facilitating transcriptional reprogramming during mono vs neutro fate specification
GAPDH, TPI1, PPIA: Glycolytic and protein folding machinery reflecting metabolic demands of early commitment phase
Early GMP dominance (39.0%) with Early ProMono (17.5%) and GMP-Mono (15.5%) confirms enrichment in uncommitted/early-committed progenitor stages
suggested_validation: Validate with single-molecule FISH or qPCR quantifying ribosomal protein and HMGN expression across sorted Early GMP, Early ProMono, and mature monocyte populations. Confirm by measuring global translation rate (e.g., puromycin incorporation) and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) in Early GMP vs committed ProMono stages to distinguish progenitor from differentiation-associated signals.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened lysosomal/endosomal maturation and catabolic activity in activated monocytes, with coordinated iron sequestration via ferritin and proteolytic processing through cathepsin S and saposin pathways. The co-expression of TYROBP (ITAM signaling), actin remodeling factors (COTL1, AIF1), and LPS-responsive genes (LST1) indicates engagement of pattern recognition receptor signaling coupled to cellular activation and antigen processing.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage and ROS detoxification—critical for monocyte oxidative stress management during inflammatory activation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing co-receptor linking pathogen recognition to intracellular signaling; marker of myeloid activation
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for MHC-II antigen presentation and phagosomal degradation
CD68: Canonical monocyte/macrophage pan-marker; lysosomal-associated membrane protein indicating phagocytic/degradative capacity
PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lysosomal hydrolase function and lipid metabolism in activated myeloid cells
COTL1: Actin-binding protein coupling cytoskeletal dynamics to 5-lipoxygenase signaling; enhanced in inflammatory monocytes
AIF1: Calcium-binding protein induced by cytokines; promotes monocyte/macrophage activation
LST1: LPS and IFN-γ-responsive immunoregulatory membrane protein; marker of bacterial PAMP sensing
CXCL16: Chemokine and adhesion molecule; mediates monocyte trafficking and TNF-responsive inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+ monocytes for TYROBP/DAP12 and CD68 expression alongside TLR4/CD14/LPS-binding. Compare CTSS, FTH1 transcript levels between CD14 Mono (high) vs CD16 Mono (low) by qPCR. Functional assay: measure ROS production (DCFDA) and phagocytic capacity (IgG-opsonized beads) in cells sorted by signature scores; correlate with iron content (Prussian blue) and cathepsin activity.

programme_name: MHC Class II Antigen Presentation CD14 Mono
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte population specialized in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation and adaptive immunity coordination. The dominance of HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, and HLA-DP loci alongside CD74 (invariant chain) and lysosomal proteases indicates active antigen processing and presentation capacity. This represents a distinct immunoregulatory CD14 mono subset poised for T cell activation rather than canonical PAMP-driven inflammation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: MHC class II α-chain; core component of HLA-DR, DQ, DP presentation complex
HLA-DRB1: MHC class II β-chain; pairs with DRA for peptide-MHC display to CD4+ T cells
CD74: Invariant chain chaperone; essential for MHC class II assembly and ER-to-endosome trafficking
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: Non-classical MHC II; catalyzes peptide exchange in endosomal compartments
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: MHC class II heterodimer; mediates presentation of diverse antigenic peptides
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: MHC class II; alternative presentation pathway with distinct peptide preferences
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease; critical for antigen processing into MHC II-compatible peptides
CPVL: Carboxypeptidase; trims peptides in endosomal compartments prior to MHC II loading
PSAP: Generates saposins; facilitates lysosomal hydrolase function during antigen degradation
CST3: Cystatin; modulates cysteine protease activity during antigen processing
FGL2: Fibrinogen-like protein; emerging immunoregulatory function in myeloid cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: sort CD14+ HLA-DR++ cells and validate elevated MHC class II surface expression; RNA-seq confirm HLA-DM and protease co-expression; functional assay measuring T cell activation capacity versus canonical inflammatory CD14 mono; interrogate whether this signature correlates with bone marrow resident versus egressed monocyte phenotype.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein synthesis capacity and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in early GMP/GMP-Mono cells. The enrichment of 40S/60S subunit components (RPS26, RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0) and ATP synthase subunits (ATP5J2, ATP5G3, UQCRH) indicates heightened biosynthetic activity and ATP generation supporting proliferation and metabolic demands of commitment-stage progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0: Core ribosomal 40S/60S subunit proteins indicating translation machinery expansion
ATP5J2, ATP5G3, UQCRH: Mitochondrial ATP synthase and electron transport chain components supporting energetic demands
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic nucleoprotein promoting cell survival during commitment
TXN: Redox regulator protecting against oxidative stress during metabolic upregulation
SNRPF, SNRPE: Spliceosome assembly enabling rapid mRNA processing for lineage genes
Early GMP: 42% composition with GMP-Mono: 27.5% indicates progenitor-level metabolic elevation before terminal differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate via bulk RNA-seq comparing Early GMP + GMP-Mono vs CD14 Mono for ribosomal/OXPHOS signature; measure mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP levels by flow cytometry in FACS-sorted GMP populations; assess translation rate via O-propargyl-puromycin incorporation in early vs mature monocytes.

programme_name: Classical monocyte antimicrobial and damage response
functional_description: This signature captures the core effector programme of CD14+ classical monocytes, dominated by S100 calprotectin family members (S100A8/A9/A12/A6/A4) that serve as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and antimicrobial mediators. The co-expression of pattern recognition receptors (FCN1 for complement-like sensing), lysosomal hydrolases (LYZ), protease inhibitors (CSTA), and metabolic regulators (TYMP, BLVRB) reflects activation of innate immune surveillance and bactericidal capacity.
key_evidence: S100A9: Central component of calprotectin heterodimer (S100A8/A9), secreted DAMP driving monocyte recruitment and antimicrobial defence; zinc/calcium sequestration
S100A8: Partner protein in calprotectin complex, hallmark of inflammatory monocyte activation; translocates to extracellular matrix upon PAMP/DAMP sensing
S100A12: Calgranulin C, S100 family member expressed in activated myeloid cells; synergizes with A8/A9 in inflammatory signalling
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (L-ficolin), pattern recognition receptor binding acetylated ligands; complement activation and pathogen sensing in monocytes
LYZ: Lysozyme, canonical monocyte hydrolase for bacterial peptidoglycan degradation; marker of myeloid differentiation and antimicrobial function
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor protein; couples immunoreceptors to Syk signalling for phagocytosis and inflammatory activation in monocytes
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; ECM component modified during monocyte extravasation and tissue remodelling in inflammation
GRN: Progranulin precursor; pleiotropic inflammatory mediator cleaved into antimicrobial granulin peptides; elevated in activated monocytes
CSTA: Cystatin A; cysteine protease inhibitor regulating cathepsin activity during phagocytosis and antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14++CD16- monocytes for S100A8/A9 protein (calprotectin) surface expression and intracellular accumulation; qPCR validation of S100A8/A9/A12 in FACS-sorted CD14+ vs CD16+ monocytes; LPS/TNF-α stimulation time-course to confirm PAMP-responsive induction; immunofluorescence of calprotectin in bone marrow monocyte infiltrates or inflammatory tissue biopsies

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Lysosomal and Antimicrobial Program
functional_description: This signature reflects the lysosomal and antimicrobial effector compartment of CD14 classical monocytes, characterized by proteolytic enzymes, bacterial killing functions, and cytoskeletal dynamics supporting phagocytosis. The gene set emphasizes intracellular degradation capacity and innate immune recognition rather than inflammatory cytokine production or PAMP sensing.
key_evidence: CTSS: Cathepsin S, core lysosomal cysteine proteinase for antigen processing and pathogen degradation
