LYZ: Lysozyme, bactericidal enzyme targeting bacterial peptidoglycan in phagolysosomes
FCN1: Ficolin-1, pattern recognition receptor for bacterial PAMP bridging phagocytosis
CST3: Cystatin C, lysosomal cysteine protease inhibitor regulating proteolytic balance
S100A9: Calprotectin component with antimicrobial and alarmin properties in myeloid cells
TYROBP: DAP12, ITAM-bearing adaptor linking Fc and pattern recognition receptors to phagocytic signaling
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein supporting dynamic cytoskeleton remodeling during phagocytosis
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase-1 for ROS detoxification post-antimicrobial oxidative burst
AP1S2: Adaptor protein complex 1 coordinating vesicular trafficking in endosomal-lysosomal pathway
HLA-DRA: MHC class II alpha chain for antigen presentation post-lysosomal degradation
RGS2: Negative regulator of G-protein signaling dampening chemotactic responses
ZFP36: mRNA destabilization factor for inflammatory mediator control
MS4A6A: Membrane-spanning 4A family, potential immunoregulatory surface molecule
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: sort CD14+ monocytes and stratify by CTSS/LYZ co-expression; correlate signature activation with intracellular peroxidase activity (MPO/oxidative burst assay), phagolysosomal capacity (pHrodo bacterial uptake), and antigen processing capacity (OVA-peptide presentation assay). Compare with CD16 monocytes which show low CTSS/LYZ expression.

functional_description: This signature captures early monocytic commitment from GMP stage, characterized by metabolic rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis capacity, with concurrent chromatin opening and apoptosis resistance. The dominance of GMP-Mono (47.5%) and Early ProMono (28%) populations indicates capture of the transition from multipotent progenitor to monocyte-committed precursor, prior to full CSF1R/CD64 upregulation seen in mature monocytes.
key_evidence: MPO: Retained expression marks myeloid lineage priming in both GMP and early monocytic differentiation, distinguishing from late ProMono
MT-CO3, MT-CO2, UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components indicate metabolic shift toward OXPHOS supporting monocyte differentiation
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor enabling survival during GMP commitment phase and early differentiation stress
HMGN1, HMGN2: Chromatin remodeling proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin, consistent with lineage-specific TF activation (SPI1, CEBPA)
GSTP1: Detoxification enzyme upregulated during metabolic activation and differentiation
RPS24, RPL37A: Ribosomal proteins indicating heightened protein synthesis during active differentiation
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase supporting nascent protein folding during expansion phase
TPI1, GAPDH: Glycolytic enzymes reflecting metabolic activation concurrent with OXPHOS shift
ANP32B: Nuclear-localized histone binding protein supporting chromatin accessibility during lineage commitment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CD34/KIT expression decline alongside MPO, combined with CSF1R/CD64 low confirmation to exclude late ProMono; RNA-FISH for mitochondrial markers (MT-CO3) with CEBPA/SPI1 to confirm active monocytic TF programs; metabolic flux analysis (Seahorse OXPHOS vs glycolysis) in sorted GMP-Mono vs Early ProMono populations

functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 monocytes with enhanced cytoskeletal dynamics, lysosomal proteolytic capacity, and ITAM-coupled innate immune signaling. The program highlights actin remodeling, intracellular antigen processing, and pattern recognition receptor (PRR) signaling infrastructure characteristic of classically-activated inflammatory monocytes primed for phagocytosis and antimicrobial responses.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: actin-binding/sequestering protein driving cytoskeletal plasticity required for migration and phagocytosis
MNDA: myeloid-specific nuclear antigen marking terminal monocytic differentiation and activation state
FCN1: ficolins/pattern recognition receptor for PAMP sensing and complement-independent opsonization
CTSS: cathepsin S in lysosomal proteolytic pathway for intracellular antigen processing and MHC-II presentation
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor protein coupling Fc receptors and myeloid DAP12-associated lectins to downstream signaling
FCER1G: FcγR common gamma chain in Fcγ receptor signaling complex (CD64/FCGR1A pathway)
S100A4, S100A11: calmodulin-like proteins involved in monocyte migration and inflammatory responses
JUN: c-Jun AP-1 component enabling pro-inflammatory transcriptional response
RGS2: G protein signaling regulator fine-tuning chemokine receptor (CCR2) responsiveness
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry/immunofluorescence: co-stain CD14++CD16- cells for MNDA, FCN1, and TYROBP; validate functional significance by Fc receptor engagement assays (anti-IgG opsonized particles) measuring phagocytosis and ROS production; assess actin dynamics via F-actin staining post-activation.

functional_description: This signature captures the transition from GMP to committed monocytic progenitors (Early ProMono), marked by elevated protein synthesis machinery, oxidative stress resistance, and metabolic activation rather than proliferation. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins, antioxidant enzymes, and energetic cofactors reflects active differentiation and preparation for terminal monocytic maturation, without cell-cycle markers characteristic of cycling GMP.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: actin remodeling protein essential for monocyte migration and cytoskeletal reorganization during differentiation
RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A: ribosomal proteins indicating active translation during lineage commitment and protein synthesis for monocytic effector molecules
MT-CO2: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation component supporting increased metabolic demand in differentiating monocytes
GPX1, GSTP1, TXN: antioxidant stress response enzymes protecting against oxidative challenge during myeloid maturation
LYZ: lysozyme induction marks monocytic lineage priming and antimicrobial functional acquisition
MIF: macrophage migration inhibitory factor supporting inflammatory monocyte phenotype and immune function
HMGN1, H2AFZ: nucleosomal remodeling proteins indicating active transcriptional reprogramming during differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of GMP-Mono and Early ProMono with CD34, CD14, CD33, CSF1R to confirm differentiation trajectory; single-cell qPCR for IRF8 vs CEBPE balance; metabolic assays (Seahorse) comparing OXPHOS and glycolysis between GMP-Mono and ProMono; immunofluorescence for LYZ, GSTP1 protein localization in committed monocytic populations

functional_description: This signature reflects a proliferative, metabolically active Early ProMono population characterized by elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity and active chromatin remodeling. The coordinated upregulation of Complex I (MT-ND1, MT-ND5) and Complex IV (MT-CO2, MT-CO3) components, combined with histone variant and nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGB1/2, HMGN2, H2AFZ), indicates heightened bioenergetic demand supporting rapid cell cycle progression and transcriptional activity during monocyte commitment.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Respiratory chain complex assembly and OXPHOS capacity in proliferating progenitors
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2: Nucleosome remodeling and transcriptionally active chromatin permissive for lineage commitment genes
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics and cell cycle regulation consistent with Early ProMono proliferation
HNRNPA2B1: RNA processing during rapid biosynthesis in actively cycling monocyte progenitors
H2AFZ, H2AFV: Histone variants marking active chromatin at commitment loci
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease expression emerging in Early ProMono differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1 staining) and electron transport chain activity (seahorse metabolic analysis) in sorted Early ProMono vs GMP; confirm histone mark enrichment (H3K4me3, H3K9ac) at KLF4/IRF8 target loci by ChIP; assess RNASE2 antimicrobial activity as Early ProMono differentiation marker

functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 monocyte innate immune response characterized by S100 calmodulin proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A4/A6) that serve as danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), calcium-responsive signaling hubs, and endogenous TLR4 ligands. The co-expression of FCN1 (ficolin-1, pattern recognition receptor) and elevated calcium-binding protein abundance indicates primed inflammatory state with enhanced pattern recognition and cell migration capacity. Hemoglobin components (HBA1/HBA2/HBB) and VCAN likely reflect phagocytic burden or recent iron handling from RBC uptake typical of inflammatory monocyte extravasation.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9/A12: Canonical DAMP/PAMP-associated calmodulin proteins; S100A8/A9 heterodimerize as calprotectin, TLR4 ligand inducing pro-inflammatory cytokine release
S100A4/A6: Calcium-responsive proteins regulating actin dynamics and cell migration—hallmarks of CCR2-driven bone marrow egress and inflammatory recruitment
FCN1: Ficolins are pattern recognition receptors activating lectin complement pathway; elevated in activated monocytes at infection/inflammation sites
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan upregulated in inflammatory myeloid cells; ECM remodeling during monocyte extravasation and infiltration
HBA1/HBA2/HBB: Elevated hemoglobin genes indicate active erythrophagocytosis or recent RBC-derived iron uptake, typical of inflammatory CD14 monocytes
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein; essential for monocyte migration and cytoskeletal dynamics during CCR2-mediated egress
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining S100A9 with CD14, CCR2, and inflammatory markers (TNF, IL-6); assess S100A8/A9 secretion by ELISA upon LPS/TLR4 stimulation; confirm FCN1 surface expression and complement-C3b deposition; validate calcium imaging response to PAMP stimulation in sorted CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono

functional_description: This signature reflects CD16 monocyte-enriched (60.5%) metabolic and antimicrobial programmes, centred on iron homoeostasis (FTH1), interferon-stimulated antiviral defence (IFITM3), and Fc-gamma receptor-mediated immune surveillance (FCGR3A). The gene set captures patrolling monocyte phenotypes with elevated metabolic stress responses and type I interferon-induced antiviral capacity.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 lineage marker; enables ADCC and immune complex handling
IFITM3: Type I IFN-induced antiviral protein; canonical CD16 mono antiviral programme
FTH1: Iron storage protein; reflects heightened metabolic demand in activated CD16 monocytes
CXCL16: IFN-γ-responsive chemokine; involved in immune surveillance and pathogen response
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibition; IFN-γ and LPS-inducible; typical CD16 mono activation marker
COTL1: Actin-binding protein; supports cytoskeletal dynamics for patrolling and crawling behaviour
TIMP1: Matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor; protects vascular integrity during CD16 mono surveillance
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism regulator; metabolic adaptation to infection and immune activation
LRRC25: Presumed immune regulatory protein; enriched in CD16 mono subset
MS4A7: CD16 monocyte-associated membrane protein; MS4A family member with immune function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining FCGR3A+CX3CR1+CD14low with IFITM3, FTH1 protein levels; qPCR validation of signature genes in FACS-sorted CD16 vs CD14 monocytes; functional assays testing iron-dependent antiviral capacity (e.g., VSV infection with iron chelation).

programme_name: Early GMP chromatin organization and protein synthesis
functional_description: This signature reflects active ribosomal protein synthesis and chromatin remodeling in early GMP progenitors, with enrichment for nucleosomal DNA-binding proteins that maintain open chromatin architecture. The predominance of Early GMP (41%) and GMP-Mono (19%) cells suggests this programme marks the transcriptionally active, proliferative phase of myeloid progenitor commitment prior to terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: HMGN2: nucleosomal DNA binding in transcriptionally active chromatin; hallmark of proliferative progenitor state
HMGB1: high-mobility-group protein regulating transcription and DNA organization; supports open chromatin in active GMP
RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A: ribosomal protein components indicating elevated protein synthesis capacity during expansion phase
PTMA: transcription factor binding and apoptosis regulation; supports survival of cycling progenitors
ANP32B: histone and RNA polymerase binding; facilitates transcriptional remodeling during lineage priming
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing; supports alternative splicing during myeloid differentiation
TXN: redox homeostasis enzyme; protects cycling cells from oxidative stress during proliferation
UBB: ubiquitin for protein degradation; required for cell cycle checkpoint regulation in GMP
suggested_validation: Validate by co-staining Early GMP/GMP-Mono fractions (CD34+KIT+CD33+) for HMGN1/HMGN2 and PCNA to confirm active chromatin in proliferating progenitors. Cross-reference ribosomal protein expression with polysome profiling or P-ribosomes in sorted GMP subsets. Compare chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) in Early GMP versus Early ProMono to confirm open chromatin signature precedes lineage commitment.

programme_name: Early GMP mitochondrial bioenergetics and translation
functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage GMP progenitors (45% Early GMP, 30% GMP-Mono) with elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity and active protein synthesis machinery. The dominance of mtDNA-encoded respiratory chain components (MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-CO3, MT-ND5) coupled with ribosomal proteins indicates metabolic priming for rapid differentiation and proliferation characteristic of GMP-Cycle cells (19.5%), before commitment-associated metabolic shifts occur.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-CO3, MT-ND5: mitochondrial Complex I/IV components indicating active OXPHOS in metabolically active progenitors
RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23: ribosomal proteins supporting elevated protein synthesis during GMP expansion
MPO: myeloid marker present in early GMP and GMP-Mono before downregulation in committed ProMono
STMN1: microtubule dynamics regulator supporting cell cycle progression in GMP-Cycle subset
HSPB1, PPIA: molecular chaperones managing proteostasis under metabolic stress of differentiation
HMGN1, PTMA: nuclear organization factors supporting active chromatin in progenitor cells with elevated transcription
Cell composition: 94.5% GMP-stage cells; only 3% mature CD14 Mono indicates progenitor rather than terminally differentiated signature
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD34+KIT+ cells for MT-CO2/MT-ND1 (MitoTracker), combined with Ki-67 to correlate OXPHOS/translation signature with cycling vs. quiescent Early GMP subsets. RNA-seq comparison of Early GMP vs. GMP-Mono vs. ProMono to confirm MPO and mitochondrial gene downregulation at commitment boundary.

programme_name: Monocyte stress response and cytoskeletal remodeling
functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 monocytes under metabolic and inflammatory stress, characterized by hemoglobin gene expression (HBA2, HBB, HBA1, HBD) indicating iron-laden phagocytic activity or erythrophagocytosis, coupled with cytoskeletal remodeling (TMSB4X, S100A4, PHACTR1) and lysosomal proteolysis (CTSS). The co-expression of immediate early response genes (FOSB, ZFP36) and TYROBP (DAP12)-mediated signaling suggests activation through pattern recognition receptors, while elevated mitochondrial respiration (MT-ND1, ATP5J2) supports the metabolic demands of activated monocytes.
key_evidence: HBA2, HBA1, HBB, HBD: hemoglobin expression in CD14 monocytes indicates iron metabolism and erythrophagocytosis capacity, consistent with tissue-resident inflammatory monocytes
CTSS: cathepsin S drives antigen presentation and lysosomal degradation, hallmark of activated professional APCs
TYROBP: DAP12 adaptor protein couples innate receptor signaling (TLR, FcγR) to intracellular activation cascades in myeloid cells
FOSB, ZFP36: immediate early genes marking recent inflammatory stimulation and NF-κB/MAPK pathway activation
TMSB4X, S100A4, PHACTR1: actin-binding proteins governing cytoskeletal dynamics required for phagocytosis and migration
MT-ND1, ATP5J2: mitochondrial OXPHOS genes supporting high metabolic demands of activated monocytes
87.5% CD14 Mono composition: strong enrichment in classical monocytes with inflammatory phenotype
suggested_validation: Validate with flow cytometry co-staining of HBA2/HBB protein (or hemoglobin measurement) with CD14/CD16/CCR2; correlate with TLR and FcγR stimulation assays; confirm TYROBP-mediated signaling via phospho-flow (pERK/pAkt) following CD64 or TLR4 engagement; assess functional capacity for RBC phagocytosis and oxidative burst (DHE staining with NADPH oxidase inhibitors).

functional_description: This signature represents classical CD14+ monocytes in an activated inflammatory state, characterized by calcium-binding S100 proteins (S100A8/A9/A12 calprotectin complex) that function as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and antimicrobial effectors. The gene set reflects enhanced innate immune sensing capacity, cytoskeletal remodeling for migration/phagocytosis, and proteolytic activity consistent with pro-inflammatory monocyte differentiation and inflammatory tissue infiltration.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin subunit; DAMP and neutrophil chemoattractant; hallmark of activated classical monocytes
S100A8: Calprotectin heterodimer partner; antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory signaling via TLR4
S100A12: Calprotectin-related protein; elevated in inflammatory monocytes; RAGE ligand
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (M-ficolin); PAMP recognition receptor on monocytes; complement pathway activation
CD14: LPS/TLR4 co-receptor; defining classical monocyte marker; bacterial lipopolysaccharide sensing
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen; marker of monocyte/granulocyte differentiation and activation
CAPG: Actin-capping protein; cytoskeletal dynamics for migration and phagocytic cup formation
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor; protease balance in inflammatory microenvironment
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; extracellular matrix remodeling during inflammatory response
PLBD1: Phospholipase B; lipid mediator generation supporting inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14+CD16- monocytes with S100A9, FCN1, MNDA intracellular markers; quantify calprotectin (S100A8/A9) secretion in LPS-stimulated CD14+ monocytes; RNA-seq comparison with resting vs. TLR4-activated monocytes; assess inflammatory chemokine production (CCL2, CXCL8) in this population.

functional_description: This signature reflects mature monocyte antimicrobial effector functions dominated by S100 alarmin proteins (S100A8/A9/A12 calprotectin complex, S100A4/A6) and lysosomal hydrolases (LYZ, CSTA) characteristic of CD14 monocytes and late-stage Early ProMono. The enrichment of calcium-binding S100 proteins and cysteine protease inhibitors indicates activation of inflammatory and pathogen-response programmes rather than commitment-stage transcriptional regulation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin component, dominates mature monocyte inflammatory signature (antimicrobial, alarmin function)
S100A8: S100A8/A9 heterodimer (calprotectin), hallmark of mature CD14 monocytes not early commitment
LYZ: Lysozyme production confirmed for mono lineage, but peaks in CD14 Mono post-commitment
S100A12: Extended calprotectin family member, amplifies inflammatory response in mature stage
FCN1: Ficolin family collectin, monocyte pattern recognition receptor upregulated post-commitment
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor supporting intracellular antimicrobial activity in mature monocytes
CAPG: Actin-regulatory protein for monocyte migration and immune synapse formation
suggested_validation: This signature captures mature monocyte function (49.5% CD14 Mono) rather than ProMono commitment. To validate ProMono-specific commitment, re-stratify by Early ProMono only (44.5%), compare against GMP (MPO/ELANE expression), and assay KLF4, IRF8, CSF1R, MS4A3, CCR2 expression to confirm differentiation trajectory rather than terminal effector programme.

functional_description: This signature reflects a mature myeloid programme characterized by robust MHC class II antigen presentation machinery combined with markers of macrophage activation and endosomal-lysosomal function. The co-enrichment of HLA-DR/DP/DQ loci with AIF1 and TYROBP indicates activated antigen-presenting cells engaged in immune surveillance, supported by iron storage (FTH1) and cysteine protease inhibition (CST3) typical of tissue-resident or inflammatory monocytes/macrophages.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRA, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DQA1: Coordinate MHC class II expression for antigen presentation to T cells
CD74: Chaperone for MHC class II trafficking and peptide loading
AIF1: Calcium-binding protein induced by cytokines; promotes macrophage activation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor linking Fc and TLR signalling to downstream activation
FCER1G: Gamma chain of FcγR, coupling antibody-mediated phagocytosis to inflammation
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor; marker of activated myeloid cells in inflammatory states
PSAP: Lysosomal saposin precursor; supports cathepsin function in degradative capacity
FTH1: Iron storage; upregulated in metabolically active, phagocytically engaged monocytes
LST1: LPS-responsive membrane protein enhancing bacterial sensing
S100A11: Calcium signalling; associated with myeloid cell activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm HLA-DR+CD14+ subset; assess co-expression of AIF1, TYROBP, FCER1G. Functional assay: antigen presentation capacity (mixed lymphocyte reaction) and phagocytic index with opsonized bacteria/IgG-coated beads. RNA-seq of sorted HLA-DR-high vs HLA-DR-low CD14+ monocytes to validate TYROBP-FCER1G effector signature.

programme_name: Monocyte Antimicrobial Defense and Oxidative Stress
functional_description: This signature represents activated CD14 classical monocytes with enhanced antimicrobial and antioxidative capacity. The program is characterized by robust bacterial peptidoglycan degradation (LYZ), reactive oxygen species (ROS) detoxification (GPX1), and immunoregulatory galectins (LGALS1/LGALS3), indicating cells primed for phagocytic defense with metabolic homeostasis. CEBPD reinforces myeloid differentiation and inflammatory competence typical of mature CD14+ monocytes.
key_evidence: LYZ: direct antimicrobial activity via bacterial cell wall degradation; hallmark of activated monocyte microbicidal function
GPX1: glutathione peroxidase critical for H2O2 neutralization and ROS homeostasis during respiratory burst
CEBPD: C/EBP family transcription factor driving myeloid differentiation and pro-inflammatory gene expression programs
LGALS1/LGALS3: galectins mediating autocrine/paracrine immunoregulation and cell-cell interactions in inflammatory context
GAPDH: metabolic enzyme with moonlighting functions in glycolysis and cellular stress responses
ZFP36: mRNA stability control via AU-rich element binding; rapid post-transcriptional regulation of cytokine mRNAs
HLA-DRA: antigen presentation capacity consistent with mature, activated CD14 monocytes
ID1: HLH inhibitor modulating proliferation/differentiation balance in differentiating monocytic lineage
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14+CD16- monocytes co-expressing LYZ, CD64 (FCGR1A), and assay intracellular ROS (DHE/DCFDA) alongside GPX1 protein levels. qPCR validation of LYZ, GPX1, CEBPD, and LGALS1/3 in sorted CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono. Functional assays: measure bacterial killing capacity and antioxidant enzyme activity in signature-defined populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects post-transcriptional maturation and cytoplasmic protein synthesis capacity in committed monocytic cells, dominated by ribosomal proteins, actin cytoskeleton regulators, and translation-associated factors. The enrichment in GMP-Mono (40%) and mature monocytes (41%) with minimal early progenitor content indicates activation during the late GMP-to-ProMono transition when lineage commitment is established and cells shift toward protein-synthetic machinery engagement.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein essential for cytoskeletal reorganisation during monocytic differentiation and cell motility
CD74: MHC class II-associated chaperone marking antigen-presenting capacity acquisition in committed monocytic lineage
RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17: Ribosomal structural proteins indicating elevated protein synthesis demand in maturing monocytes
ACTG1: Cytoplasmic actin isoform supporting cell morphological changes and migratory capacity post-commitment
SLC25A5: Mitochondrial ATP/ADP translocase supporting energetic demands of active protein synthesis
LGALS1: Galectin-1 involved in cell-cell interactions and negative growth regulation, consistent with post-proliferative monocytic maturation
YBX1: Cold shock domain protein implicated in translational regulation and mRNA stability
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor supporting survival during differentiation transition
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD74+CD14+ or CD16+ monocytes with CD34-/KIT-/MPO-low to confirm post-GMP commitment stage; single-cell proteomics to validate elevated ribosomal protein expression; polysome profiling to assess active translation capacity in sorted GMP-Mono vs mature monocyte populations

functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced translational capacity and ribosomal biogenesis in early monocytic progenitors, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS/RPL genes) and translation factors. The co-expression of NPM1 (nucleolar chaperone for ribosome assembly) and PTMA (proliferation-associated) indicates active protein synthesis supporting rapid cell division and differentiation. The presence of MPO at the tail suggests early myeloid lineage priming concurrent with high translational demand.
key_evidence: RPS24/RPS23/RPS2/RPS17: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components—core translational machinery
RPL37A/RPL7A/RPL4: 60S large subunit ribosomal proteins—scaffold for mRNA decoding
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor—active protein synthesis during GMP transition
NPM1: nucleolar protein and ribosome assembly chaperone—drives ribosomal biogenesis
PTMA: anti-apoptotic and proliferation factor—supports early GMP (53.5%) and GMP-Mono (44.0%) expansion
GAPDH/HNRNPA1: metabolic and RNA processing—coupled anabolic state
HMGN1: active chromatin remodeling—transcriptionally permissive early progenitor state
MPO: lineage priming marker—confirms myeloid GMP identity
suggested_validation: Validate with polysome profiling or ribosomal occupancy (Ribo-seq) on sorted Early GMP/GMP-Mono cells; cross-reference against cell-cycle stratified RNA-seq to confirm signature enrichment in non-cycling early GMPs (not GMP-Cycle); quantify protein synthesis rates via puromycin incorporation or O-propargyl-puromycin labeling.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery activity enriched in Early GMP and GMP-Mono stages. The dominance of RPS and RPL genes indicates heightened protein synthesis capacity typical of metabolically active progenitors preparing for differentiation, with PTMA contributing to transcription factor binding and apoptosis regulation during lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL4, RPLP0: structural ribosomal proteins defining 40S/60S subunits; coordinate elevation indicates active translation machinery in proliferating/differentiating GMP
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor (guanine nucleotide exchange), direct effector of ribosomal protein synthesis
PTMA: transcription factor cofactor and apoptosis inhibitor; progenitor protection during early commitment
PPIA: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding post-translation
HNRNPA1: pre-mRNA processing/splicing; transcript maturation support in transcriptionally active progenitors
ACTG1, UQCRH: cytoskeletal and mitochondrial support for protein synthesis and cellular energetics
Cell composition 49.5% Early GMP + 26.5% GMP-Mono (76% GMP stages): signature enriched in undifferentiated bipotent progenitors before monocyte/neutrophil lineage priming
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein (RPS24, RPL4) and translation factor (EEF1B2) expression by qPCR across sorted Early GMP, GMP-Mono, GMP-Cycle vs ProMono/mature monocytes; perform ribosome profiling or SUnSET assay to confirm elevated translation rates in GMP compared to lineage-committed stages; correlate with MYB/CEBPA expression to confirm progenitor identity.

programme_name: CD16 Mono cytoskeletal patrolling and ADCC
functional_description: This signature defines non-classical monocytes (CD16+) enriched for actin-cytoskeletal remodeling, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity via FcγRIII, and metabolic fitness through oxidative phosphorylation. The gene programme supports the patrolling phenotype characterized by active cellular crawling, vascular surveillance, and Fc-mediated immune responses.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: canonical CD16 surface receptor defining non-classical monocytes; central to ADCC and immune complex clearance
TMSB4X: actin-sequestering protein essential for cytoskeletal dynamics and monocyte crawling/migration on endothelium
COTL1: actin-binding protein regulating cytoskeletal remodeling required for patrolling behaviour and transendothelial surveillance
S100A4: calcium-binding protein involved in cell motility and migration, supporting active vascular patrolling
LST1: lymphocyte-inhibitory membrane protein with enhanced expression by IFN-γ and bacteria, consistent with CD16 mono antimicrobial priming
LTB: TNF-family cytokine involved in lymphotoxin signaling and immunological surveillance
MT-CO2, MT-ND1: oxidative phosphorylation components supporting high metabolic demand of motile, patrol-active monocytes
SOD1: antioxidant enzyme protecting against ROS generated during active immune surveillance and ADCC
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: CD16+CD14lo/- co-staining with FCGR3A-high, CX3CR1-high, and ITGAL/ITGB2 (LFA-1) surface markers. Assess TMSB4X and COTL1 protein levels via immunofluorescence or Western blot in sorted CD16 mono. Functional assays: measure crawling velocity on endothelial monolayers and ADCC capacity using IgG-opsonized targets.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Iron Metabolism and Cytoskeletal Remodeling
functional_description: This signature represents CD16 non-classical monocytes with elevated iron homeostasis, actin cytoskeleton dynamics, and lysosomal protease activity. The enrichment reflects metabolic adaptation to patrolling function, enabling rapid migration and vascular surveillance through coordinated regulation of iron storage and cellular remodeling.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage protein enriched in metabolically active CD16 monocytes supporting sustained patrolling and ROS management
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration regulating cytoskeletal polymerization critical for endothelial crawling and vascular patrolling
COTL1: Actin-binding protein linking cytoskeleton dynamics to 5-lipoxygenase signaling in leukocyte migration
LST1: Lymphocyte proliferation inhibitor upregulated by IFN-γ and bacterial PAMPs in activated monocytes
FCER1G: ITAM-bearing Fc receptor gamma chain supporting antibody-dependent cellular responses (ADCC pathway)
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor enabling Fc and lectin receptor signaling in myeloid surveillance
AIF1: Calcium-binding protein promoting macrophage activation and vascular smooth muscle interaction
CTSS: Cathepsin S for antigen processing and endosomal-lysosomal degradation in patrolling monocytes
S100A4: Calcium-binding protein regulating cell migration and endothelial transmigration
PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lysosomal homeostasis in protease-rich non-classical monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate iron-metabolism signature with Prussian blue staining and ferritin protein quantification. Confirm actin dynamics via live-cell imaging of CD16 Mono crawling on endothelium. Cross-reference with bulk RNA-seq of FACS-sorted CD16+ (FCGR3A+CX3CR1hi) versus CD14+ monocytes. Assess functional link between FTH1/iron storage and oxidative stress resistance in patrolling contexts.

functional_description: This signature represents a metabolic and structural remodelling programme enriched in CD16 monocytes (49% of activating cells), characterized by enhanced glycolytic capacity, mitochondrial ATP synthesis, and actin dynamics. The gene set supports rapid cellular motility and vascular surveillance through coordinated cytoskeletal reorganization and bioenergetic optimization, rather than canonical patrolling transcription factor or antiviral programmes.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: actin sequestering protein essential for monocyte motility and cytoskeletal dynamics in patrolling surveillance
AIF1: calcium-binding actin regulator induced by interferons; promotes myeloid activation and vascular smooth muscle interactions
ACTG1: cytoplasmic actin isoform fundamental to monocyte crawling and transendothelial migration mechanics
SLC25A5: mitochondrial ADP/ATP transporter supporting sustained energy metabolism during patrolling behaviour
TPI1: glycolytic enzyme enabling efficient glucose catabolism for energy-demanding surveillance activities
CFD: complement pathway serine protease (adipsin) linking metabolic status to complement activation in CD16 mono
SOD1: antioxidant defence against oxidative stress during active patrolling and vascular sampling
CALM2: calcium signalling orchestrator regulating cytoskeletal rearrangement and integrin-mediated adhesion dynamics
SPN: CD45RA-enriched surface glycoprotein involved in T-cell-monocyte cross-talk during immune surveillance
MGST3: eicosanoid metabolism enzyme supporting lipid mediator production in activated CD16 monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate through live-cell imaging of CD16 monocyte crawling velocity and mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1) stratified by TMSB4X/AIF1 expression; confirm actin polymerization dynamics via LatA inhibition assays; assess glycolytic dependency using seahorse extracellular acidification rates in sorted CD16 vs CD14 monocytes.

functional_description: This signature represents a monocyte differentiation or activation state characterized by robust MHC class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP) and CD74 expression, supporting professional antigen-presenting function. The programme is enriched in CD14 monocytes (59%) with substantial CD16 monocyte contribution (30.5%), indicating a shared antigen presentation capacity across classical and intermediate monocyte subsets. Concurrent expression of cytoskeletal regulators (TMSB4X, AIF1, COTL1) and post-transcriptional control genes (ZFP36) suggests active cellular remodelling accompanying heightened MHC-II display.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC class II chaperone and invariant chain, essential for HLA-II peptide loading and surface presentation
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRB5: HLA-DR heterodimer components, primary MHC-II molecules on monocytes
HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer; restricted expression pattern making co-elevation with DR/DQ significant
HLA-DQA1: HLA-DQ alpha chain; less commonly co-elevated with other class II, suggests coordinated antigen presentation
CST3: Cystatin C; protease inhibitor supporting phagolysosomal homeostasis during antigen processing
AIF1: Allograft inflammatory factor-1; promotes macrophage activation and cell motility in inflammatory contexts
TMSB4X, COTL1: Actin-binding proteins supporting cytoskeletal dynamics for intracellular antigen trafficking
ZFP36: Immediate early response gene for post-transcriptional mRNA stability control
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: co-stain CD14, CD16, HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ to confirm MHC-II co-expression pattern. Functional assay: measure antigen-presentation capacity (OT-II T cell proliferation) in sorted CD14+ HLA-DRhigh vs HLA-DRlow monocytes. RNA-FISH: visualize CD74 and HLA-DRB1 co-localization in CD14 monocytes to assess MHC-II assembly stoichiometry.

programme_name: CD14 Mono Innate Inflammatory Calcium Signaling
functional_description: This signature defines classical inflammatory monocytes characterized by elevated S100A calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A6/A4), which function as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and promote neutrophil recruitment and innate immune activation. The constellation of S100 proteins, coupled with phagocytic proteases (CSTA), metabolic enzymes (PKM), and extracellular matrix modulators (VCAN, FCN1), indicates a pro-inflammatory phenotype poised for rapid antimicrobial response and tissue inflammation.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9/A12: DAMP molecules defining inflammatory CD14 monocytes; calcium-responsive alarmin secretion
S100A6/A4: Additional calcium-binding proteins amplifying innate immune signaling
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan remodeling extracellular matrix during inflammation
CSTA: Cystatin inhibition of cysteine proteases, regulating protease activity
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition molecule for complement activation and bacterial sensing
PKM: Glycolytic enzyme supporting rapid ATP generation for inflammatory functions
CAPG: Actin-regulatory gelsolin family member enabling cellular migration and phagocytosis
FCN1: Lectin pathway activation independent of classical PAMP sensing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: S100A8/A9 co-expression on CD14+CD16- monocytes; intracellular staining post-LPS stimulation. Functional assays: assess S100A8/A9-mediated neutrophil chemotaxis and TLR activation capacity. Compare S100A8/A9 production kinetics in classical vs. non-classical monocyte subsets.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation capacity in Early GMP-stage progenitors, consistent with high biosynthetic demand during active proliferation and differentiation priming. The enrichment of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0) alongside translation factors (EEF1B2) and nucleolar/mitochondrial support factors (NPM1, UQCRH) indicates metabolically active progenitors preparing for myeloid commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPS17, RPL4, RPLP0: Ribosomal 40S/60S subunits—robust protein synthesis capacity essential for GMP proliferation and lineage priming
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor enabling aminoacylated tRNA delivery; reflects active translational output
NPM1: Nucleolar chaperone and centrosome regulator; marks proliferative progenitors undergoing cell division
HNRNPA1, PTMA: RNA-binding and DNA-binding cofactors; facilitate transcriptional/translational coordination during differentiation
UQCRH, HSP90AB1, GAPDH: Oxidative phosphorylation and metabolic support; consistent with energetic demands of GMP-Cycle and Early GMP
Cell composition (Early GMP 69.5%, GMP-Cycle 24.5%): Signature predominantly captures proliferative Early/Cycling GMP stages
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry sorting Early GMP (CD34+KIT+CD45RA+) vs GMP-Mono (CD34–CD45RA–CSF1R+) and quantifying RPS/RPL mRNA and protein synthesis rates (e.g., puromycin incorporation, polysome profiling). Cross-reference with ribosomal biogenesis programmes (rrn45s, TOP1) and confirm inverse relationship with maturation markers (MPO, ELANE upregulation in committed stages).

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and mitochondrial biogenesis
functional_description: This signature captures Early ProMono progenitors in active cell cycle with elevated oxidative metabolism. The dominant cell-type composition (65% Early ProMono) combined with proliferation markers (TOP2A, PCLAF, STMN1) and mitochondrial respiratory chain genes reflects metabolic reprogramming during monocyte commitment. LYZ expression confirms monocytic lineage specification.
key_evidence: HMGB2: Chromatin-associated protein marking transcriptionally active, proliferating Early ProMono
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complex components indicating elevated metabolic demand in committed progenitors
TOP2A: DNA topoisomerase essential for DNA replication and chromosome condensation in cycling Early ProMono
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator supporting active cell cycle progression
PCLAF: S-phase licensing and centrosome cycling factor, marks proliferative Early ProMono
LYZ: Monocytic lineage commitment marker, distinguishes ProMono from GMP
HMGB1, HMGN2: Nucleosome-associated proteins in transcriptionally active chromatin of differentiating progenitors
RNASE2: Early monocytic antimicrobial programme activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: proliferation markers (Ki-67, PCNA) with ProMono surface markers (CSF1R, MS4A3, CD33); verify absence of MPO/ELANE expression to exclude GMP-Neut; confirm mitochondrial mass elevation via MitoTracker staining in Early ProMono vs Late ProMono populations

functional_description: This signature reflects active chromatin remodeling and translational machinery in committed monocytes, characterized by nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1) that maintain transcriptionally permissive chromatin states, combined with ribosomal proteins and translation factors supporting rapid protein synthesis during monocyte differentiation. The co-expression of CD74 (MHC-II chaperone) and metabolic enzymes (TPI1, GSTP1) indicates functional maturation toward antigen-presenting monocyte phenotypes.
key_evidence: HMGN1/HMGN2: Nucleosome-binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin; hallmark of differentiated monocytes with open chromatin
HMGB1: High-mobility group box protein critical for transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization in mature myeloid cells
RPS24/RPS23: Ribosomal proteins indicating elevated translational capacity during monocyte commitment
YBX1: Cold shock domain RNA/DNA-binding protein functioning in mRNA stability and translation regulation
CD74: MHC-II-associated invariant chain; definitive marker of monocyte lineage commitment and antigen presentation function
PTMA: DNA-binding cofactor and apoptosis regulator supporting transcriptional activity in differentiating cells
GSTP1: Glutathione S-transferase reflecting oxidative stress management in metabolically active monocytes
TPI1: Glycolytic enzyme supporting energy demand of differentiating monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate by co-staining CD74 and HMGN2 protein expression in sorted CD14+ monocytes vs GMPs; confirm chromatin accessibility via ATAC-seq in committed monocytes; measure translation rate using ribosome profiling in CD74+ vs CD74- progenitor populations

functional_description: This signature reflects activated classical monocytes with enhanced antimicrobial effector functions and acute inflammatory responsiveness. The dominance of S100A8/A9 calprotectin, combined with lysozyme, ficolin-1, and myeloid differentiation markers, indicates priming for PAMP recognition and bacterial killing. The signature captures early-to-intermediate inflammatory monocyte differentiation with robust innate pattern recognition capacity.
key_evidence: S100A8: Calprotectin component; neutrophil-attracting alarmin and ROS-amplifying DAMP central to CD14 Mono inflammatory activation
S100A9: Calprotectin heterodimer partner; synergizes with S100A8 in RAGE-mediated TLR4 signaling amplification
CD14: LPS/LBP co-receptor essential for TLR4 signaling; highest discriminator of classical monocytes versus CD16 subsets
LYZ: Lysozyme; bactericidal enzyme reflecting antimicrobial effector function in CD14 Mono
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (M-ficolin); soluble pattern recognition receptor for bacterial glycans and apoptotic cells
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen; marker of granulocyte-monocyte lineage differentiation and maturation
S100A6 & S100A12: S100 family members amplifying inflammatory signaling and leukocyte recruitment
VCAN: Versican; ECM remodeling component supporting monocyte extravasation and tissue infiltration
CSTA: Cystatin-A; cysteine protease inhibitor involved in immune regulation and antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14+ cells for S100A8/A9 expression levels; validate calprotectin secretion by ELISA or multiplex cytokine array; assess TLR4 signaling dependency via NF-κB phosphorylation in LPS-stimulated CD14+ monocytes sorted from top-activating cells.

functional_description: This signature defines the antimicrobial and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) programme of CD16 non-classical monocytes. The module integrates Fc-gamma receptor signalling (FCGR3A, FCER1G), interferon-induced antiviral immunity (IFITM3), lysosomal proteolysis for antigen processing (CTSS, PSAP), and pro-migratory actin-binding proteins supporting vascular patrolling and endothelial surveillance.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: CD16 surface marker enabling ADCC and immune complex clearance in non-classical monocytes
FCER1G: Gamma-chain subunit of high-affinity Fc receptors, essential for ADCC amplification
IFITM3: Type I interferon-induced antiviral protein, hallmark of activated non-classical monocyte antiviral state
CTSS: Cathepsin S mediates antigen processing and presentation, critical for anti-pathogen responses
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein induced by IFN-γ and cytokines, supports monocyte activation and migration
S100A4, S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins promoting cytoskeletal dynamics and vascular crawling behaviour
LST1: Lymphocyte inhibition marker and IFN-γ/LPS-responsive gene, consistent with activated surveillance phenotype
PSAP, CFD: Lysosomal degradative enzymes and complement factor D supporting antimicrobial killing
RHOC: RhoC GTPase mediates actin dynamics essential for patrolling locomotion and endothelial interaction
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry (CD16+/CD14-/FCGR3A+/IFITM3+/CX3CR1+) combined with functional ADCC assay using IgG-opsonised targets and RNA-seq of sorted CD16 vs CD14 monocytes to confirm antiviral and proteolytic gene enrichment

functional_description: This signature captures activated classical monocytes with heightened immediate early transcriptional responses and pro-inflammatory effector functions. The programme integrates AP-1/FOSB-driven transcriptional reprogramming with enhanced phagocytic capacity (CTSS, PLAUR), innate inflammatory signalling (CXCL8), and metabolic activation (mitochondrial NADH oxidase), characteristic of acute PAMP-stimulated CD14+ monocytes.
key_evidence: FOSB: AP-1 family member; master TF for rapid monocyte activation and inflammatory gene expression
CXCL8: Prototypical pro-inflammatory chemokine directly regulated by NF-κB/AP-1; hallmark of CD14 Mono activation
KLF4: Master regulator of monocyte differentiation and pro-inflammatory transcriptional programmes
S100A9: Damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP); calprotectin component marking activated innate immune monocytes
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and monocyte antimicrobial function
PLAUR: Urokinase plasminogen activator receptor; enables monocyte migration and tissue infiltration
ZFP36: mRNA stability regulator of AU-rich cytokine transcripts (TNF, IL6); post-transcriptional control of inflammation
MT-ND1: Mitochondrial Complex I; energetic demand during ROS generation and pro-inflammatory metabolism
VCAN: Versican ECM proteoglycan; remodelling during inflammatory extravasation and tissue recruitment
IER3: Immediate early response gene; rapid inducible marker of monocyte activation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: validate CD14+HLA-DR+CXCL8+ and CD14+S100A9+ populations; bulk RNA-seq on FACS-sorted CD14 Mono ± LPS/TNF stimulation; in situ hybridisation for FOSB, CXCL8, S100A9 in inflamed bone marrow tissues; assess inflammatory migration capacity via CCR2-axis (CCL2 chemotaxis assays).

programme_name: Myeloid granule maturation and antibacterial effector
functional_description: This signature represents a CD14 monocyte differentiation programme characterized by abundant primary and secondary granule proteins (S100A8/A9, LYZ, CSTA) coupled with oxidative phosphorylation and redox buffering capacity. The programme reflects mature inflammatory monocyte effector function preparing for bacterial killing and antimicrobial responses.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: canonical primary granule proteins marking activated inflammatory monocytes; strong calprotectin complex for antimicrobial defense and DAMP signalling
LYZ: lysozyme encoding gene, primary granule bactericidal enzyme cleaving peptidoglycan; hallmark of myeloid maturation
CSTA: cystatin superfamily cysteine protease inhibitor; protects against granule-derived proteases during granule maturation
GPX1: glutathione peroxidase for ROS detoxification; essential for NADPH oxidase-dependent antimicrobial function without self-damage
BLVRB: biliverdin reductase from heme metabolism; byproduct of hemoglobin catabolism in phagocytic monocytes
GRN: granulin precursor, antimicrobial and immune regulatory granule protein; elevated in inflammatory monocyte activation
MT-CO2/MT-CO3/MT-ND1: mitochondrial respiratory complexes supporting ATP-intensive phagocytosis and ROS generation
PKM/GAPDH: glycolytic flux supporting Warburg effect in activated monocytes; rapid ATP generation for effector functions
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with S100A8/A9 (myeloid granule marker) and LYZ co-staining on CD14++CD16- monocytes; correlate with CD64 (FCGR1A) expression; confirm by measuring ROS production capacity (DHE/DCFDA assay) and bacterial killing assays in sorted CD14 Mono from this cluster.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte specialization in intracellular antimicrobial processing and antigen presentation, characterized by elevated lysosomal cathepsins (CTSS), cysteine protease inhibitors (CST3, CSTA), and the phagocytic receptor-associated signaling adapter TYROBP/DAP12. The program enables degradation of pathogen-derived peptides for MHC-II presentation and supports robust phagolysosomal maturation.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-bearing signaling adapter essential for Fc receptor (FCGR1A/CD64) and TLR co-signaling in monocytes; links pathogen recognition to cytoskeletal responses
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine cathepsin critical for antigen processing and degradation of pathogen proteins within phagolysosomes
CST3, CSTA: Cystatin-family cysteine protease inhibitors regulating cathepsin activity and preventing autolytic damage during antimicrobial responses
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (M-ficolin); pattern recognition receptor for bacterial carbohydrates; activates complement and enhances phagocytic clearance
LYZ: Lysozyme; bactericidal enzyme targeting peptidoglycan; abundant in monocyte granules for direct antimicrobial activity
FCER1G: FcγR common γ-chain; component of high-affinity IgG receptors (FcγRI/CD64) driving antibody-mediated phagocytosis and ADCP
GRN: Granulins; secreted peptides with antimicrobial and immunomodulatory properties; accumulate in monocyte granules
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein supporting cytoskeletal dynamics required for phagosome formation and cell migration
S100A6, S100A11: EF-hand calcium sensors regulating actin polymerization and phagolysosomal dynamics
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-express TYROBP/DAP12, CTSS, and FCGR1A (CD64) in CD14+CCR2+ monocytes. Functional assay: measure phagocytic capacity (opsonized bacteria/IgG-coated beads) and cathepsin activity in FACS-sorted TYROBP-high vs TYROBP-low CD14 monocytes. Confirm enrichment in classical inflammatory monocytes vs patrolling CD16+ monocytes.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Fc Receptor Lysosomal Program
functional_description: This signature defines the core transcriptional program of CD16+ non-classical monocytes, centered on Fc receptor-mediated innate immunity and lysosomal-mediated antigen processing. The signature is characterized by high expression of FCGR3A (CD16), iron homeostasis machinery (FTH1), and proteolytic enzymes (CTSS, CTSL) essential for ADCC and immune surveillance, coupled with actin-remodeling proteins supporting patrolling behavior.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Definitive CD16 monocyte surface marker; Fc-gamma receptor IIIa mediates ADCC and antibody-dependent cellular responses
FTH1: Iron storage protein highly expressed in CD16 monocytes; supports oxidative stress tolerance during vascular patrolling
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain; shared signaling component of FCGR3A and other Fc receptors driving activation
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin-modulating protein induced by IFN-gamma; promotes macrophage activation and vascular surveillance
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease; critical for antigen processing and MHC class II presentation in monocytes
CD68: Pan-monocyte/macrophage marker; lysosomal membrane protein reflecting high lysosomal content in CD16 monocytes
COTL1: Actin-binding protein interacting with 5-lipoxygenase; supports cytoskeletal dynamics for crawling behavior
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein; regulates actin polymerization essential for monocyte migration and patrolling
LST1: Lymphocyte proliferation inhibitor upregulated by LPS and IFN-gamma; marks activated CD16 monocytes
SAT1: Polyamine catabolic enzyme; supports differentiation and activation state of mature monocytes
MS4A7: MS4A family member with monocyte-restricted expression; potential functional role in CD16 monocyte identity
PSAP: Saposin precursor; lysosomal protein involved in lipid antigen presentation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry (CD14 vs CD16 vs CD14+CD16+) with FCGR3A, CX3CR1 high, CD14 low; RNA-FISH for FTH1/FCGR3A coexpression; functional assay of ADCC capacity in FCGR3A+ sorted cells; verify absence of CCR2/ITGAX (which would indicate intermediate monocytes).

functional_description: This signature marks the transition from GMP-Mono to early ProMono stages, characterized by active myeloid differentiation (MPO, AZU1, RNASE2, MS4A3), chromatin remodelling supporting lineage commitment (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2, H2AFZ), and stress/apoptosis resistance mechanisms (BIRC5, HSPB1, HSP90B1). The enrichment of nucleosome-associated proteins and chaperones indicates active transcriptional reprogramming during monocytic lineage commitment.
key_evidence: MPO: Myeloid peroxidase—canonical early myeloid marker present in GMP and ProMono; declining in mature monocytes
AZU1: Azurocidin—granule protein marking GMP-Mono and early ProMono stages
MS4A3: Membrane protein enriched in myeloid progenitors and early monocytic cells
RNASE2: Ribonuclease 2—antimicrobial granule constituent of myeloid cells
HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2, H2AFZ: Chromatin remodellers and nucleosome-associated proteins supporting transcriptional changes during lineage commitment
BIRC5: Survivin—anti-apoptotic factor facilitating proliferation during GMP-Mono/ProMono transition
HSPB1, HSP90B1: Heat shock proteins providing stress tolerance during differentiation
LGALS1: Galectin-1—cell-cell interaction modulator enriched in committed progenitors and monocytes
FABP5, PLAC8: Metabolic and transcriptional regulators supporting myeloid differentiation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of MPO+/AZU1+/MS4A3+ cells with CSF1R and CD64 to confirm GMP-Mono→early ProMono progression; RNA-FISH to spatially resolve HMGB1/HMGN2 chromatin activity in MPO+ subsets; assess BIRC5 expression correlation with proliferation markers (MKI67) in GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte activation characterized by immediate early transcription factor induction (FOSB, JUN, ZFP36), enhanced antigen presentation (HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, CD83), and metabolic reprogramming for sustained effector function. The program integrates ITAM signaling (TYROBP), lysosomal proteolysis (CTSS), iron homeostasis (FTH1), and polyamine metabolism (SAT1), consistent with activated inflammatory monocytes.
key_evidence: FOSB, JUN, ZFP36: Immediate early transcription factors driving AP-1-mediated inflammatory gene expression
KLF4: Master transcription factor regulating monocyte development and activation status
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor coupling Fc receptors and TLRs to downstream signaling
CD83: Surface activation marker indicative of APC maturation and antigen presentation competence
HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: Class II MHC expression essential for activated monocyte antigen presentation
CTSS: Cysteine cathepsin supporting lysosomal antigen processing and phagolysosome formation
FTH1: Iron storage reflecting metabolic adaptation in activated monocytes
COTL1: Actin regulator supporting migration and cytoskeletal reorganization
SAT1, NAMPT: Polyamine and NAD+ metabolism supporting proliferation and inflammatory signaling
CD14 Mono 71%: Dominant cell type confirms classical monocyte signature
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14++CCR2+ cells for CD83+, HLA-DR+, CD64+ to confirm maturation phenotype. qPCR validation of FOSB/JUN/KLF4 induction. Assess functional capacity via LPS stimulation (TNF, IL-6 production) and phagocytosis assays.

functional_description: This signature represents the core antimicrobial and lysosomal effector programme of CD14+ classical monocytes, characterized by high expression of pattern recognition receptors (FCN1, CD14), myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA), and a comprehensive arsenal of lysosomal proteases and antimicrobial factors. The programme is centred on intracellular degradation capacity, bacterial cell wall recognition, and oxidative stress management—hallmarks of professional phagocytes equipped for pathogen internalization and destruction.
key_evidence: CD14: surface PAMP receptor and LPS co-receptor; defines classical monocyte identity
FCN1: ficolin lectin; pattern recognition of bacterial pathogens; classical monocyte-specific
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor linking Fc and pattern recognition receptors to signalling
MNDA: myeloid differentiation antigen; lineage-restricted nuclear marker of monocytes/granulocytes
CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease; antigen processing and intracellular degradation
LYZ: lysozyme; direct bacteriolytic enzyme targeting peptidoglycan
CST3: cystatin; cysteine protease inhibitor regulating lysosomal protease activity
GRN: granulin precursor; secreted antimicrobial and immunomodulatory factor
GLRX: glutaredoxin; redox homeostasis and oxidative stress management
TMSB4X: actin regulation; essential for phagosome maturation and cell migration
AP1S2: Golgi adaptor; membrane trafficking supporting secretory capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14++FCN1+ LYZ+ CTSS+ cells; functional assays measuring phagocytic capacity, lysozyme activity, and ROS production; compare with CD16 Mono signature which should show low FCN1, LYZ, CTSS and high CX3CR1, FFAR2

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodeling and antimicrobial
functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor maturation dominated by chromatin accessibility factors (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2, H2AFZ) supporting active transcription of monocyte-lineage genes, coupled with induction of antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, RNASE2, S100A8/A9) characteristic of ProMono differentiation. The strong enrichment in Early ProMono (70.5%) with minimal GMP-Mono contamination (1.0%) indicates this is a committed progenitor programme distinct from bipotent GMP, yet lacking full CD14 Mono surface maturation.
key_evidence: HMGN2: nucleosomal DNA binding in transcriptionally active chromatin—hallmark of chromatin remodeling during ProMono commitment
LYZ: canonical monocyte lysozyme production, core marker of mono-lineage differentiation upstream of CD14 Mono
HMGB1/HMGB2: non-histone chromatin architectural proteins regulating transcription during differentiation and immune activation
S100A8/S100A9: calcium-binding proteins driving antimicrobial and inflammatory capacity in myeloid progenitors transitioning to monocyte fate
RNASE2: ribonuclease antimicrobial activity supporting early monocyte effector function maturation
LGALS1: galectin-mediated cell-cell interaction suppression consistent with ProMono transit state
Early ProMono dominance (70.5%): signature enrichment validates Early ProMono stage specificity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain Early ProMono (CD34+CD13+CD33+CSF1R+MS4A3high LYZ+) for HMGN2/HMGB1 nuclear expression and S100A8/A9 cytoplasmic intensity; compare LYZ-negative GMP-Mono (MPO+ELANE+) to exclude bipotent contamination; ATAC-seq on sorted Early ProMono to validate open chromatin at LYZ, CTSL, CTSS loci.

programme_name: CD14 monocyte metabolic maturation and antimicrobial effector
functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic and antimicrobial effector programs of mature CD14 classical monocytes, characterized by glycolytic flux (GAPDH), NAD+ biosynthesis for energy and immune signaling (NAMPT), and antimicrobial granule assembly (LYZ, CD63, PLEK). The enrichment of calcium-binding S100 proteins (S100A6, S100A12) and oxidative stress protection (GPX1) indicates active pathogen handling and ROS management during inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: GAPDH: glycolytic metabolism essential for inflammatory monocyte energy production
LYZ: primary antimicrobial enzyme in monocyte granules, bacterial peptidoglycan degradation
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis supports NAD+-dependent sirtuins and immune signaling during inflammation
S100A6, S100A12: calcium-binding DAMPs/PAMPs sensors, elevated in classical monocytes during infection
CD63: tetraspanin marker of secretory lysosomes and granule exocytosis in professional phagocytes
PLEK: phosphoinositide signaling adapter for phagocytosis and immune synapse formation
GPX1: antioxidant defense against monocyte-derived ROS during antimicrobial oxidative burst
CEBPD: CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein delta, co-factor in monocyte differentiation and inflammatory response
ZFP36L1: mRNA stability regulator of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL6, IL8)
MAFB: transcriptional repressor cooperating with C/EBPs in monocyte maturation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry/sorting of CD14+ CD16- monocytes followed by qPCR validation of LYZ, S100A12, and NAMPT; functional assays measuring bacterial phagocytosis rates, ROS production (DHE/CellROX), and LPS-induced TNF secretion in this population

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic reprogramming toward oxidative phosphorylation and anomalous haemoglobin expression in early ProMono cells. The dominance of globin genes (HBA1/2, HBB, HBD, HBM) alongside mitochondrial respiratory chain components (MT-CO2, ATP5 family) suggests either erythroid contamination in the ProMono gate or metabolic licensing of monocyte precursors via haem-driven oxidative capacity. The presence of LYZ confirms monocytic commitment, but globin expression is atypical for committed monocyte progenitors.
key_evidence: HBA2: Alpha-globin chain; unexpected in ProMono, suggests erythroid lineage contribution or contamination
HBB: Beta-globin; core haemoglobin component, not a ProMono lineage marker
LYZ: Lysozyme; bona fide monocyte marker and lysosomal hydrolase supporting mono fate
MT-CO2: Mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase; indicates energetic shift to oxidative metabolism
ATP5J2/ATP5G3/ATP5F1/ATP5B: ATP synthase subunits; support elevated mitochondrial OXPHOS in activated ProMono
TMSB4X: Actin-regulating protein; supports cell migration and differentiation phenotype
AHSP: Alpha-globin chaperone; redundant unless genuine haemoglobin biosynthesis occurs
suggested_validation: Validate ProMono cell identity via flow cytometry (CS1R+, MS4A3+, CD14−/low). Quantify haemoglobin gene expression by qPCR; if confirmed, discriminate true ProMono from erythroid progenitor or megakaryocyte contamination. Assess mitochondrial mass/OXPHOS capacity by MitoTracker and Seahorse analysis to confirm metabolic licensing independent of globin synthesis.

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive ribosomal protein and translation elongation factor expression characteristic of actively translating myeloid progenitors. The enrichment in Early GMP and GMP-Mono cells (72.5%) indicates high biosynthetic demand during lineage priming, supported by associated factors PTMA (nucleolar function, anti-apoptotic) and HMGN1 (active chromatin remodeling). This is a metabolic rather than lineage-defining programme.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL7A: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components—baseline requirement for protein synthesis across all cell types
RPLP0: P0 ribosomal stalk protein; ubiquitous translation machinery
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor (GEF); required for amino-acylated tRNA delivery
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase; facilitates nascent protein folding
PTMA: Nucleolar/nucleoplasmic factor; supports ribosome biogenesis and prevents apoptosis in progenitors
HMGN1: Nucleosomal DNA binding; marks transcriptionally active chromatin consistent with high protein synthesis demand
UQCRH, TXN, GAPDH: Metabolic cofactors (electron transport, redox balance, glycolysis) supporting energetic needs of translation
suggested_validation: This signature lacks lineage-commitment markers (IRF8, CEBPE, CSF1R, CD64) and is non-specific to monocyte differentiation. Cross-reference with cell cycle phase: if GMP-Cycle cells are enriched, signature may reflect S/G2-phase bias rather than monocyte commitment. Validate by co-expression analysis with SPI1, CEBPA, and lineage-specific TFs; perform ribosome profiling or polysome fractionation to confirm active translation state.

programme_name: Monocyte stress response and iron homeostasis
functional_description: This signature captures a stress-responsive, iron-handling programme in CD14 monocytes characterized by S100 calcium-binding proteins, cysteine protease inhibitors, and ferritin heavy chain expression. The prominence of cytoskeletal regulators (actin-binding proteins) and RNA/DNA binding proteins (YBX1) suggests active post-transcriptional control during metabolic stress or activation. KLF4 co-expression indicates regulatory differentiation beyond canonical pro-inflammatory polarization.
key_evidence: S100A6: Top-ranked EF-hand calcium sensor; stress-induced calmodulin-like signalling in activated myeloid cells
S100A4: Calcium-dependent stress response; linked to cell migration and cytoskeletal remodelling in inflammatory monocytes
FTH1: Iron storage and detoxification; essential for ROS management in phagocyte oxidative burst
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor; regulates serine proteases and inflammasome-related proteolysis
KLF4: Master TF for alternative activation but here co-expressed with S100s suggesting regulatory adaptation
YBX1: RNA-binding protein; post-transcriptional control and stress granule formation in activated myeloid cells
COTL1: Actin-binding protein; couples cytoskeletal dynamics to arachidonic acid metabolism (5-LOX interaction)
CD74: MHC-II chaperone; antigen presentation pathway activation consistent with CD14 Mono immune function
ANXA2: Calcium-dependent phospholipid binding; involved in membrane trafficking and exocytosis during activation
TMSB4X: Actin sequestration; controls cytoskeletal dynamics during migration and phagocytosis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: S100A6+ S100A4+ FTH1+ CD14 Mono subset; validate iron metabolism via ferritin ELISA and ROS production (DHE/CM-H2DCFDA); assess KLF4 protein expression to confirm non-classical activation; test for calcium flux responsiveness to TLR ligands; correlate with mitochondrial function (OXPHOS vs glycolysis) to clarify stress context.

programme_name: Monocyte antimicrobial effector and damage control
functional_description: This signature represents a CD14 monocyte-enriched programme (66% CD14 Mono) characterized by antimicrobial peptidases (LYZ, FCN1), calcium-binding damage-associated molecular patterns (S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex, S100A4/A6), and oxidative stress management (GPX1). The programme emphasizes bacterial wall degradation, innate immune pattern recognition via ficolin, and homeostatic control of protease activity (cystatins CST3/CSTA), consistent with terminal effector maturation in classical monocytes.
key_evidence: LYZ: Directly degrades bacterial peptidoglycan; cardinal CD14 mono antimicrobial weapon
S100A8/S100A9: Form calprotectin heterodimer; potent DAMP, TLR4 ligand, and antimicrobial factor enriched in CD14 mono
FCN1: Pattern recognition molecule binding microbial carbohydrates; classical monocyte collectin family member
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for ROS detoxification; essential for monocyte oxidative burst control post-phagocytosis
CST3/CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitors; regulate cathepsin and elastase activity during antimicrobial responses
S100A4/S100A6: Calcium-sensing danger signals; mobilized during inflammatory monocyte activation
GRN: Granulin secretion; involved in tissue remodeling and immune regulation by CD14 mono
ANXA2: Calcium-phospholipid binding; membrane trafficking during phagocytosis and exocytosis
VCAN: Extracellular matrix versican; remodeled by monocyte proteases in inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of S100A8/A9 calprotectin co-expression on CD14+CCR2+ classical monocytes; quantitative proteomics of LYZ, FCN1, and GPX1 across CD14 vs CD16 monocyte subsets; functional assays measuring LYZ-dependent bacterial killing and ROS production capacity in sorted populations

functional_description: This signature reflects the core biosynthetic and metabolic housekeeping functions of CD14 classical monocytes at steady-state, with emphasis on antimicrobial effector capacity and oxidative stress management. The programme is enriched for ribosomal proteins, glycolytic enzymes, and antioxidant systems rather than acute inflammatory activation or PAMP-sensing pathways.
key_evidence: LYZ: Lysozyme; canonical monocyte antimicrobial effector and secreted antibacterial enzyme for constitutive innate immunity
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase; critical antioxidant defence against ROS generated during phagocytosis and respiratory burst
GAPDH: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase; central glycolytic enzyme supporting energy demands of metabolically active monocytes
RPS4Y1, RPS24: Ribosomal structural proteins; indicate high protein synthesis capacity consistent with CD14 Mono biology
CEBPD: CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein delta; related to CEBPB family, involved in myeloid differentiation and basal TF activity
EGR1: Early growth response 1; immediate-early TF supporting homeostatic gene expression programmes
ZFP36L1: TIS11 family zinc-finger protein; early response gene implicated in post-transcriptional regulation of inflammatory mediators
PTMA: Prothymosin alpha; nuclear/cytoplasmic protein with anti-apoptotic function supporting monocyte survival
PLEK: Phospholipase C epsilon interacting protein; signalling protein in membrane-proximal events and G-protein coupled receptor biology
suggested_validation: qPCR validation of LYZ, GPX1, CEBPD, and EGR1 in sorted CD14+ vs CD16+ monocytes; flow cytometry co-staining for CD14/CD16 surface markers combined with intracellular lysozyme and GPX1 detection to confirm homeostatic baseline state; bulk RNA-seq of LPS-unstimulated vs LPS-stimulated CD14 monocytes to confirm suppression of this programme during acute inflammation.

programme_name: Monocyte cytoskeletal remodeling and stress response
functional_description: This signature reflects activation of actin-binding proteins and calcium-responsive factors that coordinate cytoskeletal dynamics, cellular motility, and stress adaptation in monocytes. The enrichment of S100 calcium sensors, actin regulators, and iron-storage proteins suggests preparation for dynamic surveillance and oxidative stress management characteristic of both CD16 and CD14 monocytes engaged in active patrolling or inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: COTL1: F-actin binding protein essential for cytoskeletal reorganization during monocyte crawling and migration
S100A6: EF-hand calcium sensor regulating actin dynamics and monocyte motility in response to calcium signaling
S100A4: Calcium-binding protein driving cell migration and cytoskeletal remodeling in activated monocytes
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein controlling polymerization for directional migration and surveillance
RHOC: Rho GTPase effector promoting actin stress fiber formation and cellular contractility
FTH1: Iron storage and oxidative stress buffering required for sustained antimicrobial surveillance
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator induced by IFN-γ, supporting macrophage activation phenotype
PSAP: Lysosomal priming through saposin production, supporting degradative capacity
YBX1: RNA-binding protein controlling stress response translation and cell proliferation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry assessing F-actin content (phalloidin) and intracellular calcium dynamics in sorted CD16 vs CD14 monocytes; correlate S100A4/S100A6 protein levels with migration velocity in transwell assays; assess whether signature enriches in LPS-activated or patrolling monocyte states from supplementary datasets.

functional_description: This signature reflects the antimicrobial and oxidative stress response capacity of mature CD14 classical monocytes, characterized by high expression of bactericidal enzymes, iron metabolism, and antioxidant defenses. The programme emphasizes pre-positioned effector molecules for rapid pathogen neutralization and ROS detoxification, consistent with CD14 Mono's role in immediate innate immune response.
key_evidence: LYZ: Lysozyme is a canonical bactericidal enzyme targeting peptidoglycan; highly expressed in phagocytic CD14 monocytes for gram-positive and gram-negative PAMP destruction
S100A9: Calprotectin component (S100A9/S100A8 heterodimer) functions as antimicrobial alarmin and damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP); elevated in inflammatory CD14 Mono
S100A6, S100A4: S100 family calcium-binding proteins mediating inflammation and cell migration; signature of activated classical monocytes
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification; essential for ROS homeostasis and prevention of oxidative damage during phagocytosis
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron storage and ferroptosis prevention; critical for metabolic stability during intensive antimicrobial activity
CEBPD: C/EBPδ transcription factor driving antimicrobial gene programmes and inflammatory response; complements SPI1 in monocyte differentiation
CD63: Tetraspanin mediating phagocytosis and lysosomal exocytosis; marker of activated, degranulating monocytes
CSTA: Cystatin A cysteine protease inhibitor; protective against elastase and cathepsin-mediated tissue damage during inflammation
ANXA2: Annexin A2 involved in phospholipid metabolism and phagocytic signalling; supports membrane remodeling during phagocytosis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of LYZ, S100A9, GPX1, and CD63 on CD14+ classical monocytes versus CD16+ non-classical monocytes; validate with functional assays measuring lysozyme-dependent bacterial killing, ROS production (DHE/2,7-DCF staining), and phagocytic index in response to TLR ligands.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation factor expression characteristic of metabolically active Early GMP cells. The enrichment of ribosomal components (RPS/RPL genes), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar proteins (NPM1) indicates robust protein synthetic capacity supporting rapid cell division and differentiation. This metabolic programme is consistent with progenitor-stage cells preparing for lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPLP0: Core 60S ribosomal subunit protein, marks translational-active progenitors
RPS2/RPS24/RPS23/RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit components, signature of biosynthetic capacity
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation in progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor, essential for active protein synthesis during GMP expansion
RPL7A/RPL4/RPL37A: 60S subunit ribosomal proteins supporting sustained translation
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA processing in proliferative cells
HSP90AB1: Heat shock protein supporting protein folding under biosynthetic stress
LDHB/GAPDH: Glycolytic enzymes providing energy for biosynthesis in proliferating GMPs
MT-CO3: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation supporting energetic demands
suggested_validation: Confirm Early GMP enrichment (91%) by protein synthesis rate assays (puromycin incorporation) and ribosome profiling; validate against late GMP/ProMono where translation machinery scales down during terminal differentiation. Compare ribosomal biogenesis rates across GMP substages.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery activity, characteristic of highly proliferative Early GMP progenitors (70% of top activators). The dominance of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS2, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation factors (EEF1B2) indicates robust biosynthetic capacity required for rapid cell division and protein synthesis during early myeloid progenitor expansion.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPL37A: core ribosomal proteins indicating high translational demand in proliferating progenitors
EEF1B2: elongation factor supporting active protein synthesis during cell cycle progression
NPM1: nucleolar protein associated with cell proliferation and ribosome biogenesis, elevated in cycling progenitors
HSP90AB1: heat shock protein supporting protein folding under high biosynthetic stress
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA processing in actively dividing cells
Early GMP enrichment (70%): signature strongest in GMP-Cycle and Early GMP compartments, not committed monocytic stages
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein expression and protein synthesis rate (e.g., puromycin incorporation assay) across Early GMP, GMP-Cycle vs. ProMono and mature monocyte stages. Confirm inverse correlation with myeloid differentiation markers (MPO, CD14, CSF1R upregulation).

programme_name: Metabolic and translational activation monocyte priming
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened oxidative phosphorylation, ribosomal protein synthesis, and RNA-binding protein activity characteristic of metabolically active, committed monocyte progenitors. The dominant enrichment of GMP-Mono cells (41%) and mature CD14/CD16 monocytes (38%) indicates a programme supporting the bioenergetic and translational demands of monocyte lineage commitment, distinct from cycling progenitor or quiescent HSC states.
key_evidence: MT-CO2: core mitochondrial respiratory chain component; dominance reflects ATP generation requirements of committed monocytes
RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPS24: ribosomal proteins indicate elevated global protein synthesis capacity in differentiating monocytes
SLC25A5, SLC25A3: mitochondrial ADP/ATP and phosphate transporters supporting oxidative phosphorylation coupling
COX5A: cytochrome c oxidase subunit; reinforces mitochondrial bioenergetics activation
TMSB4X: actin regulation and cell migration; priming monocytes for extravasation and tissue entry
