CD74: MHC-II chaperone; functional monocyte differentiation marker absent in early GMP
YBX1, HNRNPA1: RNA-binding proteins supporting lineage-specific mRNA processing in monocyte commitment
PPIA: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding during active translation
HMGN1: chromatin-associated protein supporting transcriptional remodelling during differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate with flow cytometry: confirm CD74+/CD64+ (monocyte commitment) signature with reduced MPO and CD34; measure mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker) and respiratory capacity (Seahorse) to confirm oxidative phosphorylation elevation; perform qPCR for CSF1R and CEBPA as monocyte transcription factor markers versus CEBPE/ELANE (granulocyte markers) to distinguish from GMP-Neutrophil trajectory.

functional_description: This signature defines a metabolically activated CD14 classical monocyte state characterized by heightened innate immune responsiveness, elevated glycolysis (HK2), NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT), and robust pro-inflammatory output. The programme integrates danger-sensing (S100A8/A9/A12 alarmins), chemokine production (CXCL8), post-transcriptional regulation (ZFP36L1 mRNA decay control), and metabolic rewiring to support sustained cytokine production and effector function.
key_evidence: CXCL8: canonical pro-inflammatory chemokine; hallmark of CD14 Mono activation
S100A8/A9/A12: damage-associated alarmins; PAMPs/DAMPs; neutrophil recruitment and TLR activation feedback
NAMPT: rate-limiting NAD+ biosynthesis; metabolic support for inflammatory metabolome
ZFP36L1: TIS11 family early response gene; post-transcriptional stabilization of inflammatory mRNAs (TNF, IL6)
BCL2A1: anti-apoptotic; allows prolonged inflammatory function
HK2: Warburg-like metabolic shift; glycolysis-dependent monocyte activation
PLEK: phosphoinositide signaling and PKC coupling; enhanced phagocytic priming
PLAUR: urokinase receptor; tissue infiltration and extracellular matrix remodeling
MAFB: transcriptional regulator; myeloid lineage commitment and pro-inflammatory gene expression
MARCKS: actin-membrane dynamics; migration and morphological adaptation in inflammation
S100A12: calprotectin component; neutrophil-monocyte crosstalk and paracrine amplification
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14+CCR2+S100A8/A9+ gate; validate CXCL8, NAMPT, HK2 expression via qPCR in CD14 Mono sorted from inflammatory bone marrow or bacterial LPS-stimulated ex vivo culture; measure NAD+ and lactate levels to confirm metabolic programme; assess functional outcomes (phagocytosis, ROS, cytokine secretion) in sorted cells ± metabolic inhibitors (glycolysis, NAMPT).

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte and late pro-monocyte maturation towards antimicrobial effector function, characterized by S100 calprotectin complex (S100A8/A9) expression, lysosomal proteases (LYZ, CSTA), and innate immune pattern recognition (FCN1). The programme is enriched for calcium-regulated cytoskeletal dynamics and metabolic reprogramming supporting rapid bacterial killing and NET-like responses.
key_evidence: S100A8: Core component of calprotectin (S100A8/A9 heterodimer); DAMP secretion and antimicrobial activity; hallmark of activated CD14 mono
S100A9: Calprotectin partner; amplifies TLR4 signalling and bacterial recognition in monocytes
S100A12: Extended calprotectin family; pro-inflammatory alarmin; elevated in CD14 mono responses
LYZ: Lysozyme; bactericidal enzyme in granules; high in classical monocytes
FCN1: Ficolin-1; complement lectin pathway activation; PAMP-associated molecular pattern recognition
MNDA: Myeloid differentiation antigen; lineage-specific marker of granulomonocytic maturation
CAPG: Actin-capping protein; calcium-dependent cytoskeletal regulation for phagocytosis and migration
CSTA: Cystatin A; cysteine protease inhibitor; regulates cathepsin activity during antimicrobial responses
RETN: Resistin; pro-inflammatory mediator in myeloid cells; linked to bacterial challenge responses
PKM: Pyruvate kinase; glycolytic reprogramming supporting rapid ATP generation in activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+CD64+ cells for S100A8/A9 protein levels; quantify calprotectin secretion post-TLR stimulation; compare calcium flux and actin dynamics between CD14 and CD16 monocytes; RNAseq validation of signature in LPS-stimulated vs. resting CD14 Mono from BoneMarrowMap donors

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte ADCC and Iron Metabolism
functional_description: This signature defines non-classical CD16 monocytes with enhanced Fc-gamma receptor-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and elevated iron homeostasis. The program combines surface receptor architecture for immune complex recognition with actin cytoskeletal remodeling and antigen presentation capacity, characteristic of patrolling monocytes engaged in vascular surveillance and antimicrobial responses.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Master CD16 receptor enabling ADCC and immune complex clearance; defines non-classical monocyte identity
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma-chain essential for FCGR3A signaling and inflammatory responses
LST1: Lymphocyte-inhibitory membrane protein induced by IFN-γ and bacterial PAMPs; marker of activated CD16 monocytes
FTH1: Iron storage ferritin heavy chain; elevated expression supports antimicrobial oxidative stress responses
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator promoting monocyte activation; induced by interferon and cytokines
COTL1: Actin-binding protein and 5-lipoxygenase interactor; enables cytoskeletal dynamics for crawling and extravasation
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein regulating cell migration essential for vascular patrolling
HLA-DPA1: MHC class II alpha chain for antigen presentation; CD16 mono retain some APC capacity
MS4A7: MS4A family membrane protein with monocyte-enriched expression
CD68: Lysosomal marker reflecting high endosomal activity for immune complex processing
CXCL16: Chemokine involved in IFN-γ response and monocyte recruitment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: FCGR3A+ CD14low with LST1, COTL1, and FTH1 expression; functional validation of ADCC using immune complex-coated target cells; assess CX3CR1 expression to confirm patrolling monocyte phenotype and distinguish from intermediate monocytes

functional_description: This signature reflects the mature classical monocyte (CD14 Mono) state characterized by abundant S100A calcium-binding proteins (S100A9, S100A8, S100A12, S100A6, S100A4) that serve as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and pro-inflammatory mediators. The co-expression of innate immune effectors (FCN1, MNDA, CSTA) and CD14 itself underscores terminal monocyte differentiation with enhanced capacity for pattern recognition and inflammatory response initiation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical alarmin/DAMP—highly abundant in activated monocytes; potentiates TLR4 signaling and NLRP3 inflammasome activation
S100A8: Calprotectin partner with S100A9; major extracellular ligand in infection and sterile inflammation
S100A12: S100 family member; TLR4 agonist; marker of inflammatory monocyte activation
CD14: LPS co-receptor and master monocyte identity marker; confirms CD14 Mono enrichment (82.5%)
FCN1: Pattern recognition receptor (ficolin-1); lectin pathway activation; phagocytic complement amplification
MNDA: Myeloid-restricted nuclear antigen; marks granulomonocytic lineage maturation
CSTA: Cystatin superfamily; protease inhibition in inflammatory context; suppresses cathepsin activity
CAPG: Actin-binding protein; facilitates cell migration and morphological changes during monocyte recruitment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14, S100A9, and S100A8 in CD14+ monocytes; assess correlation with pro-inflammatory transcripts (TNF, IL1B, IL6); validate DAMP secretion by multiplex cytokine assay in LPS-stimulated CD14 Mono sorted from BoneMarrowMap

functional_description: This signature is dominated by hemoglobin genes (HBA2, HBA1, HBB, HBD, HBM) and erythroid-specific proteins (AHSP, CA1), indicating contamination from erythroid lineage cells rather than a genuine monocyte commitment programme. The activating cells show mixed composition with only 52.5% bona fide ProMono cells, and the gene signature lacks canonical monocyte commitment markers (KLF4, IRF8, CSF1R, MS4A3, CTSL, CTSS).
key_evidence: HBA2, HBA1, HBB, HBD, HBM: Five of top 15 genes are hemoglobin subunits, diagnostic of erythroid contamination, not monocyte biology
AHSP: Erythroid-specific alpha-globin chaperone, completely inconsistent with ProMono commitment
CA1: Erythrocyte carbonic anhydrase, marks red blood cell lineage
LYZ: Only ProMono-relevant gene in top 15; monocyte lysozyme expression cannot compensate for overwhelming erythroid signal
TMSB4X, S100A4, RETN: General cytoskeletal/migration genes; non-specific for monocyte commitment
Absence of KLF4, IRF8, CSF1R, MS4A3, CTSL, CTSS, FCGR1A: Complete lack of canonical monocyte TFs and differentiation markers expected in ProMono
suggested_validation: Filter SAE activations to exclude cells with hemoglobin gene expression >2 SD above mean. Re-examine latent representation for erythroid cell admixture in training data. This signature should be excluded from monocyte biology interpretation; validate purity of ProMono sorting/annotation in BoneMarrowMap.

functional_description: This signature represents an active cell-cycle programme dominated by DNA replication machinery and chromatin dynamics, predominantly in CD14 monocytes undergoing proliferation. The enrichment of RRM2 (ribonucleotide reductase M2), ASF1A (histone chaperone), HJURP (centromeric histone variant assembly), and FBXO5 (cell-cycle F-box protein) indicates S-phase progression and coordinated DNA synthesis with histone deposition. This likely reflects bone marrow monopoiesis with active progenitor differentiation contributing substantially to the signature (45% non-CD14 Mono), rather than a mature CD14 monocyte inflammatory state.
key_evidence: RRM2: dNTP synthesis for DNA replication; hallmark S-phase marker
ASF1A: histone H3-H4 chaperone required for chromatin assembly during replication
HJURP: CENP-A deposition at kinetochores; essential for centromere maintenance
FBXO5: APC/C substrate with peak expression in mitotic/S-phase transitions
DNMT1: DNA methyltransferase maintaining epigenetic marks during replication
Cell composition: 54% CD14 Mono but 45% progenitor-pool (ProMono, GMP) indicates proliferative progenitors dominate signature
suggested_validation: Validate by FACS-sorting CD14 Mono subsets by Ki-67/BrdU incorporation; correlate signature with S-phase markers (cyclin E1, MCM2-7, TOP2A). Confirm progenitor contribution by sorting early/late ProMono and comparing RRM2/ASF1A/HJURP expression against quiescent mature CD14 monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic maturation of monocytic progenitors transitioning towards terminally differentiated CD14+ monocytes. The dominant genes encode mitochondrial electron transport components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH) and ribosomal proteins (RPS26, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17), indicating elevated oxidative metabolism and protein synthesis capacity characteristic of post-GMP monocytic differentiation. Hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) likely reflect erythroid-contaminated or dysplastic progenitor cells within the monocytic compartment.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH: mitochondrial respiratory chain complex assembly and OXPHOS, signature of metabolically active mature monocytes
RPS26, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating high translation rate in differentiated monocytes
HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD: hemoglobin chains typically silent in normal monocytopoiesis, suggesting either contamination or abnormal lineage priming
TPI1, PPIA, GSTP1: glycolytic/metabolic enzymes and chaperones supporting oxidative metabolism
Cell composition shows 30% CD14 Mono (mature) and 20.5% GMP-Mono (progenitor), indicating activation spans terminal maturation phase
suggested_validation: FACS sort CD14+ mature monocytes vs. early/GMP progenitors and perform qRT-PCR on MT-encoded genes and RPS components to confirm mature monocyte metabolic state. Investigate hemoglobin expression by RNA in situ hybridization to rule out erythroid contamination or abnormal myeloid dysplasia. Assess mitochondrial mass/membrane potential (TMRM, MitoTracker) in GMP-Mono vs. CD14 Mono populations.

functional_description: Feature 32 represents a translational machinery signature dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS2, RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), with supporting metabolic (LDHB) and chromatin-associated factors (HMGN1, PTMA). This signature is predominantly activated in Early GMP (44.5%) and GMP-Mono (21.5%) cells, reflecting high translational demand during early myeloid progenitor expansion and differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS2/RPS23/RPS24/RPL37A/RPL7A/RPL4: Structural ribosomal proteins indicating active protein synthesis machinery in proliferating progenitors
RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit component, consistent with anabolic metabolism in GMP stage
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis during myeloid commitment
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation (GMP-Cycle link)
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase supporting glycolytic metabolism typical of actively dividing progenitors
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA processing in proliferative cells
HMGN1: Nucleosomal protein associated with transcriptionally active chromatin in differentiating cells
Early GMP dominance (44.5%): Reflects translation requirement at progenitor stage before lineage restriction
GMP-Cycle enrichment (15.5%): Validates connection to cell-cycle associated translational upregulation
suggested_validation: qPCR validation of RPL/RPS genes in sorted Early GMP vs mature monocytes; polysome profiling to confirm elevated translation rates in GMP-stage cells; assess ribosomal protein expression correlation with Ki67 in cycling vs non-cycling GMP subsets

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery activity in early-stage GMP progenitors, indicating high biosynthetic demand during active differentiation. The enrichment of 40S and 60S subunit components (RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPLP0) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and mitochondrial respiratory genes (UQCRH, MT-CO2) suggests metabolic reprogramming supporting rapid protein synthesis in proliferating progenitors rather than lineage-specific commitment signals.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins reflecting translational capacity
RPLP0: essential 60S ribosomal protein, universally expressed in high-biosynthesis cells
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacyl-tRNA transfer, rate-limiting for protein synthesis
UQCRH, MT-CO2, LDHB: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and metabolic support for ATP-intensive translation
NPM1, HMGN1, PTMA: nucleolar/chromatin factors supporting ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation
SNRPE, LSM5: spliceosomal components enabling pre-mRNA processing during active differentiation
Cell composition 53.5% Early GMP, 24% GMP-Mono: signature driven by undifferentiated, proliferative progenitors lacking lineage-specific TFs (IRF8, CEBPE absent)
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring ribosomal content (via puromycin incorporation or polysome profiling) in CD34+KIT+ Early GMP vs. committed monocytic lineage (CD14+CSF1R+). Confirm absence of IRF8, CEBPE, MPO expression. Cross-reference with proliferation markers (MKI67, cycling analysis) to distinguish biosynthetic demand from lineage commitment.

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodeling and antimicrobial
functional_description: This signature reflects active transcriptional remodeling and metabolic priming in Early ProMono cells, characterized by abundant nucleosomal chromatin-associated proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2, H2AFZ) maintaining open chromatin architecture for monocyte commitment transcription. Co-expression of antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, RNASE2, AZU1) and survival regulators (PTMA, LGALS1) indicates preparatory activation of innate immune function concurrent with chromatin plasticity.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte lysozyme marker, antibacterial enzyme
HMGN2/HMGN1: nucleosomal chromatin remodelers in transcriptionally active state
HMGB1/HMGB2: non-histone DNA-binding proteins regulating commitment TF accessibility
PTMA: anti-apoptotic factor stabilizing Early ProMono survival
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease, innate immune priming
AZU1: azurocidin, early monocyte differentiation marker
GAPDH: glycolytic commitment supporting monocyte metabolism
HSP90B1: ER chaperone supporting protein folding in differentiating cells
suggested_validation: Perform ATAC-seq on sorted Early ProMono (MS4A3+KLF4+) vs GMP-Mono to confirm open chromatin at monocyte commitment loci; co-stain for HMGN2+LYZ+ to validate Early ProMono stage and distinguish from Late ProMono CD14 onset.

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Lysosomal and Antigen Processing
functional_description: This signature reflects enhanced lysosomal proteolysis and antigen presentation capacity in CD14 classical monocytes. The programme features cysteine cathepsin-mediated antigen processing (CTSS), MHC class II chaperone function (CD74), and supporting endosomal-lysosomal trafficking machinery, consistent with professional APCs engaged in pathogen degradation and adaptive immune priming.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen degradation and peptide generation for MHC-II presentation
CD74: MHC class II invariant chain chaperone regulating peptide loading and immune synapse formation
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor linking innate sensing to endosomal-lysosomal trafficking
GRN: Secreted granulins promoting lysosomal function and tissue remodelling in monocytes
MNDA: Myeloid lineage-restricted nuclear differentiation antigen marking mature monocyte identity
AP1S2: Clathrin adaptor at Golgi-endosomal axis coordinating receptor trafficking and antigen internalization
GLRX: Glutaredoxin maintaining redox balance in lysosomal compartments during proteolysis
MS4A6A: Membrane glycoprotein supporting endosomal maturation and antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry measuring CTSS activity (DQ-ovalbumin assay), LAMP1+ lysosomal density, and CD74 surface expression; transcriptomics comparing CTSS+ vs CTSS- CD14 monocytes; functional assay of antigen presentation capacity (T-cell proliferation with model peptides).

functional_description: This signature reflects active chromatin remodelling and nucleosome dynamics in proliferating Early ProMono cells, dominated by high-mobility group (HMG) proteins and histone variants that maintain open chromatin architecture. The enrichment of DNA-binding architectural proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2), chromatin-associated factors (NUCKS1, ANP32B/E), and cell cycle machinery (TUBA1B, STMN1) indicates ongoing transcriptional remodelling supporting commitment differentiation rather than mono-lineage terminal maturation.
key_evidence: HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA binding, transcriptionally active chromatin maintenance—hallmark of proliferating progenitors undergoing differentiation
HMGB1/HMGB2: Non-histone chromatin-associated proteins regulating transcription and DNA organization during dynamic cellular transitions
PTMA: Transcription factor binding and apoptosis regulation; elevated in cycling progenitors during lineage commitment
H2AFV/H2AFZ: Histone variants associated with open chromatin and active transcription in differentiating cells
NUCKS1: Nuclear phosphoprotein with casein kinase II sites; involved in chromatin dynamics during cell cycle
STMN1/TUBA1B: Cell cycle regulators (microtubule cytoskeleton, mitotic progression)—consistent with Early ProMono proliferation
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease; monocyte-enriched antimicrobial factor supporting mono lineage identity
ANP32B/E: Histone-binding chromatin modifiers involved in transcriptional regulation during differentiation
suggested_validation: Sort Early ProMono (MS4A3+, KLF4+, CSF1R+, CD14−) and CD14 Mono (CD14+, cyclin-low) by HMGB1/HMGN2/STMN1 expression; confirm signature marks proliferative Early ProMono (Ki67+/S-G2M), diminishes in terminal CD14 Mono; validate chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) at commitment TF loci (KLF4, IRF8) in sorted Early ProMono.

functional_description: This signature reflects high translational capacity in Early GMP progenitors, driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). The predominance of Early GMP cells (86.5%) with active protein synthesis machinery indicates a highly proliferative progenitor state prior to lineage commitment decisions.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating high protein synthesis demand
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacylated tRNA delivery, supporting active translation elongation
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein with roles in ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation regulation
HNRNPA1: pre-mRNA binding and processing, consistent with active gene expression in progenitors
HSP90AB1: molecular chaperone supporting protein folding under high synthesis flux
LDHB: glycolytic enzyme supporting metabolic demands of proliferating Early GMP cells
Early GMP 86.5% composition: signature markedly skewed toward least committed GMP stage
suggested_validation: Assess ribosomal protein abundance by flow cytometry (anti-RPS23, RPL7A); validate translation rate via puromycin incorporation in sorted Early GMP vs. GMP-Mono; correlate signature expression with Ki67 and S-phase markers to confirm proliferation-coupled activation.

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and metabolic activation
functional_description: This signature reflects a cycling, metabolically active early progenitor state characterized by elevated chromatin remodeling, ribosomal function, and oxidative phosphorylation. The dominance of Early ProMono (42%) with concurrent GMP-Cycle (18%) enrichment indicates this feature captures cells in active proliferation prior to full monocytic commitment and surface marker maturation.
key_evidence: HMGB2: chromatin architecture protein marking transcriptionally active, cycling cells
UBE2C: E2 ubiquitin ligase essential for G1/S and G2/M transition in proliferating progenitors
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1: mitochondrial respiratory chain components indicating elevated OXPHOS in cycling precursors
H2AFV, HMGN2: histone variants and nucleosome-associated proteins reflecting open chromatin in dividing cells
ACTG1: cytoskeletal actin required for cell division and cytokinesis
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme supporting biosynthetic demands of proliferating cells
LSM5, SRSF3: spliceosome components indicating high mRNA processing in active progenitors
Early ProMono dominant (42%) with GMP-Cycle co-enrichment (18%): confirms proliferative early ProMono stage
suggested_validation: Validate with Ki67/PCNA co-staining on Early ProMono-sorted cells; assess mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker) and OXPHOS activity (Seahorse) in FACS-isolated Early vs Late ProMono; confirm G1/S entry by BrdU incorporation; compare with resting CD14 Mono to confirm cell cycle downregulation post-commitment.

functional_description: This signature captures elevated ribosomal protein production and translation machinery activity in early GMP-stage progenitors (53.5% Early GMP), reflecting high anabolic demand during active progenitor expansion. The dominance of RPS and RPL genes alongside metabolic cofactors (UQCRH, LDHB, TXN) and translation factors (EEF1B2) indicates coordinated protein synthesis capacity required for rapid GMP proliferation before lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL7A: 40S/60S ribosomal structural proteins—core translational machinery elevated in metabolically active early GMP
RPLP0: Ribosomal acidic protein essential for 60S assembly and translation efficiency in proliferating progenitors
PTMA: DNA-binding co-factor and anti-apoptotic factor—protects actively dividing GMP from death signals during expansion
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating centrosome duplication and cell proliferation checkpoints—elevated in GMP-Cycle (12%) cohort
UQCRH, LDHB, TXN: Mitochondrial/cytosolic bioenergetic enzymes supporting ATP/NADH-intensive protein synthesis in progenitors
EEF1B2, SNRPE: Translation elongation and splicing factors enabling high-fidelity protein production during rapid GMP expansion
Early GMP (53.5%) + GMP-Mono (32.5%) dominance: signature absent in committed ProMono, confirming GMP-stage specificity
suggested_validation: Correlate RPS/RPL expression with MPO/ELANE (myeloid priming) and CDK1/PCNA (cycle state); confirm absence in ProMono by flow sorting CD34+CD123+CD14- vs CD14+CSF1R+ cells; validate by polysome profiling or ribosome occupancy (Ribo-seq) in sorted Early GMP fractions to confirm elevated translation rates.

functional_description: This signature represents a CD14+ monocyte state characterized by abundant expression of S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A12) and antimicrobial effectors that mimic neutrophil-like functionality. The programme is enriched for cytoplasmic granule proteins involved in pathogen containment and innate immune activation, particularly relevant to classical monocyte antimicrobial responses and trained immunity.
key_evidence: S100A8: Canonical neutrophil granule protein; calprotectin complex component (with S100A9) with strong PAMP-sensing and antimicrobial activity
S100A9: Calprotectin partner; endogenous DAMP with TLR4/RAGE signalling; pro-inflammatory alarmin in monocytes
S100A12: DAMP; calgranulin C; links to inflammasome activation and trained immunity in monocytes
S100A4: Calcium-binding protein implicated in monocyte migration and ECM remodelling
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein supporting monocyte effector function
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen; marker of differentiated monocyte-granulocyte lineage
FCN1: Ficolin lectin pathway; pattern recognition for bacterial LPS and fungal PAMPs
CSTA: Cystatin cathepsin inhibitor; balances protease activity in granule-rich cells
CD14: LPS co-receptor; core signature of classical monocyte activation and PAMP sensing
VCAN: Versican ECM component; supports inflammatory microenvironment and recruitment
CAPG: Actin-binding protein; enables rapid cytoskeletal remodelling for phagocytosis and migration
suggested_validation: Validate by surface marker phenotyping (CD14++CD16-CCR2+) combined with intracellular staining for S100A8/A9 and FCN1; correlate with ex vivo monocyte responses to TLR4 agonists (LPS) and bacterial PAMP stimulation; assess for calprotectin secretion and antimicrobial capacity

functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 classical monocytes undergoing acute inflammatory response with upregulation of pro-inflammatory mediators (IL1B, CCL3), innate immune receptors (TYROBP, CLEC7A, FCER1G), and stress-response pathways. The programme integrates antimicrobial effector functions (CTSS-mediated antigen processing, PSAP lysosomal function) with iron homeostasis (FTH1) and mRNA stability control (ZFP36) characteristic of endotoxin or PAMP-activated monocytes.
key_evidence: IL1B: canonical inflammasome output and pro-inflammatory cytokine in activated CD14 monocytes
CCL3: chemokine recruitment signal for additional myeloid cells during inflammation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing signalling adaptor essential for TLR and Fc receptor cooperativity in myeloid cells
CLEC7A: C-type lectin PAMP receptor (Dectin-1) for fungal/bacterial pattern recognition
FCER1G: FcγR signalling chain critical for phagocytic immune complexes and antibody-dependent activation
CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease for antigen processing and microbial degradation
FTH1: stress-induced iron sequestration limiting pathogenic iron availability
ZFP36: RNA-binding protein controlling TNF/IL1B mRNA stability in inflammatory monocytes
AIF1: calcium-binding protein amplifying macrophage activation signals
GADD45B: DNA damage/stress response priming cytokine production
BCL2A1: anti-apoptotic survival factor in activated myeloid cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+ monocytes for CD83, CLEC7A, and intracellular IL-1β/CCL3 in LPS-stimulated or septic samples; RNA-seq of sorted CD14 Mono ± TLR4 agonist to confirm inflammasome-activation kinetics; correlate signature with serum CCL3 and ferritin in systemic inflammation cohorts.

programme_name: Early ProMono cytoskeletal and innate activation
functional_description: This signature reflects early monocyte progenitor commitment characterised by actin cytoskeleton remodelling, chromatin accessibility for active transcription, and innate immune effector protein expression. The dominance of Early ProMono (33%) and GMP-Mono (19%) cells indicates a transitional progenitor state with emerging monocytic functions but retention of some proliferative capacity.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein essential for cell migration and differentiation during ProMono egress and tissue homing
HMGN2: Nucleosomal chromatin regulator marking transcriptionally active chromatin state consistent with active mono commitment programme
LGALS1: Galectin-1 mediates cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions required for ProMono extravasation and niche interactions
S100A8: Myeloid-enriched calcium-binding protein marking mature innate immune function (calprotectin component)
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear antigen specific to granulocyte-monocyte lineage, marking monocytic rather than neutrophilic commitment
CSTA: Cystatin-family protease inhibitor suggesting active protease regulation during mono differentiation
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease indicative of functional mono effector programme acquisition
CAPG: Gelsolin-family actin regulator supporting dynamic cytoskeletal reorganisation during migration
suggested_validation: Sort Early ProMono and Late ProMono by FACS (MS4A3+CSF1R+CD14−/low vs CD14+) and validate via RT-qPCR that TMSB4X, HMGN2, MNDA, and S100A8 show graded upregulation across GMP→Early ProMono→Late ProMono→CD14 Mono trajectory. Confirm CSTA/RNASE2 upregulation distinguishes ProMono from GMP-Neut (MPO+ ELANE+ profile).

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis capacity and translational machinery expression characteristic of early GMP progenitors (57.5% of activating cells). The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4), translation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar/chromatin-associated proteins (NPM1, HMGN1) indicates active protein synthesis concurrent with high proliferative activity. Mitochondrial respiratory chain components (UQCRH, MT-CO2, MT-CO3) support elevated metabolic demand of dividing progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins, core translational machinery upregulated in biosynthetically active early GMP
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor essential for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery during active protein synthesis in proliferating cells
NPM1: Centrosome/cell cycle regulator and nucleolar protein supporting ribosome biogenesis in cycling progenitors
HMGN1: Chromatin-associated protein maintaining open chromatin state compatible with high gene expression in early GMP
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation proteins reflecting increased metabolic capacity needed for rapid proliferation
HNRNPA1, PTMA: RNA-binding and transcription factor-associated proteins supporting active mRNA processing in progenitor cells
Cell composition: 57.5% Early GMP + 9.5% GMP-Cycle indicates signature enriched in actively proliferating, pre-commitment stage progenitors
suggested_validation: Validate by co-expression analysis with canonical GMP cell-cycle markers (CDK1, MKI67, TOP2A) and confirm negative correlation with GMP lineage commitment markers (IRF8, CEBPE, KLF4). Flow cytometry: sort early GMP (CD34+, KIT+, low CD11b) and confirm elevated ribosomal protein abundance and active protein synthesis (e.g., OPP labeling) relative to committed progenitors.

functional_description: This signature reflects a mature monocyte program centered on MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation and lysosomal proteolytic capacity. The coordinated expression of HLA-DR and HLA-DP heterodimers with CD74 (MHC II chaperone) and lysosomal cathepsins (CTSS) indicates professional antigen-presenting cell differentiation. Iron homeostasis via FTH1 and polyamine catabolism via SAT1 support sustained metabolic demands of antigen processing.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRB5, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: complete MHC class II presentation machinery (5 of top 15)
CD74: MHC II chaperone and invariant chain essential for antigen loading and presentation
CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease critical for antigen processing and MHC II peptide generation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for TLR/complement receptor signaling integration in antigen-presenting cells
PSAP: lysosomal saposins required for cathepsin-mediated protein degradation
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron storage supporting sustained lysosomal and metabolic function
AIF1: actin-binding protein supporting cytoskeletal dynamics for antigen uptake and processing
IFITM3: interferon-induced antiviral/antimicrobial protein in activated monocytes
CST3: cysteine protease inhibitor regulating lysosomal proteolysis balance
COTL1: actin-binding protein; interaction with 5-lipoxygenase links to lipid mediator signaling
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry confirming HLA-DR/DP surface expression and CD14+CD16-/+ dichotomy; functional assays of antigen processing capacity (fluorescent antigen uptake and MHC-peptide presentation); lysosomal proteolytic activity (cathepsin B/L assays); single-cell RNA-seq to verify co-expression patterns of MHC II genes and CTSS in CD14 Mono versus CD16 Mono subsets.

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive cellular processes (energy metabolism, ribosomal translation, chromatin remodelling) rather than monocyte commitment-specific transcriptional programmes. The enrichment of glycolytic enzymes, ribosomal proteins, and nucleosome-associated factors indicates active protein synthesis and chromatin accessibility during proliferative transition, but lacks lineage-defining transcription factors (KLF4, IRF8) and commitment markers (CSF1R, MS4A3, CD14) expected in ProMono specification.
key_evidence: GAPDH: glycolytic housekeeping enzyme, universally expressed regardless of differentiation state
HMGN1/HMGN2: chromatin remodelling factors maintaining transcriptional accessibility, non-lineage-specific
HMGB1/HMGB2: high-mobility group proteins involved in general DNA binding and chromatin organization, not monocyte fate determinants
PTMA/ANP32B/ANP32E: nucleosome-associated proteins; low specificity for ProMono vs GMP comparison
RPL37A/EEF1B2: ribosomal proteins and translation factors indicating active protein synthesis but no commitment signature
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing; ubiquitous, not lineage-restricted
LGALS1: galectin with immunomodulatory role but not specific to monocyte progenitor identity
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease; present across monocyte stages but not definitive of ProMono commitment
suggested_validation: This feature lacks mono-commitment specificity. Validate by: (1) comparing expression of core ProMono TFs (KLF4, IRF8, PU.1) and surface markers (CSF1R, MS4A3, CD14) across Early ProMono, Late ProMono, and GMP; (2) assessing whether this signature is similarly elevated in other proliferative progenitor states (HSPCs, GMP-Cycle); (3) confirming CD14 Mono and CD16 Mono cells show downregulation if they exit cell cycle. Consider exclusion from lineage-defining signatures.

programme_name: Early GMP ribosomal biogenesis and translation
functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis machinery in early-to-intermediate GMP populations (86.5% Early GMP + GMP-Mono), characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0), translation factors (EEF1B2), and supporting metabolic/regulatory processes. The enrichment in ribosomal biogenesis components alongside nucleosomal remodeling (HMGN1) and centrosome regulation (NPM1) indicates heightened biosynthetic capacity consistent with proliferative early GMP progenitors prior to terminal monocytic commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0: Core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—constitutive markers of active translation in rapidly dividing progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for efficient amino acid delivery; elevated in high-biosynthesis cell states
HMGN1: Nucleosomal DNA-binding protein maintaining open chromatin architecture, consistent with transcriptional activity in proliferating progenitors
NPM1: Nucleophosmin involved in centrosome duplication and cell proliferation; biomarker of active cell-cycle progenitors
PTMA: Prothymosin-alpha with DNA-binding and anti-apoptotic functions; supports survival in early myeloid differentiation
MT-CO2, UQCRH, LDHB: Mitochondrial and glycolytic metabolism supporting high energy demand in biosynthetically active GMP
SNRPE: Splicing component; supports pre-mRNA processing in transcriptionally active cells
Cell composition: 51% Early GMP + 35.5% GMP-Mono (86.5% total GMP trajectory); minimal mature mono representation (2.5%) confirms early-stage progenitor signature
suggested_validation: RT-qPCR quantification of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A) and NPM1 in FACS-sorted Early GMP vs. mature CD14 monocytes; confirm ribosomal biogenesis pathway enrichment via pathway analysis (MSigDB C2/C5); assess correlation with proliferation markers (Ki67, CDK1) to distinguish from quiescent HSCs.

programme_name: Monocyte Cytoplasmic Remodelling and Iron Metabolism
functional_description: This signature reflects shared cytoplasmic infrastructure genes encoding actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1, AIF1), calcium-responsive S100 proteins (S100A4, S100A11, S100A6), and iron homeostasis machinery (FTH1, PSAP). The co-enrichment in both CD16 and CD14 monocytes (47.5% and 41.5% respectively) indicates these represent foundational monocyte biology rather than lineage-defining functions.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: G-actin sequestration critical for monocyte migration and cytoskeletal plasticity across subsets
FCER1G: Fc-gamma receptor signalling scaffold present in all mature monocytes, enables ADCC capacity in CD16 Mono
S100A4/S100A11/S100A6: Calcium-regulated cytoplasmic proteins mediating inflammatory activation and migration—non-discriminatory across monocyte lineages
COTL1: F-actin regulator; 5-LOX interaction links to lipid mediator synthesis in activated monocytes
AIF1: IFN-inducible actin-binding protein; elevated in innate activation but not CD16-specific
FTH1/PSAP: Iron storage and lysosomal lipid metabolism—housekeeping functions for phagocytic capacity
HBA1/HBA2/HBB: Haemoglobin genes likely reflect erythroid contamination or ambient RNA, not monocyte biology
suggested_validation: This signature lacks canonical CD16 Mono markers (CX3CR1, NR4A1/2/3, FCGR3A, ISG15, IFITM3). Flow cytometry verification of CD14 vs CD16 surface expression on top-200 activating cells; RT-qPCR comparison of patrolling TFs (NR4A genes) and anti-viral ISGs to confirm CD16 enrichment. Haemoglobin genes should be validated as technical artifact vs. true expression.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis capacity and translational activity in early myeloid progenitors, driven by ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, RPS23), translation factors (EIF5A, EEF1B2), and associated chaperones. The enrichment in Early GMP (39%) alongside NPM1 (nucleolar/centrosomal function) and CDK6 (G1/S transition) suggests active biosynthetic demand during early GMP proliferation rather than lineage-specific commitment.
key_evidence: RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit structural protein; core translational machinery
RPS23: 40S ribosomal subunit structural protein; indicates high protein synthesis rates
EIF5A: Translation initiation/elongation factor; supports rapid protein production
EEF1B2: GEF for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery; essential for translation elongation
NPM1: Nucleolar protein regulating ribosome biogenesis and protein chaperoning; peaks in proliferating progenitors
CDK6: G1/S cyclin-dependent kinase; consistent with GMP-Cycle activity (7% composition)
HSP90AB1: Chaperone protein; supports nascent protein folding under biosynthetic stress
Early GMP dominance (39%): signature peaks in least differentiated GMP fraction with highest biosynthetic demand
suggested_validation: Validate with ribosomal profiling (polysome analysis) or pSer2/4-RNA Pol II ChIP to confirm active transcription; compare translational rates between Early GMP vs. differentiated GMP-Mono/ProMono using polysome fractionation. Confirm low expression of lineage-committed markers (SPI1, CEBPA, IRF8) to exclude monocytic commitment programme.

functional_description: This signature marks the transition from cycling GMP to monocyte-committed progenitors, characterized by activation of myeloid differentiation machinery (MPO, ELANE, AZU1) coupled with elevated protein synthesis capacity and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. The dominant GMP-Cycle and GMP-Mono composition (61%) with minor ProMono representation indicates capture of early monocyte lineage priming before full transcriptional commitment.
key_evidence: MPO: Myeloperoxidase, canonical early myeloid enzyme expressed in both GMP and monocyte precursors; present before CD14/CD16 differentiation
ELANE: Neutrophil elastase; co-expressed with MPO in early myeloid progenitors indicating pan-myeloid priming phase before lineage segregation
AZU1: Azurocidin, granule protein marking immature myeloid differentiation; GMP-Mono enriched
RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS17: Ribosomal proteins indicating high translational demand consistent with actively differentiating GMP-Mono cells
UQCRH, MT-CO2: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation enzymes reflecting bioenergetic activation during myeloid commitment
PLAC8: Chromatin regulator predicted to activate transcription; supports active myeloid lineage transcriptional programmes
HMGN1, PTMA: Chromatin remodelling factors facilitating open chromatin at differentiation loci
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: MPO+ELANE+CD34+/−KIT+CSF1R+CD14−CD16− to distinguish early GMP-Mono from ProMono (MPO−CSF1R++CD64+). Single-molecule FISH for MPO/ELANE in sorted GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono subsets. Functional validation: measure ribosomal protein translation rate and OXPHOS dependency in GMP-Mono using Seahorse analysis.

programme_name: Monocytic cytoplasmic maturation and stress response
functional_description: This signature reflects the cytoplasmic maturation phase of monocytic differentiation, characterized by accumulation of actin-regulatory proteins (TMSB4X, ACTG1), oxidative stress defence mechanisms (GPX1, GSTP1), and ribosomal/translational machinery supporting increased protein synthesis demands. The gene composition is consistent with post-GMP monocytic commitment (GMP-Mono 37%, Early ProMono 20.5%) where cells establish metabolic and structural readiness for terminal monocytic maturation while retaining some GMP characteristics.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein essential for cytoskeletal reorganization during monocytic maturation and migration
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase marking shift from progenitor to mature monocyte redox stress adaptation
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor and transcription factor cofactor supporting survival during differentiation commitment
ACTG1: Cytoskeletal actin supporting enhanced motility characteristic of maturing monocytes
GSTP1: Detoxification enzyme reflecting metabolic transition and oxidative stress management in committed monocytes
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease indicating initiation of functional monocyte programmes
RPS24, RPL37A: Ribosomal proteins supporting elevated protein synthesis for differentiation-associated products
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) single-cell ATAC-seq to confirm open chromatin at monocyte lineage-commitment loci (SPI1, IRF8 targets) in GMP-Mono vs Early ProMono populations; (2) flow cytometry co-staining TMSB4X/ACTG1 with CSF1R, CD64, and CD14 to stage maturation trajectory; (3) examine whether CD34 and cell-cycle markers (CDK1, MKI67) are downregulated in this signature to exclude GMP-Cycle contamination.

functional_description: This signature reflects MHC class II antigen presentation machinery and lysosomal proteolytic capacity in CD14 monocytes. The coordinated expression of HLA-DR/DP/DQ components (CD74, HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1) with cathepsin S (CTSS) and saposin precursor (PSAP) indicates active processing of exogenous antigens for immune surveillance. Actin dynamics (TMSB4X, TAGLN2) and calcium signaling (CALM2) support cellular trafficking required for antigen uptake and presentation.
key_evidence: CD74: Essential chaperone for MHC class II loading and stabilization; highest Welch t-stat indicates strong differential expression
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease critical for peptide generation from internalized antigens
HLA-DRA/DRB1/DPA1/DPB1: Complete HLA-DR and HLA-DP heterodimer components required for peptide-MHC presentation
PSAP: Saposin precursor processed to facilitate lysosomal hydrolase trafficking and lipid antigen presentation
AIF1: Calcium-binding protein induced by cytokines, promotes macrophage activation and antigen-presenting cell function
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein regulating cellular dynamics during antigen uptake and intracellular trafficking
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain component of phagocytic receptors enabling opsonized antigen recognition
CD63: Tetraspanin marking late endosomal/lysosomal compartments involved in antigen processing
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying HLA-DR surface expression and CD74 protein levels in CD14 vs CD16 monocytes; functional assays measuring antigen presentation capacity (e.g., FITC-dextran uptake, peptide presentation assays); confirm CTSS activity in CD14 monocyte lysates.

programme_name: Monocyte Antimicrobial Defense and Antigen Presentation
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte programme centered on innate antimicrobial effector functions and MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation. The dominant genes encode lysozyme for bacterial peptidoglycan degradation, HLA class II molecules (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB5, CD74) for adaptive immune priming, and stress-response proteins supporting cellular homeostasis during inflammatory activation.
key_evidence: LYZ: Direct bactericidal enzyme targeting peptidoglycan; signature antimicrobial effector of CD14 monocytes
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB5, CD74: MHC class II machinery for antigen presentation and T cell activation; hallmark of classical monocytes
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase protecting against ROS generated during phagocytosis and respiratory burst
TMSB4X, HMGN1, HMGN2: Actin regulation and chromatin remodeling supporting dynamic cell migration and transcriptional plasticity
PTMA, YBX1, HSP90B1: Stress response chaperones stabilizing proteins during inflammatory activation
MS4A6A, GPR183: Surface immunomodulatory receptors involved in immune cell trafficking and activation
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor controlling proteolysis during antimicrobial responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm CD14+ CD64+ HLA-DR+ phenotype in activating cells; validate LYZ protein expression and localization via intracellular staining; measure ROS production (DHE/DCF assay) in GPX1-expressing monocytes; perform bacterial phagocytosis assays to confirm functional antimicrobial capacity independent of inflammasome signature.

functional_description: This signature represents a lysosomal/phagolysosomal maturation and antimicrobial effector programme in classical CD14+ monocytes. The coordinate expression of cathepsin S (CTSS), ficolin-1 (FCN1), and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP supports active phagosomal degradation and pattern recognition, while ferritin heavy chain (FTH1) and iron metabolism genes reflect the metabolic demands of phagocytic oxidative burst.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein essential for Fc and pattern recognition receptor signaling in phagocytes
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease critical for antigen processing and phagolysosomal degradation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (M-ficolin) is an innate immune lectin expressed in monocytes; activates complement and enhances phagocytosis
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage and ROS homeostasis during phagocytic oxidative burst
AP1S2: AP-1 adaptor; clathrin-mediated endocytic trafficking to lysosomes
PSAP: Prosaposin; lysosomal sphingolipid activator essential for lysosomal function
GRN: Granulin; secreted granulins promote phagocytosis and tissue remodeling in innate inflammation
LGALS2: Galectin-2; lectin involved in pattern recognition and immune regulation
S100A11: Calcium-binding protein; enhanced in activated myeloid cells, marker of inflammatory monocyte state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm TYROBP+CTSS+FTH1+ subset enrichment in CD14+CD16- monocytes and validate FCN1 surface/intracellular expression. Functional assays: assess phagocytic capacity (bacteria/opsonized particles) and ROS production in TYROBP+ cells. qPCR validation of top-5 genes across sorted CD14 Mono, CD16 Mono, and GMP to confirm monocyte-subset specificity.

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Iron Homeostasis and MHC-II
functional_description: This signature reflects mature CD14 classical monocyte identity with emphasis on iron metabolism (FTH1-driven ferritin accumulation), antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DMA), and inflammatory responsiveness. The programme marks cells with high phagocytic and antigen-presenting capacity, characteristic of tissue-resident or pre-inflammatory CD14 monocytes.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage protein; elevated in metabolically active, ROS-producing classical monocytes
CD63: Tetraspanin involved in lysosomal exocytosis and phagocytic machinery maturation
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DMA: MHC-II antigen presentation complex; hallmark of CD14 Mono professional APCs
CLEC7A: Dectin-1 receptor for fungal PAMPs; pattern recognition in innate immunity
MAFB: MAFB transcription factor required for monocyte/macrophage differentiation
MARCKS: PKC substrate involved in cytoskeletal rearrangement during phagocytosis and migration
TIMP1: Matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor; tissue remodelling and resolving inflammation
ZFP36L1: Early response gene regulating TNF and IL-1 mRNA stability
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein; involved in monocyte activation and migration
LGALS3: Galectin-3; lectin involved in cell-cell adhesion and inflammatory responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14++ CD16- CCR2+ with FTH1, CD63, HLA-DR high. Functional assays: FACS-sort signature-positive CD14 Mono and assess phagocytosis capacity, iron content via Prussian blue, and antigen presentation via MHCII-peptide complex staining.

functional_description: This signature reflects active chromatin accessibility and transcriptional machinery engagement characteristic of Early ProMono progenitors undergoing proliferative expansion. The dominance of nucleosomal proteins (HMGN2, HMGB1/2, H2AFZ/V) and actin regulators (TMSB4X) combined with metabolic (PKM) and myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA, LYZ) indicates cells in S/G2-M phase actively remodelling chromatin while maintaining monocytic commitment. The modest Late ProMono representation (2%) and absence of canonical mono-commitment TFs (KLF4, IRF8) suggest this programme captures proliferative Early ProMono rather than maturation checkpoints.
key_evidence: HMGN2: nucleosomal DNA binding, active chromatin organisation in proliferating progenitors
HMGB1/HMGB2: high-mobility group proteins regulating transcriptional accessibility during cell cycle
TMSB4X: actin sequestration driving cytoskeletal dynamics during S/G2-M phase
H2AFZ/H2AFV: histone variants marking active chromatin in cycling cells
LYZ: monocytic commitment marker, distinguishes from GMP-Neut trajectory
MNDA: myeloid lineage-specific nuclear antigen, validates monocyte progenitor identity
PKM: glycolytic engagement supporting proliferative metabolism
JUN: immediate-early response to proliferation signals
suggested_validation: Validate via: (1) co-staining Early ProMono (MS4A3+ CSF1R+) cells for Ki-67/PCNA and HMGB1 nuclear localisation; (2) RNA velocity analysis to confirm these cells precede Late ProMono/CD14 Mono; (3) ChIP-seq for HMGN2/HMGB1 occupancy at monocyte commitment loci (CSF1R, LYZ, CCR2) in sorted Early ProMono vs GMP to distinguish commitment-driven from proliferation-driven chromatin remodelling.

programme_name: OXPHOS and proteostasis in monocyte maturation
functional_description: This signature reflects active oxidative phosphorylation and protein quality control mechanisms across monocyte development from early progenitors to mature CD14 monocytes. The programme prioritizes mitochondrial bioenergetics (COX5A, NDUFS6, UQCRQ) and proteostatic stress responses (PSMA4, TXN, GSTP1) essential for supporting metabolic demands during monocytopoiesis.
key_evidence: COX5A: Complex IV subunit driving terminal oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria
NDUFS6: Complex I iron-sulfur cluster protein for NADH oxidation
UQCRQ: Complex III ubiquinone-binding subunit in electron transport chain
PSMA4: 20S proteasome core subunit for regulated proteolysis
TXN: Redox buffering and S-nitrosylation regulation under metabolic stress
GSTP1: Detoxification and electrophile conjugation during oxidative metabolism
ENO1: Glycolytic enzyme linking glycolysis to OXPHOS coordination
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor supporting survival during metabolic transition
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase accelerating protein folding kinetics
RANBP1: Cell cycle regulation by nucleocytoplasmic transport coordination
suggested_validation: Measure oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and glycolytic flux across CD14 Mono, Early/Late ProMono, and GMP-Mono subsets; assess proteasome activity and mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM) by flow cytometry; validate TXN-dependent redox buffering by mass spectrometry S-nitrosylation profiling.

programme_name: Monocyte Maturation and Antimicrobial Effector Functions
functional_description: This signature reflects the transition from progenitor cells (28% Early/Late ProMono) to mature CD14 classical monocytes (52%), marked by activation of antimicrobial enzymes, oxidative stress defenses, and calcium-dependent signaling. The program emphasizes bacterial cell wall degradation (LYZ), cysteine protease regulation (CSTA, CST3), and ROS detoxification (GSTP1, GPX1), consistent with myeloid differentiation and inflammatory monocyte priming without canonical pro-inflammatory cytokine dominance.
key_evidence: LYZ: bacterial peptidoglycan degradation, hallmark of mature monocyte antimicrobial capacity
GSTP1 + GPX1: glutathione-dependent detoxification and peroxide metabolism, essential for ROS handling in inflammatory monocytes
S100A4 + S100A6: calcium-binding proteins driving cell migration and differentiation during monocytopoiesis
CSTA + CST3: cysteine protease inhibition regulating cathepsin-mediated antimicrobial responses
MNDA: myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen, marker of granulocyte-monocyte lineage commitment
ANXA2 + LGALS1: calcium-dependent phospholipid binding and autocrine signaling in differentiation
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease activity against bacterial targets
Enrichment in ProMono (40%) over CD16 Mono (1.5%): signature reflects terminal monocyte maturation trajectory
suggested_validation: Sort CD14 Mono by LYZ/GSTP1 co-expression and validate with: (1) flow cytometry for CD14+CCR2+FCGR1A+ cells; (2) functional assay of phagocytosis and ROS production (DCF staining); (3) transcript correlation with SPI1/CEBPB in bulk RNA-seq; (4) compare to resting vs. LPS-stimulated monocyte transcriptomes to confirm priming without full activation.

programme_name: GMP translational priming with myeloid differentiation
functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis machinery and mitochondrial oxidative capacity in cycling GMP-stage progenitors (73.5% GMP-Cycle + Early GMP), coupled with early myeloid granule protease priming. The dominant ribosomal proteins and mitochondrial electron transport components indicate metabolic preparation for differentiation, while MPO and PRSS57 signal initiation of azurophil granule biogenesis characteristic of GMP-to-monocyte/neutrophil commitment.
key_evidence: MPO: canonical early myeloid differentiation marker; azurophil granule biogenesis initiation in committed progenitors
RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins; sustained high translation for differentiation programme execution
PRSS57: serine protease stored in azurophil granules; myeloid-specific granule maturation marker
MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain components; elevated OXPHOS capacity supporting GMP proliferation and differentiation
HSPB1: heat shock protein; stress response and protein quality control during rapid translational upregulation
Cell composition 73.5% GMP-Cycle/Early GMP: signature enriched in proliferative early progenitors, not late-stage monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD34+KIT+ early GMP (vs CD14+ monocytes) for MPO, PRSS57, and MitoTracker intensity; qRT-PCR on sorted GMP-Cycle vs Early ProMono to confirm ribosomal protein decline with commitment; assess IRF8/CEBPE ratio to refine mono vs neutrophil priming trajectory.

programme_name: Interferon-primed monocyte activation and effector function
functional_description: This signature reflects interferon-induced activation and cytoskeletal remodeling in both CD14 and CD16 monocytes, with emphasis on antiviral/antimicrobial priming and Fc-receptor-mediated immune surveillance. The balanced CD14/CD16 composition and enrichment of interferon-stimulated genes (IFITM3) alongside actin-binding proteins and protease inhibitors suggests coordinated preparation for pathogen sensing and tissue infiltration rather than active inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: IFITM3: Canonical interferon-stimulated antiviral protein; indicates type I/II IFN priming independent of active TLR signaling
FCGR3A: CD16-enriched Fc-gamma receptor; present in both populations suggests cross-talk between classical and non-classical monocyte subsets
LST1: LPS and IFN-γ responsive membrane protein; lymphocyte-inhibitory function indicates trained immunity phenotype
AIF1: Cytokine/interferon-induced; promotes macrophage activation; supports IFN-mediated programming
S100A4/S100A11: Calcium-binding cytoskeletal regulators; associated with monocyte migration and tissue infiltration
COTL1: Actin-binding protein with 5-lipoxygenase interaction; supports eicosanoid signaling and motility
SERPINA1: Serine protease inhibitor; protects against excessive proteolysis during inflammatory tissue remodeling
TIMP1: MMP inhibitor; restrains ECM degradation; indicates controlled rather than pathological inflammation
RHOC: Small GTPase; mediates actin dynamics and cellular motility
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of IFITM3, FCGR3A, LST1 on sorted CD14+ vs CD16+ monocytes; IFN-β/γ stimulation time-course to confirm IFN-responsiveness; functional assays: Fc-receptor crosslinking response and chemotactic migration capacity in both populations.

programme_name: Early GMP protein synthesis and translation
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened translational machinery and protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP progenitors, with dominant ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS23, RPS26, RPLP0) and translation factors (EEF1B2) alongside splicing machinery (SNRPE). The inclusion of NPM1 (nucleolar/centrosome function) and CDK6 (G1/S transition) suggests coordination between active protein production and cell cycle progression characteristic of proliferative early myeloid progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS26, RPLP0: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins—direct readout of translational capacity
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery—core elongation function
SNRPE: U snRNP component—spliceosome assembly required for pre-mRNA processing during active transcription
NPM1: nucleolar organizer and cell proliferation regulator—synchronizes ribosome biogenesis with cell cycle
CDK6: G1/S cyclin-dependent kinase—consistent with GMP-Cycle enrichment (5.5%) and Early GMP dominance (59.5%)
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA processing—supports high translational demand
HSP90AB1: heat shock protein for protein folding—manages proteostasis during rapid synthesis
LDHB, NUCB2: metabolic and signaling support for energy-demanding protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Ribosome profiling or polysome analysis on sorted Early GMP vs. late ProMono to quantify active translation rates; correlate RPS/EEF1B2 expression with CDK6 and cell cycle scoring; confirm NPM1 centrosomal/nucleolar localization in Early GMP by immunofluorescence.

functional_description: This signature defines a non-classical (CD16+) monocyte program centered on antimicrobial defence and enhanced Fc-receptor-mediated cytotoxicity. The module combines actin cytoskeletal dynamics (S100A4, COTL1, TMSB4X, RHOC) required for patrolling behaviour with type I interferon-induced antiviral effectors (IFITM3) and ADCC machinery (FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP). Expression reflects activated myeloid cells poised for vascular surveillance and antibody-dependent cellular responses.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Canonical CD16 lineage marker; Fc-receptor mediating ADCC and immune complex clearance
IFITM3: Type I IFN-induced antiviral transmembrane protein; hallmark of antiviral CD16 monocytes
FCER1G: FcRγ-chain component of high-affinity IgE receptor and FcγR signalling complexes; TYROBP partner
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for FcγR and other pattern recognition receptors; amplifies cytotoxic signalling
S100A4: Calcium-binding protein driving motility and amoeboid crawling behaviour in patrolling monocytes
COTL1: Actin-binding protein and 5-LOX interactor; controls cytoskeletal dynamics and motility
AIF1: Interferon-induced actin-binding protein; marks activated innate immune cells
LST1: LPS/IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein; enriched in CD16 monocytes with antimicrobial function
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering thymosin; regulates cell migration essential for patrolling
RHOC: RhoC GTPase; coordinates F-actin dynamics and cellular locomotion
PSAP: Saposin precursor; involved in lipid antigen presentation and antimicrobial response
CST3: Cystatin; cysteine protease inhibitor in innate immune activation context
suggested_validation: Sort CD14-CD16++ cells from bone marrow; quantify by qPCR/flow for FCGR3A, CX3CR1, IFITM3, S100A4; perform functional assays (ADCC, crawling velocity, type I IFN response kinetics) to confirm non-classical monocyte patrolling and antimicrobial competence. Compare activation status against CD14++ monocytes to confirm differential enrichment.

programme_name: Early GMP translational priming and myeloid maturation
functional_description: This signature reflects a transitional myeloid progenitor state characterized by elevated ribosomal protein expression (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPS2, RPLP0) indicating active protein synthesis capacity, coupled with early myeloid differentiation markers (MPO, PRSS57). The enrichment of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components (MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, UQCRH) and chromatin-associated factors (HMGN1, PTMA) suggests cells are metabolically preparing for differentiation while maintaining nuclear plasticity.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPS2, RPLP0: Coordinate ribosomal upregulation indicates heightened translation capacity typical of early differentiating GMP (59.5% Early GMP composition)
MPO: Prototypic early myeloid marker present in GMP stages, marks lineage priming before terminal commitment
PRSS57: Arginine-specific serine protease destined for azurophil granules; signature of myeloid differentiation program activation
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRH: OXPHOS gene enrichment indicates metabolic shift from quiescent HSC toward committed progenitor with increased energy demand
HMGN1, PTMA: Nucleosomal modulation and apoptosis suppression consistent with survival and chromatin remodeling during lineage commitment
Cell composition: 82.5% GMP-stage cells (Early GMP + GMP-Cycle + GMP-Mono) confirms GMP enrichment, minimal mature monocyte contamination (6.5%)
suggested_validation: FACS sort Early GMP/GMP-Cycle by CD34+KIT+CD33+ gates and validate via qPCR for ribosomal protein coordinate expression, MPO/PRSS57 upregulation, and OXPHOS gene activation. Perform metabolic profiling (Seahorse) to confirm increased OXPHOS dependency relative to HSC. RNA-velocity analysis recommended to confirm trajectory toward monocytic vs granulocytic commitment.

functional_description: This signature reflects a nuclear remodeling and translational capacity programme enriched in Early/GMP-Mono progenitors. The dominant signal comprises chromatin-associated proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1, H2AFZ) maintaining transcriptionally permissive euchromatin, coupled with core translation machinery (RPS24, HNRNPA2B1, PPIA) and metabolic housekeeping (ENO1, MT-CO3), supporting active biosynthesis during ProMono differentiation.
key_evidence: HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA binding protein marking open chromatin in transcriptionally active ProMono cells
HMGN1: Co-regulates euchromatic state with HMGN2 during monocyte lineage commitment
HMGB1: Non-histone nuclear protein regulating transcription during ProMono maturation
H2AFZ: Histone variant incorporated into active chromatin regions
LYZ: Core monocyte lysosomal hydrolase; marks mono commitment programme (top Welch statistic)
RPS24: Ribosomal protein indicating active translation capacity in proliferating progenitors
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease consistent with early monocytic differentiation
PPIA: Peptidylprolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding during rapid biosynthesis
ENO1: Glycolytic enzyme supporting energetic demands of ProMono proliferation
suggested_validation: Validate by assessing chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) at loci of mono commitment TFs (KLF4, IRF8, PU.1) in Early vs Late ProMono; confirm HSP90B1/PPIA co-expression with CTSL, CTSS, CSF1R; quantify ribosomal activity (polysome profiling) in sorted Early ProMono vs GMP-Mono to confirm translation programme intensity.

programme_name: Early GMP ribosomal protein translation activity
functional_description: This signature captures the high translational capacity and protein synthesis machinery of Early GMP and GMP-Mono progenitors, marked by abundance of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS2) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2). The co-enrichment of mitochondrial respiratory complex components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) and nucleolar/proliferation markers (NPM1, HMGN1, PTMA) indicates active biosynthetic capacity supporting rapid cell proliferation characteristic of early myeloid progenitors prior to lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS2: Core 60S and 40S ribosomal subunit proteins - dominant signature indicating high translational demand
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF - supports active protein synthesis capacity
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain - elevated OXPHOS activity fueling biosynthesis in proliferative progenitors
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in centrosome duplication and cell proliferation - marks actively cycling cells
PTMA: DNA-binding co-factor with anti-apoptotic function - supports progenitor survival during expansion
HMGN1: Open chromatin association - consistent with transcriptionally active early GMP state
Cell composition 61% Early GMP + 21.5% GMP-Mono: Signature enriched in multipotent, pre-committed GMP stages rather than committed monocytes
suggested_validation: Sort Early GMP and GMP-Mono by this signature and validate via ribosome profiling or polysome-seq to confirm enhanced translation rate; co-measure metabolic activity (seahorse OXPHOS/glycolysis) and compare to committed ProMono and mature CD14 monocytes; perform ATAC-seq to confirm open chromatin enrichment at ribosomal biogenesis loci.

programme_name: Myeloid differentiation and innate effector activation
functional_description: This signature reflects a mature CD14 classical monocyte state characterized by cytoskeletal remodelling (TMSB4X), myeloid lineage commitment markers (MNDA), and calcium-regulated inflammatory proteins (S100A4, S100A6, S100A11). The programme integrates innate sensing capacity (FCN1 collectin), lysosomal protease activity (CTSS for antigen processing), and interferon-stimulated genes (IFI6, IFI27) indicative of activated myeloid effector function.
key_evidence: MNDA: lineage-restricted myeloid nuclear antigen marking monocyte/granulocyte differentiation commitment
TMSB4X: actin sequestration regulating migration and monocyte egress from bone marrow
S100A4/S100A6/S100A11: calcium-binding proteins driving inflammatory amplification and myeloid activation
FCN1: pattern recognition collectin (mannose-binding lectin pathway) for bacterial PAMP sensing
CTSS: cathepsin S for lysosomal antigen degradation and MHC-II presentation
TYROBP: ITAM-signalling adaptor coupling FcγR and TREM-1 for enhanced inflammatory output
IFI6/IFI27: interferon-stimulated genes indicating type-I IFN priming or viral PAMP exposure
GLRX: glutaredoxin redox regulator supporting ROS homeostasis during oxidative burst
suggested_validation: Co-expression analysis with classical CD14+ markers (CD14, LYZ, S100A8/A9); validate FCN1 and TYROBP protein levels by flow cytometry; assess functional capacity via LPS-induced TNF/IL-6 secretion and Fc-receptor-mediated phagocytosis in TYROBP+ versus TYROBP- sorted CD14 monocytes.

programme_name: Mitochondrial OXPHOS and metabolic priming CD14
functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocytes with elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity, poised for metabolic demands of pro-inflammatory responses and phagocytic activity. The dominance of Complex I (MT-ND1, MT-ND5) and Complex IV (MT-CO2, MT-CO3) genes indicates heightened ATP production supporting inflammatory effector functions. Concurrent expression of iron storage (FTH1) and NAD metabolism (NAMPT) supports sustained redox and biosynthetic capacity during activation.
key_evidence: MT-ND1: Core Complex I NADH dehydrogenase; essential for OXPHOS-driven ATP generation in metabolically active monocytes
MT-CO3: Complex IV component; indicates sustained respiratory capacity for ROS production and energy demands
MT-CO2: Cytochrome c oxidase subunit; required for terminal oxidative phosphorylation in activated monocytes
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage for heme synthesis and protection against iron-mediated ROS
NAMPT: NAD salvage pathway; supports glycolytic and OXPHOS flux critical for monocyte activation
CSF3R: G-CSF receptor; marks inflammatory monocyte mobilisation and maturation status
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; ECM interactions during monocyte recruitment and inflammatory infiltration
RPS26, RPL37A, RPS17: Ribosomal proteins; elevated translation capacity for cytokine and inflammatory mediator synthesis
suggested_validation: Measure mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1), oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse), and steady-state ATP levels in CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono; validate NAD+ metabolism and iron status; correlate with inflammatory activation markers (TNF, IL-1β production) and phagocytic capacity.

programme_name: Translational machinery in early myeloid progenitors
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation elongation factor expression characteristic of highly proliferative early GMP and GMP-Mono cells with active protein synthesis. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0) and translation factors (EEF1B2) combined with glycolytic enzyme GAPDH indicates metabolic demands of rapid myeloid commitment and differentiation. Supporting proteins like NPM1 (nucleolar/centrosomal function during cell division) and HMGN1 (active chromatin remodeling) further suggest the active biosynthetic state characteristic of progenitor-to-monocyte transition.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal structural components indicating sustained translation capacity in proliferating progenitors
EEF1B2: elongation factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, marks high translational flux during commitment
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme supporting bioenergetic demands of early GMP and GMP-Mono cells
NPM1: nucleolar protein and cell-cycle regulator consistent with 41.5% Early GMP composition
HMGN1: chromatin-associated protein reflecting transcriptional remodeling during myeloid lineage commitment
YBX1: RNA binding protein supporting mRNA stabilization during differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate by comparing ribosomal protein expression levels across sorted Early GMP, GMP-Cycle, and GMP-Mono populations via qPCR or Western blot. Assess correlation with cell-cycle markers (CDK1, MKI67) and early myeloid TFs (SPI1, CEBPA). Measure protein synthesis rate using puromycin incorporation or O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) labeling to confirm elevated translational capacity in activating GMP cells.

functional_description: This signature represents a constitutive metabolic and translational programme enriched in GMP-stage progenitors, particularly GMP-Mono cells. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17), translation factors (PPIA, HNRNPC, HNRNPA2B1), and glycolytic/mitochondrial machinery (GAPDH, UQCRH, MT-CO3) reflects high biosynthetic capacity and ATP demand during active myeloid differentiation rather than lineage-specific commitment signals.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17: core ribosomal structural proteins, elevated in metabolically active GMP-Mono (44.5%) and Early GMP (22.5%)
PPIA: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase essential for ribosome assembly and protein folding during translation acceleration
GAPDH, UQCRH, MT-CO3: glycolytic and oxidative phosphorylation enzymes supporting energy-intensive protein synthesis in progenitors
HMGN1, PLAC8, ANP32B: chromatin-associated proteins maintaining transcriptionally permissive state compatible with multi-lineage plasticity
PTMA, ACTG1: cell stress response and cytoskeletal dynamics consistent with progenitor proliferation
Absence of lineage-defining TFs (SPI1, IRF8, CEBPE) or late monocyte markers (CD14, CD16 in mature mono subset only 8%)
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring proliferation (Ki67) and metabolic activity (TMRM/JC1) in sorted GMP-Mono vs. mature CD14 Mono; confirm ribosomal protein co-expression via qPCR in Early GMP and GMP-Cycle populations; assess whether signature declines in Late ProMono/mature monocytes where biosynthesis attenuates post-commitment.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 classical monocyte activation characterized by upregulation of myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA), calcium-binding alarmin S100 proteins (S100A8, S100A6, S100A4, S100A11) involved in innate immune signaling and inflammation, and lysosomal proteinases (CTSS, CSTA) supporting phagolysosomal antimicrobial function. The program integrates pattern recognition (FCN1 ficolin), ITAM signaling (TYROBP/DAP12), and cytoskeletal dynamics (TMSB4X) required for monocyte activation, migration, and bactericidal response.
key_evidence: MNDA: myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen—canonical monocyte lineage marker and nuclear transcription factor associated with myeloid maturation
S100A8/S100A6/S100A4/S100A11: calprotectin complex and alarmins—hallmark of activated monocyte innate immune response, Ca2+-sensing, and DAMP/PAMP signaling
FCN1: ficolin-1—collectin pathway pattern recognition receptor for bacterial PAMP sensing independent of TLR
TYROBP: DAP12—ITAM-bearing adaptor coupling Fc receptors and TREM family to downstream monocyte activation
CTSS/CSTA: cathepsin S and cystatin A—lysosomal proteases essential for antigen processing and antimicrobial killing within phagolysosomes
TMSB4X: thymosin β4—actin sequestration regulating monocyte migration and phagocytic capacity
IFI6: interferon-stimulated gene—suggests priming by type I IFN or activation state
HBA2/HBB: hemoglobin genes—consistent with iron-dependent antimicrobial metabolism in activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-express S100A8/A9 with CD14 and CD64 (FCGR1A); functional assays: measure phagocytic capacity (FITC-opsonized bacteria), ROS production (DHE assay), and cathepsin S activity; RNA-FISH to validate MNDA nuclear localization in CD14 Mono subset

programme_name: Early GMP Basal Translation and Chromatin
functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery activity in early GMP-stage progenitors (67% Early GMP), coupled with chromatin-organizing nucleolar proteins. The predominance of ribosomal subunit components (RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPS2, RPLP0) and translation factors (PPIA, EEF1B2) indicates high basal protein synthesis capacity typical of metabolically active early progenitors, while HMGN1 and HMGB1 suggest open chromatin architecture supporting active transcription.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS2, RPLP0: 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—direct markers of translation apparatus abundance in actively synthesizing early GMP
PPIA, EEF1B2: Translation elongation factors mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery—hallmark of high protein synthesis demand in progenitors
HMGN1, HMGB1: Non-histone nucleosomal proteins regulating chromatin accessibility and transcription—consistent with open chromatin of proliferative early GMP
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in ribosome biogenesis and centrosome duplication—links ribosomal production to proliferative capacity
HNRNPA1, SNRPE: Pre-mRNA processing and splicing machinery—support for active gene expression in early progenitors
LDHB: Glycolytic enzyme in lactate metabolism—metabolic signature of proliferating hematopoietic progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor with TF-binding activity—survival signal in early myeloid progenitors
Composition 67% Early GMP, 21% GMP-Mono: Signature enriched in the least lineage-committed myeloid progenitors
