suggested_validation: RT-qPCR quantification of RPS and EEF1B2 across FACS-sorted Early GMP, GMP-Mono, and ProMono populations; ribosome profiling or polysome analysis to confirm translational activity differences; chromatin accessibility assay (ATAC-seq) in Early GMP vs. downstream stages to validate HMGN1/HMGB1 chromatin state; correlate signature expression with cell cycle phase (GMP-Cycle enrichment expected if S/G2-phase specific).

functional_description: This signature reflects the mature antimicrobial effector state of CD14+ classical monocytes, dominated by S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9 heterodimer calprotectin, S100A6, S100A12, S100A4) that function as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and antimicrobial agents. The co-expression of FCN1 (ficolin-1, pattern recognition receptor), MNDA (myeloid differentiation antigen), and CSTA (cystatin A, cysteine protease inhibitor) indicates activation of innate immune granule biogenesis and antimicrobial responses characteristic of pro-inflammatory classical monocytes.
key_evidence: S100A9: Core component of calprotectin heterodimer; antimicrobial, DAMP, calcium-dependent inflammation
S100A8: Calprotectin partner; neutrophil-monocyte recruitment and ROS amplification
FCN1: Pattern recognition receptor; complement-independent innate immune activation
MNDA: Granulocyte-monocyte lineage marker; nuclear antimicrobial response coordination
S100A12: Calprotectin family member; alarmin function in sterile inflammation
CD14: LPS co-receptor; bacterial PAMP sensing and monocyte identification marker
CSTA: Cystatin superfamily; protease inhibition during antimicrobial degranulation
S100A4: S100 family; cell migration and inflammation amplification
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; extracellular matrix remodeling in inflammatory microenvironment
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting CD14++CD16- monocytes and validating S100A8/A9 co-expression alongside FCGR1A and CCR2 positivity; RNA-FISH confirmation of S100A protein granule localization; functional assays measuring calprotectin-dependent ROS production and bacterial killing capacity.

functional_description: This signature captures enhanced oxidative phosphorylation capacity during GMP-to-monocyte transition, characterized by coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial electron transport chain components (Complex I and IV subunits). The signature reflects metabolic reprogramming supporting the bioenergetic demands of early monocytic commitment, coupled with myeloid differentiation markers and stress response mechanisms.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-ND6: Core OXPHOS machinery (Complex I/IV), essential for ATP generation during monocytic differentiation
MPO: Classical early myeloid marker present in GMP and monocytic lineage; retained in Early ProMono but downregulated in mature monocytes
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator, facilitates cellular reorganization during commitment
HMGB1: Chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation during differentiation; stress response mediator
HSP90B1: ER-localized chaperone supporting protein folding demands during differentiation
ATP5IF1: Mitochondrial ATP synthase inhibitor; fine-tunes bioenergetic status
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor supporting survival during commitment
GMP-Mono enrichment (31%) + Early ProMono (27%): Signature activates in committed monocytic progenitors, declining in mature monocytes (8.5% CD14 Mono, 1.5% CD16 Mono)
suggested_validation: Quantify mitochondrial mass (TMRM/MitoTracker) and ATP levels across sorted GMP-Mono→Early ProMono→CD14 Mono; correlate with MPO/STMN1 protein expression; validate OXPHOS dependency via Seahorse mito stress test on progenitor subsets

functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 classical monocytes in an acute inflammatory state, characterized by abundant S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A12) that serve as PAMPs and danger-associated molecular patterns, combined with antimicrobial effectors (LYZ, FCN1) and myeloid differentiation markers. The dominance of S100A8/A9 heterodimer (calprotectin) indicates strong innate immune activation with robust oxidative burst and bacterial killing capacity.
key_evidence: S100A8: Core component of calprotectin (S100A8/A9), released upon bacterial/inflammatory triggers; ligand for TLR4 and RAGE
S100A9: Calprotectin partner; marks immature/activated myeloid cells with heightened antimicrobial function
S100A12: Extended calprotectin family member; neutrophil and monocyte activation marker
LYZ: Lysozyme; key antimicrobial enzyme for bacterial peptidoglycan degradation in phagolysosomes
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor and complement pathway activator for bacterial/fungal recognition
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen; marks granulomonocytic lineage and transcriptional activation
CD14: High expression confirms classical monocyte identity; LPS co-receptor with TLR4
CAPG: Gelsolin-like actin regulator; enables cytoskeletal dynamics for chemotaxis and phagocytosis
S100A4: Fibroblast-associated protein; elevated in inflammatory monocytes with enhanced migration
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of S100A8/A9 co-expression with CD14+CD16- monocytes; LPS stimulation timecourse RNA-seq to confirm TLR4-driven induction; assess calprotectin secretion and antimicrobial activity (ROS, bacterial killing assays) in sorted S100A8/A9-high vs -low CD14 Mono subsets.

functional_description: This signature represents a shared metabolic programme across monocyte developmental stages, driven by oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) complexes and glycolytic enzymes. The programme supports energy production and cellular biosynthesis in differentiated monocytes and early progenitors, with accompanying chaperone and proteostasis functions for protein quality control.
key_evidence: MT-CO2: Core OXPHOS complex IV component; consistently top-ranked mitochondrial electron transport gene
MT-CO3: OXPHOS complex IV assembly and function; validates mitochondrial respiration signature
MT-ND1: OXPHOS complex I; NADH oxidation essential for ATP generation
TPI1: Glycolytic enzyme; bridges glycolysis-gluconeogenesis and energy metabolism
TMSB4X: Actin dynamics regulator; supports cell motility and metabolic adaptation in monocytes
GSTP1: Detoxification enzyme; protects against metabolic stress and ROS from OXPHOS
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase; protein folding chaperone for proteostasis
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor; metabolically active cells require survival signals
YBX1: RNA-binding protein; post-transcriptional regulation of metabolic transcripts
CALM2: Calcium signalling; mitochondrial calcium handling couples energy metabolism
suggested_validation: Seahorse metabolic flux analysis comparing CD14 vs CD16 monocytes and GMP subsets for OXPHOS and glycolytic capacity; validate by measuring ATP production and mitochondrial membrane potential across developmental stages.

functional_description: This signature captures active protein synthesis and metabolic support machinery in early GMP-stage progenitors. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0), translation factors (EEF1B2), and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components (UQCRH, MT-CO2) reflects the elevated biosynthetic demand of proliferating myeloid progenitors during early commitment phases.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0: 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit constituents, indicating active translation in progenitor population
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, essential for protein synthesis rate
UQCRH, MT-CO2: Oxidative phosphorylation complex components, supporting high ATP demand in cycling progenitors
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase B, indicating active glucose metabolism and energy production
NPM1, PTMA: Nucleolar phosphoproteins involved in ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis control
TXN, PPIA: Redox and protein folding support for nascent protein maturation
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator active during mitotic cycling
37.5% Early GMP + 35.5% GMP-Mono + 14.0% GMP-Cycle = 87% early progenitors requiring robust biosynthesis
suggested_validation: Confirm through polysome profiling or metabolic flux analysis (glucose consumption, oxygen consumption rate) in sorted Early GMP vs GMP-Mono populations; validate mitochondrial mass by MitoTracker or JC-1 staining; assess ribosome biogenesis via 45S pre-rRNA qPCR. Compare translational activity (puromycin incorporation) between GMP-Cycle vs Early ProMono to distinguish cycling vs. early committed stages.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in CD14 monocytes, indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity and metabolic activity. The enrichment of S100A12, a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) and neutrophil marker, alongside EGR1 and SOCS3 suggests stress-responsive transcriptional regulation in activated classical monocytes.
key_evidence: RPL37A, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17: ribosomal proteins indicating global translational capacity and active protein synthesis in inflammatory CD14 monocytes
MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-CO2: core mitochondrial respiratory chain components reflecting elevated oxidative metabolism for ATP production
S100A12: alarmin and neutrophil antimicrobial protein; serves as DAMP and pro-inflammatory mediator, strongly associated with acute monocyte activation
EGR1: immediate early transcription factor responding to stimulation and stress, consistent with TF-mediated inflammatory responses
SOCS3: negative feedback regulator of cytokine signaling, indicating dampening of excessive JAK-STAT and TLR-induced inflammation
LTB: TNF family cytokine involved in lymphoid tissue development and immune cell activation
CD14 Mono dominance (68%) with minimal CD16 Mono (10%) and progenitor contamination (<18%) confirms cell-type specificity
suggested_validation: Validate by RNA-seq or qPCR in FACS-sorted CD14+ monocytes stimulated with TLR ligands (LPS, Pam3CSK4); assess mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1) and ROS production (DHE/DCFDA) in S100A12+ CD14 monocytes; confirm EGR1 and SOCS3 dynamics by Western blot or flow cytometry phospho-STAT3 over LPS time-course.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated cellular metabolism and housekeeping functions characteristic of proliferative Early ProMono progenitors. The enrichment of mitochondrial electron transport genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1) and ribosomal proteins indicates high oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis capacity, consistent with metabolically active progenitors prior to terminal differentiation and cell cycle exit.
key_evidence: MT-CO2: Core mitochondrial electron transport chain complex IV component; metabolic demand of proliferating progenitors
MT-CO3: OXPHOS complex IV assembly and respiratory function in metabolically active cells
MT-ND1: Complex I NADH oxidation; fundamental to ATP generation in proliferative cells
HMGB2: Non-histone chromatin protein; marks transcriptionally active chromatin in dividing progenitors
HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA binding; associated with open chromatin in actively transcribed regions
RPS26: 40S ribosomal protein; elevated protein synthesis in proliferating Early ProMono
TUBB, TUBA1B: Microtubule components; active cytoskeletal dynamics during cell cycle progression
HNRNPA2B1: RNA processing and splicing factor; coupled to active transcription
PPIA: Prolyl isomerase; protein folding support during high-throughput protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Validate metabolic signature via flow cytometry with MitoTracker/TMRM for mitochondrial mass and membrane potential. Use BrdU/Ki67 to confirm proliferative status of Early ProMono vs Late ProMono. Cross-reference with published metabolic profiling of sorted ProMono subsets (Seahorse OCR/ECAR). Note signature lacks monocyte commitment markers (KLF4, IRF8, CSF1R, MS4A3) and surface markers (CD14, CD64), reflecting bulk metabolic rather than lineage-defining programme.

programme_name: Early ProMono proliferation and innate immunity
functional_description: This signature captures early-stage monocyte progenitor commitment marked by active cell cycle progression (PCNA, MKI67, PCLAF, DUT) combined with antimicrobial effector gene expression (LYZ, RNASE2, S100A8/A9). The dominance of Early ProMono (63.5%) with robust proliferative and innate immune machinery reflects a progenitor population still cycling while beginning to acquire monocytic functional programmes prior to full CD14 surface maturation.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: S100 calcium-binding proteins marking early myeloid activation and innate inflammatory response in committed progenitors
LYZ: Canonical monocyte antimicrobial lysosomal enzyme, upregulated during ProMono commitment
RNASE2: Ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity, component of monocyte effector armoury
MKI67/PCNA/PCLAF/DUT: Proliferation signatures indicating Early ProMono retains cell cycle activity before exit at Late ProMono/CD14 Mono stage
HMGB2/H2AFZ: Chromatin remodelling factors supporting active transcriptional programme during progenitor transition
STMN1/TUBB: Cytoskeletal dynamics consistent with morphological changes during monocyte commitment
RETN/CES1: Metabolic enzymes reflecting monocyte-specific lipid and xenobiotic handling capacity
MT-CO3: Oxidative phosphorylation supporting energetic demands of proliferating committed progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: co-express KLF4, IRF8, and CSF1R with Ki67+ and S100A8/A9+ status in MS4A3+ Early ProMono; confirm loss of MPO/ELANE relative to GMP controls; quantify CD14 expression (low/absent in Early ProMono vs high in CD14 Mono fraction); single-cell RT-qPCR to verify proliferation-immunity gene coordination.

functional_description: This signature defines a CD16 monocyte-enriched programme centered on actin cytoskeleton reorganization and Fc-gamma receptor signaling for immune surveillance. The coordinated expression of actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1, VASP, RHOC) with FCGR3A and signaling adaptors (FCER1G, AIF1) enables dynamic cellular morphology changes required for vascular crawling and antibody-dependent cellular responses. Transcriptional regulation via SPI1 (PU.1) orchestrates this myeloid activation state.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Definitive CD16 monocyte marker; enables ADCC via Fc-gamma engagement on endothelium
TMSB4X: Top-ranked actin sequestrant; essential for actin polymerization dynamics in patrolling cells
COTL1: Actin-binding protein with 5-LOX interaction; supports crawling behaviour on vessel walls
VASP: Ena-VASP family member; regulates actin dynamics and cell motility in patrolling surveillance
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein; induced by IFN-gamma; promotes macrophage activation phenotype
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain; amplifies FCGR3A signaling for immune complex recognition
LST1: LPS and IFN-gamma inducible membrane protein; supports anti-microbial surveillance
SPI1: Master ETS transcription factor; drives myeloid differentiation and CD16 monocyte identity
S100A11, S100A4: Calcium-binding proteins; support cytoskeletal reorganization in activated monocytes
Cell composition: 82% CD16 Mono confirms signature specificity to non-classical subset
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain FCGR3A+ cells for VASP phosphorylation, actin polymerization assays (phalloidin), or live-cell tracking of crawling velocity on endothelial monolayers. RNA-seq validation on sorted CD16 Mono (CX3CR1+FCGR3A+CD14lo) versus CD14 Mono. Functional assessment: measure ADCC capacity and endothelial transmigration in presence of immune complexes.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthetic capacity and translational activity, driven by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS2, RPL7A, RPLP0), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation machinery (MT-CO2, UQCRH). The enrichment in early GMP (47%) and GMP-Cycle (31%) cells indicates active biomass accumulation and energy metabolism required for rapid progenitor proliferation and lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPLP0: Coordinate ribosomal protein expression supporting high translation demand in proliferating GMP
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor enabling efficient ribosomal function during biosynthetic expansion
MT-CO2, UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components reflecting oxidative ATP generation for anabolic processes
NPM1: Nucleolar protein and cell cycle regulator consistent with S/G2-phase GMP-Cycle enrichment (31%)
HMGN1: Chromatin accessibility factor supporting transcriptionally active state in proliferating progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic and DNA-binding protein stabilizing progenitor survival during transit amplification
H3F3A, GAPDH: Metabolic and chromatin remodelling support for rapid cell division
suggested_validation: Validate by correlating with Ki-67/MKI67 expression, BrdU incorporation, and mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM) in sorted Early GMP and GMP-Cycle populations. Confirm absence of lineage-specification markers (IRF8, CEBPE, MPO) to exclude ProMono commitment. Perform ribosomal RNA quantification and oxygen consumption rate assays to confirm translational and oxidative state.

functional_description: This signature represents activated monocytes with enhanced pattern recognition receptor signaling, lysosomal-mediated antigen processing, and interferon-responsive innate immunity. The program reflects early PAMP sensing and inflammatory priming through ITAM-coupled signaling (TYROBP, FCER1G) coupled with cytotoxic granule and lysosomal proteolytic capacity (CTSS, PSAP). Strong enrichment in CD14 classical monocytes (62.5%) indicates a pro-inflammatory, antimicrobial effector state.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein essential for FcγR and pattern recognition receptor signaling; hallmark of activated myeloid cells
FCER1G: Common γ-chain of Fcγ receptors (CD64) critical for immune complex and IgG-mediated phagocytosis and activation
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine cathepsin required for antigen processing and presentation; marker of activated antimicrobial monocytes
PSAP: Saposin precursor supporting lysosomal function and lipid antigen presentation to T cells
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein induced by inflammatory cytokines; promotes macrophage activation
IFI6, IFITM3, IFI27: Interferon-stimulated genes indicating type-I interferon signaling and antiviral/antimicrobial priming
FCN1: Ficolin family pattern recognition receptor; complement-like pathway activation in response to bacterial PAMPs
LST1: LPS-inducible gene with lymphocyte inhibitory function; enhanced in bacterial sensing states
TMSB4X, CALM2: Actin polymerization and calcium signaling regulators supporting cellular migration and activation
S100A11: Calmodulin-like calcium sensor; inflammatory monocyte marker
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD14+CD64+TYROBP+ with intracellular CTSS and surface FCN1; RNAscope or qPCR validation of TYROBP, FCER1G, FCN1 in sorted CD14 monocytes stimulated with LPS or heat-killed bacteria; correlate with inflammatory transcription factors (IRF5, CEBPB) not listed but expected upstream drivers.

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis and lysosomal degradation capacity characteristic of CD14 classical monocytes, with prominent ribosomal proteins (RPS26) and cysteine cathepsin (CTSS) supporting both anabolic and catabolic functions. The inclusion of calcium-binding S100 proteins and actin-regulatory proteins (TMSB4X) indicates active cytoskeletal remodeling and calcium signaling required for inflammatory responses and phagocytic function.
key_evidence: RPS26: Ribosomal 40S subunit protein - reflects high protein synthesis capacity in metabolically active CD14 monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-containing signaling adapter - essential for Fc receptor and TLR signaling in monocyte activation
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine cathepsin - required for antigen processing and phagolysosome function in innate immunity
S100A6, S100A4: Calcium-binding proteins - involved in calcium signaling and inflammatory responses in myeloid cells
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein - supports cytoskeletal dynamics for migration and phagocytosis
FOSB: AP-1 transcription factor component - mediates immediate-early inflammatory gene expression
HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD: Hemoglobin subunits - markers of early erythroid contamination or monocyte-associated hemoglobin uptake
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry for CD14+ CD16- surface phenotype; assess CTSS and TYROBP protein expression; confirm minimal hemoglobin gene expression is not indicative of erythroid contamination using CD235a/GPA gating; compare FOSB activity under TLR4 stimulation vs baseline

programme_name: Activated CD14 monocyte iron and proteolysis
functional_description: This signature reflects activated classical monocytes engaged in iron homeostasis, lysosomal proteolysis, and inflammatory responses. The co-expression of ferritin (FTH1), cathepsin S (CTSS), and TYROBP-dependent signaling indicates cells primed for antigen presentation and antimicrobial responses, with elevated S100 alarmin family members suggesting tissue-damaging inflammation or recent activation.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage protein, marks metabolically active monocytes under oxidative stress or iron acquisition
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor protein critical for TLR/CLR-dependent inflammatory signaling in myeloid cells
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease required for MHC-II antigen processing and inflammasome maturation
S100A4, S100A6, S100A11: Alarmins associated with inflammatory monocyte activation and tissue infiltration
MAFB: Master transcription factor for alternative activation and tissue-resident macrophage specification
CXCL16: Membrane-anchored chemokine supporting monocyte recruitment and T cell interactions
ZFP36L1: Post-transcriptional regulator of pro-inflammatory cytokine stability (IL6, TNF, IL1B)
BCL2A1: Anti-apoptotic factor preserving survival of activated inflammatory monocytes
TIMP1: Matrix metalloproteinase inhibitor balancing extracellular remodeling during inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-gating FTH1/TYROBP/CTSS in CD14+ vs CD16+ subsets; RNA-FISH for S100A family in inflamed tissues; assess correlation with TLR/CLR ligand stimulation and iron uptake assays.

functional_description: This signature represents activated CD14+ classical monocytes characterized by dominant S100 calprotectin expression (S100A8/A9/A12), acute phase response proteins, and myeloid pattern recognition machinery. The programme reflects calcium-dependent antimicrobial effector functions and rapid inflammatory responses typical of pro-inflammatory classical monocytes during acute immune activation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin component; major neutrophil/monocyte alarmin driving DAMP-mediated inflammation and TLR4 signalling
S100A8: Calprotectin S100 heterodimer partner; potent neutrophil chemoattractant and danger signal
S100A12: S100 family member; TLR4 ligand amplifying pro-inflammatory signalling in classical monocytes
CD14: LPS co-receptor essential for TLR4/MD-2 complex formation; defines classical monocyte identity
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor; couples pattern recognition receptors (TREM-1/2) to inflammatory signalling cascades
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition lectin activating complement and opsonization in activated monocytes
VCAN: Versican; ECM proteoglycan supporting monocyte adhesion and extravasation during inflammation
FOSB: AP-1 component; immediate early TF enabling rapid NF-κB-dependent pro-inflammatory gene expression
JUN: c-Jun AP-1 partner; integrates inflammatory signalling for TNF/IL-6/IL-8 transcription
GPX1: Antioxidant defence; balances ROS burden during oxidative phagocytic responses
CSTA: Cystatin protease inhibitor; modulates cysteine protease-mediated inflammation in myeloid cells
AP1S2: Clathrin adaptor; facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis and intracellular trafficking of PAMP sensors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying S100A8/A9 surface co-expression with CD14-high/CCR2+ classical monocytes; validate calprotectin secretion and TLR4 responsiveness in isolated CD14 Mono stimulated with LPS; assess TYROBP-DAP12 association with TREM-1 engagement and NF-κB reporter activity.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression across the monocytic continuum (GMP-Mono through mature CD14/CD16), indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity during myeloid commitment. The dominance of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPS24, RPL37A, RPLP0) coupled with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and mitochondrial metabolic support (SLC25A5, UQCRH) suggests active biomass accumulation characteristic of differentiating monocytic progenitors transitioning from GMP stages.
key_evidence: RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPS24, RPL37A: Constitute 5/15 top genes—core 40S/60S ribosomal structure enriched in actively translating monocytes
RPLP0: Large subunit ribosomal protein, consistent with increased protein synthesis during lineage commitment
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—indicates sustained ribosome function in differentiating cells
SLC25A5: Mitochondrial ATP/ADP transporter—reflects elevated mitochondrial capacity supporting protein synthesis
GSTP1: Detoxification enzyme—protects translating cells from oxidative stress during differentiation
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic, nucleosomal modulator—stabilizes chromatin accessibility during monocytic commitment
HMGN1: Nucleosomal protein associated with active chromatin—permits transcription of differentiation genes
Cell composition: 35.5% GMP-Mono + 20% CD14 Mono = 55.5% committed monocytic cells vs 19% Early GMP
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression (RPS23, RPL37A by qPCR/flow) across sorted GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono vs ProMono vs mature CD14 Mono; correlate with polysome profiling or surface CD14/CD64 upregulation to confirm translational activation precedes final monocytic maturation markers.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and energy metabolism in early monocytic progenitors transitioning from GMP to ProMono stage. The enrichment of respiratory chain complex subunits (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5) alongside nuclear chromatin remodellers (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN1, HMGN2) and apoptosis regulators (PTMA, ANP32B) indicates heightened bioenergetic demand and active transcriptional remodelling characteristic of committed monopoietic differentiation.
key_evidence: MT-CO3: Cytochrome oxidase subunit; respiratory chain complex IV core component driving ATP synthesis
MT-CO2: Cytochrome c oxidase catalytic subunit; electron transport chain activity
MT-ND1: NADH dehydrogenase; complex I assembly and mitochondrial electron transport
MT-ND5: NADH dehydrogenase; NADH oxidation and respiratory chain coupling
HMGB1: Chromatin architectural protein regulating transcription; elevated in activated immune cells
HMGB2: Nucleosomal DNA binding; maintains open chromatin during transcriptional activation
HMGN1/HMGN2: Chromatin remodellers associated with active transcription and epigenetic accessibility
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic regulator; protects progenitors during lineage commitment
STMN1: Microtubule regulator and signalling integrator; high in proliferative progenitor states
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase; protein folding under metabolic stress
suggested_validation: Validate via MitoTracker staining and Seahorse mitochondrial stress assay on sorted Early GMP/Early ProMono vs Late ProMono to confirm oxidative phosphorylation dependency. Confirm monopoietic commitment by CD14/CD64 surface markers and IRF8/CEBPA qPCR. Cross-reference with independent scRNA-seq metabolic module analysis.

programme_name: MHC-II Antigen Presentation and Oxidative Defense
functional_description: This signature reflects a mature CD14 monocyte programme centered on MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation and intracellular oxidative stress management. The coordinated expression of HLA-DR, -DM, and -DP complexes with CD74 (invariant chain) establishes robust antigen presentation capacity, whilst GPX1-mediated peroxidase activity provides cytoprotection against endogenous ROS. This phenotype is consistent with tissue-resident or patrolling monocytes engaged in immune surveillance rather than acute inflammatory activation.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC-II invariant chain essential for class II loading and trafficking; hallmark of professional APCs
HLA-DRA/DRB1/DMA/DMB/DPB1: Complete HLA class II presentation machinery enabling peptide-MHC complex formation
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase catalyses H2O2 reduction; protects from ROS-induced damage during pathogen sensing
LYZ: Lysozyme bactericidal activity; constitutively high in CD14 Mono for immediate bacterial wall degradation
CST3: Cystatin C protease inhibitor; balances proteolytic activity in endolysosomal compartments
ZFP36: AU-rich element binding protein; post-transcriptional suppression of inflammatory mRNA (TNF, IL-6)
GPR183: EBI2 oxysterol receptor; involved in immune cell trafficking and positioning within lymphoid tissues
PTMA: Prothymosin-alpha; antiapoptotic factor supporting monocyte survival during antigen presentation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14/HLA-DR/CD64; confirm GPX1 activity via dihydrorhodamine oxidation assay. Single-cell RNA-seq validation of HLA-II cluster coexpression. Functional assay: measure antigen presentation capacity (OT-II T-cell proliferation) and oxidative stress resistance in sorted signature+ monocytes versus inflammatory CD14 Mono controls.

functional_description: This signature represents early-stage CD14 monocyte activation focused on calcium-dependent antimicrobial and pattern recognition functions. The dominant S100A8/A9/A6/A12 calprotectin complex drives innate immune sensing, recruitment, and myeloid differentiation, complemented by ficolin-1 (FCN1) for complement-independent bacterial opsonization and proteolytic regulation via CSTA.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9: Core calprotectin dimer (40% of top 15), hallmark of activated classical monocytes and early myeloid differentiation; calcium-binding enables antimicrobial activity and DAMPs/PAMPs sensing
S100A6/A12: Additional S100 family members amplifying calcium signalling and pro-inflammatory priming in CD14+ cells
FCN1: Ficolin pattern recognition receptor for PAMP sensing and complement-independent bacterial recognition, characteristic of classical monocyte innate immunity
MNDA: Myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen, monocyte lineage-restricted marker of active myeloid commitment
CSTA: Cystatin family cysteine protease inhibitor, regulates proteolytic environment during inflammatory activation
LGALS1: Galectin-1 autocrine negative feedback regulator, tempering excessive inflammation
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan production, ECM remodelling during monocyte recruitment and tissue infiltration
68.5% CD14 Mono + 28.5% progenitor enrichment: signature active in classical monocytes and their immediate precursors, not CD16 Mono (2.5%)
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: S100A8/A9 intracellular protein expression and surface FCN1; compare CD14++ vs CD16+ cells. Functional assays: calprotectin-mediated bacterial killing, calcium flux activation via TLR ligands. Spatial transcriptomics: track S100A8/A9 high cells in inflamed vs homeostatic bone marrow niches.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Iron Homeostasis and Antimicrobial Response
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD16-enriched monocyte state (52.5% composition) characterized by iron metabolism regulation via FTH1-mediated ferritin storage, coupled with interferon-gamma-responsive antimicrobial effector functions. The programme integrates FCGR3A-dependent ADCC capability with LST1-mediated lymphocyte regulation and polyamine catabolism (SAT1), consistent with patrolling monocyte metabolic reprogramming during systemic or localized immune surveillance.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Canonical CD16 Mono surface marker; enables antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and immune complex handling
FTH1: Top-ranked gene; ferritin heavy chain essential for intracellular iron storage in activated monocytes with high metabolic demand
CXCL16: IFN-γ-responsive chemokine; bridges innate-adaptive immunity and antimicrobial signalling in CD16 Mono
LST1: LPS/IFN-γ-inducible membrane protein with lymphocyte proliferation inhibition; marks inflammatory monocyte activation
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism rate-limiting enzyme; reflects metabolic shift supporting antimicrobial effector functions
COTL1: Actin cytoskeleton regulator and 5-lipoxygenase interactor; supports monocyte motility and lipid inflammatory mediator synthesis
CXCL16, LST1, SAT1: Convergent IFN-γ responsiveness indicates type II interferon-primed antimicrobial state
BCL2A1, BID: Apoptosis regulators consistent with activated monocyte homeostasis during immune challenge
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain FTH1 (intracellular) with CD16/FCGR3A/CX3CR1/CD14 to confirm iron-loaded CD16 Mono subset; validate IFN-γ responsiveness by stimulation experiments measuring CXCL16, LST1, SAT1 induction; functional assays: ADCC killing capacity (FCGR3A) and antimicrobial ROS/NO production in sorted FTH1-high vs FTH1-low CD16 Mono; assess iron dependency of ADCC function.

functional_description: This signature reflects the lysosomal and phagolysosomal machinery of mature monocytes, with emphasis on proteolytic antigen processing, iron homeostasis, and actin-driven phagocytosis. The 37.5% CD16 Mono contamination suggests this programme is shared across inflammatory monocyte subsets but peaks in classically-activated CD14 Mono engaged in tissue-resident immune surveillance.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and presentation; hallmark of professional APCs
CD68: Pan-monocyte/macrophage marker; saturated expression in activated myeloid cells
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for FcγR and complement receptor signalling; critical for phagocytic triggering
FCER1G: γ-chain subunit of FcγRI/III; mediates antibody-dependent cellular responses and opsonin recognition
PSAP: Saposin precursor; lysosomal lipid hydrolysis and sphingolipid catabolism in phagosomes
FCN1: Ficolin-1 pattern recognition receptor; innate immune opsonisation and complement pathway activation
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron sequestration and oxidative stress management in inflammatory monocytes
CD74: MHC-II chaperone; elevated in antigen-presenting monocytes
AIF1: Calcium-actin binding protein; macrophage activation and inflammatory response amplification
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein; supports cytoskeletal dynamics for phagocytosis and migration
COTL1: F-actin binding protein; coordinated with 5-LOX for eicosanoid signalling in inflammation
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism; metabolic reprogramming in activated immune cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14+ cells for CD68, CTSS (LysoTracker/cathepsin activity assay), and FCER1G (CD64) intensity; RNA-FISH or qPCR validation of CTSS, FCN1, and PSAP in sorted CD14 mono vs CD16 mono; functional assay of phagolysosomal capacity via fluorescent zymosan or E. coli bioparticles; assess phospho-TYROBP and FcγR signalling in stimulated populations.

functional_description: This signature represents technical artifact from erythroid cell contamination rather than a monocyte programme. Hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD, HBM) and erythroid-specific chaperones (AHSP) dominate the feature, indicating co-capture or doublet contamination with red blood cells. The modest CD14 Mono enrichment (68%) with substantial CD16 Mono (27%) representation further suggests this reflects batch effects or multiplet events rather than genuine monocyte biology.
key_evidence: HBA2/HBA1/HBB/HBD: α- and β-globin genes—hallmark of erythroid lineage, absent from normal monocyte transcriptomes
AHSP: erythroid-specific α-globin chaperone; functionally irrelevant to monocyte biology
HBM: variant globin gene with restricted erythroid expression
CTSS: cathepsin S (lysosomal protease) is monocyte-relevant but overwhelmed by hemoglobin signal
TMSB4X: actin-binding protein with low specificity; insufficient to override erythroid dominance
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain; elevated in iron-rich erythroid precursors, not characteristic of inflammatory monocytes
ATP5J2/ATP5F1/ATP5C1: mitochondrial ATP synthase subunits—metabolic housekeeping, not discriminative
27% CD16 Mono composition: unusual for a CD14 Mono-enriched signature; suggests doublet contamination
suggested_validation: Filter out hemoglobin-expressing cells (HBA/HBB/HBD >0) before re-analysis; examine for erythroid doublets via CellBender or similar doublet-removal algorithms; validate monocyte identity using established markers (CD14, SPI1, CEBPB, pro-inflammatory cytokines). This feature should be excluded from functional annotation of monocyte biology.

functional_description: This signature marks a metabolic transition in early monocytic progenitors characterised by elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP synthesis capacity. The enrichment of respiratory chain complex subunits (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-ND6) alongside MPO and stress response chaperones reflects heightened metabolic demand during GMP-to-ProMono commitment and early differentiation, supporting the biosynthetic requirements of myeloid maturation.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-ND6: Core respiratory chain complex I and IV components indicating OXPHOS activation during early monocytic commitment
MPO: Myeloperoxidase present in both GMP (31%) and Early ProMono (33.5%), validating myeloid lineage priming before terminal monocyte maturation
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator associated with cell cycle and cellular plasticity during progenitor-to-committed transition
HSP90B1, PPIA: Molecular chaperones supporting protein folding during differentiation-driven proteome remodelling
HMGB1, HMGB2, NUCKS1: Nuclear chromatin remodellers facilitating transcriptional reprogramming of lineage commitment
ATP5IF1: Mitochondrial ATP synthase inhibitor component, fine-tuning OXPHOS for differentiation state
HNRNPD, PTMA: RNA-binding and transcription factor cofactors supporting post-transcriptional control during monocytic specification
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: MPO+CD34-/low CD14-/low cells (Early GMP/ProMono) versus MPO-/low CD14+ (mature monocytes) with TMRM/JC-1 mitochondrial membrane potential and Seahorse OXPHOS profiling to confirm metabolic shift. Validate STMN1 and chaperone expression by qPCR in sorted GMP-Mono vs Early ProMono populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein abundance and translation machinery activity in CD14 monocytes and early GMP progenitors, indicating high protein synthesis capacity. The dominance of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPS26, RPL4, RPLP0) combined with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) suggests active anabolic metabolism. This represents a housekeeping biosynthetic programme rather than the inflammatory or antimicrobial effector functions characteristic of activated CD14 monocytes.
key_evidence: RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit protein, core translational machinery
RPL37A: 60S ribosomal subunit protein, core translational machinery
RPS23: 40S subunit component, abundant ribosomal protein
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor, active protein synthesis
RPLP0: Ribosomal P0 protein, 60S subunit structural component
NPM1: Nucleophosmin, cell proliferation and protein chaperoning
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein supporting mRNA processing
RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit, consistent ribosomal signature
suggested_validation: This signature lacks canonical CD14 monocyte inflammatory markers (TNF, IL1B, IL6, CCL2, TLR genes) and PAMP-sensing machinery. Validation should assess whether elevated ribosomal genes reflect proliferative progenitor activity (37.5% Early GMP) versus genuine CD14 monocyte biology. Compare ribosomal protein expression across sorted CD14 vs CD16 vs GMP subsets by qPCR; examine correlation with cell cycle markers (Ki67, MKI67) and differentiation stage.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and mitochondrial activity
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated translational capacity and oxidative metabolism characteristic of early myeloid progenitors transitioning through the GMP compartment. The coordinate upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and mitochondrial electron transport components indicates metabolically active cells preparing for rapid protein synthesis during differentiation and proliferation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPS26, RPL37A, RPL7A: multiple ribosomal protein genes (40S and 60S subunits) indicating high translational machinery abundance
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis capacity
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunits reflecting elevated oxidative phosphorylation in metabolically active progenitors
UQCRH: mitochondrial complex III component consistent with respiratory chain engagement
NPM1: nucleolar chaperone and centrosome regulator associated with proliferating and differentiating cells
HNRNPA1, HMGN1: RNA-binding and chromatin-associated proteins supporting active transcription during GMP differentiation
Early GMP dominance (56.5%) with monocytic intermediate representation (GMP-Mono 12.0%, CD14 Mono 18.5%) validates GMP-stage metabolic priming
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry sorting early GMP (CD34+KIT+) and measuring mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM) and protein synthesis rate (O-propargyl-puromycin) alongside ribosomal protein abundance by immunoblot. Cross-reference with IRF8 and CEBPE expression to confirm monocytic vs neutrophilic trajectory in the activated population.

programme_name: Translational priming in early monocyte development
functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis capacity and RNA processing machinery activation in Early GMP and immature monocytes. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPL/RPS family), translation factors (EEF1B2), and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, NPM1) indicates translational readiness during early monocytic differentiation, likely supporting rapid protein production for lineage commitment and differentiation.
key_evidence: RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS2, RPS23: Multiple large and small ribosomal subunit components indicating active translation factory assembly
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA splicing and nucleocytoplasmic transport critical for differentiation
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in centrosome duplication and protein chaperoning during cell proliferation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor (guanine nucleotide exchange factor) essential for sustained protein synthesis
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting roles in translation and RNA binding
TALDO1: Pentose phosphate pathway enzyme providing NADPH and ribose-5-phosphate for biosynthetic demands
SERPINB1: Proteinase inhibitor providing proteostasis maintenance during rapid protein synthesis
H3F3A: Histone variant associated with active chromatin and transcription during differentiation
suggested_validation: Validate by measuring translation rates (puromycin incorporation), ribosomal loading (polysome profiling), and correlate with TF activity (SPI1, CEBPA) in sorted Early GMP vs CD14 Mono populations. Confirm HNRNPA1/NPM1 involvement in early monocytic commitment through CRISPR perturbation assays. Distinguish from housekeeping baseline by comparing to non-differentiating cell types.

functional_description: This signature reflects terminal differentiation and antimicrobial activation of CD14 classical monocytes, marked by upregulation of bactericidal proteins (lysozyme, ficolin), calcium-dependent signalling (S100A8, ANXA2), and oxidative stress management. The enrichment in myeloid lineage markers (MNDA) and cytoplasmic effector molecules indicates functional commitment to phagocytosis and pathogen clearance.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical lysozyme for bacterial peptidoglycan degradation, CD14 Mono signature enzyme
S100A8: calprotectin family member marking inflammatory monocyte activation and antimicrobial responses
FCN1: ficolin innate immune pattern recognition and complement-mediated opsonization
MNDA: myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen, lineage-restricted maturation marker
GRN: secreted granulins with antimicrobial and tissue-remodelling functions in myeloid cells
ANXA2: calcium-dependent phospholipid binding supporting phagocytic membrane dynamics
GLRX: glutaredoxin for intracellular redox homoeostasis during oxidative burst
CSTA: cystatin cysteine protease inhibitor preventing autoproteolysis during antimicrobial granule release
TMSB4X: actin sequestering protein supporting migratory and phagocytic morphodynamics
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14/CD16/S100A8/LYZ with LPS stimulation; validate MNDA nuclear localisation as lineage commitment marker; assess antimicrobial function via bacterial killing assay with TLR4 agonist priming.

functional_description: This signature reflects aberrant or residual hemoglobin gene expression within activated CD14 monocytes, coupled with S100 calcium-binding proteins (S100A8/A9/A4/A6) characteristic of myeloid inflammation. The co-expression of globin chains (HBA1/HBA2/HBB/HBD), AHSP (alpha-globin chaperone), and heme catabolism genes (BLVRB) suggests either contamination from erythroid precursors or a metabolic state involving heme handling in proinflammatory monocytes.
key_evidence: HBA2, HBA1, HBB, HBD: Adult hemoglobin structural genes—unexpected in monocytes; indicates possible erythroid contamination or cross-lineage expression
AHSP: Alpha-globin-specific chaperone; functionally incompatible with monocyte differentiation; strong marker of erythroid lineage
S100A9, S100A8: Calprotectin subunits; canonical myeloid danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) in inflammatory monocytes
S100A4, S100A6: S100 family members involved in myeloid migration and calcium signaling; supportive of monocyte activation state
BLVRB: Biliverdin reductase; heme catabolism enzyme; unusual enrichment suggests heme-processing metabolism or mixed cell population
RPS26: Ribosomal protein; generic indicator of protein synthesis demand, consistent with activated monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate by: (1) flow cytometry gating to exclude CD235a+ erythroid contamination in sorted CD14 Mono; (2) single-cell RNA-seq quality control filtering for hemoglobin transcript content per cell; (3) verify S100A8/A9 protein expression by flow cytometry (canonical markers); (4) investigate whether globin genes are from ambient RNA/doublets or genuine monocyte expression under specific inflammatory conditions (e.g., hemolytic anemia models).

functional_description: This signature represents acute innate immune activation in classical CD14+ monocytes, characterized by massive upregulation of S100 alarmins (S100A8/A9/A12/A4/A6) that function as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). The program integrates myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA, FCN1) with calcium-binding proteins that regulate pro-inflammatory responses and cell migration to sites of infection or sterile inflammation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Canonical alarmin and neutrophil recruitment factor; hallmark of activated monocyte inflammasome response
S100A8: Co-expressed calprotectin component with S100A9; synergizes TLR4/RAGE signaling and amplifies IL-1β production
S100A12: S100 family member with RAGE-binding capacity; drives leukocyte recruitment and endothelial activation
MNDA: Myeloid-restricted nuclear antigen marking monocyte/granulocyte lineage commitment and terminal differentiation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (serum amyloid P-like); pattern recognition molecule for bacterial acetylated carbohydrates; bridges innate immunity
CD14: LPS/LBP co-receptor for TLR4 signaling; high expression confirms classical monocyte identity
CSTA: Cystatin A; cysteine protease inhibitor regulating cathepsin activity in inflammatory contexts
S100A4: S100 family with RAGE and TLR4 co-activation; promotes monocyte migration via CCR2
suggested_validation: Quantify S100A8/A9 protein by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry in CD14+ monocytes during bacterial infection (e.g., LPS challenge or live Gram-negative challenge); validate DAMP secretion by ELISA; correlate S100A9 surface/cytoplasmic levels with intracellular IL-1β and active caspase-1 to confirm inflammasome coupling.

functional_description: This signature reflects activation of the monocyte phagocytic and antimicrobial effector programme, centered on calcium-responsive S100 proteins and Fc-receptor signaling machinery. The prominence of S100A6, S100A4, S100A11 alongside FCER1G, TYROBP, and FCGR3A indicates coordinated engagement of pattern recognition and antibody-dependent cellular activation pathways characteristic of classical and intermediate monocytes responding to immune complexes and microbial challenge.
key_evidence: S100A6/S100A4/S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins essential for monocyte migration, cytoskeletal rearrangement, and antimicrobial responses
FCER1G: γ-chain of Fc receptors (FcγRI, FcγRIII), critical for immune complex sensing and antibody-dependent cellular responses
TYROBP: DAP12 adapter protein mediating ITAM signaling from FcγRI/FcγRIII, coupling to downstream effector activation
FCGR3A: CD16 Fc receptor for IgG, particularly enriched on intermediate (CD14++CD16+) monocytes for enhanced antibody-dependent activity
LST1: LPS-induced, IFN-γ-responsive membrane protein involved in lymphocyte regulation and bacterial sensing
CTSS: Cathepsin S for antigen processing and lysosomal proteolysis in phagocytic degradation
COTL1: Actin-binding protein supporting cytoskeletal dynamics and 5-lipoxygenase interaction for eicosanoid synthesis
TMSB4X: Thymosin-β4 for actin polymerization control during cell migration and phagocytic activity
Hemoglobin genes (HBA1/2, HBB, HBD): Likely indicate erythrophagocytic activity or iron-handling capacity in inflammatory contexts
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with surface CD14/CD16/CD64 (FCGR1A) markers combined with intracellular S100A6 and phospho-TYROBP; assess FCGR3A+ monocyte enrichment; functional assay of immune complex-driven activation (anti-IgG stimulation) and phagocytic capacity; single-cell proteomics to validate S100 protein abundances across CD14 vs CD16 subsets

functional_description: This signature reflects active cell cycle progression and nucleotide metabolism in proliferating ProMono progenitors. The enrichment of chromatin remodeling factors (HMGB1, HMGN2, H2AFZ), microtubule dynamics (STMN1, TUBB), and DNA replication/repair machinery (RPA3, DUT, RANBP1) indicates cells undergoing active division before terminal monocyte maturation. This programme is characteristic of Early ProMono cells transitioning through S/G2 phases prior to CD14 surface marker acquisition and exit from cycle.
key_evidence: STMN1: Microtubule destabilization required for mitotic progression; high in cycling progenitors
HMGB1/HMGB2/HMGN2: Chromatin accessibility and transcriptional activation during active proliferation
RPA3/DUT: DNA replication and nucleotide biosynthesis essential for S-phase
RANBP1: RanGTP-dependent nuclear transport and mitotic checkpoint control
H2AFZ: Histone variant associated with active chromatin in dividing cells
PTMA: Antiapoptotic factor protecting cycling progenitors from death
Early ProMono dominance (48%): Confirms cell-cycle-active progenitor enrichment over terminal CD14 Mono (4%)
suggested_validation: FACS-based cell cycle analysis (Ki67, PCNA, EdU incorporation) stratified by ProMono stage; co-stain for CD34/CD38/MS4A3 to confirm Early ProMono vs Late ProMono kinetics. Validate reduced STMN1/RPA3 expression in sorted CD14+ monocytes versus CD34+ progenitors.

programme_name: Monocyte metabolic and oxidative stress resilience
functional_description: This signature reflects metabolic and antioxidant programmes supporting CD14 monocyte survival and effector function during inflammatory conditions. The enrichment of GPX1, mitochondrial OXPHOS components (MT-CO3, MT-ND1, NDUFB9), and pentose phosphate pathway enzymes (TALDO1) indicates heightened metabolic demand and ROS detoxification capacity. This is consistent with activated, tissue-infiltrating classical monocytes prepared for phagocytic and antimicrobial responses.
key_evidence: GPX1: glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification; essential ROS scavenging in activated phagocytes
LYZ: lysozyme for bacterial peptidoglycan degradation; canonical CD14 Mono antimicrobial effector
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron storage; critical for heme metabolism and NADPH oxidase function
TALDO1: transaldolase for pentose phosphate pathway; supplies NADPH for NADPH oxidase (NCF complex) and biosynthesis
MT-CO3, MT-ND1, NDUFB9: mitochondrial respiratory chain; elevated OXPHOS for ATP production in metabolically active monocytes
CD63: tetraspanin marking lysosomal/granule compartments; involved in degranulation and exocytosis
ANXA2, LGALS1: phospholipid binding and cell-matrix interactions; support migration and adhesion
H3F3A, H2AFY, PTMA: chromatin remodelling and nuclear processes; enable rapid transcriptional responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain GPX1, CD14, CD64 and measure ROS (DHE/H2DCFDA) in sorted CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono. Functional assay: Seahorse OXPHOS/glycolysis in freshly isolated CD14 Mono. qPCR validation of GPX1, TALDO1, LYZ, FTH1 in FACS-sorted CD14 Mono vs progenitors.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery activity, marking a metabolically active state characteristic of Early GMP and CD14 monocytes with high biosynthetic demand. The enrichment of 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components (RPS23, RPS24, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and RNA processing machinery (HNRNPA1, SNRPE) indicates active protein synthesis rather than lineage-specific differentiation signals.
key_evidence: RPS23/RPS24/RPS2/RPL37A/RPL7A/RPL4: Core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins, predominant in rapidly synthesizing cells
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, marks active translation
HNRNPA1: Pre-mRNA binding protein regulating splicing and mRNA stability in transcriptionally active cells
NPM1: Nucleolar protein associated with ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation checkpoints
UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport component reflecting high oxidative metabolism in biosynthetically active GMP/monocytes
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase supporting glycolytic-oxidative balance in metabolically demanding progenitors
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression (RPL/RPS families, RPLP0) and translation factor activity (EEF1B2) across Early GMP vs. mature CD14 monocytes by qPCR or proteomics. Confirm elevated polysome content in Early GMP/GMP-Cycle via polysome profiling. Validate that this signature marks the biosynthetically active progenitor/early monocyte transition rather than lineage commitment per se by distinguishing from IRF8, CEBPE, or CSF1R-driven differentiation programs.

functional_description: This signature reflects the innate immune effector state of CD14 classical monocytes, characterized by abundant expression of calcium-binding S100 proteins (S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex, S100A6, S100A12, S100A4) that function as damage-associated molecular patterns and antimicrobial agents. The programme combines myeloid lineage markers (MNDA, LYZ lysozyme for bacterial cell wall degradation, FCN1 ficolin for pathogen recognition) with cytoskeletal regulators (CAPG gelsolin family actin control, CSTA cystatin protease inhibition) that support microbicidal granule mobilization and phagocytic capacity.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin complex member; canonical inflammatory monocyte marker; calcium-dependent antimicrobial activity
S100A8: Calprotectin S100A8/A9 heterodimerization; DAMP signalling; neutrophil and monocyte recruitment
MNDA: Myeloid cell-restricted nuclear differentiation antigen; lineage commitment marker for granulocyte-monocyte axis
LYZ: Lysozyme bacteriolytic enzyme; direct bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan cleavage; phagocyte antimicrobial function
FCN1: Ficolin lectin pathway activation; pathogen-associated molecular pattern recognition; complement-independent opsonisation
S100A12: Calprotectin family; RAGE ligand; amplifies inflammatory signalling in acute phase response
CAPG: Gelsolin-family actin capping protein; enables cytoplasmic-to-membrane granule translocation required for exocytosis
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein in phagocytic granules; supports antimicrobial granule trafficking and function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14+ monocytes should show high S100A8/A9 protein (calprotectin) by intracellular staining; quantify surface CD14 and assess CD16 negativity. RNA-seq on sorted CD14 vs CD16 monocytes to confirm suppression in CD16+ cells. Functional assay: measure bactericidal activity and ROS production in S100A8/A9-high vs -low sorted monocytes. Microscopy: validate CAPG-dependent granule trafficking in stimulated CD14 monocytes.

functional_description: This signature captures a proliferative early myeloid progenitor programme centred on cell cycle progression, nucleotide metabolism, and transcriptional activity. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS23, RPS24), mitochondrial function (MT-CO2, NDUFS5), and chromatin remodellers (HMGN1, HMGN2, H2AFZ) reflects active protein synthesis and transcriptional remodelling in cycling GMP populations. The co-expression of HMGB1 and PTMA suggests ongoing DNA-binding transcription factor activity and anti-apoptotic signalling characteristic of actively proliferating progenitors.
key_evidence: STMN1: Stathmin drives microtubule destabilisation during mitotic progression in cycling GMP-Cycle cells (20% composition)
HMGB1: Non-histone chromatin regulator enabling transcription factor binding and DNA organisation in proliferative progenitors
HMGN1/HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA-binding proteins marking transcriptionally active euchromatin in Early GMP (31.5%)
H2AFZ: Histone variant associated with active chromatin and transcriptional plasticity during lineage priming
RPS23/RPS24: Ribosomal protein components reflecting high translation demand in proliferating progenitors
MT-CO2/NDUFS5: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation enzymes supporting ATP production in cycling cells
TXN: Thioredoxin involved in redox regulation and protein S-nitrosylation in proliferative environments
PTMA: Nucleoside pyrophosphatase-like 1 regulating transcription factor availability and apoptosis suppression
LSM5/SNRPE: Spliceosome components enabling pre-mRNA processing during active transcription
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of HMGN1/HMGN2 with cell cycle markers (Ki67, phospho-H3) and flow cytometry sorting by STMN1/HMGB1 expression to isolate early GMP-Cycle populations for validation of proliferative versus committed monocyte transcriptomes.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte Activation and Innate Response
functional_description: This signature reflects CD16 monocyte (non-classical) activation characterized by interferon-induced antiviral immunity, iron metabolism, and pattern recognition receptor signaling. The enrichment of FCGR3A (CD16), alongside S100 calcium-binding proteins and IFITM antiviral factors, indicates a state of pathogen-associated immune surveillance distinct from classical CD14-dominant inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: defines CD16 monocytes; CD16+ subset marker with distinct Fc-receptor mediated responses
IFITM3: interferon-stimulated antiviral protein indicating type-I IFN priming typical of CD16 subset
S100A4, S100A6, S100A11: calcium-binding proteins involved in monocyte migration and immune activation
FTH1: ferritin heavy chain for iron homeostasis during immune activation and oxidative stress
COTL1: actin dynamics regulator supporting monocyte motility and transmigration
LST1: lymphocyte proliferation inhibitor upregulated by LPS and IFN-γ in activated monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor for pattern recognition receptor signaling in innate immunity
SERPINA1: protease inhibitor supporting tissue integrity during inflammation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining (CD14/CD16/FCGR3A) to confirm CD16+ enrichment; RNA-seq validation of S100 and IFITM3 expression in FACS-sorted CD16+ vs CD14+ monocytes; assess baseline IFN priming status via phospho-STAT1/p65 in CD16+ subset.

functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 monocyte specialization in antigen processing and presentation via MHC class II, coupled with iron metabolism and immune receptor signaling. The enrichment of HLA-II machinery (DR, DP, DQ, CD74) indicates active professional antigen-presenting capacity, while concurrent expression of FTH1, AIF1, and TYROBP supports phagocytic competence and calcium-responsive immune activation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA/DRB1/DPA1/DPB1/DQA1/DQB1: Complete MHC class II presentation pathway for antigen-dependent T cell activation
CD74: Essential chaperone for MHC-II α/β assembly and antigen loading in endosomal compartment
HLA-DMA: Peptide exchange factor required for optimal MHC-II peptide binding
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor supporting intracellular antigen processing and phagolysosomal function
FTH1: Iron storage and ROS detoxification during oxidative burst associated with Fc receptor engagement
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for immunoreceptor signaling (FcγRI, TLR co-receptors)
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator promoting macrophage activation and phagocytosis
FCGRT: IgG recycling and Fc region engagement supporting antibody-dependent cellular responses
PSAP: Saposin processing for lysosomal lipid antigen presentation and microbial defense
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation: Sort CD14 Mono by HLA-DR/CD74 expression levels and quantify Fc receptor (CD64/FCGR1A) co-expression; functional assays including MHC-II dependent T cell activation capacity and LPS-stimulated IL-1β/TNF secretion to confirm antigen presentation-competent inflammatory monocyte state rather than steady-state patrolling subset.

functional_description: This signature captures the transition from GMP-Mono toward committed monocytic lineages, characterized by intense ribosomal and translational machinery upregulation coupled with early myeloid differentiation markers. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2) and translation factors (PPIA, YBX1) reflects heightened protein synthesis demand during lineage commitment, while LYZ and MPO mark active monocytic priming at the promyelocyte-promonocyte interface.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2: Ribosomal 40S/60S subunit proteins indicating active translation for differentiation-associated protein synthesis
LYZ: Antimicrobial lysozyme, hallmark of committed monocyte lineage, rises steeply during GMP→ProMono transition
MPO: Myeloperoxidase present in top 15, marks early myeloid differentiation; retained in monocytic lineage despite decline in mature mono
PPIA, YBX1: Translation/RNA processing factors supporting rapid biosynthesis during commitment phase
MT-CO3, MT-CO2, GPX1: Oxidative phosphorylation and antioxidant capacity reflecting elevated metabolic demand
PTMA, HMGN1: Chromatin remodelers facilitating lineage-specific transcriptional reprogramming
TMSB4X: Actin regulation supporting cytoskeletal remodeling during morphological differentiation
GMP-Mono (44%) + Early ProMono (19.5%) comprise 63.5% of activating population, confirming GMP commitment stage
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining (CD34/CD13/CD14/CD64/MPO/LYZ) to confirm GMP-Mono→ProMono trajectory; correlate ribosomal protein expression with CD14 upregulation; RNA-seq of sorted GMP-Cycle vs GMP-Mono to distinguish proliferation from monocytic priming signals

functional_description: This signature reflects active lysosomal proteolysis and oxidative metabolism in CD14 monocytes, marked by cysteine protease CTSS and saposin processing via PSAP for antigen presentation. The prominence of ATP synthase subunits (ATP5F1, ATP5J2, ATP5B, ATP5G3) and actin-regulatory proteins (TMSB4X, COTL1) indicates metabolic priming and cytoskeletal remodelling for effector functions. Haemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB) and FCER1G/TYROBP suggest active ITAM signalling in Fc receptor and phagocytic pathways.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen degradation and monocyte antimicrobial function
PSAP: Saposin precursor processing required for lysosomal hydrolase activation and phagolysosomal maturation
ATP5F1, ATP5J2, ATP5B, ATP5G3: ATP synthase subunits indicating oxidative phosphorylation and metabolic activation
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor critical for Fc receptor (FCGR1A/CD64) and TLR signalling integration
FCER1G: Gamma chain of Fcε receptor enabling FcγR co-signalling in phagocytic response
TMSB4X, COTL1: Actin-sequestering proteins regulating cytoskeletal dynamics for migration and phagocytosis
HBA1, HBA2, HBB: Globin genes indicating haem metabolism and metabolic reprogramming in activated monocytes
S100A4: Calcium-responsive cytoplasmic protein involved in monocyte migration and inflammatory response
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with CD14, CD64 (FCGR1A), and CTSS activity assays; correlate PSAP and CTSS expression with phagocytic capacity and lysosomal mass (LysoTracker); validate TYROBP/FCER1G co-expression in CD14+CD64+ subset to confirm ITAM signalling module in classical monocytes.

functional_description: This signature reflects early ProMono metabolic activation and transcriptional licensing, characterized by chromatin-associated proteins (HMGN2, HMGB1, HMGB2) that maintain open chromatin architecture, coupled with oxidative stress management (GPX1) and translation factors (PTMA, ANP32B). The co-expression of LYZ alongside housekeeping/metabolic genes (GAPDH, MT-CO2/3, TUBB) indicates transition from GMP quiescence toward committed monocyte biosynthetic demands.
key_evidence: HMGN2: nucleosomal DNA binding in transcriptionally active chromatin—hallmark of ProMono lineage commitment initiation
LYZ: cardinal monocyte hydrolase—confirms shift from neutrophil (MPO/ELANE-low) toward mono fate
GPX1: antioxidant capacity—ProMono elevation reflects heightened metabolic activity and ROS from mitochondrial respiration
HMGB1/HMGB2: chromatin remodeling and transcription regulation—consistent with active TF binding (KLF4/IRF8 target sites)
PTMA: transcription factor cofactor and apoptosis suppression—supports survival during differentiation checkpoint
MT-CO2/MT-CO3: electron transport chain—metabolic shift toward OXPHOS-dependent monocyte energy demands
RNASE2: antimicrobial RNase—early expression of mono-specific effector function
suggested_validation: Validate by co-staining Early ProMono (CD34+CD13+CD33+MS4A3+) for HMGN2/HMGB1 nuclear localization; confirm LYZ+/MPO−/ELANE− profile; assess GPX1 activity via ROS flow cytometry; measure KLF4/IRF8 ChIP-seq enrichment at HMGN2, LYZ, and RNASE2 promoters in sorted Early ProMono vs GMP.

programme_name: Classical monocyte damage-associated molecular pattern response
functional_description: This signature reflects the innate immune effector state of CD14+ classical monocytes (89% of top activators), characterized by abundant calcium-binding S100 proteins (S100A8/A9/A12/A6/A4) that function as danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), extracellular matrix remodeling (VCAN), and metabolic/enzymatic activity supporting pro-inflammatory responses. The dominance of S100 family members indicates activated, recently-recruited monocytes engaged in tissue inflammation and neutrophil recruitment.
key_evidence: S100A9: Top-ranked calprotectin component; NETosis trigger and monocyte recruitment signal in inflammation
S100A8: Co-component with S100A9 of calprotectin (MRP8/14); TLR4 ligand driving pro-inflammatory activation
S100A12: DAMP/RAGE ligand; marker of activated myeloid cells in acute inflammation
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein expressed during monocyte activation and differentiation
S100A4: Pro-inflammatory S100 family member; involved in migration and inflammatory responses
LGALS1: Galectin-1; immunomodulatory role in monocyte/macrophage function and cell-cell interactions
CD36: Scavenger receptor for apoptotic cells and thrombospondin; key to efferocytosis and anti-inflammatory signaling
VCAN: Extracellular matrix proteoglycan; indicates tissue remodeling during inflammatory infiltration
CAST: Calpain inhibitor; regulates protease activity during activation
CES1: Carboxylesterase; metabolic enzyme supporting activated monocyte phenotype
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of S100A8/A9 co-expression with CD14, CCR2, and CD64 in bone marrow and peripheral blood monocytes; correlate S100 protein abundance with inflammatory markers (CRP, TNF-α, IL-6) in clinical samples; perform spatial transcriptomics to confirm co-localization with active inflammatory lesions.

functional_description: This signature represents a translational programme dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS26, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), with contaminating hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB) likely reflecting co-sorting of erythroid or progenitor-derived material. The high enrichment in Early GMP (38.5%) and moderate CD14 Mono representation (46%) suggests this captures proliferative, protein synthesis-active myeloid progenitors rather than mature monocyte effector functions.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: 40S/60S ribosomal subunit structural proteins indicating active translation machinery
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: large ribosomal subunit components
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor (GEF function)
HNRNPA1, GAPDH: RNA-binding and glycolytic proteins supporting biosynthesis
HBA1, HBA2, HBB: erythroid contamination or progenitor-derived signature
Early GMP enrichment (38.5%): progenitor-biased, not mature monocyte inflammatory signature
suggested_validation: This signature deviates markedly from canonical CD14 monocyte inflammatory/effector programmes (absent: TLR2/4/5, IL1B, TNF, IL6, CCL2, FCGR1A). Validate by: (1) confirming Early GMP contamination in top-200 activating cells via flow cytometry; (2) assessing ribosomal protein expression correlation with Ki67/proliferation markers; (3) excluding hemoglobin genes and re-testing if CD14 Mono signal remains coherent or collapses. If robust in purified CD14 Mono, may indicate translation-dependent activation state distinct from canonical inflammation.

functional_description: This signature represents aberrant expression of hemoglobin genes and erythroid-associated factors in what should be myeloid progenitor populations. The dominant hemoglobin subunits (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) and hemoglobin assembly chaperone (AHSP) indicate either erythroid lineage contamination, erythroid-myeloid hybrid cells, or technical artifacts in the scRNA-seq dataset. Ribosomal proteins and metabolic genes are secondary housekeeping signals without lineage specificity.
key_evidence: HBA2: Alpha-globin chain component of hemoglobin; highly erythroid-specific, inappropriate in GMP
HBB: Beta-globin chain; core adult hemoglobin structural protein; definitive erythroid marker
HBA1: Second alpha-globin locus; reinforces erythroid lineage identity
HBD: Delta-globin in fetal/minor hemoglobin variants; erythroid-restricted expression
AHSP: Hemoglobin assembly chaperone specific to erythroid differentiation
RPS26, RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPL37A: Ribosomal proteins; housekeeping genes without discriminatory power
CA1: Carbonic anhydrase abundant in mature RBCs; erythroid enrichment
ATP5J2, ATP5G3: Oxidative phosphorylation; secondary housekeeping markers
suggested_validation: Perform flow cytometry gating on CD14+CD16- monocytes and Early GMP with hemoglobin staining (anti-HbA, anti-HbF) to quantify erythroid contamination rates. Re-evaluate SAE training data for RBC contamination in bone marrow mononuclear cell preparations. Consider whether sorting strategy or sample processing introduced cross-lineage doublets or erythroid-myeloid hybrid cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects active monocyte granule biogenesis and lysosomal protease activity, enriched in classical CD14 monocytes (70.5%). The coordinated expression of S100 calcium-binding proteins, tetraspanins (CD63), cysteine proteases, and their inhibitors (cystatins) indicates preparation for phagocytic and antimicrobial effector functions. The signature bridges innate immune granule release with intracellular proteolytic regulation.
key_evidence: S100A8/S100A9: Canonical monocyte danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and calprotectin components; hallmark of activated CD14 monocytes
S100A6/S100A4: Calcium-sensor proteins regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and granule mobilization during phagocytosis
CD63: Tetraspanin on secretory lysosomes; marker of granule exocytosis and antimicrobial degranulation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 (collagen-like lectin); innate immune pattern recognition and opsonisation in monocytes
GRN: Granulin precursor; secreted monocyte protease with inflammatory and tissue-remodelling properties
CSTA/CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitors; modulate elastase and cathepsin activity in granules
TYROBP: DAP12 signalling adaptor coupling Fc-receptors and TLRs to calcium mobilisation and degranulation
FCER1G: Fc-receptor gamma chain for phagocytic signalling amplification
CD74: MHC-II chaperone; antigen presentation competence of CD14 monocytes
GPX1: Antioxidant defence against ROS generated during phagocytosis
ANXA2: Calcium-regulated phospholipid binding; mediates vesicle trafficking and granule exocytosis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+/S100A8+/CD63+ to confirm active monocyte granule mobilisation state; quantify secretion of calprotectin (S100A8/A9 heterodimer) and GRN in LPS/TNFα-stimulated CD14 monocytes; correlate with TYROBP/FCER1G phosphorylation as proxy for Fc-receptor activation state.

functional_description: This signature reflects activated monocyte lysosomal and phagosomal function, characterized by iron storage, cysteine protease inhibition, and actin cytoskeleton remodeling. The dominance of FCER1G, TYROBP, and lysosomal proteases (CST3, PSAP) alongside iron homeostasis (FTH1) suggests cells primed for enhanced phagocytosis and intracellular antigen processing rather than canonical inflammatory cytokine production.
key_evidence: FCER1G: ITAM-bearing Fc receptor gamma chain essential for phagocytic receptor clustering and TYROBP signaling in activated monocytes
TYROBP: ITAM adaptor enabling FcγR and TLR cross-talk for amplified phagocytic and antimicrobial responses
FTH1: Heavy-chain ferritin upregulation indicates iron sequestration during activated phagocytic state and oxidative stress resistance
CST3: Cystatin-family cysteine protease inhibitor regulating phagosomal proteolysis and antigen presentation
PSAP: Saposin precursor involved in lysosomal lipid metabolism and antimicrobial peptide function
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin-regulatory protein induced by IFN-γ and cytokines; promotes macrophage activation
COTL1: Actin-binding protein and 5-LOX interactor supporting cytoskeletal remodeling in phagocytosis
IFITM3: Interferon-induced antiviral transmembrane protein reflecting Type-I IFN priming
LST1: LPS- and IFN-γ-responsive membrane protein regulating lymphocyte proliferation and immune licensing
UCP2: Mitochondrial uncoupling protein modulating ROS and metabolic flexibility in activated immune cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD14+ monocytes for FCER1G, TYROBP, and CD64 surface expression combined with LysoTracker staining to quantify lysosomal activation. RNA FISH or qPCR validation of FTH1 and CST3 in sorted CD14+ vs CD16+ subsets. Functional assays: phagocytosis capacity (opsonized E. coli), intracellular iron levels (ferrozine assay), and phagosomal proteolytic activity in activated vs resting monocytes.

programme_name: Early ProMono chromatin remodelling and activation
functional_description: This signature reflects transcriptional activation and chromatin accessibility programmes characteristic of Early ProMono progenitors undergoing monocytic commitment. The dominance of HMG-box proteins (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2) and histone variants (H2AFZ, H1FX) indicates active chromatin remodelling, while inclusion of LYZ and EGR1 marks onset of monocytic gene expression and immediate-early transcriptional responses.
key_evidence: HMGB2: Chromatin-associated protein enriched in transcriptionally active regions during ProMono transition
HMGB1: Non-histone DNA-binding protein regulating transcription during lineage commitment
HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA binder associated with open chromatin; facilitates accessibility
LYZ: Lysozyme; canonical monocyte/macrophage differentiation marker, low in GMP
EGR1: Immediate-early transcription factor driving proliferative response in Early ProMono
H2AFZ: Histone variant marking active promoters; chromatin remodelling signature
JUN: AP-1 component; early activation marker during myeloid commitment
PCLAF: S-phase protein; reflects cycling state of Early vs Late ProMono
UBE2C: E2 ubiquitin conjugase; supports protein turnover during active differentiation
NUCKS1: Nuclear protein with phosphorylation sites; chromatin remodelling regulator
suggested_validation: Co-stain Early ProMono (CD34+CD133+CSF1R+) for HMGB1/HMGB2 nuclear localization; ATAC-seq on sorted Early ProMono vs GMP to confirm chromatin accessibility at LYZ/CSF1R loci; RNA velocity analysis to validate directionality toward Late ProMono/CD14 Mono trajectory

programme_name: Basal protein synthesis and nucleolar biogenesis
functional_description: This signature captures constitutive ribosomal protein (RPS/RPL genes, RPLP0) and nucleolar functions (NPM1, HMGN1) with proteostasis support (HSP90AB1, TXN). The enrichment in Early GMP (37.5%) and CD14 Mono (19.5%) reflects high translational demand during myeloid differentiation, independent of lineage commitment or cell cycle phase.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal structural components; universally expressed housekeeping
NPM1: nucleolar protein involved in ribosome assembly and protein chaperoning; marks proliferative and protein-synthetic capacity
HNRNPA1: pre-mRNA processing cofactor; supports high translational demand
HSP90AB1, TXN: proteostasis chaperones; enable protein folding during active synthesis
HMGN1: chromatin architectural protein marking transcriptionally active loci; supports ribosomal gene expression
PTMA: apoptosis suppression and TF binding; prosurvival signal in progenitors
Early GMP dominance (37.5%): immature progenitors exhibit highest absolute ribosomal biogenesis
