suggested_validation: Validate as ribosomal biogenesis/housekeeping signature by: (1) confirm equal expression across CD14 vs CD16 monocyte subsets (no lineage specificity); (2) verify orthogonal enrichment in G1/S-phase cells via cell-cycle scoring; (3) compare against known GMP cell-cycle markers (MKI67, CDK1) to disambiguate from GMP-Cycle signature; (4) FACS sort Early GMP and ProMono and confirm RPS2/NPM1 protein levels by flow cytometry.

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive cellular housekeeping and bioenergetic processes rather than pro-inflammatory or antimicrobial specialization. The predominance of glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, PKM), chromatin-associated proteins (HMGN2, HMGB2, H2AFZ), mitochondrial electron transport components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3), and general protein synthesis machinery (TUBA1B, PPIA) indicates active baseline metabolism and nuclear organization in transitioning monocytic precursors and early CD14 monocytes.
key_evidence: GAPDH: Central glycolytic enzyme; marks metabolically active cells
PKM: Pyruvate kinase; glycolytic ATP generation in differentiating cells
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Oxidative phosphorylation; energy-demanding differentiation process
HMGN2, HMGB2: Chromatin remodeling during lineage commitment; not inflammatory
LYZ: Antimicrobial effector; present in mature monocytes but not signature of activation
PTMA: Nuclear protein involved in anti-apoptosis; survival during differentiation
GSTP1: Detoxification; metabolic housekeeping, not inflammatory response
TUBA1B: Cytoskeletal organization; basic cellular infrastructure
suggested_validation: Compare with sorted CD14 Mono activated by LPS/TNF (should show lower expression of this signature) and with resting bone marrow monocytic progenitors (should show similar or higher expression). Validate that this signature is absent in CD16 Mono and enriched in early differentiation stages.

functional_description: This signature captures a metabolically active, protein synthesis-dominant state marked by elevated ribosomal proteins (RPS26, RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0) and hemoglobin genes (HBA2, HBA1, HBB, HBD). The enrichment reflects high translational capacity and residual erythroid gene expression, likely representing early myeloid progenitors (31.5% Early GMP) with ongoing ribosome biogenesis rather than classical monocyte inflammatory programming.
key_evidence: HBA2/HBA1/HBB/HBD: Hemoglobin cluster genes indicate residual erythroid lineage priming in early myeloid progenitors
RPS26/RPS24/RPS17/RPS23/RPL37A/RPL7A/RPLP0: Coordinated ribosomal protein upregulation reflects active protein synthesis machinery
GAPDH/HNRNPA1/EEF1B2: Glycolysis and translation elongation factors support anabolic metabolism
Early GMP enrichment (31.5%): Signature driven by progenitor-pool rather than mature CD14 Mono (50.0%), indicating differentiation-stage rather than activation status
ANOVA rank 471: Moderate discriminatory power, consistent with housekeeping/metabolic rather than lineage-defining signals
suggested_validation: This is a progenitor maturation signature rather than a monocyte functional program. Validate via: (1) flow cytometry confirming Early GMP enrichment within SAE activation; (2) RNA-FISH for HBA2/RPL37A co-expression in CD34+ progenitors vs mature CD14 Mono; (3) ribosome profiling to confirm translation rate differences; (4) absence of classical monocyte markers (IRF5, TNF, IL1B, CCR2) confirms this is not inflammatory activation but rather biomass accumulation during myeloid commitment.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and translation elongation
functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal and translation machinery components (40S/60S subunits via RPL37A, RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPL4; elongation factors via EEF1B2) coupled with glycolytic metabolic support (GAPDH, LDHB). The enrichment pattern suggests active protein synthesis capacity in CD14 monocytes and committed granulomonocytic progenitors during their rapid differentiation and effector function preparation.
key_evidence: RPL37A, RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPL4: core 40S/60S ribosomal structural proteins indicating elevated translation machinery
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor GEF activity supporting active protein synthesis
GAPDH, LDHB: glycolytic enzymes providing ATP and NADH for anabolic synthesis and energy metabolism
UQCRH: mitochondrial Complex III component indicating oxidative phosphorylation support for protein synthesis energy demand
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating pre-mRNA splicing and stability of inflammatory transcripts
Cell composition: 45% CD14 Mono + 38.5% Early GMP suggests signature captures rapid translational activity in monocyte lineage commitment
suggested_validation: Validate via ribosome profiling or polysome-associated mRNA analysis in FACS-sorted CD14 monocytes vs. CD16 monocytes and GMPs. Assess translation rate via Click-iT pulse-chase labeling (e.g., O-propargyl puromycin incorporation). Cross-reference with metabolomics to confirm glycolytic/OXPHOS coupling. Note: signature lacks canonical monocyte inflammatory markers (TNF, IL1B, TLR signaling), indicating this programme reflects basal translational capacity rather than activation state.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and translational machinery activation characteristic of GMP-Mono and Early GMP populations transitioning toward monocytic commitment. The dominance of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0) coupled with translation factors (EEF1B2, PPIA) and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism (UQCRH) indicates heightened protein synthesis capacity required for monocytic differentiation. Supporting factors include chromatin remodelling (HMGN1), oxidative stress management (GSTP1), and apoptotic regulation (PTMA), reflecting the biosynthetic and metabolic demands of early lineage commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPLP0: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins—elevated translation rates during commitment
EEF1B2, PPIA: Translation elongation and proline isomerization—protein folding capacity for monocytic differentiation
UQCRH: Mitochondrial electron transport—metabolic support for biosynthetically active progenitors
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic function and TF binding—survival signal during lineage commitment transition
HMGN1: Nucleosomal remodelling—transcriptional plasticity during GMP-to-monocyte transition
GSTP1: Oxidative stress detoxification—cellular protection during metabolic reprogramming
GMP-Mono 32.5% + Early GMP 23.0%: Clear GMP enrichment; CD14 Mono 22.0% confirms signal persists in early committed monocytes but declines in mature CD16 Mono (3.5%)
suggested_validation: Verify ribosomal protein and translation factor elevation by flow cytometry (anti-RPS24, anti-EEF1B2) in sorted GMP-Mono vs Early ProMono/CD14 Mono populations. Assess functional dependency via puromycin incorporation assay or polysome profiling in GMP subsets. Cross-reference with protein synthesis rate measurements (e.g. pulse-chase) to confirm translation capacity distinguishes GMP-Mono from more differentiated monocyte stages.

functional_description: This signature defines pro-inflammatory CD14 classical monocytes with enhanced pattern recognition, iron metabolism, and tissue-damaging effector capacity. The programme is characterized by TREM1-mediated innate immune activation, DAMPs/PAMPs sensing (C5AR1, CLEC7A, CLEC4E), and metabolic reprogramming (FTH1, NAMPT) supporting sustained inflammatory responses.
key_evidence: TREM1: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1; amplifies TLR/NLRP3 inflammatory signalling in classical monocytes and drives pro-inflammatory cytokine production
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage and sequestration supporting ROS generation and redox-dependent metabolic rewiring in activated monocytes
S100A12: Calcium-binding alarmin; DAMP-associated molecule released by activated monocytes, amplifies TLR4 signalling and attracts immune cells
VCAN: Versican proteoglycan; ECM remodelling and migration support; upregulated in inflammatory monocyte subsets
C5AR1: Complement C5a receptor; ligand-induced chemotaxis and activation of classical monocytes towards inflammation sites
CLEC7A: Dectin-1; fungal PAMP recognition receptor driving inflammatory monocyte activation and IL-1β/TNF production
CLEC4E: Mincle; glycolipid antigen recognition; synergises with TLR in monocyte inflammatory responses
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis; metabolic fuel for inflammatory macrophage differentiation and sustained immune activation
FOLR3: Folate receptor-γ; high in activated immune cells; supports one-carbon metabolism in proliferative inflammatory states
THBS1: Thrombospondin-1; endogenous danger signal and TLRs ligand promoting monocyte activation and ECM remodelling
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-gating TREM1+S100A12+ on CD14++CD16− monocytes; RT-qPCR confirmation of TREM1, S100A12, VCAN in FAC-sorted CD14 Mono versus CD16 Mono; functional assays: C5a/LPS stimulation measuring NF-κB activation and IL-1β/TNF secretion; iron metabolism assessment via FTH1 expression correlating with ROS production (DCFDA assay).

functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis machinery, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (RPS/RPL families), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar processing components (FBL, NPM1). The enrichment in Early GMP (33.5%) and CD14 Mono (40.5%) indicates heightened translational demand during myeloid differentiation and monocyte maturation, supporting anabolic biosynthesis required for cell expansion and functional protein acquisition.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins—constitutive high expression supports active translation in proliferative progenitors and differentiating monocytes
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor mediating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery; elevated in metabolically active myeloid cells undergoing rapid protein synthesis
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting roles in translation/RNA binding; marks metabolically engaged cells with high biosynthetic demand
NPM1: Nucleolar phosphoprotein regulating ribosome biogenesis and cell proliferation; consistent with GMP-stage active cycling (Early GMP 33.5%)
FBL: Nucleolar fibrillarin involved in pre-rRNA processing; required for ribosome assembly in cells with elevated translational capacity
UQCRH, LDHB: OXPHOS/glycolytic proteins supporting energy demand of protein synthesis machinery
suggested_validation: Cross-reference with polysome profiling or ribosome occupancy data (Ribo-seq) in sorted Early GMP vs. Late ProMono to confirm elevated translation rates. Compare with lineage-specific translational control markers (e.g., PABPC1, eIF4E) to distinguish monocytic vs. granulocytic biosynthetic priorities. Verify enrichment in S/G2-M phase GMP-Cycle cells (20% of signature) using cell-cycle regression.

functional_description: This signature is dominated by hemoglobin subunit genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) and ribosomal proteins, indicating contamination from erythroid progenitors or stressed immature red blood cells rather than a genuine monocyte programme. The presence of FOSB suggests some inflammatory signal, but the overwhelming hemoglobin burden and absence of canonical monocyte effector genes (TLR2, TLR4, IL1B, TNF, NCF genes, NADPH oxidase components) argues against authentic CD14 monocyte activation.
key_evidence: HBA1/HBA2/HBB/HBD: constitute 4 of top 5 genes; hallmark of erythroid lineage, not monocytes
RPS26: ribosomal protein suggests ribosome biogenesis/translation stress; atypical for monocyte programs
TYROBP: ITAM adaptor present but insufficient alone to define inflammatory monocyte phenotype
CTSS: cathepsin S is a lysosomal protease expressed across myeloid cells but not signature-defining
S100A12: calcium-binding protein with some inflammation association but weak support without pro-cytokine context
ABSENCE of TLR2, TLR4, IL1B, TNF, NLRP3, FCGR1A, NCF genes: critical monocyte effectors entirely absent
FOSB: immediate-early gene; generic stress response, not monocyte-specific
suggested_validation: This feature likely represents batch effect or doublet/multiplet contamination with erythroid progenitors. Recommend: (1) inspect original scVI latent space for erythroid cluster mixing; (2) validate by flow cytometry excluding CD45+CD71+ cells; (3) confirm CD14 Mono purity (80.5%) was assessed post-filtering for hemoglobin-high outliers; (4) re-train SAE with erythroid masking if BoneMarrowMap includes substantial erythroid representation.

functional_description: This signature reflects Early ProMono cells establishing oxidative metabolic capacity and biosynthetic machinery concurrent with early monocyte commitment. The dominance of mitochondrial oxidoreductases (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1), nucleosome remodeling proteins (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2), and LYZ expression indicates a population transitioning from GMP quiescence into active metabolic commitment while initiating antimicrobial effector programmes.
key_evidence: LYZ: canonical monocyte antimicrobial marker, present in Early ProMono and CD14 Mono
MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1: respiratory chain complex assembly genes indicating heightened oxidative metabolism required for monocyte differentiation
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2: chromatin remodeling and transcription regulation supporting active differentiation programme
PTMA: apoptosis suppression consistent with committed progenitor survival
RNASE2: antimicrobial ribonuclease reflecting mono effector maturation
TUBA1B, TUBB: cytoskeletal organization supporting cytoplasmic expansion during commitment
suggested_validation: Validate by (1) flow cytometry confirming co-expression of LYZ, MS4A3, and CSF1R on ANOVA-top 200 cells to confirm Early ProMono identity; (2) Seahorse metabolic profiling showing elevated OXPHOS in sorted LYZ+ MS4A3+ progenitors vs GMP; (3) Confirm absence of MPO and ELANE to exclude GMP-Neutrophil contamination; (4) qPCR for IRF8 and KLF4 as ProMono-committed transcription factors.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened protein synthesis machinery and ER/mitochondrial proteostasis, with concurrent activation of ribosomal proteins, histone chaperones, and heat shock proteins. The programme is prominently expressed across developmental stages from GMP-Mono through CD14 Mono, suggesting it supports biosynthetic demands during monocyte maturation and antimicrobial differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24: Ribosomal protein indicating active translation capacity
HSP90B1: ER-resident chaperone mediating protein folding under ER stress
HMGN2: Nucleosome-associated protein maintaining transcriptional accessibility for ribosomal genes
HMGB1/HMGB2: Non-histone chromatin regulators facilitating transcription of biosynthetic genes
UQCRH: Mitochondrial respiratory chain component supporting oxidative phosphorylation for protein synthesis
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic regulator stabilising cells under biosynthetic stress
MPO: Antimicrobial peroxidase consistent with monocyte differentiation
LYZ: Lysozyme reflecting functional monocyte maturation
STMN1: Microtubule dynamics regulator supporting cell division in progenitor pool (8.5% GMP-Cycle)
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring ribosomal protein S6 phosphorylation and HSP90 levels across CD14 vs CD16 Mono; confirm ER stress markers (XBP1s, ATF4) via qPCR; assess mitochondrial mass/OXPHOS capacity using MitoTracker/Seahorse in GMP-Mono vs mature monocytes

functional_description: This signature reflects monocyte specialization in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation coupled with lysosomal cathepsin activity for proteolytic processing of antigenic peptides. The enrichment of HLA-DR, HLA-DP molecules, CD74 (invariant chain), and CTSS (cathepsin S) indicates activated antigen-presenting capacity. Iron homeostasis via FTH1 and calcium signaling through S100 proteins support metabolic demands of professional APCs engaged in immune surveillance.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: HLA class II α-chain core component for peptide presentation
HLA-DRB1: HLA class II β-chain; constitutively expressed on classical monocytes
HLA-DPB1: HLA class II β-chain; broadens peptide repertoire presented
CD74: Invariant chain chaperoning HLA-II assembly and trafficking
CTSS: Lysosomal cathepsin S; proteolytically processes antigenic proteins for peptide generation
FCER1G: FcγRI γ-chain (CD16a component); links Fcγ receptor signaling to antigen uptake
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor; couples FCGR1A to downstream signaling in phagocytic APCs
CST3: Cysteine protease inhibitor; regulates cathepsin activity and antigen processing kinetics
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage supporting metabolic demands of antigen processing
S100A6, S100A4, S100A11: Calcium-binding proteins; regulate actin dynamics and cell trafficking during antigen uptake
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14+ monocytes for HLA-DR, CD74, CTSS (intracellular), and FCGR1A; compare antigen presentation capacity via FITC-dextran or opsonized E. coli phagocytosis assay between CD14 and CD16 monocyte subsets; quantify lysosomal cathepsin activity using activity-based probes or Z-VAD-fmk inhibition in subset-specific sorted populations.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein expression and antigen presentation machinery in CD14 monocytes, coupled with oxidative stress management via glutathione peroxidase. The dominance of ribosomal components (RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0) indicates high translational capacity, while MPO and GPX1 suggest active antimicrobial oxidative metabolism characteristic of classical inflammatory monocytes.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: Coordinate ribosomal protein expression supporting high protein synthesis rate
CD74: MHC class II antigen presentation pathway activation, typical of CD14 monocytes
MPO: Myeloperoxidase-dependent ROS generation for microbial killing and inflammatory responses
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for detoxification of H2O2, balancing pro-inflammatory oxidative stress
TMSB4X: Actin dynamics supporting monocyte migration and phagocytic activity
UQCRH: Mitochondrial respiration supporting energy demands of metabolically active monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CD14+ monocytes for MPO, CD74 surface expression, and intracellular ROS production; RNAseq on sorted CD14 vs CD16 monocytes to confirm monocyte subset specificity; functional assay of phagocytic capacity and oxidative burst in high-expressing cells

programme_name: CD14 Monocyte Iron Homeostasis and Antigen Processing
functional_description: This signature reflects a CD14 monocyte population engaged in iron metabolism and MHC class II antigen presentation. The dominance of hemoglobin genes (HBA2, HBA1, HBB) and ferritin heavy chain (FTH1) suggests active iron scavenging from heme catabolism, coupled with robust lysosomal proteolytic capacity (CTSS, CST3) for antigen processing. Co-expression of KLF4 (master TF for M1/inflammatory macrophages) with HLA-DRA and CD74 indicates classical monocytes poised for immunogenic antigen presentation.
key_evidence: HBA2, HBA1, HBB: Hemoglobin chain genes indicating heme-iron salvage capacity characteristic of CD14 mono in inflammatory/phagocytic state
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain essential for iron detoxification and storage in monocytes exposed to hemolytic inflammation
KLF4: Master transcription factor for inflammatory M1 polarization; marks classical CD14 monocyte activation state
HLA-DRA, CD74, CTSS: Antigen presentation machinery (MHC class II loading, chaperone, cysteine protease) for immunogenic responses
FOSB, ZFP36: Early immediate genes and mRNA stability regulators typical of activated inflammatory monocytes
COTL1: Actin-binding protein supporting cytoskeletal dynamics for phagocytosis and migration
RPS26: Ribosomal protein consistent with high protein synthesis demand in activated CD14 mono
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain CD14++CCR2+KLF4+ cells and assess FTH1/ferritin protein levels; Functional assay: measure phagocytic capacity and heme-induced iron uptake in sorted CD14 mono from this SAE feature versus CD16 mono (low ferritin); RNA-seq validation of KLF4, HLA-DRA, CTSS coordinate expression in inflammatory CD14 subsets.

functional_description: This signature represents constitutive cellular machinery for protein synthesis and glycolytic metabolism, with no monocyte-specific inflammatory or immune effector function. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0), translation factors (EEF1B2), and metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, LDHB) indicates a programme driven by basal translational capacity rather than monocyte activation or differentiation state.
key_evidence: GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme; present in all cell types; not monocyte-specific
RPS24, RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Core 40S/60S ribosomal subunits; housekeeping translation machinery
EEF1B2: Elongation factor for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery; basal translation initiation
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase; glycolytic NAD+ recycling; metabolic baseline
ACTG1: Cytoskeletal actin; structural maintenance absent monocyte-specific context
NPM1: Nucleolar protein and general cell cycle regulator; not CD14 Mono inflammation marker
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein; general mRNA processing; lacks monocyte differentiation specificity
Absence of: SPI1, CEBPB, IRF5, TLR2, TLR4, CD14, IL1B, TNF, CCL2, NLRP3, NCF1—all cardinal CD14 Mono markers
suggested_validation: This is a technical artifact or noise signature. Validate by: (1) confirming no cell-type-specific enrichment of monocyte markers (CD14, SPI1, CEBPB, CCL2, TNF, IL1B); (2) comparing to housekeeping gene reference sets (HK genes should cluster separately); (3) examining if signal is driven by high-quality cells with active translation or by low-quality/dying cells; (4) correlating with ribosomal protein expression burden across all BoneMarrowMap cell types to assess generality.

functional_description: This signature reflects cytoplasmic antimicrobial and calcium-signaling capacity characteristic of Early ProMono transitioning toward functional monocytes. The dominance of S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex, LYZ lysozyme, and RNASE2 represents the assembly of innate immune effector molecules. Supporting nucleosome remodeling (HMGN2, HMGB2/3) and actin dynamics (CAPG, TMSB4X) enable cellular maturation and motility in committed monocyte progenitors.
key_evidence: S100A9/S100A8: Core calprotectin complex, Ca2+-binding antimicrobial effectors central to monocyte innate immunity
LYZ: Canonical monocyte lysozyme for bacterial peptidoglycan degradation; strong ProMono commitment marker
RNASE2: Non-secretory ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity; acquired during monocyte differentiation
LGALS1: Galectin-1 involved in monocyte adhesion and autocrine growth modulation during commitment
S100A6: Calgranulin C, additional S100 family antimicrobial cofactor in early monocytes
HMGN2/HMGB2/HMGB3: Chromatin architecture remodeling supporting transcriptional changes in monocyte commitment
CAPG/TMSB4X: Actin-regulatory proteins enabling cytoskeletal reorganization and pre-egress motility
GPX1: Oxidative stress management required during monocyte terminal differentiation
suggested_validation: Co-expression validation of S100A8/A9 with LYZ and RNASE2 in flow cytometry (CD34+ CD38+ CD45RA- MS4A3+ cells); confirm Early ProMono dominance (49.5%) and intermediate CD14 Mono expression (38%); spatial transcriptomics to localize to ProMono zone in bone marrow; assess S100A9 intensity as maturation gradient marker distinct from GMP (which retain MPO/ELANE).

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened ribosomal protein synthesis machinery and mitochondrial energy metabolism, characteristic of metabolically active progenitors transitioning through monocytic differentiation. The enrichment of ribosomal structural components (RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPL4, RPLP0, RPL37A) coupled with mitochondrial electron transport (MT-CO2, SLC25A5) and translation factors (EEF1B2) indicates cells with elevated anabolic demand and bioenergetic capacity.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPL4, RPLP0, RPL37A: core ribosomal proteins enabling rapid protein synthesis in proliferative/differentiating progenitors
MT-CO2, SLC25A5: mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP/ADP exchange supporting energetic demands of early myeloid differentiation
YBX1: cold-shock domain RNA-binding protein regulating translation and mRNA stability during stress/differentiation
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor facilitating aminoacyl-tRNA delivery, marking active translation state
NPM1: nucleolar protein involved in ribosome biogenesis and centrosome function, elevated in proliferating progenitors
HSP90AB1, TXN: molecular chaperones and redox regulators supporting protein folding during terminal differentiation
HNRNPA1: mRNA-binding protein controlling splicing and stability of myeloid lineage-specific transcripts
suggested_validation: Compare ribosomal protein expression (RPLP0, RPS2) and mitochondrial genes (MT-CO2) across sorted Early GMP vs CD14/CD16 monocytes via qPCR or Western blot. Cross-validate with proliferation markers (MKI67, PCNA) to distinguish between cell-cycle-dependent vs differentiation-driven translational upregulation. Assess whether signature correlates with functional assays of protein synthesis rate or ATP production in purified populations.

functional_description: This signature captures CD14+ classical monocytes executing acute inflammatory and antimicrobial defence responses. Dominated by S100 calprotectin components (S100A8/A9 heterodimer) and associated damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), alongside iron homeostasis and phagocytic machinery, indicating activated innate immune effector cells responding to bacterial PAMPs and tissue damage.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin heavy chain, released by activated monocytes during PAMP/DAMP sensing and bacterial infection
S100A8: Calprotectin light chain, forms S100A8/A9 complex with antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory properties
S100A6: Calcium-binding protein upregulated during monocyte activation and inflammation
S100A12: DAMP released by activated myeloid cells, binds RAGE and TLR4 to amplify inflammation
FCN1: Ficolin-1 pattern recognition receptor expressed on classical monocytes, binds acetylated PAMPs
CD14: LPS co-receptor and master monocyte lineage marker, enriched 95.5% in activating CD14 Mono population
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain, iron sequestration during pro-inflammatory monocyte activation
CD36: Scavenger receptor for apoptotic cells and thrombospondin, phagocytic function
PLAUR: Urokinase plasminogen activator receptor, promotes monocyte extravasation and inflammation
MAFB: MAF basic leucine zipper transcription factor, involved in monocyte maturation and polarization
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis enzyme supporting metabolic demands during acute immune activation
CSTA: Cystatin A, cysteine protease inhibitor modulating immune cell proteolysis
VCAN: Versican, extracellular matrix component involved in monocyte-endothelial interaction
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for S100A8/A9 (calprotectin) with CD14 and inflammatory markers (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β intracellular staining) on BM CD14 Mono; quantify by CyTOF or mass cytometry; validate DAMP-mediated activation by stimulating sorted CD14 Mono with LPS or S100A12 ligand and measuring signature upregulation

functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14+ classical monocytes engaging innate immune responses through pattern recognition and inflammatory effector functions. The gene set combines interferon-stimulated genes (IFI27, IFI6), myeloid differentiation markers (MNDA), and key components of phagocytic machinery (FCN1, TYROBP/DAP12, FCER1G) with lysosomal proteases (CTSS) and calcium-binding S100 proteins involved in inflammation and cytoskeletal dynamics.
key_evidence: IFI27, IFI6: Type I interferon response genes, indicating sensing of viral PAMPs or inflammatory signals in CD14 monocytes
MNDA: Myeloid-specific nuclear antigen marking differentiated monocyte lineage commitment
TYROBP/DAP12: ITAM-containing adaptor required for FcγR and TLR signaling in myeloid cells
FCER1G: FcγR gamma-chain component essential for Fc receptor-mediated phagocytosis and immune complex sensing
FCN1: Ficolin-1, pattern recognition receptor for bacterial and fungal PAMPs
CTSS: Cathepsin S, lysosomal protease for antigen processing and pathogen degradation
S100A4, S100A6, S100A11: Inflammatory S100 proteins regulating calcium signaling and cell migration
TMSB4X: Actin-regulating protein supporting cytoskeletal remodeling during phagocytosis and chemotaxis
86.5% CD14 Mono composition strongly validates classical monocyte identity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CD14+CD16- cells co-expressing IFI27/IFI6 with FCGR1A (CD64) and FCN1; quantitative RT-PCR of IFI27 and MNDA in sorted CD14 monocytes stimulated with LPS or immune complexes; assess whether this signature correlates with TLR4-MyD88 pathway activation markers

functional_description: This signature represents the mature CD14 classical monocyte antimicrobial and metabolic effector state, characterized by high expression of the canonical bactericidal enzyme lysozyme and coordinated upregulation of oxidative stress handling (GPX1, FTH1), iron homeostasis for haem synthesis (SLC25A37, FTH1), and metabolic reprogramming (GAPDH, HK2, NAMPT for NAD+ biosynthesis). The programme reflects active monocyte differentiation with metabolic priming for phagocytic function and inflammatory cytokine production capacity.
key_evidence: LYZ: Canonical antimicrobial peptidoglycan hydrolase, hallmark of mature bactericidal monocytes
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification; critical for ROS-mediated antimicrobial function
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron sequestration; enables iron-dependent enzyme synthesis and limits pathogen iron acquisition
SLC25A37: Mitochondrial iron importer essential for haem and Fe-S cluster synthesis in activated monocytes
CEBPD: C/EBP family transcription factor related to CEBPB; regulates myeloid differentiation and inflammatory response
MAFB: MAF bZIP transcription factor; critical regulator of late monocyte maturation and antimicrobial gene expression
NAMPT: Rate-limiting enzyme in NAD+ salvage pathway; supports energetic demands of phagocytosis and inflammatory signalling
HK2: Hexokinase supporting glycolytic reprogram required for monocyte inflammatory activation
ZFP36L1: Early response gene; RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA stability of cytokines and inflammatory mediators
PLEK: Phosphoinositide signalling protein; supports phagocytic receptor signalling downstream of pattern recognition
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining LYZ, CD14, CD64 (FCGR1A) with activation markers (HLA-DR, CD11b); correlate NAMPT/GPX1 expression with functional assays of ROS production and antimicrobial killing capacity in sorted CD14 monocytes; qPCR validation of CEBPD and MAFB in LPS-stimulated monocytes

functional_description: This signature captures a translational protein synthesis programme dominated by ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), alongside metabolic support genes (GAPDH, LDHB) and the nucleolar chaperone NPM1. The cellular composition (43.5% Early GMP, 37.5% CD14 Mono) and prominence of ribosomal machinery suggests metabolically active, protein synthesis-engaged early myeloid progenitors with elevated anabolic capacity.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS2, RPS23, RPS17: ribosomal small subunit; core translational machinery in proliferative progenitors
RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: ribosomal large subunit; abundant in actively differentiating early GMPs
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor; marks translational engagement and protein synthesis flux
NPM1: nucleolar chaperone and centrosome regulator; high in proliferative early GMP and GMP-Cycle (10.5%)
GAPDH, LDHB: glycolytic and anaerobic metabolism; sustains energy for protein synthesis in committed progenitors
HSP90AB1: heat shock protein; supports protein folding during rapid differentiation
SPINK2: protease inhibitor; potentially involved in protease regulation during monocytic commitment
suggested_validation: Confirm translational activity via polysome profiling or puromycin incorporation assay in FACS-sorted Early GMP and GMP-Cycle populations; validate NPM1 nucleolar localization and centrosomal/spindle functions; measure ribosome biogenesis (47S pre-rRNA, rDNA transcription) as prognostic marker of progenitor proliferative state versus ProMono quiescence.

programme_name: Nuclear organisation and OXPHOS in cycling progenitors
functional_description: This signature reflects a programme of active chromatin remodelling and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism enriched in early monopoietic progenitors transitioning through proliferation. The programme combines nuclear HMG-box proteins governing transcriptionally permissive chromatin states with mitochondrial respiratory chain components supporting ATP production in metabolically active cells.
key_evidence: HMGB1: HMG-box protein regulating transcription and chromatin organisation in proliferating cells
HMGB2: HMG-box protein associated with open chromatin architecture in transcriptionally active cells
HMGN2: Nucleosomal DNA binder maintaining transcriptionally active chromatin during S-phase
MT-CO3: Cytochrome c oxidase subunit driving OXPHOS in metabolically demanding progenitors
MT-CO2: Respiratory chain complex IV component supporting mitochondrial bioenergetics
HSP90B1: Endoplasmic reticulum chaperone stabilising proteins during ER stress of proliferation
NUCKS1: Nuclear protein with cyclin-dependent kinase phosphorylation sites marking cell-cycle progression
STMN1: Cytosolic phosphoprotein regulating microtubule dynamics during mitosis
RNASE2: Antimicrobial ribonuclease accumulated in developing monocytes
ANP32E: Histone-binding protein involved in chromatin remodelling and transcriptional regulation
suggested_validation: Correlate expression with Ki-67 and BrdU incorporation in Early ProMono/GMP-Cycle subsets; validate OXPHOS dependency via Seahorse analysis; assess chromatin accessibility at HMGB1/HMGB2 target loci via ATAC-seq in cycling versus quiescent monopoietic cells.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein translation and cellular metabolism
functional_description: This signature represents a constitutive translational programme enriched in CD14 monocytes, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation elongation factors. The co-expression of metabolic enzymes (GAPDH, UQCRH) suggests active protein synthesis coupled to oxidative phosphorylation, characteristic of metabolically active classical monocytes.
key_evidence: RPL37A: 60S ribosomal subunit structural protein, top-ranked gene
RPS24, RPS26, RPS23, RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit components, consistent high expression
RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4: Additional ribosomal structural proteins indicating translation machinery assembly
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor (GEF activity), essential for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting functions, marks metabolically active cells
UQCRH: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation component, supports energy-intensive protein synthesis
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing and translation regulation
CD14 Mono enrichment: 53.5% of top-200 activating cells; progenitor contamination (39.5%) reflects differentiation trajectory
suggested_validation: Quantify polysome abundance via polysome profiling or measure global protein synthesis rates (puromycin incorporation) in CD14 vs CD16 monocytes and progenitors. Correlate ribosomal protein expression with mitochondrial mass (TMRM staining) and oxidative capacity to confirm the metabolic signature of classical monocytes.

programme_name: CD14 Mono oxidative stress and antimicrobial
functional_description: This signature reflects CD14 classical monocyte activation characterized by iron homeostasis (FTH1), antioxidant defence (GPX1), and antimicrobial effector functions (LYZ, CTSS). The module integrates metabolic reprogramming via NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT) with innate immune signalling (TYROBP/DAP12 ITAM) and C/EBP-family transcriptional control (CEBPD), supporting pro-inflammatory macrophage differentiation.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage for Fenton chemistry and ROS regulation in activated monocytes
LYZ: Lysozyme expression defining bactericidal capacity of classical monocytes
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase central to H2O2 detoxification during oxidative burst
TYROBP: DAP12-mediated ITAM signalling amplifying TLR and phagocytic receptor responses
CEBPD: C/EBP family transcription factor driving monocyte to macrophage differentiation
MAFB: Maf bZIP TF essential for monocyte maturation and pro-inflammatory phenotype
CTSS: Cathepsin S lysosomal protease supporting antigen presentation and intracellular pathogen degradation
NAMPT: NAD+ salvage pathway fuelling metabolic remodelling in activated innate immune cells
ZFP36L1: TIS11-family early response gene stabilizing inflammatory mRNA (e.g. TNF, IL6)
HLA-DRA: MHC-II expression consistent with activated antigen-presenting monocyte phenotype
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry for CD14+CD16- monocytes co-expressing LYZ, CTSS, and HLA-DR; ROS assays (DCF/DHE) in FTH1+ and GPX1+ gates; single-cell RNA-seq validation of CEBPD and MAFB co-expression with inflammatory cytokine transcripts.

programme_name: Monocyte cytoskeletal remodelling and lysosomal proteolysis
functional_description: This signature reflects basal monocyte homeostasis driven by actin cytoskeletal dynamics (TMSB4X, COTL1, S100A4) and lysosomal cysteine protease activity (CTSS) essential for antigen processing. The prominent hemoglobin and mitochondrial gene content indicates metabolically active cells with potential artifact from ambient RNA or early erythroid contamination, though expression of FCER1G, AIF1, and TYROBP (ITAM signalling hub) confirms authentic monocyte identity with engagement of Fc receptor and pattern recognition pathways.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: actin sequestering protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and cell migration—core monocyte remodelling
CTSS: lysosomal cysteine cathepsin essential for antigen processing and presentation in professional APCs
FCER1G: γ-chain of Fc receptors and other ITAM complexes; direct effector of antibody-dependent cellular responses
TYROBP: DAP12 ITAM adaptor linking FcγR and TLR signalling to monocyte activation
AIF1: calcium-binding effector induced by cytokines; promotes macrophage activation and inflammatory remodelling
S100A4, S100A11: calcium-modulated actin-binding proteins involved in monocyte migration and inflammation
COTL1: actin-binding protein linked to lipid mediator signalling via 5-lipoxygenase interaction
HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD, MT-CO2: high abundance suggests metabolic priming or ambient RNA contamination
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of CD14+ CD64+ CCR2+ monocytes for CTSS, FCER1G, AIF1 protein expression. Quantify hemoglobin gene contribution via RNA-ISH to exclude RBC contamination. Functional assay: test phagocytic capacity and ROS production in response to IgG-opsonised pathogens. Assess response to TLR2/4 ligands to confirm inflammasome-priming competence absent from signature.

functional_description: This signature captures elevated protein synthesis machinery and metabolic activity in mature CD14 monocytes and Early GMP progenitors, dominated by ribosomal structural components (RPS/RPL family) and translation factors. The enrichment reflects the heightened translational demand during monocyte terminal differentiation and the metabolic activity of committed early progenitors prior to lineage specification.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS2, RPS17, RPS23: core 40S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating active global translation
RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit components supporting ribosome assembly and protein synthesis capacity
GAPDH: glycolytic enzyme and translation regulator; elevated in metabolically active monocytes
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor required for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery
NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein involved in ribosome biogenesis and proliferation
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating translation and mRNA stability
SERPINB1: serine protease inhibitor abundant in neutrophil/monocyte granules; marks myeloid differentiation
LDHB: lactate dehydrogenase supporting glycolytic metabolism in differentiated monocytes
suggested_validation: Validate by correlating ribosomal protein expression with monocyte maturation markers (CD14, CD11b) and assessing protein synthesis rate (puromycin incorporation) across Early GMP vs CD14 monocyte stages. SERPINB1 presence in mature monocyte compartment supports authentic differentiation rather than proliferative state.

functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive protein synthesis and oxidative phosphorylation capacity, hallmarks of metabolically active CD14 monocytes. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0) and mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) indicates high translation rates and ATP generation required for monocyte effector functions. Co-expression of GAPDH and LDHB reflects glycolytic-oxidative metabolic switching characteristic of activated monocytes.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS2, RPS17, RPLP0: 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits; robust protein synthesis capacity enabling rapid cytokine/chemokine production
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: Respiratory chain complexes III/IV; oxidative phosphorylation for sustained ATP production in inflammatory monocytes
GAPDH: Central glycolytic enzyme; metabolic reprogramming during monocyte activation and migration
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase B subunit; lactate production and NADH/NAD+ cycling during high metabolic demand
GSTP1: Glutathione S-transferase; antioxidant defence against ROS generated during respiratory burst
H2AFY, H3F3A, HMGN1: Histone variants and chromatin remodelling factors; support transcriptional accessibility in activated monocytes
CD14 Mono dominance (43%): Signature enriched in classical inflammatory monocytes; early progenitors (GMP, ProMono) represent developmental trajectory
suggested_validation: Validate via functional metabolic assays (Seahorse oxidative phosphorylation/ECAR) and correlate ribosomal protein co-expression with inflammatory cytokine production capacity (IL1B, TNF, IL6 by qPCR/FACS) in sorted CD14 versus CD16 monocytes. Confirm mitochondrial mass/activity by MitoTracker or TMRM staining in signature-high cells.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis machinery and oxidative metabolism in early monocytic differentiation. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPL/RPS family) and translation factors (EEF1B2) coupled with OXPHOS components (UQCRH, MT-CO2, LDHB) indicates metabolic reprogramming supporting the biosynthetic demands of GMP-to-monocyte transition, with enrichment in Early GMP (32%) consistent with metabolic priming prior to committed mono differentiation.
key_evidence: RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A: Core 60S/40S ribosomal subunit proteins—elevated in rapidly differentiating progenitors requiring high protein synthesis rates
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity—supports sustained translation during GMP maturation
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting functions in RNA binding and cell proliferation—marker of metabolic shift in early differentiation
UQCRH, MT-CO2, LDHB: OXPHOS and anaerobic metabolism enzymes—indicate increased mitochondrial respiration during mono commitment
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA stability and splicing—supports dynamic transcriptome remodeling in early GMP
Early GMP dominance (32%) and CD14 Mono enrichment (43.5%): Signature captures transition-state metabolic activation prior to terminal mono differentiation
suggested_validation: RT-qPCR quantification of RPL37A/RPS24 and UQCRH across Early GMP → Late ProMono → CD14 Mono trajectory; co-stain CD34+CD13+ Early GMP for ribosomal protein expression by flow cytometry; assess polysome profiling in sorted GMP-Cycle vs Late ProMono to confirm translational capacity correlation.

programme_name: CD16 Monocyte ADCC and Immune Surveillance
functional_description: This signature defines mature CD16 monocytes (non-classical, patrolling) specialized in antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inflammatory immune responses. The transcriptional programme emphasizes Fc receptor signaling, lysosomal proteolysis, iron metabolism, and myeloid activation pathways characteristic of tissue-patrolling and endothelial surveillance monocytes.
key_evidence: FCGR3A: Master marker of CD16+ monocytes; central to ADCC and immune complex handling
FCER1G: Gamma chain of Fc receptors (FcγRIIA, FcγRIIIA, FcεRI); critical for ADCC signaling via ITAM
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein; couples Fc receptors to downstream myeloid activation
AIF1: Calcium-binding actin regulator induced by IFN-γ; promotes macrophage activation and monocyte mobility
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease; essential for antigen processing and phagolysosomal degradation in patrolling cells
CD68: Pan-myeloid marker; high in activated monocytes undergoing phagocytosis and tissue remodeling
LST1: Membrane protein enhanced by IFN-γ and bacterial/LPS stimuli; marker of activated tissue-surveying monocytes
MS4A7: MS4A family member; marks mature monocyte subset with enhanced inflammatory potential
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; indicates iron-loaded, metabolically active tissue macrophages and non-classical monocytes
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism; supports sustained cellular metabolism and proliferation during immune activation
S100A11: Calcium-binding protein; involved in cell motility and cytoskeletal dynamics of patrolling monocytes
SERPINA1: α1-antitrypsin; modulates protease activity and prevents excessive tissue damage during inflammatory surveillance
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14lo/neg, CD16+, CX3CR1high, FCGR3A+, and functional assays for ADCC (NK cell-like killing via IgG opsonization). RNA-FISH or qPCR validation of FCGR3A, FCER1G, TYROBP, and AIF1 in sorted CD16 monocytes vs CD14 monocytes. Investigate NR4A orphan nuclear receptor expression (NR4A1/NR4A2) as putative master regulators not captured in top 15.

functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 monocytes specialized in antigen presentation via HLA class II molecules (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ), coupled with iron storage and cysteine protease inhibition. The programme supports professional antigen-presenting cell (APC) function and maintains intracellular iron homoeostasis critical for sustained metabolic activity during immune responses.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA: HLA class II alpha chain; core antigen presentation molecule
HLA-DRB1/HLA-DRB5: HLA class II beta chains; CD14 monocytes are potent APCs
HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: HLA-DP heterodimer; alternative class II presentation pathway
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: HLA-DQ heterodimer; completes class II repertoire
CD74: MHC class II chaperone and invariant chain; essential for peptide loading
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain; iron storage and ROS protection in activated monocytes
CST3: Cystatin C; cysteine protease inhibitor; regulates phagolysosomal proteolysis during antigen processing
YBX1: Cold shock domain protein; RNA/DNA binding; supports translational regulation in activated state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: confirm HLA-DR high, CD74+, FTH1+ in CD14 Mono (vs CD16 Mono low); functional assays for antigen presentation capacity (MLR) and iron uptake; assess CST3 activity in phagolysosomes during bacterial antigen processing

programme_name: Early ProMono myeloid differentiation and maturation
functional_description: This signature represents early monocyte progenitor maturation characterized by innate immune effector protein expression (S100A8/A9 calprotectin complex, LYZ lysozyme) and active chromatin remodeling supporting lineage commitment. The enrichment of histone variants (H2AFZ, HIST1H1E/C), chromatin regulators (HMGB2, HMGN2, PCLAF), and cell cycle machinery (TUBB, GAPDH) indicates concurrent proliferation and transcriptional reprogramming during ProMono differentiation.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin complex component; hallmark of early myeloid differentiation and monocyte commitment
S100A8: S100 calcium-binding protein; co-expresses with S100A9 in committed monocyte progenitors
LYZ: Lysozyme; canonical monocyte lineage marker reflecting acquisition of antimicrobial function
HMGB2: Chromatin-associated protein enabling transcriptional plasticity during lineage commitment
HMGN2: Nucleosomal protein enriched on active chromatin; supports epigenetic remodeling in differentiating cells
PCLAF: Cell cycle and chromatin binding; indicates active proliferation during ProMono phase
H2AFZ: Histone variant in nucleosomes; marks regulatory regions during myeloid differentiation
HIST1H1E/C: Histone H1 variants; support chromatin compaction and lineage-specific transcription
RETN: Resistin-like molecule; innate immune function consistent with monocyte effector maturation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting Early ProMono (CD34+CD13+CD115+MS4A3+CD14−) vs Late ProMono (CD34+CD13+CD115+MS4A3+CD14+) to confirm S100A8/A9 and LYZ elevation specifically in early-stage cells; qPCR validation of chromatin remodelers (HMGB2, HMGN2) relative to commitment TFs (KLF4, IRF8); assess RETN expression as potential early ProMono-specific marker distinct from GMP or mature CD14 Mono

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated ribosomal protein (RPS, RPL subunits) and translation factor expression (EEF1B2), coupled with nucleolar/spliceosomal components (FBL, SNRPE), indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity. The inclusion of PRSS57 (serine protease precursor storage) and UQCRH (mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation) suggests metabolic support for rapid translation and biosynthesis in early monocytic differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPS26, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins—constitutive signature of translational machinery upregulation in differentiating monocytes
RPLP0: Acidic ribosomal phosphoprotein; stabilizes ribosome assembly and function during biosynthetic demand
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor (GEF for EEF1A); essential for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery and elongation rate control
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting roles in translation initiation and stress response; marker of metabolic reprogramming
FBL: Nucleolar fibrillarin; rRNA processing and ribosome biogenesis—indicates ribosome demand matching GMP-to-monocyte transition
SNRPE: Spliceosomal U snRNP component; supports pre-mRNA processing of lineage-specific transcripts during monocytic commitment
PRSS57: Serine protease; early maturation/azurophil granule biogenesis signal in monocyte lineage
UQCRH: Complex III of OXPHOS; energetic demand for active translation and biosynthesis
suggested_validation: Measure polysome abundance and translation rates (polysome profiling, SUnSET assay) in sorted Early GMP, GMP-Cycle, GMP-Mono, and CD14 Mono. Correlate with ribosome biogenesis markers (nucleolar occupancy, rRNA synthesis). Validate PRSS57 and UQCRH as co-drivers of metabolic reprogramming during GMP-monocyte transition using qPCR and western blotting.

programme_name: Myeloid Cytoskeletal Activation and Innate Sensing
functional_description: This signature reflects activated monocyte effector functions centered on cytoskeletal remodeling, pattern recognition receptor signaling, and phagocytic competence. The enrichment of S100 calcium-binding proteins, actin-regulatory factors, and ITAM-coupled receptors (FCER1G, TYROBP) indicates priming for rapid migration and immune complex handling characteristic of inflammatory CD14 monocytes.
key_evidence: S100A4/S100A6/S100A11: calcium-mediated cytoskeletal dynamics and inflammatory amplification
FCER1G: ITAM signaling adaptor for Fc receptor and integrin cross-talk in phagocytosis
TYROBP: DAP12-mediated innate immune receptor signaling coupled to migration
COTL1: actin-binding protein regulating leukocyte motility and chemotaxis
FCGR3A: Fc-gamma receptor supporting antibody-dependent cellular responses
AIF1: calcium-binding protein promoting macrophage activation and cytoskeletal rearrangement
VASP: Ena-VASP family member controlling actin polymerization during migration
CD68: pan-monocyte lysosomal marker indicating phagocytic maturity
LST1: LPS-inducible membrane protein enhancing pattern recognition responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of S100A4/A6 protein co-expression with CD14+CD16- monocytes; functional assays measuring actin polymerization, chemotaxis, and Fc-receptor-mediated phagocytosis in sorted S100A4-high vs. low monocyte subsets; assess activation state correlation with inflammatory context (LPS, TNF stimulation).

functional_description: This signature represents a translational capacity programme enriched in early GMP and CD14 monocytes, characterised by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation elongation factors. The dominance of ribosomal protein genes (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0) alongside GAPDH and EEF1B2 indicates heightened protein synthesis machinery activity, consistent with biosynthetic demand in progenitors undergoing rapid proliferation and differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit protein, marks translational active cells
RPL37A: 60S ribosomal subunit protein, structural ribosome component
RPS23: 40S ribosomal subunit, core translation machinery
RPS2: 40S ribosomal subunit, fundamental synthesis component
RPS17: 40S ribosomal subunit, ribosomal architecture
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting roles; marks metabolically active progenitors
RPLP0: 60S acidic ribosomal protein, ribosomal function
RPL7A: 60S ribosomal subunit, translation complex stability
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor, active protein synthesis
UQCRH: Complex III component, supports ATP generation for anabolic demand
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in mRNA stability and processing
suggested_validation: Assess ribosomal protein expression via flow cytometry (RPL4-GFP reporter) and polysome profiling in sorted Early GMP vs Late GMP to confirm translational activity gradient. Correlate ribosomal abundance with Ki-67/cell cycle markers to validate association with proliferation rather than terminal differentiation; distinguish from CD14 Mono signal by co-staining CD14/CD64 to exclude mature monocyte contamination in signature.

programme_name: Nucleolar protein homeostasis and translational control
functional_description: This signature reflects early GMP stress-response and housekeeping metabolism, centered on nucleolar proteins (NPM1), heat-shock chaperones (HSP90AB1), and RNA-binding proteins supporting ribosome biogenesis and mRNA stability. The dominant activating population (50% Early GMP) and enrichment in translational machinery components (RPS23, SNRPE) suggest elevated anabolic demand during early myeloid progenitor proliferation, with secondary contribution from monocytes (26.5% CD14 Mono) maintaining basal protein quality control.
key_evidence: NPM1: nucleolar phosphoprotein essential for centrosome duplication and protein chaperoning in cycling progenitors
HSP90AB1: heat-shock chaperone supporting signal transduction and protein folding under proliferative stress in early GMP
PTMA: DNA-binding cofactor and apoptosis suppressor, stabilizing cycling GMP against differentiation signals
HNRNPA1/HNRNPA2B1: RNA-binding proteins regulating splicing and mRNA trafficking in high-turnover progenitors
RPS23: ribosomal protein indicative of active translation demand during GMP expansion
SNRPE: spliceosomal component supporting mRNA maturation in proliferating cells
LDHB/MT-CO2: metabolic effectors (glycolysis/mitochondrial respiration) driving ATP production in cycling progenitors
TXN: antioxidant thioredoxin protecting high-metabolic progenitors from ROS during proliferation
suggested_validation: Validate via: (1) co-staining NPM1 and Ki-67 in Early GMP vs. late GMP to confirm nucleolar enrichment correlates with cell-cycle entry; (2) bulk RNA-seq of sorted GMP-Cycle vs. GMP-Mono to confirm loss of this signature upon monocytic differentiation; (3) functional knockdown of NPM1/HSP90AB1 in GMP to test proliferation dependency. Note: SPINK2 appears anomalous (genital tract protease inhibitor) and may reflect batch annotation artifact.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis machinery and metabolic pathway activity in CD14 monocytes, driven by ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPS17, RPL37A, RPS23), translation factors (EEF1B2), and pentose phosphate pathway enzyme (TALDO1). The enrichment indicates enhanced translational demand and NADPH generation for biosynthetic and antioxidant functions characteristic of metabolically active classical monocytes.
key_evidence: GAPDH: moonlighting protein with roles beyond glycolysis; marker of metabolic activity in activated monocytes
RPS2, RPS24, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPS17, RPL37A, RPS23: ribosomal structural proteins indicating high protein synthesis capacity
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor required for efficient protein synthesis during activation
TALDO1: pentose phosphate pathway enzyme supplying NADPH for NADPH oxidase-mediated ROS production
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein regulating mRNA processing and stability in response to inflammatory signals
SERPINB1: neutrophil elastase inhibitor supporting monocyte survival during oxidative stress
NPM1: nucleolar protein supporting cell proliferation and ribosome biogenesis in progenitor-enriched subset
suggested_validation: Verify signature reflects translational state via polysome profiling or ribosome occupancy (Ribo-seq); confirm NADPH oxidase functional capacity through ROS assays (DHE/DCFDA); validate metabolic profile using seahorse analysis of oxidative phosphorylation and glycolysis in FACS-sorted CD14 versus CD16 monocytes. Consider whether elevated ribosomal proteins reflect anabolic priming or impending differentiation of the Early GMP/Late ProMono subset (35.5% and 8.5% composition).

programme_name: Early myeloid translation and mitochondrial priming
functional_description: This signature reflects early GMP-stage myeloid progenitors undergoing active protein synthesis and metabolic preparation for terminal differentiation. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS26, RPS2, RPL37A, RPS17, RPLP0) combined with mitochondrial OXPHOS components (MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) and MPO expression indicates cells actively translating myeloid-specific proteins while establishing the energetic capacity required for monocytic and granulocytic commitment.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS26, RPS2, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0: robust ribosomal protein expression indicating high translational demand characteristic of GMP stage
MPO: critical myeloid lineage marker present in early GMP, GMP-Mono, and committed ProMono stages; distinguishes from HSCs
MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial respiratory chain proteins reflecting increased OXPHOS capacity required for energetically demanding differentiation
PTMA: anti-apoptotic factor stabilizing proliferating progenitors during commitment transition
RANBP1, SNRPF: cell cycle regulation and RNA processing supporting active differentiation rather than quiescence
Cell composition: 22% Early GMP + 13% GMP-Cycle + 12% GMP-Mono (47% GMP pool) confirms progenitor identity; 40% CD14 Mono indicates signature captures transitional GMP→monocyte trajectory
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: MPO+CD34+/KIT+ early GMP (RPS high), MPO+CD34-KIT- late GMP (RPS high), versus MPO+CSF1R+CD64+ ProMono (RPS lower). qPCR validation of ribosomal protein cluster in sorted GMP-Mono vs mature CD14 Mono. Metabolic assessment: Seahorse OXPHOS capacity in RPS-high vs RPS-low GMP fractions.

functional_description: This signature reflects early-stage monocyte progenitor commitment with robust innate immune effector function, characterized by elevated antimicrobial proteins (S100A8/A9, LYZ, RNASE2) and myeloid differentiation markers. The programme shows active chromatin remodelling and cell cycle dynamics consistent with proliferating Early ProMono cells transitioning toward functional monocyte identity.
key_evidence: S100A8: Calcium-binding antimicrobial protein; hallmark of activated myeloid cells and Early ProMono innate function
S100A9: Calprotectin component; S100A8/A9 heterodimer is pre-inflammatory signature of committed monocyte progenitors
LYZ: Lysozyme; canonical monocyte lineage marker and antibacterial effector upregulated during ProMono commitment
MNDA: Myeloid cell nuclear differentiation antigen; granulocyte-monocyte lineage-restricted marker supporting ProMono identity
RNASE2: Ribonuclease with antimicrobial activity; part of monocyte innate immune arsenal during commitment
HMGB1/HMGB2/HMGN2: Chromatin remodelling and transcriptional activity markers; consistent with Early ProMono proliferation phase
STMN1/NUSAP1: Cell cycle progression markers; indicates Early ProMono cells are mitotically active before terminal differentiation
CSTA: Cysteine protease inhibitor; protease regulation during monocyte maturation
RETN: Resistin-like antimicrobial protein; additional innate immune effector in activated progenitors
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of S100A8/A9 with MS4A3 and CSF1R on Early ProMono-enriched populations; in situ validation of S100A8/A9 co-expression with KLF4/IRF8; assess cell cycle status (Ki67) correlation with STMN1/NUSAP1 expression to confirm proliferative phase

functional_description: This signature reflects the lysosomal protease and antigen presentation machinery of CD14 classical monocytes, centered on CTSS-mediated degradation of ingested pathogens and endogenous proteins for MHC-II presentation. The program integrates bactericidal effectors (LYZ lysozyme), ITAM-signaling adaptors (TYROBP/DAP12), and vesicular trafficking components essential for phagolysosomal maturation and cross-presentation.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease (cathepsin S) driving protein degradation for antigen presentation; highest ranked gene
LYZ: Bactericidal lysozyme hydrolyzing peptidoglycan; hallmark of monocyte microbicidal capacity
HLA-DQB1: MHC-II antigen presentation beta chain; links to professional APC function in CD14 Mono
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor for pattern recognition and Fc receptor signaling; myeloid-restricted
MNDA: Myeloid differentiation antigen; monocyte/granulocyte lineage marker confirming cell identity
AP1S2: Adaptor for clathrin-mediated endocytic trafficking; essential for phagolysosomal pathway
CLEC7A: C-type lectin receptor; fungal/bacterial PAMP sensing coupled to endosomal degradation
suggested_validation: Quantify CTSS protein via flow cytometry on CD14 Mono; co-stain with HLA-DR and CD64 to confirm APC phenotype. Assess phagolysosomal function via bacterial killing assays or BacLight-opsonized E. coli uptake. Compare CTSS expression between CD14 and CD16 monocytes to validate subset specificity.

functional_description: This signature reflects heightened global protein synthesis capacity in Early GMP progenitors, characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation elongation factors. The signature is dominated by translational infrastructure components, with secondary contributions from metabolic enzymes (LDHB) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1), consistent with the anabolic demands of proliferating myeloid progenitors poised for differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins; highly abundant in protein synthesis-active progenitors
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins; coordinated upregulation indicates active ribosome biogenesis
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor; GEF for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to ribosome during elongation
NPM1: Nucleophosmin; central hub for ribosome assembly and cell proliferation; high in cycling progenitors
LDHB: Lactate dehydrogenase B; glycolytic metabolism support for energy demands of translating cells
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein; roles in pre-mRNA processing and mRNA stability regulation
SERPINB1: Serine protease inhibitor; protects against proteolytic stress during high-protein-synthesis states
H3F3A: Histone variant; associated with active chromatin and proliferation
suggested_validation: Validate via flow cytometry measuring ribosomal protein content (e.g., RPS24-GFP) or translation rate assays (puromycin incorporation) in Early GMP vs. CD14 Mono populations. Confirm that signature correlates with actively cycling vs. post-mitotic progenitors and that it decreases during monocyte maturation as translational demand normalizes.

functional_description: This signature reflects a mixed monocyte population enriched for hemoglobin gene expression (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD, HBM), suggesting iron-laden or erythrophagocytic monocytes undergoing maturation. The co-expression of lysosomal proteases (CTSS), actin regulators (TMSB4X, S100A4), and TYROBP (ITAM-signaling adaptor) indicates active phagocytic capacity and antigen processing, consistent with classical CD14 monocytes engaged in tissue remodeling rather than acute inflammatory sensing.
key_evidence: HBA2, HBA1, HBB, HBD, HBM: Hemoglobin genes unusually high in monocytes, indicating erythrophagocytosis or iron scavenging function
CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for antigen processing and phagolysosomal degradation
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor protein critical for Fc receptor signaling and phagocytic activation
S100A4, TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal regulators supporting cell migration and morphodynamic processes
AHSP: Alpha-globin binding chaperone, consistent with hemoglobin handling capacity
CD14 Mono 61%: Dominant classical monocyte composition with phagocytic/tissue-remodeling phenotype
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD14/CD16 with hemoglobin-uptake markers (CD163, HO-1); assess phagocytic activity via opsonized RBC uptake assay; validate CTSS/TYROBP axis in FCGR1A+ CD14+ subset to confirm erythrophagocytic vs inflammatory monocyte substate

functional_description: This signature reflects early-to-intermediate monocyte differentiation marked by acquisition of antibacterial effector functions (LYZ lysozyme for peptidoglycan degradation) and innate immune priming (S100A8/A9 calprotectin for DAMP signalling). The prominent hemoglobin genes (HBA1/2, HBB, HBD) and metabolic enzymes (CA1, TIMM10) indicate retained erythroid transcriptional priming typical of ProMono and GMP-derived monocyte populations during bone marrow egress.
key_evidence: LYZ: Direct bactericidal activity; hallmark antimicrobial monocyte effector
S100A8/A9: Calprotectin complex; neutrophil-mimicry innate immunity marker in inflammatory monocytes
HBA1/2, HBB, HBD, HBM, AHSP: Hemoglobin synthesis genes; erythroid lineage priming in early monocytic differentiation
LGALS1: Galectin-1 immune tolerance modulator; balances antimicrobial activation
CA1: Carbonic anhydrase; metabolic enzyme supporting glycolytic inflammatory metabolism
CSTA: Cystatin cysteine protease inhibitor; modulates proteolytic environment in phagosomes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: co-stain LYZ+ S100A8+ S100A9+ in CD14+ CD163low/negative gate and assess CCR2+/- distribution; assess hemoglobin gene expression (RNA FISH) as developmental clock in GMP-Mono and Early ProMono; functional assay: LYZ enzymatic activity and calprotectin secretion upon LPS/fMLP stimulation to confirm maturation-stage antimicrobial competence.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated protein synthesis machinery, dominated by ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation factors. The enrichment in CD14 monocytes and progenitor-like cells (42.5% CD14 Mono, 35.5% Early GMP) suggests heightened translational capacity associated with myeloid differentiation and monocyte maturation rather than inflammatory activation.
key_evidence: RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit protein, top-ranked, fundamental translation machinery
RPL37A: 60S ribosomal subunit protein, structural rRNA component
RPS2: 40S ribosomal subunit, core translation initiation
GAPDH: Glycolytic enzyme with moonlighting roles in translation regulation
LDHB: Anaerobic glycolysis enzyme, supports high biosynthetic demand
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor, GEF for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery
NPM1: Nucleophosmin, ribosomal biogenesis and protein chaperoning
PTMA: Prothymosin alpha, translation-associated chaperone activity
HNRNPA1/C: RNA-binding proteins coordinating pre-mRNA processing and translation
suggested_validation: qPCR for RPS24, RPL37A, EEF1B2 in sorted CD14 monocytes vs CD16 monocytes and progenitors; polysome profiling to confirm active translation; ribosomal biogenesis assays (NPM1 localization, rRNA levels). Consider whether this represents metabolic priming for differentiation rather than inflammatory activation—compare with TNF/IL1B signature activation patterns.

programme_name: Myeloid stress response and antimicrobial effector
functional_description: This signature reflects activated CD14 classical monocytes under inflammatory stress, characterized by abundant antimicrobial proteins (S100A8/A9 calprotectin, LYZ lysozyme), oxidative stress response (GPX1), and active chromatin remodeling (HMGB2, HMGN2, histone variants). The co-expression of JUN and cell-cycle chromatin factors (PCLAF, PTMA) indicates an early activation state balancing immediate effector function with proliferative capacity.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin subunit; canonical CD14 monocyte antimicrobial alarmin and neutrophil recruitment factor
S100A8: Calprotectin heterodimer partner; released upon TLR/DAMP activation; pro-inflammatory PAMP sensor output
LYZ: Lysozyme; primary bactericidal enzyme in monocyte granules; marks functional antimicrobial effector state
GPX1: Glutathione peroxidase; ROS scavenging during oxidative burst; indicates NADPH oxidase activation phase
JUN: c-Jun AP-1 component; IRF5/NF-κB-driven early inflammatory response in classical monocytes
HMGB2: High mobility group box; chromatin accessibility factor during cytokine gene activation
PCLAF: PCNA-associated factor; S-phase chromatin dynamics; suggests G1/S transition in activated monocytes
PTMA: Prothymosin-α; anti-apoptotic; maintains survival of activated inflammatory monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: CD14+CD16− with S100A9/A8 and LYZ protein expression; correlate PCLAF/JUN with cell-cycle markers (Ki-67, PCNA); functional assays measuring bactericidal activity (CFU killing) and ROS production (DHE/CM-H2DCFDA) upon TLR4 stimulation; confirm IRF5/NF-κB binding to S100A8/A9 promoters via ChIP-seq.

functional_description: This signature reflects elevated mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity and protein synthesis machinery in CD14 monocytes, predominantly characterized by OXPHOS complex subunits (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5, UQCRH, UQCRQ) and ribosomal proteins. The enrichment suggests heightened metabolic demand for ATP generation and rapid effector protein synthesis, consistent with pro-inflammatory CD14 monocytes primed for rapid response to PAMPs and tissue recruitment.
key_evidence: MT-CO2: Complex IV subunit; OXPHOS capacity for ATP generation in metabolically active monocytes
MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Complex I subunits; NADH oxidation driving mitochondrial electron transport chain
UQCRH, UQCRQ: Complex III subunits; ubiquinone reduction maintaining proton gradient
RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPLP0: 40S and 60S ribosomal proteins; global translation capacity
TIMM13: Mitochondrial protein import chaperone; supporting OXPHOS protein biogenesis
GSTP1: Glutathione conjugation; ROS detoxification during inflammatory activation
PLAC8: Transcriptional co-regulator; potential metabolic priming of CD14 monocytes
suggested_validation: Measure mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 or TMRM) and oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse assay) in CD14 vs CD16 monocytes. Quantify nascent protein synthesis via puromycin incorporation or metabolic labeling. Correlate with phospho-IRF5 and phospho-NFκB signaling in response to LPS or TLR4 agonists.

programme_name: Myeloid Progenitor Maturation with ER Stress
functional_description: This signature reflects active protein synthesis and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response during myeloid differentiation, with enrichment in ribosomal proteins, molecular chaperones, and proteolytic enzymes. The cell composition (43% CD14 Mono but 57% early GMP/progenitors) indicates activation in differentiating monocyte precursors undergoing massive translational demands and quality control. MPO expression confirms myeloid lineage commitment with azurophil granule biogenesis.
key_evidence: MPO: Cardinal myeloid differentiation marker; stored in azurophil granules of maturing monocytes
RPS24, RPL37A, RPS17: Ribosomal proteins indicating high-rate protein synthesis during lineage commitment
HSPA5: ER-resident HSP70 chaperone essential for ER stress response and protein folding during secretory protein production
CANX: Calnexin involved in ER protein quality control; co-translational chaperoning of nascent proteins
XBP1: Transcription factor for ER stress response (unfolded protein response pathway); regulates MHC-II genes
PRSS57: Serine protease localized to azurophil granules; undergoes proteolytic activation during monocyte maturation
PTMA: Nuclear chaperone supporting transcriptional activity and suppressing apoptosis in proliferating precursors
NUCB2: Calcium regulation and TNF release; involved in inflammatory monocyte physiology
NPM1: Nucleolar protein supporting protein chaperoning and cell proliferation in progenitors
LDHB: Glycolytic enzyme supporting aerobic-anaerobic transition in activated myeloid cells
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining MPO, CD33, CD14, and surface markers (CD64, CCR2) in CD34+ GMP and CD14+ monocyte populations; confirm XBP1 splicing status and HSPA5 expression by qPCR in sorted early vs. late monocyte progenitors; assess ER stress markers (ATF4, CHOP) in activated CD14 Mono subsets.

functional_description: This signature captures the pro-inflammatory state of classical CD14+ monocytes characterized by high expression of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and calcium-binding proteins of the S100A family, which are key mediators of sterile inflammation and pathogen-associated immune sensing. The transcriptional program reflects mobilization of innate immune effector functions including calcium signaling, iron metabolism, and cellular stress responses typical of activated inflammatory monocytes.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin (S100A8/A9 heterodimer) is a hallmark DAMP released by activated CD14+ monocytes; promotes TLR4 signaling and recruits additional immune cells to inflammatory sites
S100A8: Partner protein in calprotectin complex; drives NF-κB activation and inflammasome priming in classical monocytes
S100A12: S100 family member expressed during monocyte activation; ligand for RAGE and TLR4, amplifies pro-inflammatory responses
S100A4: S100 family calcium-binding protein; facilitates monocyte migration and extravasation during inflammation
S100A6: S100 family protein involved in calcium-dependent signaling and cytoskeletal dynamics in myeloid cells
VCAN: Versican expression in activated monocytes contributes to ECM remodeling and leukocyte recruitment in inflammatory microenvironments
LGALS1: Galectin-1 mediates immunoregulatory feedback on activated monocytes; involved in resolution phase of inflammation
LGALS2: Galectin-2 regulates monocyte-lymphocyte interactions and innate immune responses
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain upregulation reflects increased iron metabolism required for ROS generation and oxidative burst capacity
MAFB: MAF basic leucine zipper transcription factor; supports myeloid differentiation and maintenance of monocyte identity
IFI6: Interferon-stimulated gene; indicates type I/II interferon priming of CD14+ monocytes
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: Sort CD14+CD16- monocytes and validate S100A8/A9, S100A12 protein expression by intracellular staining; correlate with surface CD14 intensity and CD64. qPCR validation of S100A family, VCAN, and MAFB in sorted CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono. Functional assay: Measure calprotectin (S100A8/A9) secretion and ROS production (DHE staining) in response to TLR4 stimulation (LPS) in activated CD14+ monocytes.

functional_description: This signature represents CD14+ classical monocytes with enhanced antimicrobial effector functions, characterized by S100 calprotectin complex (S100A8/A9) and myeloid differentiation markers. The programme reflects active bacterial sensing and phagocytic capacity rather than master transcriptional regulation or inflammatory cytokine production.
key_evidence: S100A9: Calprotectin heterodimer component; Ca2+-binding alarm signal and DAMP; antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory mediator in monocytes
S100A8: Calprotectin partner; myeloid-specific alarmin promoting monocyte antimicrobial responses and recruitment
S100A12: Extended calprotectin family member; danger-associated molecular pattern in activated myeloid cells
LYZ: Lysozyme; bacterial peptidoglycan degradation; classical monocyte antimicrobial effector
FCN1: Ficolin-1; pattern recognition receptor for bacterial and fungal PAMPs; complement activation
MNDA: Myeloid nuclear differentiation antigen; lineage-restricted marker of monocyte maturation
CD14: LPS co-receptor; PAMP sensing; classical monocyte identity marker; high expression in CD14 mono
CSTA: Cystatin; cysteine protease inhibitor; antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory in myeloid cells
S100A6: S100 family; calcium signaling; myeloid activation-associated
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining S100A8/A9 with CD14, CD64, and inflammatory markers (TNF, IL-6 or phospho-p38) across monocyte subsets. Compare S100A8/A9 expression in LPS-stimulated versus unstimulated CD14 mono. Single-molecule FISH for S100A8/A9 and LYZ in CD14 vs CD16 monocytes.

programme_name: Cytoplasmic protein synthesis and stress response
functional_description: This signature reflects constitutive cellular housekeeping and proteostasis functions rather than lineage-specific myeloid differentiation. The gene set is enriched for ribosomal proteins (RPS17, RPS23, RPLP0), molecular chaperones (HSP90AB1, PTGES3), nucleic acid binding proteins (YBX1, HNRNPA1), and anti-oxidant enzymes (SOD1), indicating active translation capacity and stress tolerance typical of metabolically active progenitors and early monocytes.
key_evidence: RPLP0, RPS23, RPS17: ribosomal structural proteins indicating high translation demand in proliferative GMP and early mono populations
