HSP90AB1, PTGES3: heat shock proteins mediating protein folding and chaperone function, supporting cellular stress resilience
SOD1: antioxidant enzyme protecting against oxidative damage during myeloid differentiation
YBX1, HNRNPA1: RNA-binding proteins regulating post-transcriptional gene expression and mRNA stability
CALM2, PPIA: calcium and prolyl isomerase signalling, supporting early signal transduction in progenitors
PTMA: anti-apoptotic factor and transcriptional co-regulator preserving progenitor viability
suggested_validation: Confirm this represents a housekeeping/metabolic programme rather than GMP-specific commitment by comparing expression across HSC, GMP, and differentiated myeloid populations. Validate with functional assays: assess translation rate via puromycin incorporation; measure ROS levels in SOD1-knockout GMP analogues; assess dependence on HSP90 via inhibitor sensitivity. This signature may represent a co-factor of GMP identity rather than a discrete differentiation programme.

functional_description: This signature captures a cellular stress-response and protein quality control programme dominated by heat shock proteins (HSP90B1, HSP90AB1), nucleosome-associated chromatin factors (HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2), and antioxidant enzymes (GSTP1, GPX1, TXN). The enrichment in CD14 classical monocytes with concurrent progenitor composition suggests activation of protective mechanisms during myeloid differentiation and inflammatory priming, rather than acute pro-inflammatory cytokine production.
key_evidence: HMGB1: high-mobility group damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) and transcriptional regulator; elevated in activated monocytes under stress
HSP90B1 and HSP90AB1: canonical molecular chaperones stabilizing signalling proteins critical for TLR and cytokine receptor function
GSTP1 and GPX1: glutathione-dependent detoxification and peroxide reduction; mitigate ROS produced during monocyte activation
HMGN1 and HMGN2: chromatin remodelling factors associated with transcriptionally active loci; maintain accessibility for inflammatory gene expression
TXN: thioredoxin system component mediating redox signalling and S-nitrosylation; regulates NF-κB and inflammasome activation
PTMA: apoptosis inhibitor; promotes survival of activated monocytes during inflammatory response
GAPDH and ENO1: glycolytic enzymes with moonlighting roles in transcriptional regulation and DAMP signalling
TPI1: glycolytic enzyme; supports ATP production for monocyte effector functions
suggested_validation: Validate via bulk RNA-seq or qPCR in FACS-sorted CD14 Mono stimulated with TLR ligands (LPS, Pam3CSK4) ± oxidative stress (H₂O₂). Confirm coordinate upregulation of HSP90/GSTP1/GPX1 and assess phospho-p65 NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Compare against CD16 Mono and progenitors to confirm CD14 Mono enrichment. Examine if this signature predicts inflammatory monocyte commitment from GMP and ProMono subsets.

functional_description: This signature captures the constitutive metabolic state of mature CD14 monocytes, characterized by active oxidative phosphorylation, antioxidant defence, and robust translation machinery. The enrichment of mitochondrial respiration genes (MT-CO3, UQCRH), glycolytic capacity (GAPDH), and ROS scavenging (GPX1) reflects the high bioenergetic demand of inflammatory monocytes poised for rapid effector responses. This represents a housekeeping/metabolic baseline rather than activation-specific immune programming.
key_evidence: GAPDH: glycolytic hub essential for ATP production and metabolic flexibility in activated monocytes
MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial respiratory complex proteins enabling oxidative ATP synthesis
GPX1: glutathione peroxidase for H2O2 detoxification, critical for monocyte ROS homeostasis
RPS24, RPS26, RPS17, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPS23, RPS2, EEF1B2: ribosomal and translation factors supporting high protein synthesis capacity
ACTG1: actin required for monocyte morphology and migratory capacity
High CD14 Mono (53%) with progenitor contamination (46.5%) suggests metabolic maturation signature
suggested_validation: Validate against inflammatory activation markers (TNF, IL1B, IL6, CXCL8) to confirm this is basal metabolism rather than inflammatory programming. Use FACS sorting of CD14+CCR2+ monocytes and compare metabolic flux assays (Seahorse mito stress test) and ROS production (DCFDA) between this signature-high and -low populations to functionally confirm oxidative capacity.
